Avot, Chapter Five.
"According to the effort is the reward" (Mishnah 23).
A king commissioned artist-painters to paint his palace. Each was to paint a different wall. Three painters set to work energetically, while the fourth, knowing he was skilful, idled, whiling away the weeks and living it up. Without his noticing, the deadline suddenly drew near, and there was no time left to paint. So he thought it over and covered the fourth wall with a mirror, which reflected all the other walls. The picture was splendid. The king comes in and admires the fourth wall, which reflected all the other walls. Knowing that the painter had in the end not worked and was therefore not entitled to a fee, he took three little bags of money (for the other three painters) and set them down by each one's wall, opposite the mirror wall, and said to them: Here is your fee; and to the fourth painter he said: You have three times as much as each of them (for the mirror reflected all three bags of money).
When the other three took their bags, nothing was left for the fourth, and the king said to him: "According to the effort is the reward" — you wanted to earn easily, not to work, only to enjoy reflecting another's labour; so you too have earned only reflected money. — Sichat Chulin.
Our Spiritual Leaders

(Who takes an interest in today's youth? How does our rabbinate relate to it?)
Last week the Będzin gymnastics and sports association "Hakoach" celebrated its 15th anniversary. The board took pains to make the celebration as interesting as possible, as festive as possible. For the same reason [?] the board decided that both members and guests should visit the town synagogue, where memorial prayers (hazkarot) were to be said for the deceased members — but this "action" did not succeed.
True, they put a great deal of work into it with the kehilla leaders, with whom they managed to obtain the synagogue; but that is still far too little, because the rabbinate also has a say over the synagogue, and the rabbi dug in his heels: he would not permit the synagogue unless he had an assurance that they would play no matches on the Sabbath.
Actually [?] the question is a purely religious one, and perhaps it should not concern us at all; still, it is worth pausing here — let us, on the contrary, take a look at the way religious questions concerning youth are handled.
It is quite logical and understandable that the rabbi, as mara de-atra [the local religious authority] of the town, wanted to use his power when the opportune hour came, when he had the favourable moment for it; yet on the other hand he ought to have reckoned with the fact that getting the synagogue is not the "credo" of a sports and gymnastics institution, in which all sorts of elements are found. On the contrary, we hold that the rabbinate ought to have handed over the synagogue with pleasure, at a time when there was a guarantee that everything would be in the best order and that they would remember they were in a holy place. The rabbinate, as a religious leadership, should even have used the favourable moment to say a few warm words to them — for when else does the rabbinate have the chance to gather this youth together and speak to it?
But they did not understand how to use the favourable situation for religious Judaism. At the conference between the rabbi and the "Hakoach" representatives, the latter declared that they cannot give up playing on the Sabbath purely for economic reasons, because — so they declared — Saturday and Sunday are the days that bring the institution its whole income. They therefore proposed that the kehilla board subsidise them with a sum of two to three thousand złoty a year, as was done for the Sosnowiec "Maccabi" by the Jewish kehilla board there; they would then be able to give up the Sabbath work. But as soon as people heard that money was involved, the whole matter was "folded away" [?], as if nothing at all had been discussed, and the delegates left empty-handed.
We do not, God forbid, mean to attack anyone here, nor are we out to lecture anybody; but how can one treat in such a dilettante fashion, and make light of, matters that are of the first rank for a rabbinate? What does it mean, that for the sake of a certain sum of money one should help the youth desecrate the Sabbath? It would seem that whoever else might — but a rabbinate should not have let such a favourable opportunity [?] slip out of its hands, all the more so when the money was to come from the Jewish kehilla board. It is, after all, an old rule that "there is no such thing as a poor community" — and all the more so if the rabbinate had come to intervene with the kehilla leaders, who are able to push anything through. If Sosnowiec, which has a considerably smaller budget than Będzin, could afford such a thing, then Będzin surely, surely could easily have achieved it.
You understand: in Sosnowiec, which has a great many assimilationists, where Jewish shops are open on the Sabbath, and where a large part of the "golden youth" is far from Jewish traditions — there a plan could be created that the "Maccabi" would receive two thousand złoty on condition that they not play on the Sabbath, and they succeeded in bringing it about. In Będzin, on the contrary, it was the other way round: "Hakoach" sent to the rabbinate and asked to be granted the same as Sosnowiec gave its sister association, but their proposal was rejected and they had to leave the rabbinate's doors with a refusal both of the subsidy and of the synagogue.
It is questionable [?] whether such a tactic can be understood, questionable whether we know what the rabbinate aimed at, or wished to aim at, by not letting the young people into the synagogue.
Is it really so balanced, logical and understandable to push the youth away at every opportunity? Whom does one do a favour by this, what does one achieve by not letting them come close, at a time when the youth does not want to distance itself from certain traditions that were planted in them in their childhood years? Why do you want to tear out of them what still pulses in their veins with so much warmth and enthusiasm? Should it not rather have been the opposite — that you strive to follow them step by step and see to it that they are not pushed away from the Jewish people?
They did not want to give the young people the synagogue — without which, incidentally, they managed quite well — and they did not want to talk with them when [?] they wished to receive a subsidy so as not to play on the Sabbath. Even this last point the rabbinate belittled, at a time when we know that people come to the kehilla board with all sorts of projects and with subsidies large and small, sensible and unreasonable, ridiculous and comical — and everything gets obtained; and now, when it is a matter of a subsidy of a mere two thousand złoty so that the youth will not have to desecrate the Sabbath, it is not worth it to the rabbinate, and it throws it away without any pangs of conscience.
On the other hand, when it comes to pushing through a subsidy for "anshei shlomenu" [our own people], or when someone [?] is to be squeezed into the kahal's carriage [?], then they will raise heaven and earth that the Torah is in danger, that Judaism must be saved, and see to it for Heaven's sake to push through what is so badly needed, in order to strengthen this or that position that can come in handy in a time of trouble.
Youth — what role does it play among all peoples and in all countries? Everything — the dearest and most necessary, the most beloved and most unattainable — is sacrificed for it. It is studied in every possible way, only to find out how to win it as a healthy and viable [youth] for the people and for its national interests.
With us, by contrast, nothing more is done than pretences; important problems, serious and painful questions get muddled [?] into petty, trivial deeds not even worth dwelling on. The youth is pushed away by those who ought to be its spiritual leaders, its educators and its guides.
R. Let.
A Little Feuilleton — Jews-Protestants

Jews have no idea how grateful they ought to be to Rabbenu Gershom, who decreed that one must not have two wives. I do not understand how one can describe such a noble deed with “decreed“? That is to say, a “harsh decree“? Why, it is a means of rescue for mankind. Do you really give yourselves a proper account of what economy it has brought into family life? Just imagine today, in the bitter time of crisis: two portions of Bystra [a resort], twice Marienbad, double shares of [—], two lipsticks for the lips, and not to speak of clothes, furs, foxes[?] and who knows what else and more. I am a bit of an ignoramus in these matters, because mine, may she be well, still wears long hair and is a [?]. [?] the pretensions in [—]?..
What does He who sits above do? He sends us a scholar who makes a whole revolution, he alone, and who announces[?] that from today on “every man to his own kind“: one man — one wife, and life becomes light and sweet; like little doves, quiet, calm and devoted, the little couples stroll about God's little world, at home and abroad — a real paradise. Can anyone have any complaint against Rabbenu Gershom? But I do have, to our [good?], a great complaint against him: he came a little too late. Had he popped into God's little world in the days of our father Abraham, we would not have known many troubles. First, we would have been fewer in number — and surely the Jewish question in Poland would not have been so acute; and second, and perhaps this is the most important today, there would have been no affair of Ishmael... the Arab question..
Have you ever properly thought the matter over? Ever since the days of Hagar in the desert a bit of a mess has been cooking, so that to this day we cannot get out of it. Had the little Jews at least, in this case too, suffered from forgetfulness, they would have forgotten this fatherland as well; but Israel is a stiff-necked people: pogroms he forgets, etatism together with numerus clausus he does not remember, the monopolies he long ago threw out of his memory, but some sandy piece of land, for which his forefathers fought and which they built — that sits in his mind, that he cannot forget, and he gets an idée fixe into his head: “Eretz Israel“. Everyone, the whole world shouts “Palestine“, and the Jew [?]: “Eretz Israel“. He has nothing, God spare us, to pay the rent with, he has nothing with which to redeem a little promissory note, but Eretz Israel he must build. For Eretz Israel nothing is too hard or too dear for him. Not only money — souls, young, refined, educated souls he sends off across the sea, in order to build, to build up the old, dried-out land which our stepbrother Ishmael let grow wild and desolate.
Rabbenu Gershom, why were you born so late? Only because of this have we lately become “Protestants“. The Inquisition did not have enough strength to turn us into Catholics, Nicholas could not make us Orthodox, then came Luke with Ishmael and made us “Protestants“. We keep protesting all the time: not only do we protest our own bills of exchange, we have already risen to the rank of a [?] and we protest someone else's bill — and of a very sound firm at that. Could one have believed that such a firm would go bankrupt? A firm that has so much wealth and riches: it is an “Eng-land“ [pun: “narrow land“], it has Dominions with Mandates, it is of a conservative character and it has a Labour Party. In a word, it has every good thing, and after all that it lets its bill go to protest. And if the authorised signatory (procurist) who signed the bill has died, is one then exempt from paying? After all, it was signed under the firm's stamp. Where are you, endorsers? Why don't you open your purse and buy off the protest? What do you think[?] — that because you have all joined together and made one association under the pseudonym “League“, you bear no responsibility for the guarantee you signed? Say it openly: what kind of firm is this “League“? We want to know its meaning; enough of playing hide-and-seek.
Dr. Sarne.
Homely Letters

With God's help, the week of “and they shall bring thee“...
My friend R' Shlomo, may his light shine.
I have received your letter. Your letter — received. Reading it, I was greatly astonished that you have remained so backward and do not grasp that we must go forward. How can it be that a Jew like you should complain about the great event that took place at the end of the month of Sivan in Lublin, where, thank God, the opening of the “Yeshivat Chachmei Lublin“ was celebrated? You do not like the modernisation of the Torah; we have — you write — a saying in Pirkei Avot that the way of studying Torah is: “to eat bread with salt, to sleep on the ground, to live in sorrow, and above all to study Torah for its own sake“. You bring me proofs from the Chafetz Chaim, may he live long, who runs a yeshiva in the little town of Radin, where 300 young men study under those same conditions of: the way of the Torah.. Why, you ask, would it not have been better if, with the heavy thousands of dollars that the “Lublin Temple“ cost — may it be erased — one supported the great class of Torah students, the tens of thousands of young men who suffer hunger by day and sleep in attics, and today's anusim from Russia, who break across the state borders at the risk of their lives in order to be able to enjoy the sea of the Talmud, which swims quietly, without noise, in hundreds of Jewish towns and townlets?
Oy, oy, R' Shlomo, when I read through your naive questions, I feel like asking the same question as Rashi: “Korah, who was clever, what did he see to do this?“ You, R' Shlomo, the clever one, come in our present time and stand there like the wise son of the “Ma Nishtana“, who also asks: “What is this?“ What a to-do, what noise and tumult arose when one opens a yeshiva of 50 young men in all, under the name “Yeshiva of Politics — pardon — Chachmei Lublin“!
In truth one must willy-nilly admit that in your words of reproof, in your critical remarks, there is indeed “a little bit“ of truth: the Lublin yeshiva can be compared to golden tongs with which the rabbinic throne of Lublin was seized. It is true, and it is no longer any secret, that with the yeshiva the aim was to fill the Maharshal's chair in the synagogue there... that the “Agudah“ promised Rabbi Shapira: if you manage to build the building, you will be given the Lublin rabbinate as a reward; and if the Agudah says: “taking“ is forfeit[?], then to save the “honour of the Torah“ they take sick people out of their beds, bring them to the green table, and when the sick man raises his hand they shout:
— Mazel tov!..
True, true, it annoys you, no wonder; we on the other hand are indifferent to all this, we are already used to it.. But all this is not even worth mentioning compared to what has happened! After all, we live in the twentieth century! In the epoch of modernisation. For God's sake! Perhaps you want people nowadays to sit and study Torah for its own sake as in the “dark“ times?.. You long for those types of diligent scholars who for 16 years, round the clock, wore creases into the bench?.. No, no! That is a matter for the non-party Hasidim, but not for the “Agudah“...
In the mechanised Lublin yeshiva the same system will be introduced as in all the schools, to make a distinction. The “dzwonek“ [bell] will announce at the Gemara lessons when it is the “początek“ [beginning] and when — the “koniec“ [end]; besides that a central radio station will be installed, from which the memoranda of the “Agudah“ to the League of Nations will be broadcast, and the scientific lectures entitled “How the Gerer took 'Lublin'“ and “How to drive the RMB“N [Rabbi Meir Baal HaNes?] charity boxes out of Jewish homes“...
To the question: why did the rebbes of Aleksander, Modzhitz, Sokolow, etc. not take part? — this is not the place to explain everything properly. What is quite clear is that Aleksander has a sense of smell and sensed that “what they're after is not the Haggadah but the knaidlach“: the yeshiva is secondary, and the rabbinate is the main thing — tongs made with tongs.. And since Aleksander did not travel, the Modzhitzer rebbe, an in-law of Aleksander, also stayed at home.
The Sokolower rebbe is actually inclined towards the “Agudah“, but the voice of Jerusalem concerning the RMB“N charity boxes prevailed over Agudah politics..
About this matter I will write to you at length, God willing. In the great heat I must be brief this time; so have a good Sabbath, as always wishes you
Ben Amotz.
The main thing I forgot! Perhaps there is in your parts a barometer that would show what the tangled veil of the Sosnowiec rabbinate looks like?.. Send it to me, I need it for the Sosnowiec kehilla representatives...
The above.
What's Happening in Zagłębie? — Będzin: The Old Ones Are Gone and the New Ones Don't Come...

[Będzin — Kehilla.]
What's happening in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 8 Tammuz 5690 — Piątek 4 lipca 1930.)
Będzin
The old ones are gone and the new ones don't come...
As is known, the starosta (district head) appointed Messrs. Liwer, Buchwajz[?], Szenwald and Goldsztajn as members of the kehilla board.
The new "dozors" (kehilla board members) are summoned to meetings, but they do not come. At the first meeting, which was supposed to take place last week, Mr. Goldsztajn declared that, given such a cold attitude of the kehilla board towards its duties, he cannot take the responsibility upon himself, and that he will consult with his comrades whether he should accept the office of board member.
Jewish Merchants Are Being Ruined and Nobody Cares About It.

[Będzin — Taxes and Trade.]
More than once we have already touched in the columns of our paper upon the painful question that in the "Izba Skarbowa" (Treasury Chamber) in Kielce, where the tax appeals are dealt with, the local [—] merchants and petty traders do not have a single representative who would defend [them against] the great tax injustices.
As we are informed, at the last session in Kielce a great many appeals of local Jewish merchants were not considered, because Będzin is not represented at the sessions.
— Merchants' associations! Where are you? Why do you allow Jewish merchants to be ruined through no fault of their own?
From Public School No. 2

[Będzin — Education.]
We are asked to announce that the boys who have qualified to go to the summer colony in Słojków[?] should report to the school's secretariat.
—o—
[Czeladź — Municipality.]
No-Confidence Vote Against the Czeladź Mayor.
At Tuesday's session of the Czeladź town council a vote of no confidence in the local mayor, Piwowar, was passed by a majority. Afterwards Piwowar declared that he places himself at the disposal of the central authorities.
"If You Have Sinned, Then Pay a Bribe"...

[Będzin/Dąbrowa — Extortion.]
Mr. B. of Dąbrowa, a young Hasidic man who prays at the Ger shtibl in Dąbrowa, was walking at 10 o'clock in the evening from the Warpie towards the old station. As he walked he noticed that an unknown young man was following him. Because of this Mr. B. went to the tram stop in order to wait for the tram to Dąbrowa. The unknown "observer" also got onto the same tram. On the way the young man turned to Mr. B. with these words: "Listen here, young man, I know where you have just been; if I get 50 gulden from you, well and good; if not, I'll ride with you to Dąbrowa and tell your wife what I saw"...
When Mr. B. saw that the fellow was speaking "serious words," he began to haggle with him, and in the end they settled on 20 zł.
Only when the young man had taken his "wages" did he release "the captive soul" from Dąbrowa, and he rode back home to Będzin.
When he came home to his friends, they laughed at him: "20 gulden — we would have taken [more] from such a sitting duck! — they shouted — go out to him, let him add another 30 gulden"...
The young fellow followed his friends' advice, and the next morning he did indeed travel to Dąbrowa, where he waited for the "sinful man" as he was going to pray...
Mr. B. began to convulse[?] and begged his "executor" (bailiff) to leave him in peace. "After all — he cried — I owe my soul to God"..
— "You'll add 30 gulden; if not, I'm already at your apartment and your wife will soon know where you were in Będzin."
Mr. B., seeing that "he was stuck in the barrel," barely managed to persuade his observer to wait until he had finished praying, and then he would pay the rest.
The young fellow agreed to this, went for a while into a nearby confectionery, and Mr. B. went into the shtibl to pray.
Having finished praying[?], he went to one of his friends, before whom he poured out his bitter heart.
The friend immediately called a plain-clothes agent, to whom he told what had happened here.
The plain-clothes agent then went down into the street and, according to the previously agreed plan, took up a position to the side, from where he watched the further course of events.
When he saw that the "business" was continuing, he arrested the young man from Będzin and took him to the police station.
While the report was being drawn up, the young fellow declared that he had been watching Mr. B. on suspicion that he was passing counterfeit money...
The epilogue of the "sensational" story will take place in court.
A Tourist Society Founded.

[Będzin — Societies.]
At the starostwo (district office) a meeting was held to found a tourist society in Zagłębie.
The meeting was opened by Engineer Ferk[?], who explained the aims of the society. After the discussion a board was elected, which Mr. Eswan[?] also joined.
In Honour of the End of the School Year

[Będzin — Education.]
A large number of schoolchildren from the so-called "public" schools gathered in the synagogue, where the cantor Mr. Żupewicz[?] sang a chapter of Psalms and the school orchestra played the Polish and the Jewish anthem.
It is worth noting that none of the kehilla leaders, nor the members of the rabbinate, found it necessary to come to the synagogue and attend the ceremony of the public-school children...
Guest Performances of the Łódź Yiddish Theatre.

[Zagłębie — Theatre.]
The well-known Łódź troupe of the local "Philharmonia" there, under the direction of Mr. Bezman[?], has come to Zagłębie for several guest performances. Taking part in the troupe are the artists well known in Zagłębie: Bezman, Herszkowicz, Hamburger, Rakow and others.
This Saturday the sensational play "On the Way to Buenos Aires," a portrayal of underworld life, will be performed for the second time.
2 Children Buried Alive

[Czeladź — Accident.]
In Czeladź the following tragic incident occurred, which cost the lives of 2 children.
The 7-year-old Zygmunt and the 4-year-old Arela[?] Łukaszewska went to a place where sand is dug. While playing with the sand, the children stood on an undermined spot. At that moment a lump of earth broke off and buried the unfortunate children under it.
When the parents came back from work, they began to look for the children and did not find them. Only towards evening were the 2 little dead bodies taken out of the sand.
Sosnowiec — City Council Resolves to Build a Bus Station

[Sosnowiec — City council.]
Sosnowiec
City council resolves to build a bus station.
At Thursday's city-council meeting Eng. Rzeszkoski[?] reported on the claims which the city has against the firm Ulen, which carried out the sewerage system and the water mains.
The sum of the claims amounts to 900,439 zł.
The request to exempt from tax the performances of the Polish theatre in Grudziądz is rejected.
Then President Wilger[?] reported on the plan to build a bus station. The station will be built on Dęblińska[?]–Graniczna street and will cost about 70 thousand zł.
After this information the city council approved the plan.
During the Funeral of 2 Tragically Killed Workers a Fire Breaks Out and a Fireman Breaks a Leg

[Sosnowiec — Disaster.]
In Klimontów the funeral took place of 2 workers who were killed in the „Stabara“[?] coal mine.
As soon as the funeral began, a fire broke out in the house, and when a fireman drove off to bring water, he fell off the cart and broke his left leg.
Saved from a Catastrophe

[Sosnowiec — Accident.]
On Sunday a group of Jewish young people went on an excursion to Ojców. On the way back a wheel of the car broke and all the passengers fell out onto the highway. Luckily nobody was hurt.
The Board „Spurs On“ the Vice-Chairman of the Kehilla Council

[Sosnowiec — Kehilla.]
The kehilla board has already several times turned to the vice-chairman of the kehilla council asking him to call a meeting of the council. The vice-chairman, however, does not want to hear of it and calls no meeting. Because of this the board has notified the vice-chairman that if he does not call a meeting in the next few days, the board will itself settle what lies within the competence of the council.
A Jewish Painters' Guild Founded

[Sosnowiec — Artisans.]
In the presence of Referent[?] Mr. Lechowski, the founding meeting of the Jewish painters' and glaziers' guild (cech) in Sosnowiec took place on Sunday in its own premises.
After the reading of the statutes the following board was elected: starszy (guild master) — Michał Herman Cymberknas[?]; podstarszy (deputies) — Wolf Meller, Józef Brechner and J. Brumer. Board members: A. Sprinc and L. Zilberberg; substitutes: J. Kalb, A. Abramczyk.
On the audit committee: Isakow, Kugelman[?] and Garfinkel.
Sosnowiec Gets 5 More Kiosks

[Sosnowiec — Economy.]
Through the intercession of the Invalids' Union, the management of the State Tobacco Monopoly has decided to set up another 53 tobacco kiosks in a number of towns in Poland. Of this number Sosnowiec gets another 5 kiosks.
A 14-Year-Old Boy Drowned

[Sosnowiec — Disaster.]
On Kaliska street the 14-year-old Sztajfer and the 12-year-old Rachwalski were bathing in the local river. While bathing both boys began to drown. At the cries Rachwalski's father arrived, went into the water and saved his child, whereas Sztajfer was taken out already dead.
The Magistrate treats Mandżewska Street like a stepchild...

The residents of Mandżewska Street [Yiddish „Mandzhever gas“; ?Mandżewska] complain about the Magistrate (municipal council), which treats the street like a stepchild. All the not-busy[?] streets are sprinkled with water every day; only Mandżewska Street is an exception in this respect.
Came to sell writing materials and stole an object.

A young man entered the flat of Mr. Y. M. Wigreb[?] and asked that they buy writing-material articles from him. When Mrs. W. went out into another room, the young man took from the table a glass vessel, an antique, and disappeared with it.
Dąbrowa; Olkusz — news

Dąbrowa [Dąbrowa Górnicza]
Instead of the army — into prison.
Several recruits were to depart from the local station. Before departing they „bade farewell“[?] to the army and shouted anti-state slogans. The policeman on duty wanted to detain the recruits, but they put up resistance. The policeman then used his weapon and lightly wounded them.
—o—
The hands are the hands of Esau...
In Zagórze 2 Christian neighbours had a quarrel between them. From words they passed to deeds, and both gave each other a severe beating[?]. The local doctor found serious wounds on them.
—o—
Deputy mayor of Dąbrowa — school inspector
The Minister of Education has appointed the deputy mayor (vice-president) of Dąbrowa, Mr. Kuszgiak[?], as school inspector for the Będzin district (powiat).
—o—
Olkusz.
Starostwo forces the kehilla to lease out the mikveh.
For a number of years the Jewish community (gmina) maintained the mikveh from its budget, and it was free for everyone. After an inspection (lustracja) by the Starostwo the community received an order to lease out the mikveh. The community set an auction (licytacja) for 26 June, but because no bidders came forward, the auction was postponed. The price[?] was set at 500 zł. for half a year.
—o—
A car ran over a child.
On 3 Maja Street a car seriously ran over a 6-year-old Christian child.
It is worth noting that there is hardly a day on which some accident with cars does not happen. Such accidents often occur because of the fast driving of the cars that run to Ojców.
—o—
„Fine“ deeds of a school headmaster.
On the order of the prosecutor in Sosnowiec [printed „Pasnowiec“], the local police arrested and took to the Będzin prison the headmaster of the elementary school (szkoła powszechna) in Żurada near Olkusz. The headmaster is accused of committing immoral acts with his female pupils. The children's parents wanted to lynch the scoundrel, but by a miracle he was saved.
A. B.
—o—
Toward an artificial leg for a cripple.
There is in Będzin a respectable Jew who has become a cripple and needs an artificial leg.
For this worthy purpose the following have given: the Magistrate 50 zł., the Charitable Society 25 zł., „Ahavat Chesed“ 25 zł., and the Jewish community 15 zł.
Further donations are accepted at our editorial office.

Sienkiewicza, which are the property of the town and occupy an area too small to house an artillery regiment, will be moved to the grounds by ul. Grzychowska [sic] and Grodziecka. Tragic Death of a Jewish Woman in Dąbrowa

[Dąbrowa — accident.] On Monday morning a terrible accident occurred at the railway station in Dąbrowa, which cost the life of a Jewish woman, a resident [?] of Dąbrowa.
As soon as the terrible news spread through the town, it could not be established who the unfortunate woman was, because the body was badly crushed, so that at first it was hard to recognise who she was; but it did not take long before it was recognised that the tragic victim was the 38-year-old Mindl [?] Nusbaum of Dąbrowa.
As is reported, the tragic incident occurred under the following circumstances:
A daughter of Mrs. Nusbaum is staying at a summer residence in Olkusz, and the devoted mother travelled to visit her on Monday. She also took along one of hers [?], a boy, who also wanted to stay in Olkusz with his sister.
When she arrived at the station the train was already standing there, and the doorman at first did not want to let her out to the train, but at her pleas he let her out with the boy. The boy went into the carriage first and after him Mrs. Nusbaum, but as the train began to move off, the woman fell out of the carriage and down under the wheels. Nobody noticed it, and several carriages passed over the unfortunate woman's body.
The tragic incident made a shattering impression throughout Zagłębie.
On the evening of the same day the funeral took place, at which heart-rending scenes were played out. The very stones wept together with the 7 young orphans left behind.

“Articles that Incite.”

[Będzin — municipality and the water question; Tenants' Association.] (The water question continued. — Almost a reply to the president of the “Tenants' Association” [Lokatorn-Fareyn].)
Not long ago, in one of our articles, we touched, among other things, on the question of the water mains in Będzin, and in discussing the matter we pointed out emphatically [?] that it is an injustice that the “Tenants' Association” says not a word on the question and that it takes no position at all.
We said: whoever else, but the “Tenants' Association” as such ought to have dealt more intensively with this topical question, and we ought to have heard what this institution says about the question, which has only just come into force. But the said institution, after we pressed it to the wall, deliberated for two weeks and then sent in a reply that... that was neither here nor there: neither do we know what the president answered in his own honoured person, nor could the readers draw anything out of the printed letter.
The president did not tell us what his association did do and what it did not do, what could and what could not be done — upon my life, that is incitement! Merely to discharge his duty he apparently told us about the decree of the President of the State, which can only be changed with the help of the Sejm, and one cannot reach that far, since one swallow does not make a summer...
But what are these inquiries for, why break down open doors? Nobody demanded that of you. We merely said, and we repeat it a second time, that the “Tenants' Association” ought at least to have told the tenants what they should do — whether they should pay for the water or not. You speak about [“about” printed twice] the “decree” of the President of the State and pity the writer of these lines, saying it is not your fault that he does not know of it; but it is quite indifferent whether he knew of it or not. Besides, he is also your member, and you ought to have informed all your members what they should do and how they should conduct themselves. Your task, after all, is to protect the interests of the tenants, and even now the tenants hear nothing from your association about how they should conduct themselves. You ought to have issued an official communiqué to your members on what they should do — whether they have to pay for the water or not — with what was said properly justified, and then we would have had no complaints against you. If we do have complaints against you, they are only because you do not give the proper instructions, thanks to which the public is led into needless expenses.
And even now you must say clearly and plainly what the tenant has to do, because to this very day you have not done so. That is what should lie within your competence; that is the responsibility that rests on you.
This we demand of you in the name of the tenants and their interests — is that to be called, as you put it, demagogy? Or, as you say further, that with our “articles that rouse the public one cannot improve the situation”? We are not at all out to attack you, because we hold that the “Tenants' Association” must exist and act in society as long as the tenants' question is not solved; otherwise we would have had to point out to you that you were far from standing on guard in many questions, and indeed in the latest one, which the [?] president holds to be already definitively solved — regardless of how unfavourably it has been settled for your members, the tenants.
The city councillors ought at least to have protected the tenants to the extent that the house-owners pay the Magistrat for the water the sum the water has cost them until now, and the tenants pay the difference; the councillors could surely have taken that into account, and the tenants' representatives ought to have stood on guard here and protected the interests of their members.
Not to lift a finger [literally: not to put one's hand into cold water] and to say that “we act quietly and modestly and you write incitement articles” is more than unfair and immodest, Mr. President! That the water question has been badly settled — about that there are no two opinions anywhere around; everyone sees it; whereas at the “Tenants' Association” everything is in the best order. They see nothing — is that to be called a clear view? Can one not call it short-sightedness?
Fate has willed that precisely now, in the most critical time in Poland, the tenant in Będzin should be burdened with yet another tax — the payment for water, which is treated as nothing other than a kind of tax, since one is fined if one does not pay punctually. Thus, for example, we know of tenants to whom the house-owners did not send to collect for the water and who afterwards returned the receipts to the Magistrat, which sent its collector to collect; the tenant argued that the house-owner had not notified him and that he wanted to pay, but without a fine — a sum the collector refused to accept, arguing that he had had time to pay without a fine before he received the collection notice. So the question arises: must the tenant really be so sinful that he has to suffer and pay a fine for another's lack of punctuality, which is committed by whoever committed it [?]? Does it mean that if the landlord does not live in peace with his tenant, he will not notify him that he has to pay for water, and then the tenant will already be liable to a fine of such-and-such? Or when a landlord keeps no order at all, and the tenant has, besides the water, some other matter on his mind, such as paying a bill of exchange or running about to earn a loaf of bread — will he then already be liable to a fine? One cannot call this a splendid economy, an excellent order, an exemplary management.
It is altogether impossible to understand on what grounds the fines are imposed; at most one should leave the client a reminder [monit] that he has time until such-and-such a date to pay. In what is this worse or better than any other debt, or, for example, than the electricity [bill]?
Upon my life, wonderful ideas, magnificent powers our city councillors have given the municipal self-government.
And this, Mr. President of the “Tenants' Association”, you will say is good and fine and right and just, and as soon as we want to point out such, in our opinion unjustified, wrongs, you will come and say that we write articles that incite the public?
That is how far short-sightedness reaches, once people persuade themselves that everything they do is good and fine, and that all the mistakes made must be carried on their shoulders by the citizens who sent their representatives there to administer the city's interests.
R. Let.
Examinations for Masters and Apprentices ("Terminators") (3)

3.
There are 67 kinds of industrial branches that fall under Art. 142 of the Industrial Law, i.e. those that must hold craftsman's cards and diplomas. Considered as industry in the sense of the law are all gainful occupations or enterprises carried on independently and professionally, regardless of whether they are producing, processing, commercial or service-providing — insofar as they are not run in a factory manner.
The craftsman's cards enabled all artisans in the sense of the Industrial Law (about which we spoke in more detail in the previous article) to run their workshops independently and to employ apprentices ("terminators") only until 15 December 1930. After that date every artisan will be required to have an appropriate diploma.
In circular No. 16 of 21 May of this year the Kielce Chamber of Crafts published the regulations of the examination commission for journeyman's and master's diplomas, of which we give here the most important points. Incidentally, it must be stressed at the outset that since the majority of artisans hold no diploma whatsoever, the journeyman's and master's examinations will take place together.
The application for admission to the said examination must be submitted by the candidate to the president of the Chamber of Crafts in writing or orally. To the application must be attached: 1) a birth certificate (metric) or a passport, 2) a short curriculum vitae, 3) a craftsman's card or a certificate from the relevant gmina (municipal) office concerning independent work in the trade in question before 15 December 1927, 4) the fixed fee for the examination (140 zł.). If the candidate already holds a journeyman's diploma, he must also attach it to the same application, and the fee is then only 100 zł.
The examining commission consists of a chairman, who is in principle a master in the given trade or a person with higher technical education who is professionally employed as a teacher or holds [?] a managerial post in an industrial enterprise, and in addition 2 members who have the right to employ apprentices in the trade in question and who live within the district of the Kielce Chamber of Crafts (i.e. the 2 commission members may also be Sosnowiec or Będzin masters when it concerns the artisans of Zagłębie). During the examination the candidate is asked questions by the chairman and the 2 commission members.
The programme of the examinations is more or less as follows: for the journeyman candidate — general knowledge needed by a journeyman in the given craft; and for a master — a discussion of the work carried out in his workshop and a demonstration [?] of his production.
The chairman notifies the 2 commission members and the candidates of the place and date of the examinations.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion

Torah sayings and remarks on this week's Torah portion
Collected and adapted by Y. L.
Parshat Balak
—o—
a) "Lo, it is a people that shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations" (23:9).
Because "it shall not be reckoned among the nations" — because the Jew is not esteemed among the peoples, but loathed and hated — because of that, "it shall dwell alone": this is what preserved his separateness, his distinctiveness. It is precisely this lack of esteem among the gentiles that has kept us alive in exile, for were it not so, we would long ago have mingled with them; it is a miracle that the gentiles do not want us and push us away from themselves. Degel Machaneh Ephraim.
* * *
When they began to take Jews into the army, the Noda BiYehuda[?] said about it: "I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly" — when it is a matter of "to destroy them," to exterminate us, to send Jews to the front, into the fire — then "I will not reject them": then they no longer find us disgusting; to send us into the fire, they are not repelled by us...
—o—
b) "Let me die the death of the righteous" (23:10).
To die — they all want to die like pious Jews, "let me die the death of the righteous"; but to live like Jews they do not want: in life to do every evil, and to die like pious Jews. Or Pnei Moshe.
—o—
c) "Now it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel: What hath God wrought!" (23:23).
When R' Yitzchak Elchanan [Spektor, rabbi of Kovno] together with other rabbis once appeared before a Russian minister to plead for the annulment of a decree against the Jews, one of the statesmen present, a great hater of Israel, set upon the rabbinic delegation and reviled them; among other things he said: "Everything God created in the world has some use, but for what did He create such a base and vulgar people as the Jews?"
The delegation left downcast, but R' Yitzchak Elchanan smiled. "A verse in the Torah," he said, "has become clear to me: 'Now' (a time will come when) 'it shall be said of Jacob' (when they will say of the Jews) 'what hath God wrought?' (for what did God create you?) — and when things are already that sad, then it will be: 'Behold, the people shall rise up as a lioness, and lift itself up as a lion.'"
—o—
d) "And he saw Israel dwelling according to their tribes" (24:2).
Rashi says: Balaam saw "that their doorways were not aligned facing one another" — that their doors did not face each other, so that no one looks in on what is happening at his neighbour's — and he said: they are worthy that the Divine Presence should rest upon them.
For the Gemara lists, among the qualities one must possess to be worthy of the Divine Presence resting upon a person, also "rich." Does the Divine Presence, God forbid, wish to associate only with a man of wealth? Rather, what is meant is "Who is rich? He who rejoices in his lot": the one who is content with his own and is not vexed that more wealth peers out of someone else's door — he is worthy that the Divine Presence should rest upon him. Pninei Yekarim.
—o—
e) "How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, thy dwellings, O Israel" (24:5).
It is right when "how goodly are thy tents, O Jacob" — when beautiful, splendid synagogues are built; but "thy dwellings, O Israel" — in the synagogues there should be Jews who study and pray, not mere museum-synagogues... Toldot Yaakov Yosef.
—o—
f) "Come, I will advise thee what this people shall do to thy people" (24:14).
Thus Balaam advised Balak: with no decrees and wars will you overcome the stubborn Jews. On the contrary, they will come out of it strengthened and purified. There is only one plan: give them equal rights, assimilate them — "this people shall do to thy people." Let them be counted as your people, "[…][?] of the Mosaic faith" — with that you will overcome them. From[?] the Kotzker Rebbe.
—o—
g) "I behold him, but not nigh... and Israel doeth valiantly" (24:17).
According to the homily, this speaks of the days of the Messiah. "I behold him, but not nigh" — not so soon will he come, the Messiah, because "Israel doeth valiantly": Jews still have some property, and "the son of David will not come until the last penny is gone from the purse" — until all Jews are paupers... Rabbi Moshe of Przeworsk.
* * *
When money lies in a purse, one does not hear it; on the other hand, "a coin in a jug cries 'kish, kish'" (Bava Metzia 85) — when it does not lie in its proper place but in a metal vessel, it jingles and makes a noise. Now, during the war the money went away from its proper places, from the honourable[?], pedigreed families, over into metal vessels — to upstart rich men. And indeed it makes a noise, it jingles and shouts...
That is the meaning of "the Messiah will not come until the last penny is gone from the purse": when the money is taken out of the proper places, out of the purse, and handed over to the "jugs," the upstarts — those are truly the days of the Messiah... Milei de-Rabbanan.
—o—
Avot, chapter six.
"Bread with salt shalt thou eat, water by measure shalt thou drink... if thou doest thus, happy art thou and it shall be well with thee" (Mishnah 5)
"The way of the Torah" is indeed thus: "bread with salt shalt thou eat... upon the ground shalt thou sleep, and a life of hardship shalt thou live." The rich men know this — that a yeshiva student must sleep on the ground and eat bread with salt; after all, the Mishnah says so. But "if thou doest thus" — if you too do so, if you too eat bread with salt and sleep on the ground... Overheard.

[Sport — "Hakoach"; essay.] (Reflections after the "Hakoach" celebrations)
Shimon Rotenberg.

Parallel with the decline of the political independence of the Jewish people begins the decline of the physical culture which had existed among Jews, in the most varied forms, while they lived as an independent kingdom in the Land of Israel.

But when, before the gates of Jerusalem, the last act was played out of the bloody drama which history calls "the Fall of Judah," the Jewish sages of that time understood that this was the end of the Jews' political power and that, despite the extraordinary heroism with which they had defended themselves, they would still not succeed in overcoming the mighty Roman legions, which had then spread their bloody wings over the whole ancient world.

The Jewish sages therefore realised that the only way to save the Jewish people from extinction was to create a spiritual centre — which was indeed founded at Yavneh — and in this way to create spiritual values that would penetrate among the nations, and thereby to win for themselves a right to exist in the family of nations.

We carried out this plan brilliantly. We created a colossal output of spiritual values and of the most varied ideas; but while we were always merely the theoreticians, others exploited our ideas and made a life out of them. That is how it is in life: those who hold power exploit the ideas of the weak — exclusively for their own selfish ends. Schopenhauer could in no way forgive us our love of life, our talent for living. But he was mistaken when he regarded our crippled pseudo-life as love of life.

We did indeed, in our earliest youth, enter history with "therefore choose life," but the makers of history arranged things so that life in this world became loathsome to us, and we were forced, in order not to perish, to become mere "world-to-come people," while the whole of "this world" others meanwhile took for themselves.

Beginning with the Roman street-urchins and their "Hep! Hep," we were driven out of the ancient world into the dark Middle Ages, where every living soul had power over us [printed "shlise", read "shlite"], from the knights down to the guild journeymen. We were the target-board for every maniac, for every outcast, for everyone who merely had "God" in his heart; they made of us the best fuel for the "autos-da-fé," at which the black, sinister Jesuits, with a hypocritical, foul prayer on their lips, supposedly wanted to redeem our souls, meanwhile burning our broken and tortured bodies.

Crammed into the ghettos, lacking the most elementary conditions for existence, we still had to live, and so we became a people of fakirs who know the art of living buried in the earth, without air, without light, and yet managing to reproduce new generations and to stay on the surface of life.

Hunted by the enraged mob like mice into their holes, the Jews became so weakened, so downtrodden and so inferior that it could not even enter their minds what physical resistance is [the original wording is slightly garbled]. Popular fantasy therefore had, as a substitute for real physical strength, to create the "Golem," the avenger and protector of the Jewish communities, the one who possesses metaphysical qualities, the one who can overcome all difficulties and rescue in a time of trouble.

Thus on the stage of the world theatre we played the role of the Charlie Chaplins, of the tragicomedians; but it always turned out that while we were living through the bloodiest tragedies, we were, for the world, the comedians, the clowns, who have to put on merry spectacles for the great gallery called "the world of mankind."

Our whole literature, our whole art is permeated with sad motifs, reminiscent of the ghost motifs of "Peer Gynt." There is no sign of joy, no trace of zest for life. And if we do sing, we are the singers of our own sorrow. Our humour is gallows humour, that is, the mocking of our own weaknesses, of our pitiful life, which has always been a "khish latens" [?], a hidden cave-life.

Therefore, seeing the splendid joy-march of the young gymnasts, the heart rejoiced at the fruits of the renaissance of physical culture among us. It was impossible to remain indifferent watching the various exercises performed by the male and female gymnasts with such grace, with such a fine rhythm. What an enormous abyss there is between the "joy-march" of the gymnasts and the well-known classic "Exile March" of Hirschberg [?].

Such a youth will no longer remain passive in life; it will no longer be the dough out of which anyone who feels like it can knead a toy for himself and destroy it once he has finished playing with it. Such a youth can be led into the struggle for its existence without fear of desertion. This is attested by their whole bearing, their healthy muscles and the gleam that sparkles from their eyes.

Life today [printed "heyt" for "haynt"] is no romance, and if once one could walk through life, today one must push one's way through, and for that one needs healthy fists — despite the fact that we live in an epoch of supposedly high civilisation, which has perhaps managed to create "Homo sapiens," the wise man (in fact, the cunning one), but man has not become better thereby; on the contrary, he has become worse.

It is therefore the duty of the whole community to support the sports movement among Jews, which can be regarded as the best preventive means of preserving health and improving the race. These are old axioms among other nations, but among us, unfortunately, people do not realise the necessity of sport, and a large part of society still regards it as a game.

Everyone must therefore know that sport, properly applied, is a necessity for every person; it is the best [remedy?] for driving away illnesses. And even those who cannot themselves take up sport, but find themselves among sportsmen, become infected with the microbe of joy of life and immediately feel their state of mind improve on hearing the call of the gymnasts' watchword, the four magic letters "Chazak ve-ematz" ("Be strong and of good courage").
Będzin Needs a Beach (Plaża)...

Oh, the heat! Oh, the heat!
I can't stand, I can't sit,
Instead of lying on the beach
I must, poor me, write jokes..
A scandal, gentlemen, a tremendous scandal! It's enough to make you cry out "Shema Yisrael". Będzin, which possesses grandiose factories, which has such a "modern" mikveh on the Grablia[?] and possesses such a Jewish kehilla whose name rings from one end of Poland to the other... Będzin, which is rich in such wonderful institutions of culture and education as "Góra Zamkowa" (Castle Hill) and wszymne[?] d... — should not have even one single beach where one could, in summer, in the great heat, after hard work, rest one's tired, broken bones.
I ask you, gentlemen, is this not a scandal?
For Będzin, you should know, is by nature itself suited to a first-class beach.
Let us see, gentlemen, what does one need for a beach?
We know, after all, that the first thing is sand.. So show me, gentlemen, another town in Poland that has as much sand as Będzin?
My wife brings me a black roll for breakfast in the morning, and as soon as I take the first bite, I already have a mouthful of sand... I go to the New Market and want to sit down on a bench — first I have to shake the sand off with a handkerchief...
I stroll along our Broadway — along Małachowskiego Street — a car drives by and fills my eyes with sand..
In short, as for sand, it seems there is no shortage. So what will you say — water? A beach needs water too, and who else is as rich in water as our Będzin...
On the contrary, just go, if you'll pardon me, to a session of the town council and listen to one debate — you will immediately feel so much water [i.e. empty talk] that it could be enough to water a whole herd of oxen..
So there is no shortage of water either..
Then why is everyone silent? Why doesn't anyone make a beach?...
Będzin needs a beach even more than a "garden"... because a beach is the best place to rest after the great heat and to take stock of one's soul (cheshbon ha-nefesh)...
And a beach brings tremendous benefit not so much to us as to our wives...
And not so much to our wives as to our daughters... For them the beach seems to have been created in the six days of Creation...
For apart from the "hygienic" conditions a beach offers, a beach can sometimes serve our daughters as a matchmaker...
How many girls, do you think, have already become brides on the beach?.. And not only brides, but even wives.. More than one has already found her true destined one there...
More than one girl on the beach
Gets helped in a single while,
There no one looks at clothes —
Nakedness is quite a virtue...
Men, women, boys, girls,
Old grannies and old men too —
There democracy reigns —
They all lie there together...
There no one asks about a dowry,
On the beach in the heat,
One slogan holds there for all —
Tanning[?], flirting and sweating...
Graf Kali.

Snakes at the Dachas.

(Reports sent in by our special dacha correspondents).
Olkusz: In the local forest a snake was noticed at 12 o'clock at night. It was looking for someone to bite. The snake is a metre and a half long, brown in colour.
One man, a father, an "expert", explained that he had once met this snake in Sosnowiec on Glowaga[?] Street, but that time it did not bite...
———
Leśniów near Żarki: Last Wednesday, between Mincha and Maariv, a poisonous snake was noticed here. Later it turned out that it was a — cat.
———
Krynica: A commotion broke out here among the dacha guests. Not far from the "Deptak" (promenade), among the dense trees, some suspicious creature was noticed crawling on its belly; it is presumed to be a snake.
As your correspondent learns, the story is true, but it was not a four-legged creature, only a two-legged one..,

What's New in Zagłębie?

[Page header — the local section.] Friday, 15 Tammuz 5690.
Piątek 11 lipca 1930 [Friday, 11 July 1930].
Będzin — Thank God, We Are Already Provided with an 'El Male Rachamim' Maker...

[Będzin — community; cantors and the burial society.]
Będzin
Thank God, we are already provided with an 'El Male Rachamim' maker...
The kehilla board has received a letter from the rabbinate announcing that henceforth the future new cantor of the synagogue is to receive at his disposal one cemetery on Rosh Chodesh Elul, and the beit-midrash cantor too is to receive one cemetery..
The gabbaim of the Chevra Kadisha were greatly surprised by this announcement and decided to deal with the matter at a special meeting.
A Loan of 300 Thousand Złoty for Small Traders and Craftsmen

[Będzin and the region — economy; credit for small traders and craftsmen.]
As we have already reported, the Polish and Jewish small traders and craftsmen of Będzin, Sosnowiec, Dąbrowa and Czeladź are receiving a loan from the Bank Gosp. Krajow. [Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego] in the amount of 300,000 zł.
The sum will be repaid in instalments over two and a half years.
As we are told by a reliable source, the loan will be disbursed at the beginning of the month of August (sierpień) of this year.
Those interested must register for it with their organisations in each town.
Get Yourselves Craftsman's Cards

[Będzin — craftsmen; police inspections.]
This week an order arrived from the voivode to the police that inspections (lustrations) are to be carried out among the craftsmen, in order to check whether the owners of the workshops hold craftsman's cards.
In this connection, in the course of the week inspections were carried out at a number of craftsmen, and those who did not have the above-mentioned cards were made criminally liable.
A 'Scholar' Out of the Society...

[Będzin — the free-loan (gemilut chesed) fund.]
On the board of the Gemilut Chesed fund there is also Mr. Elazar Prechtcwajg [?], who is a 'recalcitrant' and does not nod 'yes' to everything that is done in the institution.
Because of this, at the last board meeting a proposal was brought to expel the 'apikores' (heretic) from the board...
Yesterday — Judgment Day for the City Budget

[Będzin — municipality; the city budget.]
Yesterday, Thursday, this year's city budget was dealt with at the Kielce voivodeship office.
The budget was defended by: Mayor Michel, Vice-Chairman of the City Council Jakub Erlich, and Alderman Błażejewicz.
Received the Lawyer's Title

[Będzin — personal news; academic studies.]
The young men Yitzchak Zilbershats and Heniek Levin passed their examinations at the Kraków University this week and received the title of lawyers (jurists).
City Council Sessions — Postponed

[Będzin — city council.]
The city council sessions, which were to have taken place last Wednesday and Thursday, will take place next Monday and Tuesday with the same agenda.
The presidium of “Hachnasat Kala”

[Będzin — charitable societies.] The new board of the “Hachnasat Kala” (dowering of poor brides) society elected at its first meeting a presidium consisting of: Hirsh Ber Goldblum [?] (president), Chavele [?] Unger (vice-president), Noach Ojaud [?] (treasurer), Hershel Szpigeler (secretary).
A conference on sanitary matters

[Będzin — traders; sanitation.] Last Sunday a conference took place in the premises of the Small Traders' Association, with the participation of the police commissioner, small traders and owners of beer-houses. The conference dealt with the question of improving the sanitary condition of the beer-houses and of the storerooms for foodstuffs.
After the discussion, in which Messrs. Chairman Rechnic, Gutsztajn and Altman took part, it was resolved to urge the merchants to keep their shops clean in order to avoid police reports (protocols).
At the international congress

[Będzin — municipality.] At the international congress of local self-governments in Antwerp the local city administration is represented by its vice-president, Mr. Rubinlicht, who already left yesterday.
Paid the “debt” with interest
[Będzin — street incident.] On Wednesday afternoon a Jewish carter from Modrzejów met his “rival” in Kołłątaja Street. Without thinking long he paid him the “debt” with his whip..
A railway disaster beyond Gołonóg

[Dąbrowa area — accident.] On Tuesday towards evening a disaster occurred at the level crossing of the railway station in Gołonóg, which fortunately caused no human casualties.
At the moment when a cart with passengers was passing over the crossing, a goods train came up and struck the cart with great force [?].
The result: a horse was killed, the cart smashed, and the passengers got off with light injuries.
Last date for paying the advance instalments

[Będzin — taxes.] We remind all our readers that Tuesday, 15 July, is the last day on which one can pay the first advance instalment (zaliczka) of this year's turnover tax.
If one does not pay by that day, one will be pressed the next day with distraint proceedings and charged a penalty from 15 May onwards at 2 per cent monthly. That means that on the 16th of July they will already charge six per cent for three months and, in addition, 5 per cent distraint costs.
Wholesale merchants of foodstuffs who do not keep commercial books must apply to the head (naczelnik) of the local [tax] office with a request that, on the basis of the latest circular of the Ministry of Finance, the advance instalments for this year be reduced by half, calculated at 1 per cent of turnover.
Bloody clash between police and communists. 1 killed, 2 seriously wounded

[Sosnowiec — communists; police.] On Sunday morning a crowd of several hundred people gathered on the “hałdy” (slag heaps) in order to hold a protest meeting against the death sentence on communists in Lemberg [Lwów]. Since the meeting had not been permitted by the starostwo (district office), the police ordered the crowd to disperse.
At that moment the crowd, under the slogan “Disarm them”, began throwing stones and bricks and also shooting at the police. The police then answered with gunfire, and the result was this: of the crowd, 19-year-old Piotrowski was killed and 2 were seriously wounded. Of the police, policeman Szczechmacki [?] was seriously wounded, and a large number, also 2 horses, were wounded.
Many of the demonstrators were also wounded in the shooting.
When the shooting stopped, the crowd was dispersed and 11 of them, the ringleaders, were arrested. After the investigation the arrested were taken to the Mysłowice prison.
The Ministry of Religious Affairs takes care that Jews should have a cemetery...

[Sosnowiec — kehilla; budget.] This week the Jewish kehilla received the approval of the kehilla budget for the year 1930. The budget was operated on very “expertly”, so that of the budget almost only a “skeleton” has remained. It is therefore no wonder that the most important items were struck out, except for the item for the cemetery (beit ha-chaim), which the Ministry increased.
The following sums for the following purposes were struck out: the subsidy for the “Gemilut Chesed” (free-loan) fund was reduced from 15 thousand to 5 thousand zł. The subsidies for “Maccabi” (2000 zł) and for artisans' courses (4000 zł.) were struck out entirely; the pensions for the shochtim (ritual slaughterers) were reduced from 9 thousand to 6 thousand zł.; “Beit Yaakov” from 2500 to 1500 zł.
The total amount cut comes to about 45 thousand zł. According to the Ministry's wish this sum is to be used for the benefit of the cemetery.
The budget also notes that the public subsidies of the year 1929 may be paid out to the institutions concerned only with the consent of the starosta..
In connection with the reduced subsidy for the “Gemilut Chesed” fund, the board of that institution has resolved to take appropriate steps so that this important institution be subsidised according to the wish of the kehilla board and council.
As can be seen, the 30 kehilla representatives have the same rights as the Chevra Kadisha (burial society)..
A Hoard of Dollars and Złotys Found on a Dying Beggar

[Sosnowiec — incidents.] About 12 years ago a certain Berl Jurkiewicz came here from Działoszyce; he "worked" the district and collected alms, and, paying no heed to his extreme old age — about 90 years old — he did not give up his profession.
Last Friday afternoon, while coming down from the second floor of the house at Targowa 18, he suffered a heart attack and remained lying dead on the stairs.
A commission of representatives of the authorities arrived at the scene and examined the deceased's clothes, in which were found 290 dollars in cash and 1917 zł. and bills of exchange.
The Wife of the Great Industrialist Dietel Perished Tragically

[Sosnowiec — disaster.] The widow of the well-known industrialist Dietel was travelling on Sunday[?] with her son by taxi to Berlin[?]. Before Oppeln a terrible accident befell the car: a tyre[?] burst and the car went into a ditch. The result was terrible: Mrs. Dietel was killed on the spot, and her son had both legs broken.
The body was brought to Sosnowiec, where the burial took place.
A Jewish Girl Run Over
[Sosnowiec — accident.] On 1 May Street a cart ran over the 2-year-old girl Bielińska[?]. The child was taken to hospital in a serious condition.
An Association of Commercial Representatives Founded

[Zagłębie — trade.] Following the example of other commercial centres, an association of commercial representatives and agents has been founded in Zagłębie too. At the founding meeting, held on Sunday, the importance of creating the association for the large number of representatives and agents in Zagłębie and Upper Silesia was pointed out.
Then the following board was elected: [—]. Frenkel (chairman), S. Laudan (vice), J. M.[?] Szwarcbaum (vice), J. Proskirowski[?] (treasurer), S. Rozenman (secretary), M. Merin and Z. Epsztajn, deputies; M. Weinsztok and J. Fiszel, audit committee: M. Trajman and A. Kohn[?].
—o—
If You Can't Go Over, You Must Go Under
[Zagłębie — labour.] The management of Dischel's[?] factory decided to reduce wages, or else to close the factory altogether.
Because of this a conference took place between the industrialists and the workers' representatives, who signed an agreement under which the workers give up receiving the free coal that every worker gets.
—o—
A Big Bill-of-Exchange Fraud
[Zagłębie — economy.] Panic has broken out in merchant circles in Zagłębie over the news that the bills of exchange supposedly endorsed by the Lublin cement factory "Firlej" are forged.
The forged bills, as we are told, were discounted at a number of banks in Będzin, Sosnowiec, Dąbrowa and Zawiercie, and some are also in the hands of private discounters.
—o—
Drank a "L'chaim" and Then Took His Own Life
[Sosnowiec — suicide.] The 23-year-old Stuszemiński[?] borrowed a revolver from his brother-in-law Zygmunt Pszerawnik[?], went with it to the Grojec[?] forest, where he first drank a small bottle of vodka and then shot himself.
—o—
The Tunnel Will Soon Be Finished
[Sosnowiec — municipality.] The magistrate has received a telegraphic notice from the Ministry of Railways announcing that 24 thousand zł. have again been assigned for completing the tunnel on Piłsudska Street.

A Memorial Academy on Saturday Night
[Sosnowiec — Zionism.] This Saturday night a memorial academy dedicated to the memory of Dr. Herzl and Dr. Abraham Perlman[?] will take place in the "Angielski" hall. Besides Dr. Melarista[?], Dr. Higies[?] of Warsaw is also to speak at the academy.
— Next Tuesday the local "Keren Kayemet" committee is organizing an academy dedicated to the 26th anniversary of the death of Dr. Herzl.
The academy will take place in the "Angielski" hall.

Meeting of the Butchers' Guild
[Sosnowiec — butchers.] In connection with the voivode having raised the slaughter fee from 5 to 8 zł., a protest meeting of all the butchers of Sosnowiec and the surroundings will take place next Sunday at 4 p.m., to take a stand against the unjust increase.

[Będzin — municipal budget; Jewish subsidies.]
Jewish subsidies — struck out.
Last Wednesday the budget of the city of Będzin was dealt with at the Kielce voivodeship office. The budget was defended by President Michał, the deputy chairman of the city council Jakub Ehrlich and councillor Błażejewicz.
The following „operations“ were performed on the budget:
The subsidies for „Tarbut“ (500 zł.), craftsmen's courses (1000 zł.), the „Achva“ society courses (500 zł.) and the „Dom Ludowy“ [People's House] (2500 zł.) were struck out entirely.
The subsidy of 10 zł. [sic] for the chadarim Talmud Torah, „Mizrachi“ [?] and „Yesodei HaTorah“ was reduced to 5 thousand zł.
The subsidies for the Jewish orphanage (35,000 zł.) and for the commercial school (40,000 zł.) were reduced to 23 thousand zł. They will receive the rest when the municipal revenues reach the level foreseen in the budget.
The voivode reproached the city administration for not making proper use of the investment tax.
The extraordinary budget too has been badly „damaged“ — almost half of the items were struck out.
—o—
A New Jewish Bank in Sosnowiec
Last week a new Jewish bank was opened in Sosnowiec under the name „Kasa Udziałowa“ [Share Credit Fund]. At the founding meeting a board and a supervisory council were elected, consisting of the following persons:
On the board: Abraham Chajnryb [?] (chairman), Duktowicz [?] (deputy), Lubelski, Awigdor Beri and Julian Ajbeszyc.
On the supervisory council: Julian Jungster (chairman), Binyamin Peryn (deputy), Hochberger, Kalman Langer, Kornfeld, Goldkorn, Rozenryn [?].
The well-known office clerk Becalel Fernes has been engaged as bank manager.
—o—
From the Sosnowiec Craftsmen's Association
Craftsmen are asked to note that those who wish to benefit from the reductions at the examinations must be registered with the craftsmen's association.
Applications for the government loan for craftsmen will be written from next Sunday on.
—o—
The Supervision of „Zawiercie“ Is Being Lifted
The „nadzór sądowy“ [court supervision] over the well-known textile factory „Zawiercie“ will soon be lifted.
A settlement has been reached between the creditors and the factory, the creditors having granted the most far-reaching payment facilities.
—o—
20 Tammuz Commemorations in Zagłębie
On Wednesday evening a mourning academy took place at „Katerinia“ [?]. It was opened by the chairman Kornfeld, who in a few words described the great merits of our unforgettable, esteemed leader for Zionism in general and for the Jewish population of Sosnowiec in particular. After the memorial prayers for Dr. Herzl and Dr. Perlman the floor is given to Mr. Feldman [?], who delivers a speech rich in content; Mr. Glatnik [?] speaks about the state of the library, expresses thanks to the Perlman family for its support and proposes the organisation of Hebrew evening courses. The mourning academy closes with the singing of „Hatikvah“.
— In Będzin the memorial took place in the city synagogue. After the Mincha prayer the cantor of the beit midrash [?], Mr. Piotrkowski, sings „If I forget thee, O Jerusalem“ and „El Male Rachamim“. Messrs. Gelbard [?], Herszlewicz and Wygodzki [?] speak on current affairs.
— In Dąbrowa a rich Herzl academy will take place this Saturday night at „Chesnus“ [?], in which editor Joseph Heftman and the instructor of „Keren Hayesod“, Mr. Jakub Gruszalka [?], are also to take part.
—o—
The Jewish Children at the Summer Colony in Sławków Are Already, Thank Goodness, Drinking Kosher Milk
About 2 weeks ago the Będzin rabbinate received a „confidential“ report that the milk given to the Jewish children at the summer colony in Sławków was treif.
On the strength of this report the rabbinate sent, only last Thursday, a letter by post to Sławków in which the rabbinate announces that the milk is treif.
When the head of the colony, alderman (ławnik) Goldsztajn, received the news, he went at once to the said rabbinate and proved to it with facts that the report had been provoked for reasons of competition [?].
In addition, the supplier of the milk, Mr. Lefti [?] of Charsznica, enclosed several certificates of kashrut from the local rabbi, who writes that the milk supplied to the colony is kosher without any doubt or suspicion.
When the Będzin rabbinate became convinced that its prohibition had been issued „hastily“ [?], without any firm proof, it issued the following certificate:
[In Hebrew in the original:] „Whereas there was a rumour concerning the milk sent from Charsznica by Mr. Moshe Szrepniawski [?] on the account of Mr. Chaim Lefti [?] of Zambrawa [?] to Sławków, to the colony of Jewish children run by the Będzin community, that it is not kosher milk — we have therefore found it necessary to publish that after investigation and inquiry it has become clear to us that the milk is kosher milk without any doubt, and the children shall eat and be satisfied. Będzin, Thursday of the portion Pinchas, 21 Tammuz 5690.
The Rabbinical Court of Będzin and the region.“
In Yiddish translation: „Since there was a rumour that the milk sent from Charsznica for Jewish children at the summer colony in Sławków is treif, we find it necessary to make public that after investigation and inquiry it has become clear to us that the milk is kosher without any doubt.“
—o—
Supervisors of a Jewish Children's Colony Boycotting Jewish Merchants?
The Jewish charitable society in Sosnowiec has this year organised the summer colony for Jewish children at Buczawno [?] (near Olkusz). During the time the colony has existed we have received information that the Jewish supervisors of the colony are boycotting Jewish merchants.
As we are informed, the chairman of the institution, Dr. Hercman, promised that he would look into the matter, but the promise has not been kept and the Jewish merchants are again being shunned.
We await an explanation on this matter from the directors of the institution.
—o—
A Suitcase of Clothes Has Disappeared
On Wednesday evening Mr. Rozenblum dispatched from the Będzin station a suitcase of clothes to Kraków.
In the middle of the night Mr. R. received word that the suitcase had been stolen between Będzin and Dąbrowa.
This is already the second case of dispatched luggage disappearing.
—o—
Robbed and Tied to a Tree
On the road to Andruszewice [?] bandits attacked the merchant Szmul Lewkowicz and, threatening him with a revolver, the bandits robbed him of a sum of 5 gulden with a few groszy.
The attackers were not content with this and tied Lewkowicz's hands and feet to a tree in the forest.

Memorial Assembly for Dr. T. Herzl and Dr. A. Perlman in Sosnowiec

[Sosnowiec — Zionism; memorial assembly.] (Sh) In connection with the yahrzeit of Dr. T. Herzl and Dr. A. Perlman of blessed memory, which fall together, the Zionist Organization in Sosnowiec held a memorial "academy" in the "Angielski" hall.
On the platform were the portraits of Dr. Herzl, Dr. Perlman and Lord Balfour. All three portraits were draped in black crêpe.
Before a packed hall Mr. B. Rozman opened the assembly with a few warm words of remembrance; as the speaker mentioned the names of the leaders who died before their time, those assembled honoured [?] their memory by rising.
The choir under the direction of Mr. L. Mangel sang "Shiviti", and Mr. Mangel recited "El male rachamim".
Then city councillor Dr. Pelarista/Peladista [?] took the floor and spoke for nearly 2 hours; while speaking Dr. Peladista could not control himself and tears kept choking him.
"The day of 20 Tammuz — said Dr. Peladista — is for us like a symbol, because on the very day when the Jewish people lost one of its best sons — Dr. Herzl — we here in Sosnowiec lost one of our best and most faithful comrades, Dr. Abraham Perlman of blessed memory. On this 20th of Tammuz, when Zionism is living through such heavy blows, we must take account of what Herzl did for the Jewish people. Were Herzl alive today, his only answer to all the wrongs being done to the Jewish people would have been: keep working tirelessly, and our victory will be assured.
The idea of Dr. Herzl — Dr. Peladista went on — powerfully gripped Dr. Perlman; like a faithful soldier he carried out everything precisely, from the greatest to the smallest Zionist tasks. Year in, year out we will recall the heavy loss that struck us with the death of Dr. Perlman. Dr. P. was one of the first who rooted Jewish tradition in Sosnowiec in the finest sense of the word; he created the Jewish hospital and the Jewish girls' gymnasium, and there was not a single institution in which he did not take part.
Further speakers: on behalf of the girls' gymnasium, Mrs. Jungster; on behalf of "Dobroczynność" [charity society], Dr. Jungster; and finally a very fiery speech was given on behalf of the Zionist Organization in Sosnowiec by Mr. J. Sh. Feldman.
Closing the first part of the assembly, the chairman Mr. B. Rozman read out a sharp resolution against the English government, which to this day has not abolished the decree against aliyah. The resolution was adopted unanimously.
The second part of the assembly consisted of solo singing by Mr. Triger, and the choir sang very beautifully the Hebrew songs "Zion tamati" and "Yibane ha-mikdash".
With "Hatikvah" the memorial assembly was concluded.

A Letter to the Editor

Dear Mr. Editor!
Reading in your paper the note "A. G. — a scholar out of the gang", I have the honour to point out that this is not correct, for had I been a scholar I would at once have grasped it and thrown up my hands; but I am not to blame for it, for when someone takes on an apprentice, the boy must at first run errands, play with the child, etc., so that the boy should not meddle[?] in the craft. We had the same errands in the "Gemilut Chesed [free-loan] Fund": the gentlemen chairmen did everything on their own responsibility, and no member of the board had any say; and later, when I raised an outcry, I received a few curses as my reward, and there they went on doing whatever they wanted.
The note further says that a motion was tabled to expel me from the board as "harmful". It is true — certainly I am "harmful", for I cannot stand by and watch what is being done in the free-loan fund; unfortunately I am one of those who cry out and are not answered, and perhaps I am suspected of being after the chair itself. Where is your weight[?] in the press? Why do you allow the pennies of the poor to be so ownerless? It is a crying injustice that such an institution should, God forbid, go under, for things have already reached the point where expenses equal income; quite enough money has already been lost, and if I am asked, I shall present all the details of everything that has been done until today on their own authority without asking anyone; it is like a private little shop of "watch mine [and I'll watch yours]", etc. I am also very surprised that the gentlemen auditors N. Herzinger and S. Szpigelman have not reported to this day on the state of the institution.
Elazar Frachtzweig.
Editorial remark: Mr. Frachtzweig's complaints against our editorial office are unfounded. For quite some time we have not said our word about the "Gemilut Chesed" institution, because when we voiced our opinions for the good of this very important institution, its managers — who possess scant sense for public work — out of revenge tossed a bagel or a lunch to the hooligans[?], to the youths of the "mikveh sheet", who fell upon us like wild creatures while singing songs and praises to those at the head of the free-loan fund; so we kept away from them and gave up on the whole thing.
