From Sports Life

"Hakoach" — "C.K.S." 0:1 (0:0)
The match between the above-mentioned teams aroused great interest among sportsmen in Zagłębie. Before we analyse the technical outcome of the match, we must dwell on the conduct of the Będzin public. It is unheard of that outside onlookers should behave in such a manner on the "boisko" [pitch]. The spectator must not interfere in any matters whatsoever that occur during play. The Czeladź public, being dissatisfied with the referee's decisions, went onto the pitch and did not allow the match to be finished. The intervention of the police did not help either.
The match itself was played at a tremendous pace; the ball went lightning-fast from player to player; the guests play with the wind and have a slight advantage; the "Hakoach" defence is in its place and foils every effort of the "C.K.S." Several chances of "Hakoach" also go unused. After the change of ends "Hakoach" plays more cohesively; a series of attacks end on the guests' good defence. The game becomes more interesting, and after a series of fine combinations Gutman shoots the first and also the last goal. 25th minute, the game becomes more interesting, the Będzin side still have chances to shoot, but without success. 10 minutes before the end the public bursts onto the field and the referee is forced to break off the match. Of the players the following excelled: Bechman, Jankielewicz 1 and 2, Szywek[?] 1 and 2, and Sztajner. Of the guests: the defence and the centre-forward Przybyłek. Referee Mr. Wiger — very good.
"Zagłębie" — "Maccabi" 3:6 (2:3)
And again "Maccabi" has lost a championship match. The Sosnowiec side always start well and fight, but do not hold the result to the end. The management must now use every means to remove the danger of dropping out of the first class; the players too must give their all, in order to save the honour of Jewish sport.
Already in the first 7 minutes "Maccabi" scores two goals through Klinger 2. The "Zagłębie" players get to work and by the break score three goals. After half-time the guests add three more goals with the help of the "Maccabi" goalkeeper. The Sosnowiec side score one more goal through Piekarski, and the result is settled. The best of "Maccabi": Klinger 2, Jakubowicz and Seliger; of the Dąbrowa side: Szpruch and Benaszyk. Referee Kozibucki — good.

"Sarmacja", thanks to the very poor play of its goalkeeper Jelenkiewicz, lost two important points. Despite the superiority of the Będzin side, the excellent "Victoria" won, thereby improving its position in the championship. The goals were scored by Margula 2 and Regula 1 for the guests, Żmijewski[?] and Petranek for Będzin. Referee Mr. Wiger — good.
"Sosnowiec" — "Świt" 1:7 (1:)
"Sosnowiec" does what it likes with its opponent and achieves a high victory. Goals were scored by Kubala 4, Durek 2 and Andruszewicz 1. For "Świt" the centre-forward.

Representatives Without Rights

Representatives Without Rights. (Our people's delegates as representatives on the kehilla council. — Does the Ministry take them into account?)
It is interesting and characteristic: we, the Jewish citizens of Sosnowiec, have in all neither more nor less than 30 — I say, thirty — kehilla representatives. One would think that, no evil eye, such a number of members could at last manage our little bit of communal money; at least so we believe. Meanwhile it all comes to nothing [a "boydem"]: it does not matter what we believe and what we think. It means, then, that we may hold whatever opinion of ourselves we like, while in reality the situation looks quite different.
Take our kehilla council — a rather fine representation, one would think; after all, every movement managed to send its best people there, and yet we are not trusted. We in our homely little community trust [?] one another, and only the authorities cannot rely on us and cannot entrust to us what they themselves placed within our competence.
We were given the right to run our communal affairs, and yet we cannot be relied upon. The conditions under which the kehilla councils in Poland were created have been brought to such a pass that they cannot properly manage our public life, so that apart from drawing up budgets almost nothing gets done — but even over this very budget our representatives have no say.
Interesting: the Sosnowiec kehilla representatives drew up a budget. Well, they sweated and toiled over it, bargained back and forth — what these wanted to add, those wanted to remove — and so they debated and debated without end, until somehow they came to terms among themselves, and the budget, with luck and blessing, was sent off to the authorities for approval. But it is only called "for approval"; in reality it means making a second budget.
The subsidies that the kehilla council had recognised were struck out or reduced without consultation with, or the consent of, those who had sweated and toiled over the budget for weeks on end. It goes without saying that this is more than vexing; it is a slap in the face — in other words, it means that they are to be merely executive elements doing what they are told, and on their own they are powerless to do anything.
We would still understand it if subsidies were struck out that the Ministry cannot agree with; but one cannot say it is acceptable when subsidies for charitable or cultural institutions are struck out or reduced.
What, for example, can one have against a subsidy given to an interest-free loan fund meant to grant Jews loans? You understand: thanks to the terrible crisis and the tax screw, Jews have become impoverished, so that they now need gemilut chesed funds — so why should we be prevented from subsidising such an institution out of our own money? This is incomprehensible, simply monstrous; at the same time the Ministry orders the subsidy for the cemetery to be increased.
Since the Ministry is better versed in our affairs than our representatives themselves, why then do we need these comedies with meetings and frictions and getting heated over what the world "stands on [quotation not closed in the original], only for everything to come to nothing afterwards? Why do we need all this running around, when everything ends in disappointments and surprises that offend the feelings of our people's delegates? Why then, in that case, do we need our own representatives at all, when the government has no trust in them? Why, then, do we need the kehilla administrations with their councils? If so, better [?] not to have the whole theatre at all.
But we say: if it is more convenient for the government that the representative bodies should exist after all, then they can, at the given moment, together, jointly, draw up the budgets right on the spot, as is done, for example, in the tax-assessment commissions.
When the Ministry makes certain changes in the budget and gives its reasons at the same time, that is quite understandable; but to tear everything down and alter it, so that the whole thing becomes a kind of caricature — that is simply ridiculous, and we can then also understand the indignation of our kehilla representatives, who after all were not elected so that their public activity should be made light of [?], an activity for which they are nevertheless answerable to their voters, to whom they must also render an account.
True, we are not satisfied with them today; we have not got from them what we hoped to get. We thought that the Jewish kehilla councils would be our self-governing bodies, which would beautify and modernise [?] inner Jewish life; but those are our own affairs — our pains [?], our sorrows and joys — which should be reflected within our own four cubits and have nothing to do with the outside public.
The Ministry ought to know that when the plans of our representatives — in whom all strata of the Jewish population are represented — are brought to nothing, this at the same time means slighting their voters, that is, the entire Jewish population.
And in that case it is one of two things: either one must have trust in our people's delegates, since they come in the name of the people; or, if not — if there is no trust in them at all — they should not be permitted to manage our institutions and interests at all, and then it will be known that neither we nor our representatives are entitled [?] to the right to manage our public institutions and funds.
With all this, one thing must not be forgotten at the same time: that we live in a free, independent Poland, and that the right to manage the Jewish kehillot was given to us on the basis of democratic rights; and therefore we indeed have the right to feel offended when we see our rights trampled underfoot.
The Sosnowiec kehilla council must therefore, as such, as a united body, react properly at the moment when its rights are curtailed and when no account is taken of the representatives, who embody the entire Jewish citizenry of Sosnowiec.
Such conduct, such slighting, is an insult to Jewish Sosnowiec.
Dr. Papuri.
Merchants Must Help Themselves

[Zagłębie — economy and trade; opinion.] Our merchant is dying; he grows weaker with every day, and we sit with folded hands and do not show the slightest attempt to help ourselves.
Can we help ourselves? It may be that yes; if not a great deal, then at least a little — trying, in any case, does no harm!
I am not speaking here of our industry and wholesale trade, whose sales markets lie outside the bounds of our town and country.
Their trouble is a world trouble, a national plague, bound up with politics, and it is not in our power to supply the cure for it.
I am speaking of the small trade — of the hundreds of individual shopkeepers who stand with folded hands at the doors of their smartened-up shops and yawn.
Their market is the town, and the town is dead!
Yet we have already seen how one breathes a spirit of life into such "corpses" and they begin to show signs of life!
Let it be a tormented life, let it be an artificial holding-off of the death-throes — but anything is better than complete death, from which one can no longer hope to come alive... Będzin and Sosnowiec are not the only towns in Europe; there are many such towns which the angel of death holds in his pincers, especially in the off-season[?] — and nonetheless the merchants of these towns know what to do: they do not throw up their hands, but shake themselves up and shake up their market.
They look for various ways to reach the fainted consumer and to suggest things to him, to draw out of him his trembling groszy and set them circulating again; they make use of all kinds of advertisements and clearance sales.
The European merchant prepares for the after-season no less than for the season itself, because he knows that the interest on every piece of merchandise that remains with him on the shelf will eat him up and bring his end nearer...
So he beats the drum and turns worlds upside down: he holds an end-of-season clearance sale and slashes prices like mad, so that even the poorest consumer gets the urge to treat himself[?] and splurge[?], just to buy something.
Besides clearance sales, modern merchants have still other means of livening up turnover in bad times.
One need only know how to get something done, and not stand with folded hands on the threshold of the shop.
Izydor.
Girls, Guard Your Fiancés, So Your Girlfriends Don't Cast an "Eye" on Them...

[Zawiercie — local gossip; matchmaking.] Zawiercie is abuzz with the story of how a local girl lost her fiancé because of an introduction.
Miss M. had become engaged, in a good hour.
She got her fiancé from no less than Katowice (actually he — the fiancé, that is — is from Mandoszew[?]), a decent young man, and the bride was happy with him.
As usual, she invited him to visit her in Zawiercie. In honour of the guest she invited her girlfriends and introduced her fiancé to each of them:
— Mój narzeczony ("my fiancé") —
The fiancé bowed politely, good-naturedly held out his hand, and "eyes" met...
Among the girlfriends there was a young lady who possessed a "magnetic" power, and she cast the "evil eye" on the fiancé..
The "evil eye", however, was so strong that the fiancé fell for it and
— got a "heart" for the girlfriend..
The first bride began to make a racket, to shout: how can it be? Such a thing? To shame a Jewish daughter? Is this how a modern young man behaves? But it did not help at all: the fiancé turned "cold" and signed the tna'im (engagement contract) with the bride's girlfriend...
In revenge the former bride served him with a "psak" (a judgment/lawsuit) in Sosnowiec, but the fiancé took the psak, and also
— the second bride...
Our Panorama

[Panorama — local satire; Sosnowiec, Strzemieszyce, Dąbrowa.] (Bein ha-Metzarim. — To spite the gabbai he does not say Kaddish. — What sin did the congregation commit? — With complaints they drove out the rebbe. — The shoemaking trade is being revived. — Ingenious[?] people.)
Bein ha-Metzarim.
The reports we have received in the course of this week are very well suited to the days of Bein ha-Metzarim (the Three Weeks). The national destruction and its causes from 2 thousand years ago become almost fresh when one takes a look at how far our understanding reaches and over what causeless hatred is sown among us.
There is in Sosnowiec a Chevra Tehillim (psalm-reciting society). Ordinary everyday Jews, far from the political racket[?], they are followers of King David and say Psalms evening and morning.
Satan could not rest and set to work, so that into this society too the bacilli should creep that disturb peace and unity among simple honest Jews.
And Satan prevailed. On Sabbath morning a member of the society, a mourner, went up to the reader's stand and said the blessings.
This did not please the gabbai, and he prevented the mourner from praying "at the front" (leading the service).
Then the prayer leader took revenge, and to spite the gabbai he refused to say Kaddish.. "Eleheï[?]" — he said — "let my late mother find out who is to blame, who does not let me say Kaddish"...
When the gabbai heard this, a "fear" fell upon him and he laid down his mandate.
— "No longer gabbai, from now on a plain soldier."
So they come, the worshippers of the Chevra Tehillim, with their complaints: 1) what is the mother guilty of, if the gabbai is strict? and 2) "shall one man sin, and wilt Thou be wroth with all the congregation?" — if one worshipper "sins", does the gabbai[?] get angry with everyone?
— All sorts of just complaints, but the only answer we have for the Chevra Tehillim is:
— It is Bein ha-Metzarim; in these days the Temple was destroyed and the people of Israel was driven into exile..
———
The "Gordonists" in Strzemieszyce are no longer "children of exile": they do not sulk, they do not take revenge, but with the song "Am Yisrael Chai" they "sweep" even their opponent into the dance...
A rebbe came to Strzemieszyce, one of those rebbes who, poor things, must seek their bounty in foreign parts, serve out an exile and wander from town to town.
So the rebbe went to his hasid, a Jew who has his own house, and there the rebbe wanted to put up.
The hasid said to the rebbe thus: Rebbe! This time I am not able to give up an apartment for the rebbe, but if the rebbe wishes and if it suits you, I give permission to use[?] the premises of "Gordonia" in my house, and there the rebbe will be able to hold his "tish" gatherings.
And so it was: the rebbe's attendant said "Vihi No'am" 7 times, and the door of the "Gordonia" premises opened, and
— the rebbe went in..
And it came to pass, when the Gordonists learned of the occupation, that they first held a "zbiórka" (assembly) and then went into their premises and
— struck up a little dance..
The rebbe of course protested and resisted, but "Gordonia" sang and danced until
— the Sitra Achra prevailed, and the rebbe, poor man, had to leave the "[—]"[?] — the premises, that is — and "Gordonia" again has premises in which to dance horas...
———
The report on the activity of the gabbaim in the Dąbrowa Ger shtibl really ought to have been published fresh in honour of Shabbat Nachamu, because the "ingenious" plan of the said gabbaim will, with the Almighty's help, make it possible for Jewish artisans to have employment, for merchants to have turnover, and above all:
— Jewishness will be strengthened..
— You are "ciekawe" (curious)? Then listen:
The gabbaim of the Dąbrowa Ger shtibl, after the opening of the Lublin yeshiva, in order "to enlarge the business", issued the following ordinance:
Everyone who prays in the Ger shtibl must go about in boots; the boots may not be made according to the form used until now, but must be made in the very same form in which our ancient grandfathers went; the bootleg (cholewa) must be sewn at the top with white stitching[?] ("pszegrue"[?]), so that everyone can see the "strzepe"[?] of the bootlegs...
The ordinance has already come into force, and among the Dąbrowa shoemakers a "revival" reigns...
There is a conjecture that our Finance Minister intends to invite the gabbaim of the Dąbrowa Ger shtibl to consult with them on how to improve the economic situation in the country, since the foreign advisers have not managed to accomplish anything real...
Ben Amoc.
Did Not Live to See It...

[Sosnowiec — In memory of Dr. Perlman.] (On Dr. Perlman's second yahrzeit.)
Once again we stand deeply bowed at the grave of the prematurely departed comrade, friend and unforgettable Dr. Perlman, and once again thoughts and memories crowd in of the radiant figure who lit up Jewish life in Sosnowiec and in Zagłębie as well. We see him as if alive — the builder of national Jewish life among us, the awakener to work for the common good. Twenty-five years ago, when Dr. P. took his place in the front ranks of public activity, it was an impressive deed; it required a great dose of devotion, idealism and strength to break through the obstacles both within Jewish society itself and in the surrounding outside world, where there reigned so little understanding, least of all for the groundbreaking ideas of the problem of Jewish national revival.
Dr. P. went forward with tenacity in his quiet work, step by step, and swept along everyone who had even a spark of understanding, a spark of longing for a better future of the Jewish people. And now we see among us a strongly pulsating Jewish national public life and a long row of public institutions; the hardship of Jewish life in exile is reflected in them, but there is also a sensitive barometer of all our spiritual, economic and national problems. Here people stand on guard according to the testament of Dr. P., who created all this.
On the second yahrzeit of our friend we come to his grave, and, giving an account of the work accomplished, we can say that the edifice whose foundations he laid is growing from day to day, that the work has borne fine fruit. The tragedy of leaders and fighters lies in this: that unfortunately they do not live to see with their own eyes the results of their toil and devotion. Such was also the fate of Dr. Perlman — he did not live to see it.. he did not have the good fortune and the feeling of satisfaction for the time and strength he sacrificed. How he would have rejoiced, for example, how his deep gaze would have shone, had he seen the latest matura celebration of the Jewish gymnasium in Sosnowiec, of which he was one of the first founders; how happy he would have been hearing representatives of the authorities praise the school and stress that Jewish tradition is cultivated here; how deeply gratified he would have been had he heard a Jewish girl finishing the gymnasium deliver an exemplary Hebrew speech and give thanks for the Jewish education she had received there.
— He did not live to see it!..
And many other phenomena and moments in public life would have given him joy and contentment.
On the day of his second yahrzeit we bring him our living greetings, and his spirit receives them, and we all feel that his radiant soul feels the satisfaction for the sacrifices made. We all also fulfil the wish and the strong call that comes from Dr. P.'s grave — the call to further work, to still greater deeds, until the final revival of the people and the land.
The second yahrzeit of our great friend falls this year, however, in a sad time of severe trials for our highest ideal. The aliyah decree of the English authorities is [printed: "and"] the sorest point on the great front of our struggle for revival. And perhaps this is the right moment that precisely today, precisely at the grave of our leader, the great will to hold out in the struggle for our elementary rights should be strengthened. Our bitter protests, which are heard throughout the whole world, must today be confirmed by our strong will and readiness for sacrifice. That must be our answer, and one can be sure that if our dear comrade Dr. P. could come to us today, at this critical moment, to encourage us and give us the answer to the bitter question of what we must do now, he would certainly call out to us with the full force of his personality: Brothers! Do not despair! We must go forward, we must keep working, fighting and winning!
Dear comrade! Rest in peace! We feel your spirit, we hear your voice, and we will continue your deeds.
Dr. T. Meladista [?].
A Little Feuilleton — How Does One Get Rid of Summer?

[Feuilleton — international politics.] How does one get rid of summer?
This wish sounds a little mad — summer is, after all, the most beautiful season of the year, when everything grows and everything rises, the true symbol of life and flourishing; and nevertheless more than one of us wishes to be rid of it as quickly as possible.
And we wish this not because we long so much for our wives, who have settled down at the dachas — after all, we are not such ardent supporters of private property — what [? word unclear] has said do we have, and what do we own?
No, our wish to be rid of summer is because of something else: because of the black cat that has lately run between the nations and countries.
Somehow there is too much talk lately about "peace". Hardly a day goes by without your reading in the newspapers that a "new way" has been found to secure world peace!
And with us it is already a rule: when neighbour women begin kissing on the lips, it is a sign that they will soon fall out [?]; and when a dangerously [?] sick person suddenly feels better and begins to talk, it is a sign that he is close to his last agony..
Take, for example, the latest news of this week:
Lord Dusharush [?] made a great speech about peace and whispered the secret that, despite all the peace treaties, strong war preparations are now being made everywhere, far exceeding the preparations before the war, and that the fate of mankind now depends on an understanding between America and England. And who can bring about [?] this understanding? Says that very "Lord" [printed: "Layd"] Dusharush himself — the intervention of the cloister is needed..
You understand? This far-sighted politician is a great heretic; Lord Dusharush gives us the true popular [?] hint and shows us where a "good Jew" [a Hasidic rebbe] lives — one has to turn to Heaven for help..
And here is another item:
The semi-official organ of the French Foreign Ministry, "Tatn" [? probably Le Temps], comes out with a demand that, in order to secure peace in Europe, Germany should be given Pomerania and the Danzig Corridor and be allowed to create a strong army.
Well, about the swinishness of our "faithful" sister France, who wants to be a philanthropist out of our pocket, we had better not speak now — that is a chapter in itself.
But what will you say about France's niceness towards Germany? For ten years she held its Rhineland and only trembled before "lest they multiply" [Exodus 1:10], and suddenly that very same Germany is too small and too weak for her — so she wants to secure peace with England and Italy.
And what about the little news items on the unrest in Egypt, on the Persian arms orders and on the speeches of the Soviet leaders, who say they are far from waging wars, only they boast that the Russian army is the strongest in the world..
In short: with this peace we would be anything but [? "foyglreyn" — reading and sense uncertain]!
We found ourselves in just such a situation sixteen years ago — before the World War.
Our only salvation here can be — to get rid of summer as fast as possible;
in the autumn mud and in the winter frosts no one will have any desire to take up the sword — even in the last [?] World War there used to be peace at these times of year.
And therefore our best wish now is — how does one get rid of summer?
Y. G. Shteynsapir.

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on today's portion (Pinchas)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings and remarks on today's portion.
Collected and adapted by Y. L.
Parashat Pinchas
—o—
a) Pinchas.
The famous Gaon Rabbi Pinchas Horowitz, author of the „Hafla'ah“, led a simple, almost poor life in his own home. On the other hand, whenever he travelled somewhere, magnificent receptions were arranged for him everywhere with lavish banquets fit for a king. He was, after all, a world-renowned Gaon. Once, during such a reception banquet, he said to a fellow townsman:
— Look, when Pinchas (meaning parashat Pinchas, using the pun on himself) is at home, he is no aristocrat at all: it is read during the Three Weeks (parashat Pinchas always falls between the 16th [sic; = 17th] of Tammuz and the 9th of Av) and nobody makes a fuss of it; but when Pinchas comes abroad (when parashat Pinchas is read at another time, i.e. on the festivals, when all the festival maftir readings are taken from parashat Pinchas), banquets are arranged in its honour, people eat and drink — a whole celebration. See the difference between Pinchas at home and Pinchas abroad...
Heard.
• • •
The everyday, homely „Aleinu“ is spat out, recited [?] standing on one foot, when one is already standing on the threshold of the synagogue. People treat it dismissively. But one meets that same „Aleinu“ abroad, e.g. on Yom Kippur during the „Avodah“ [?] — one bows down to the ground, falls before it in respectful prostration. (Folk saying)
—o—
b) „He has turned away My wrath from the children of Israel“ (Num. 25:11).
An important, respected merchant had to go bankrupt; creditors came and made scenes. A few good friends of the merchant gathered and begged the creditors to wait a while. But that did not help the merchant at all, for after a while — again the same scenes and rows. Then a good [?] friend came, settled with the creditors at a certain percentage and took back the bills of exchange from them. He rescued the merchant once and for all, whereas the first ones merely prolonged his misery.
That is the difference between Moses and Pinchas. When the Jews sinned with the Golden Calf, Moses asked that the sin be deferred; God did so — indeed „the Lord repented of the evil“, but „in the day when I visit, I will visit“ [printed „ביום פקדי פקדתי“] — merely a deferral of the kind that [?] at some occasion there would be a reckoning. But Pinchas, with his bold deed, with his Zimri operation, wiped out the Jews' sin once and for all. „He has turned away My wrath from the children of Israel“ — settled and wiped out.
The Dubno Maggid.
—o—
c) „Harass the Midianites“ (Num. 25:17).
The Egyptians and the Edomites wanted to annihilate the Jews with fire and sword. Nevertheless it was said of them: „You shall not abhor an Egyptian“, „You shall not abhor an Edomite“. Moab and Midian, however, wanted to destroy the Jews spiritually [?], sending their daughters to seduce the Jewish leaders, wishing to infect the Jews with their idolatry [?] — and upon them the Jewish wrath of vengeance was poured out: „Harass the Midianites“, „An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord“, for spiritual seduction is worse than death by the sword.
Midrash Tanchuma.
—o—
d) „Then came the daughters of Zelophehad“ (Num. 27:1).
The section on inheritance, the legislation on inheritance, was given through women, through the daughters of Zelophehad, because inheritance comes, after all, after a dead person, and it was women who brought death into the world...
Rabbeinu Bachya.
—o—
e) „And Moses brought their cause before the Lord“ (Num. 27:5).
Zelophehad's daughters wanted to flatter Moses and told him: „Our father was not among the company of them that gathered themselves together against the Lord in the company of Korah“, and thought to win him over with the fact that Zelophehad had not belonged to Korah's campaign. But Moses our Teacher regarded this as a bribe of words and no longer considered himself entitled to decide the case, and „brought their cause before the Lord“.
Asifat Genuzim.
—o—
f) „Let the Lord... set a man over the congregation“ (Num. 27:16).
Moses reckoned that God would make Pinchas leader, because he had so heroically carried out God's vengeance. But Moses knew that Pinchas was unsuited to be a leader, because he was a zealot [?]; so he prayed: „Let the Lord set a man over the congregation“ — he asked that someone else be the leader.
R. Mendel of Kotzk.
—o—
g) „As sheep which have no shepherd“ (Num. 27:17).
In a flock of sheep a he-goat goes in front. He is the leader, but he [printed „he he“] is after all also a beast like the whole flock... One needs a shepherd who knows how to lead the flock.
Malbim.
—o—
h) „You shall have a solemn assembly“ (Num. 29:35).
The Midrash says about this: „Your parting is hard for me“ — it is hard for me to part from you. What does parting mean with God? Surely the whole earth is full of His glory.
The meaning is: „Your parting is hard for me“ — it is hard for me that you are divided among yourselves, torn apart and split up.
Rabbi Mendel of Warka.
Avot, Chapter One

[Oneg Shabbat — Pirkei Avot.]
a) „Let the poor be members of your household“ (Mishnah 5)
The Mishnah tells the wealthy man who opens a „house wide open“ where charity is distributed to the poor, that only poor people should manage the distribution — „let the poor be members of your household“; for if you appoint well-fed administrators, who do not know the taste of hunger and want, they will dole out nothing but troubles to the poor folk.
Yadayim Moshe [?].
—o—
b) „Do not talk much with the woman“ (ibid.)
There are wives who, when the husband brings home a guest for Shabbat, give the guest specially of the finest and best, so that the husband will regret bringing a guest home a second time. So the Mishnah says „al tarbeh“ — „talk with the woman“: you should say to the wife: „al tarbeh“ — don't give too much, [?] your kindness.
Idle Talk.
—o—
c) „Loving people and bringing them near to the Torah“ (12)
Not like those who say: with sinners, with heretics one must not associate. No — „loving people“, all of them, even the freethinkers, and in this way „bringing them near to the Torah“: you will make them pious through your influence — but only with love.
Alshich.
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin — There Was No Minyan...

What's new in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 22 Tammuz 5690 — Piątek 18 lipca 1930 [Friday, 18 July 1930].)
Będzin
There was no minyan...
On Monday a session of the city council took place. Before the agenda was taken up, several non-Jewish councillors put questions to the president [mayor]: why are the streets in the suburbs of Ksawera, Gzichów etc. not sprinkled with water? (On the part of the Jewish councillors no interpellation was made that the Old Market and Shul Street, too, should be sprinkled at least once a week.)
The first item was the motion of councillor Figer that the magistrate should regulate the "Przemsza" [river]. After the president's explanation that such a "regulation" would cost no less than 120 million złoty, the item was taken off the agenda.
Then they proceeded to elect 2 representatives to the supervisory board of the power station (elektrownia), but already while the votes were being counted councillor Rechnic[?] pointed out that there was no quorum in the hall. When they began counting and saw that "the reckoning is right", the president honestly[?] closed the session.
A Big Fire on Czeladzka Street — President Michel's Rope Warehouse Burned Down

A big fire on Czeladzka Street.
President Michel's rope warehouse burned down.
On Monday at 12 at night the residents were alarmed by the fire that broke out in the rope warehouse of president Michel on Czeladzka Street. Because for half an hour there was no water, the fire spread quickly and engulfed Feigenblatt's upholstery workshop, which was next door. Despite the rescue efforts of the fire brigades from Będzin, Koszelew, Saturn and Dąbrowa, the wooden buildings went up in flames.
Feigenblatt suffered heavy losses and was left without goods and without a place to work.
2 persons, unemployed, were arrested on suspicion of arson.
In the Cucumber Season We'll at Least Hear Some Singing... — Kehilla Board Decides on a Competition

In the cucumber season we'll at least hear some singing...
The kehilla board decides on a competition.
On Monday the kehilla board held a session on the cantorate question, which has suddenly become topical in our town.
It was decided to publish a competition for a cantor.
This Sabbath a Galician "cantor" is already leading the prayers "on trial".
Now That's What You Call a Devoted 'Al HaMishmar' Man

Now that's what you call a devoted "Al HaMishmar" man.
This week a world conference of the "Al HaMishmar" group was held in Lemberg [Lwów]. During the discussions the local delegate Meir Cymberknopf got so agitated that he fainted, and a doctor had to be called, who gave him medical aid.
On Wednesday the Cymberknopf family received a telephone message from Lwów that their son is in a hospital.
She Went to Sleep at Her 'Auntie's', So She Was Removed from the Summer Colony

She went to sleep at her "auntie's" (ciocia), so she was removed from the summer colony.
On Monday at 10 in the evening Lowik[?] Goldsztajn received a telephone message from Sławków that the girl Sorele Gutfrajnd had disappeared and could not be found anywhere.
When Mr. G. enquired about the child with the parents, they became very frightened, and at dawn the father, Chaim Dawid Gutfrajnd, set off for Sławków to find out where his Sorele was.
After a thorough search the "lost" child was found at an "auntie's", who had taken the child away from the colony without anyone's knowledge.
Because of this the colony committee decided that children who go away to spend the night, or go for a walk, without the knowledge of the colony's leaders will be sent home from the colony.
The decision has already been carried out with regard to Gutfrajnd's child.
The Cashier Dispatching Luggage 'Makes Mistakes'

The cashier dispatching luggage "makes mistakes".
Mr. Płusznik[?] informs us of several facts concerning the cashier at the luggage office of the local station, who often "makes a mistake" when giving change. The merchants [one word unclear] should react to such "mistakes".
From the 'Muza'

From the "Muza".
On Saturday the 12th of this month, under the chairmanship of Mr. Manszajn[?], the annual general meeting of the members of the "Muza" took place. After hearing the reports it was decided to reorganise the society. Elected to the auditing committee were Y. Tuchman[?] (chairman), Dawid Klajger (treasurer) and Buszecki[?] (secretary). Among other things it was also decided that members to be admitted must first be examined.
A Thunderbolt's 'Tricks'

A thunderbolt's "tricks".
On Wednesday at midday, during a storm downpour, a thunderbolt struck Feldbaum's flat at Małachowskiego 4; then the thunderbolt went in to Zalewski in the same house, where it burned a curtain and damaged a window.
The thunderbolt also tore down the electric wires.
A Herzl Academy.

[Będzin — Zionism.]
On Tuesday a Herzl Academy took place in the Zionist premises, chaired by Mr. N. Langer.
The presidium was made up of representatives of almost all the Zionist groupings (except the Poalei Zion and the "Hitachdut").
Successful speeches were delivered by Messrs. N. Langer, Moshe Openheim and Zyga Grundman.
Right Poalei Zion expelled from the Keren Kayemet committee.

[Będzin — Zionism; Keren Kayemet.]
On Monday a consultation of the Zionist groupings took place in the Zionist premises, in order to organise the 20 Tammuz [anniversary of Herzl's death] campaign in our town.
The representative of the Right "Poalei Zion" declared that his group, on principle, takes no part whatsoever in the event called "20 Tammuz", and that he had come to disrupt the campaign.
After this declaration a motion by Mr. N. Langer to expel the Poalei Zion from the "Keren Kayemet" committee was adopted.
From the Revisionist organisation

[Będzin — Zionism; Revisionists.]
On Saturday the Revisionist-Zionist Union organised a public lecture, given by Mr. Tanelewicz [?], which drew an enormously large audience, almost exclusively young people.
The lecture, given in Yiddish, on the subject "The liberation of the nations and their influence on the Jewish revival", provoked a passionate discussion that stood at a very high cultural level. One must admire the restraint of the Revisionists — possibly thanks to the chairman — who, even in the face of Mr. M. Freners' [?] rather tactless interventions, waited until everyone had been given the opportunity to develop their views.
In prominent, thoroughly formulated responses by a series of speakers, the positive Revisionist programme in all fields found its expression.

Sosnowiec — Shochtim summon the kehilla board before the labour inspector.

[Sosnowiec — kehilla; ritual slaughter.]

[Sosnowiec — memorial; Keren Kayemet.]
On Wednesday morning a solemn memorial service took place at the Sosnowiec cemetery with the participation of a large number of admirers and of Rabbi Hager, who delivered a warm speech devoted to the loss of the late Dr. Perlman.
During the "El Malei Rachamim" prayers, recited by the cantor Mr. Lejchter, a number of people donated about 50 trees for the "Perlman Garden" in Eretz Israel.
That's What You Call a "Loyal" Son-in-Law...

Robs his father-in-law and then throws him into the water.

On Monday during the day, Józef Janeta, a resident of Szopienice, was walking home from Sosnowiec. On the way he was met by several persons, among whom was also Janeta's son-in-law, and these people opened fire. A bullet hit him and Janeta fell into a pool of blood; then the bandits robbed him of 180 zł. and afterwards threw him into the Brynica.

In the water Janeta regained consciousness and with great effort swam to the bank, where a policeman pulled him out and took him to hospital.

Janeta's condition is hopeless.
2 Weeks' Arrest for Committing an Immoral Act.

Mr. P. stood before the local court, having been brought to criminal responsibility for committing an immoral act in public. Mr. P. was sentenced to 2 weeks' arrest.
—o—
Leader of the Left PPS Arrested

On the order of the prosecutor's office, the leader of the Left PPS, Chrański [?], has been arrested; he is accused of organizing the attack on the police on Sunday, the 6th of this month, in Sosnowiec.
—o—
From the Revisionist Movement.

From the 22nd to the 29th of this month a world congress of all Trumpeldorians takes place in Warsaw. The Revisionist leader Ze'ev Jabotinsky is also to come to the congress. It is reckoned that some 8 thousand Betarim from the whole world will gather in Warsaw.

In connection with the above-mentioned congress, the Sosnowiec Trumpeldorians are preparing very intensively. Almost every evening gymnastic exercises take place in the Betar clubroom under the direction of the commander of the branch (mefaked ha-ken), Mr. Menachem Glidman.
—o—
One Killed and Another Injured.

At the "Saturn" coal mine a terrible accident occurred on Monday at noon. In the pit a lump of coal broke loose and buried 2 workers.

One was killed on the spot and the other was taken to hospital in a serious condition.
—o—
Echoes of the Embezzlement at the "Huta Katarzyna."

The following trial took place this week at the local district court.

In the dock sat the storekeeper of the metal department, Wiczarek, the officials Mazur and Czarniecki, and the supplier Mr. Jungster [?], who were accused of committing embezzlements at the "Huta Katarzyna."

During the trial Wiczarek confessed his guilt, but he declared that Mr. Jungster had "organized" [?] him to do it.

The court sentenced Wiczarek to 3 months in prison, and the others were acquitted.
—o—
The Bakers against the Price Commission.

On Sunday a congress of the bakers of Zagłębie and Upper Silesia took place here.

At the congress the following questions were discussed: 1) that the price commissions at the municipal councils set incorrect prices for baked goods, and 2) that the bakers pay more than 1 percent turnover tax.

Regarding these questions it was decided to apply to the chambers of crafts and of commerce.
Correction.

[Zagłębie — crime.] A dynamite bomb thrown into a barn.
A whole family seriously injured.
In the village of Rogoźnik an unknown person threw a dynamite bomb into a barn (stodoła) in which the Gubis family was sleeping.
The bomb exploded, and Mr. Gubis, his wife and daughter were injured.
The injured were taken in a serious condition to the hospital in Szarlej.

[Local — street story.] The maid spent Sunday night in town.
A certain family, in the area of Polga [?] Street, went away to a summer house (dacha), and only a son remained at home.
On Sundays the Christian maid would also sometimes drop in at the house; she used to come in from the dacha to town in honour of Sunday.
Last Sunday too she came, and since it was already late she did not go back to the dacha but stayed overnight with her employers in the flat.
Their son was so delighted with the „guest“ that he immediately let his three pals know, and they came to spend the night with him, and all four wanted to celebrate the festival of „Zman Simchatenu“ [„the season of our rejoicing“].
But the maid made a scandal, smashed all the mirrors in the house and various dishes, and knocked out several window panes.
The scandal drew quite a crowd; the three pals promptly vanished, and the „gem“ fled out of shame [?] into a room, where he lay low the whole night, while the maid meanwhile tidied up — she gathered up the broken glass.

What Is Happening with the Loans for Artisans?

[Będzin — artisans; loans.]
Yesterday, Thursday, in the meeting hall of the Będzin starosty (county office), under the chairmanship of the starosta Mr. Baksa[?], a conference took place of Christian and Jewish artisans' representatives concerning the manner of distributing the loans in the amount of 300 thousand zł. which had been allotted to small industry (artisans) in the Będzin powiat (county).
After a lengthy discussion it was decided that the loans would be distributed by agreement with the representatives of the guilds (cechy); the size of the loans will correspond to the trade concerned. Besides this it was unanimously decided, on the proposal of the starosta Mr. Baksa[?], to address an appropriate petition to the management of the „Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego“ in Warsaw, that the allotted 300 thousand zł. should remain as an interest-free loan fund in the local „Communal Savings Bank“ (Komunalna Kasa) until the economic situation improves.
Since on the question of the manner, i.e. according to what plan the loans should be handed out — both individually and through the guilds — it has not yet been possible to reach a decision, it was resolved to call a second conference in the near future in order to settle the said matter definitively.
The money was already deposited last week in the Będzin savings bank, and individual applications will be accepted from next Monday onward, directly through the „Kasa“ or through the guilds.

A Mother Throws Her Child to the Worms
In Pekin[?] the residents saw lying beside the local river a newborn child, a little girl, of whom the worms and flies were having a great feast....
The little soul was taken to the home for abandoned children, where Dr. Malicki established that it was impossible to keep the little soul alive.
The police are on the trail of the murderous mother.

Who for Life and Who for Death
Yesterday at 2 in the afternoon young Górski of Czeladź, a student of the pilots' school, fell and was killed on the spot.
A few days ago Górski wrote a letter to his parents, in which he says: „Don't be afraid; whoever is destined to live will live.“

Under the chairmanship of engineer Mr. Icchak Szpinkeler[?] the first general meeting of „Hechalutz“ took place here [in Zawiercie]. The chairman spoke about the significance of the meeting and at the same time read out the statutes.

A Couple in Love from Łódź Arrested in Sosnowiec
He is 17 years old, she — 20, both from Łódź and head over heels in love, and since their parents did not consent to the match, she made a „raid“ on the drawers, took a little jewellery and also some sum of money — and off they went to Sosnowiec.
The couple took a room at the Hotel „Victoria“ and the next morning went to the pawnshop on Targowa Street, where they wanted to pawn the jewellery.
At the best moment a plain-clothes agent arrived, who took them to the police station, and from there they were sent back to Łódź.

[Grodziec — road accident; followed by four short news items: Sosnowiec, Będzin.]
A few days before the wedding the bridegroom is killed
On Tuesday a terrible accident occurred on the road between Grodziec and Czeladź.
On Tuesday the 28-year-old Wiśniewski of Grodziec and his future in-law Tripnen[?] of Wojkowice were riding on a cart loaded with wood.
On the way the horse took fright at a passing automobile and began to run fast, as a result of which Wiśniewski and Tripnen[?] fell onto the roadway.
The case was fatal. Wiśniewski fell onto a stone slab, suffered a concussion and died a few minutes later; Tripnen[?] broke both his arms and legs.
The tragic victim was to have married Tripnen's[?] daughter next Sunday.

Yesterday afternoon, while the Jewish tinsmith Lakai was roofing the new 4-storey building on Wspólna Street in Sosnowiec, he lost his balance and fell onto the pavement.

[Będzin — Zionism; JNF.]
On Tuesday a meeting of the JNF (Keren Kayemet LeIsrael) took place, with the participation of a „gallery“ (public audience).
The first point raised by the Poalei Zion: to deny the notice in „Y. Ts.“ about their exclusion from the JNF — the motion was rejected by a majority of votes.
On the other hand it was resolved that the Poalei Zion (P.Z.) take part in the meetings, since only the Central Committee (C.C.) in Warsaw is entitled to exclude an organisation.
At the meeting the student Sternfeld (Revisionist) was elected, whose task is to put the finances of the JNF in Będzin in order.

The Prague Fair

(From our Prague correspondent)
In the period from the 7th to the 14th of September this year, the great fair will be opened in Prague; it is held there twice a year.
Of all the trade fairs that have sprung up after the war in almost every larger city of Europe, Prague is without any doubt the only place that is justified in founding a fair of its own. Czechoslovakia is today already known all over the world for its mighty industry. There is no branch in the world that does not have its large factories in Czechoslovakia with specialised products [?], from the cheapest to the most expensive article. It is certainly important that this great industry should show, in the capital of Czechoslovakia, to merchants from the whole world what it is capable of producing.
The fairground, which was set up in Prague for this purpose, is open the whole year and serves so that every day, when somebody comes to Prague from abroad or also from within the country, he can view here in one place all the most important industries that Czechoslovakia possesses; he can obtain there exact information regarding prices, quotas, changes in the patterns and the like, since the office of the Prague fairground always receives the latest information from every firm.
Twice a year foreign countries too exhibit their industries there, in the fairground and in the houses around it — for example Germany, Austria, France, England, Japan, Russia, America and so on — which wage a struggle there with Czechoslovak industry. In this way one can see there the greatest industries of the whole world competing with one another. The merchant who comes there to buy has here the best opportunity to see and to select for himself the best and most useful things he needs for his business.
At the fair, which begins on the 7th of September, besides the countries mentioned, a whole series of new countries will exhibit for the first time, among them also Bulgaria and South Africa, and therefore it is confidently expected that the fair will be better and more heavily attended than the twenty fairs held in Prague up to now.
P. Langstein.

A Herzl Commemoration.
On Sunday a festive Herzl commemoration ("academy") took place in the guesthouse of Mr. Frenkel, with the participation of Dr. Wodawiński [?] of Bielsko.
After the opening by Mr. S. Frenkel, the floor is given to the guest, Dr. Wodawiński [?], who delivers an exemplary speech (in Polish) on the significance of Dr. Herzl. We must educate — says the speaker — our youth in the spirit of Dr. Herzl, not in a religious-national and not in a Zionist-socialist spirit, but in a purely Zionist one.
Messrs. Dor [?] Hoffer and J. Wygodzki also speak. With the singing of "Hatikvah" the commemoration is closed.
Great thanks are due to Mr. Shlomo Frenkel and Miss Mandel for their work in organising the commemoration.
A certain sum was also collected for the Jewish National Fund (KKL).
A Flower Day.
Next Sunday, thanks to the efforts of Mr. S. Frenkel with the local committee, a flower sale will take place here for the benefit of the Jewish National Fund. The committee appeals to the guests to support the campaign as is fitting.
"Hashachar" of Bielitz will also take an active part in the flower sale.
The Summer Guests,
who are mostly our brethren, the children of Israel, from Będzin, forget here their economic troubles, feel very comfortable and pass the time not at all badly in the local Jewish guesthouses, which are growing in number.
Ger ve-Toshav ("Stranger and Resident").
Letters to the Editor

[Będzin — letters to the editor.]
I.
Most esteemed Mr. Editor!
We have the honour to ask you to grant us space in your esteemed newspaper.
Having read the letter by Mr. Prachtzweig in your esteemed newspaper, issue no. 25, concerning the Gmilus Khesed (interest-free loan) fund, we have the honour to reply as follows:
It is not true, Mr. Prachtzweig, that the institution is already on the verge of collapse. The Gmilus Khesed fund, which operates with a capital of over 110 thousand zł. (of which its own capital is 60 thousand and deposit [?] money over 50 thousand zł.), from which 1,500 families constantly benefit, is prospering quite normally and will not go under.
Nor is it true that the expenses are equal to the income, for in spite of the fact that the income has decreased thanks to your harmful tactics in the street regarding the Gmilus Khesed fund, the expenses still do not exceed 30 per cent of the income, for which we can produce documents.
It is also not true that in our institution things are done on their own authority by the presidents, for for every decision there exists a protocol of the board.
We do, however, find it necessary to tell the public what it is that vexes Mr. Prachtzweig.
1) At the last constitution of the board he was eager for a seat as vice-president, and the whole board found this harmful and of course did not elect him; in revenge he began to conduct a public agitation against the Gmilus Khesed fund.
2) Since the new board took over the mandates, it has been introduced that loans are approved by a special loan committee, and Mr. Prachtzweig was not satisfied with this change, because he could no longer grant loans on his own authority to his [?] soap-shops — and that is the "they cry out and are not answered" [?].
For the reasons mentioned above the board came to the agreement that such a member is not wanted, and expelled him from the board.
We point out that we shall not carry on any further polemics with you, Mr. Prachtzweig, for we would rather devote our time to the benefit of the Gmilus Khesed fund.
Hoping that the esteemed Mr. Editor will fulfil our request, we sign with respect,
The board of the interest-free loan fund "Gmilus Khesed" in Będzin.
II.
A reply to the author, Mr. R. Les [?], on his article in the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" of 11 July of this year, under the title "Articles that incite".
In the said article the author, who, as it turns out, takes an interest in municipal questions, attacked the Tenants' Association, which in his opinion took no position on the water question and did not defend the interests of the tenants whom it supposedly represents.
Among other things the author writes:
"It is a wonder that the Tenants' Association does not say a word on the question, and why it takes no position at all."
And in another place:
"The councillors should surely have protected the tenants to the extent that the house-owners pay the magistrat for the water the sum that the water has cost them until now, and the tenants pay the difference — this the councillors could certainly have taken into account, and the tenants' representatives should have stood on guard here and protected the interests of their members."
The board of the Tenants' Association considers it its duty to explain the following to the public:
When the town council began to consider the water question, the Tenants' Association called a special board meeting on 24 November 1929 in order to take a position on this important question, and as a result it was decided to submit to the town council a memorandum expressing the wishes and demands of the broad masses of tenants (those curious can see it at the magistrat, file no. 25/199). The content of this memorandum was made known to the public through the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" and "Express Zagłębia". That is the actual state of affairs. The further fate of the water question lay in the hands of the town council, which, as the outcome of the debate held, took into account only a small part of our memorandum, while at the same time rejecting a whole series of points.
Finally, we state that councillor Mr. Michał Lewin, who is at the same time president of the "Tenants' Association", although he was not elected councillor with the votes of our members, rose to the height of his task on the water question and supported our demands to their full extent.
Respectfully,
The board of the Tenants' Association in Będzin.
III.
We hereby earnestly ask the esteemed editorial board to publish the following lines in your esteemed newspaper, for which we thank you.
The report of Mr. Poglewicz's [?] lecture, in which mention was made of a supposedly tactless intervention by Mr. Y. Preger, does not correspond to reality. The best proof is that the chairman did not consider it necessary to stop him or to react to his intervention.
The Revisionist Union in Będzin.
What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — short news items.]
A Visit by French Financiers.
On Sunday a group of French bankers visited Katowice; they toured a series of factories and government institutions in Katowice, Chorzów and Mysłowice.
Afterwards a conference was held at the vice-voivode's.
—o—
Punished for Fraud.
Before the Katowice district court stood a certain Al. Heftal [?] of Będzin, who had defrauded the firm Blitz [?] in Katowice of 3000 zł. At the request of the local police Heftal was brought from Düsseldorf, where he had fled after carrying out the fraud.
Heftal was sentenced to 3½ months in prison.
—o—
He Added 3 Zeros...
Into the jewellery store "Jubilea" [?] in Katowice came a certain Jan Gruszka and bought a diamond for 1500 zł. He paid the sum with a P.K.O. [Postal Savings Bank] book for a sum of 10 thousand zł. The owner of the shop suspected that the sum in the book was forged and called a policeman, who discovered that the "buyer" was well known to the police and that Gruszka had carried out the fraud in this way: he had deposited 10 zł. at the P.K.O. and received a savings book for just those 10 zł. Then he added another 3 zeros and "received" a sum of 10,000 zł.
—o—
Unemployment Is Growing.
According to the statistical figures, the number of unemployed in the Silesian voivodeship grows from week to week. According to the latest figures the unemployed number 34,072 persons.
—o—
A Bankruptcy of Thirty Million zł.
The timber firm "Oberschlesische Holzindustrie" [Upper Silesian Timber Industry] in Beuthen [Bytom] has gone bankrupt; its liabilities amount to 14 million German marks.
—o—
Herzl Academy.
On Saturday night a memorial evening was held in Mysłowice for the 26th yahrzeit of Dr. Theodor Herzl of blessed memory.
The chairman, Mr. Bena Duhl [?], greeted the gathering of 70 persons, and the chief cantor, Mr. Chaim Leib Ehrlich, recited El Male Rachamim, which brought tears to those present. Then Mr. A. Silbering [?] (Kraków) gave a lecture, appealing for work for our homeland and for our people.
—o—
For Forging Trade Books
the police in Königshütte [Chorzów] arrested 2 local merchants who are accused of forging trade books, through which the government suffered a loss of 58 thousand zł.
—o—
A Tragic Event on an Outing.
On Monday 4 motorcyclists from Mysłowice made an excursion to Imielin [?]. On the way a collision occurred, and the result was terrible: one was killed on the spot, the others were seriously injured and are fighting for their lives.
—o—
The Hat Was to Blame...
In Zabrze a woman was walking along the local railway line. At that moment the wind tore her hat off her head. When the woman ran to catch her hat, a train came along, which struck the woman and broke her arm.
A Great Fire in Szczekociny. 20 Jewish Families Left Without a Roof.

On Monday morning a fire broke out in Szczekociny at the premises of a local Christian butcher. The fire spread quickly and engulfed the surrounding buildings. Despite energetic rescue efforts, 8 houses went up in smoke and 20 Jewish families were ruined and left without a roof over their heads.
Kozłów near Miechów.

As we are assured, the Rebbe will stay here about 6 weeks.
The Rebbe, may he live long, is staying with Mr. M. Słabecki [?], right by the station.
M. Gotlib.
