"For Tomorrow, Let God Take Care"

[Opinion — economy and the middle class.] (The economic interests of the middle class. — The tragedy we do not see among us.)
"Today is today; for tomorrow let God take care" — to this very day it is not only the lower strata of the Jewish population that cling to this formula, but in fact the middle strata too, those who are supposedly "well-off", those for whom the street [?] has "provided" [?] and says that they are well situated.
"Today is today, and for tomorrow let God take care" was quite good once, in the times of our great-grandfathers, when people lived on miracles and on fasts [?], and whoever [?] spent six [coins?] a week was counted among the wastrels. But today one must, after all, finally forget those times; now we live under different conditions, so that even if things need not now be calculated, and even if one means to spend little, one cannot compare oneself with those times. And yet the above-mentioned formula still exists today among a large part of the middle strata of the Jewish population.
A merchant, a shopkeeper, a craftsman has a bill of exchange (wechsel) to pay today. Well, does he have the money lying ready? Who knows — like yesterday's day. "If I had the money lying ready," he answers you, "it would be no trick at all." And how, he explains to you, can he even think about paying the bill when he has not yet returned the interest-free loan (gmilut chesed) he took and borrowed, and any minute the other man comes after his few gulden. A bill, you must know, the other gives you to understand: if he has to pay today, he has a way out — he asks the bank to put it off [?] for a day; and if tomorrow there is still no money, never mind, he can still pay it at the notary (rejent) as well; true, it costs something, but for that he gains another two days, and in the course of such a time there are still many good hours, and the Master of the Universe can still help — help him to take in some money and get another loan, and perhaps he will even be able to borrow [?] a few more gulden from someone else for a few hours.
That is how one fixes things here and props oneself up there, shifts this way and that, takes an interest-free loan from this one and gives it to that one, and the next day one turns the same thing over from the right side to the left. It is simply a wonder and a miracle how one gets through such a week, and more than once you have the chance to hear from such a Jew of the marvels he went through before he managed to get [the bill] stamped [?]. Say what you will — such wire-walking work is to be admired; and people have grown so accustomed to this "work" that now it is for them a normal phenomenon, a daily occupation, a natural thing that is no longer regarded as abnormal or extraordinary. And the truth must be told: the expertise and ingenuity in this field are simply admirable, and when one thinks about it one comes to the firm conviction that here we are invincible. No nation in the world could imitate it: neither the capable German nor the crafty Englishman could stand alongside and compete with ours [?] — a Jew has X tricks of setting himself up and fixing himself up, with the speed of, let us say, motion pictures.
So, so our abilities are used up among us on nothing and again on nothing. Had we applied these abilities to something substantial, one would know that something would come of it in the future; but since one looks only for a way to push through the day, and with that one is already happy — who gets from such "happiness" the salvation one aims at with the much-sought [?] institutions?
The upshot of all this is characteristic: none of us gives his children the occupation that he has, whether he is a shopkeeper, a merchant or has some trade or other. Everyone is disgusted with his own occupation, and so he says: why should I harness my child into the same yoke (khomut)? It is enough that I must drag the inhuman burden on my weak shoulders; let my child at least have a better, an easier livelihood.
It is therefore no wonder that parents push their children away from the same occupations — but precisely in this pushing-away lies the tragedy.
Once and for all we must take stock and turn the page to the other side, when we come to realize that it is not the businesses or the trades our popular strata possess that are worthless, but just the opposite: the management, the direction, the supervision are not good, not normal, not sound.
We live in the 20th century, when not only hours but seconds, one may say, decide; when everything beats with unheard-of speed; and if we have no time to find our bearings as to what changes are arising, how can one keep up with the times? And once one does not keep up with the times, it means one stays behind — and what it means to stay behind in business instead of going forward, every modern [?] person will know how to discern.
With us it is "Today — today, and for tomorrow let God take care." A modern [?] person knows that business does not consist in pushing through the day, in snatching a few gulden from Shmerl and handing them to Berl — and a year later exactly the other way round.
It is no longer a secret that if a firm wants to make itself popular and attract sympathy and customers, it must advertise strongly, must have attractive shop windows, fine treatment [of customers], good access to the shop, must know how to make use of every opportunity. Besides that, one must know where and which goods to buy and in what way to calculate their prices. That is what it means to run a business on normal foundations, and only in such a way can one work with love and devotion, both in commerce and in handicraft; and then parents will not grow disgusted with their businesses, and will watch with pleasure how the inheritance is carried on by their children.
An occupation can become repugnant only when it is not run on any sound foundations, when the business's credo is scheming how to pay a bill of exchange — which takes up all his time, so that one is unable to buy the goods well, one has no possibility of calculating their prices, and one does not strive [?] to draw customers in a forward-looking way (not in a grabbing one).
And therefore we say: if we want to exist, we too must place our economic interests on sound, normal foundations, where we will have the possibility to calculate carefully and to buy goods well and cheaply, and where we will have time to see how to sell better and cheaper [?]; and then one can hope to reach a firm basis such as every citizen in the 20th century prides himself on [?].
If things are arranged among us in such a way, everyone will work at his occupation with love and self-sacrifice and will have joy when he sees how his best energy [?] is carried on into the second generation, as we see it in all civilized countries among the healthy nations.
Y. T.
"Trzeba wybrukować"... (A Little Feuilleton)

[Będzin — satirical feuilleton; city council.]
"Just give me the agenda of today's 'posiedzenie' [meeting] at the Magistrat [city hall]," Shmerl the Ratman [city councillor] turned to his wife. "I have to read it through, to know what it's about. You know, my wife, that I am a councillor, and when one is a councillor one has to be able to read."
"And if one can read, one is precisely not a councillor," says his wife with a smile.
"Ah, show [?] me the agenda quickly, I have to be at the session today."
Shmerl buried himself in the minutes.
First item: water is no longer to be taken from the [shops?]. Good, he thinks to himself, one really should give it a thought, maybe.. Second item: a request from Egipska Street [Egyptian Street] that their district be paved. Very important, I must put my name down; after all I come to Egipska Street every day. "Trzeba wybrukować ulicę Egipską" [Polish: Egipska Street must be paved]; one must [?] our brethren.. lay down stones, so that at the coming elections I can again stand on the bimah and shout:
"Jews, I, I was the only one who was the first to shout with my mighty voice: 'Trzeba ulicę Egipską wybrukować!' There is no more mud by you, I took it upon myself!.." He liked the thought himself and smiled to himself. Further items: reducing the fee for trading in the market halls, claims of the Magistrat officials, loans for the Magistrat — all important. Well, my wife, I'm off to the session.
While listening at the session to the reading of the previous minutes, he dozed off, and in a dream it seemed to him that he was speaking in the city council and, above all, that everyone understood him. A ring of the bell woke him; they moved on to the agenda, and Shmerl, against his will, had to take the floor in the discussion, and indeed he said:
"Trzeba wybrukować ulicę Egipską"...
A. Goldzbarg.
Dacha Troubles.

[Humorous feuilleton — summer holidays.]
Y. Oberżanek.
Where around here does a blister-doctor live? You don't know where a blister-doctor lives around here? Jews, have pity, give me a blister-specialist!
You don't know what a blister-specialist is? Until now I didn't know either. I knew of doctors with various specialties: specialists in internal and external diseases. I knew that there are gall specialists and liver specialists, just as — no comparison intended — with tailors: "damskie" [ladies'] doctors and "męskie" [men's] doctors; but blister-doctors? Have you ever heard of such a specialty? How should you know? But if you had a wife called Tsipe Breyne, who keeps frying herself and "smażyć"-ing [roasting] herself in the sun, you would already know what a doctor who is a blister-specialist is.
My Tsipe Breyne is a "nadzwyczajna" [extraordinary] lover of the sun. Sun, she says, is life. The sun, she argues, gives off violet rays that heal all ailments, and since my Tsipe Breyne has all sorts of ailments, she keeps frying and "smażyć"-ing herself in the sun. She eats sun — she swallows the sun...
As every year, this year too my Tsipe Breyne went off to a dacha [summer cottage]. And what does my Tsipe Breyne go to a dacha for? You think she wants to recuperate, that she wants to put on weight, or even to snatch a flirt in the "świeże powietrze" [fresh air]? God forbid — she goes for "słoneczne kąpiele" [sunbaths]. When she rents a dacha, the first thing she looks for is a "nie krępująca" [?] [secluded] "polanka" [clearing], where she can fry and roast like a young duck in a frying pan.
So she did indeed find the true dacha with all the "wygody" [comforts]. The dacha itself is not even so-so: the room is as big as a cigarette kiosk, the ceiling rests on your head, the walls are like the "showbread" — see-through. And as for flies, gnats, bedbugs and other pests — one mustn't sin by complaining. But to make up for it she has other "wygody" — a "polanka".
And why am I telling you this story? After all I asked you about a doctor who is a blister-specialist? I'm telling you precisely because it bears on the matter: the "polanka", that is, bears on the blister-specialist. Surely you too have a wife, and so surely you too are a [?] — so you may as well hear the story out.
Yes, where were we? At the "polanka". As soon as my Tsipe Breyne arrived at the dacha, she quickly unpacked her bathing [?] paraphernalia: the short black trunks, the [—] cap [?], the little box of Vaseline — and off to the "polanka".
A minute later my Tsipe Breyne was already dressed in her bathing "majtki" [drawers], the cap on her head, a gauze handkerchief on her forehead, a green leaf on her nose, smeared with Vaseline from head to foot — and Tsipe Breyne is burning!.. First she lies face up. The sun fries her and roasts her. The Vaseline sizzles [?] till it actually smokes, the sweat runs, and Tsipe Breyne soaks up violet rays...
When she has finished frying her face, she turns to her back, later to her legs, and so on without end.
When I see my Tsipe Breyne roasting, I start begging her: Tsipele, Breyneshi, perhaps you've burned enough already? How long is one supposed to torment oneself like this? You already look like a cholent potato!... Rest a little and then burn some more... If you want, I say, to burn — burn in good health, but bit by bit, "stopniowo" [gradually].
But talk to her today, talk to her tomorrow — she does her own thing. As long as there is sun, she has to "skorzystać" [make the most of it].
You say, I see, that it's "ciekawe" [interesting] to know what connection my Tsipe Breyne's burning herself has with the blister-specialist I'm looking for? You'll hear in a moment:
It happened just this week. I'm still lying in bed thinking about.. about.. well, never mind what I was thinking about; what can a "słomiany wdowiec" [grass widower] think about when he lies [?] all alone in his bed? You're a "słomiany" too, so there's no need to spell it out for you. But that's not what I'm getting at; I only want to tell you why I'm now looking for a blister-specialist.
Yes, where were we? At my bed, as I lie there thinking about this and that, about bygone [?] days. Suddenly — a knocking at the door. Ha, who's knocking so early? And before I even try to ask who's knocking, I hear behind the door whimpering and groaning, and who do you think was groaning and whimpering? — my wife, my Tsipe Breyne.
I take a look at my darling [?] and everything goes dark before my eyes: her head wrapped [?] in a kerchief, her hands bandaged, she walks bent double, groaning and moaning. Every groan stabbed me like a knife.
"What's wrong with you, Tsipe Breyne, have you, God forbid, had a cramp?"
"Oy.. oy... worse [?]... not a cramp."
"Then what's wrong with you?"
"Oy, oy, I'm dying."
"Tsipele, Breyneshi," — I lost my temper — "tell me quickly, what happened to you? Perhaps a bee sting?"
"Woe is me, not a cramp and not a bee."
"Ay, ay, oy, my blisters!"
"What blisters? Who blew and what blew?" [pun: Yiddish "blozn" = blisters / to blow]
May the enemies of Zion feel as dizzy as I felt when I saw my Tsipe Breyne's face: the whole face nothing but blisters, the skin of her hands peeling, as though she had just been pulled out of a boiling kettle.
Where did my Tsipe Breyne get the blisters from? From the violet rays; she "skorzystała" [made the most of it] so long that she got a little burned..
Now I'm running to look for a doctor who is a blister-specialist.
Jews, perhaps you do know where a blister-specialist can be found around here?
The First Synagogue in Germany

(A page of Jewish history.)
(Especially for the "Zaglembier Tsaytung".)

In the archives of the Leipzig trade-fair office (Messeamt) one can find exactly what difficulties the Jews had to endure hundreds of years ago.

The first traces of Jews in Germany are found in the year 1411. It is recounted that at that time a dispute broke out at the Leipzig fair between the Jewish and the Christian merchants over competition at the fair. When the Jews first came to the fair is not known. This much is certain: in 1411 they were already regular guests and gave the Christian merchants strong competition, so that the city of Leipzig had, "at the request of the Christian inhabitants", to expel[?] the Jews.

From 1411 to 1429 there are no records concerning Jewish merchants at the Leipzig fair. Only in 1436 was an edict issued again that Jewish merchants may not come to Leipzig "to compete with the Christian merchants at the fair".

These decrees affected only those small Jewish merchants who used to come to Leipzig without a pass. The big merchants, who had their own passes and came to trade in Leipzig, were not counted[?], and they were not expelled[?] either. For the period from 1436 to 1664 there are no records at all concerning Jews. Whether Jews really did not come to the Leipzig fair during that time, whether they were mixed up in the records with all the other fair guests, or whether the records concerning Jews were lost — nobody knows. Only once, in 1598, does the name Moshe Levi appear among the fair guests — a sign that Jews did come to Leipzig for the fair.

In 1689 Jews for the first time received permission to form a minyan and to pray communally on Sabbaths and holidays, but "the worshippers must not offend the feelings of the Christian inhabitants". Together with this permission, which for the first time in history granted Jews privileges, they also received the right to bury their dead, paying for each deceased a sum of 12 thalers to the monasteries and schools.

This permission, however, lasted only a few years. In 1699 the clergy protested against it, arguing that the Jewish prayers contain chapters in which "Christianity is insulted", and therefore "honest Christians cannot permit such an outrage". In 1703 the Saxon Elector Augustus forbade the Jews who came to the Leipzig fair to pray in the city and also outside the city. Evidently the Jews did not obey him and went on forming minyanim, for in 1704 another edict was issued that Jews may not form any minyanim. This edict, made stricter with heavy penalties, was posted in all the streets of Leipzig "so that they may know". The owners of all houses were warned that as soon as they allowed Jews to pray communally in their houses, they would be very severely punished. Whether the Jews indeed did not gather to pray is not known to this day. In 1724 Rabbi Nachman ben Yechiel came to Leipzig; he received permission to come to Leipzig at any time without any payment, solely in his capacity as "a rabbi in Israel".

Only in 1736 did the Jews complain to the new Saxon Grand Prince about the edict forbidding Jews to pray communally. In this letter to the Saxon Elector they list how much benefit the Jews bring to the city of Leipzig, and they declare that if their request to be allowed to pray communally and to keep Sabbaths and holidays as is the custom (Sukkot then used to fall during the time of the fair) were not granted, they would stop coming to Leipzig, and "the Leipzig fair without Jews will go to ruin just as the fairs in Breslau or in Frankfurt went to ruin".

To this petition the Saxon government has not replied to this day. The end of it was that after a short time the Jews no longer waited for any answer; they began in Leipzig to form one minyan after another and prayed communally even on weekdays. The government and the Leipzig municipality knew about it and kept silent...

Thus the first "synagogues" in Germany came into being...

Z. Haber.
A Victim of His Wife's Cousin.

[Feuilleton — a humorous tale.]
(From the homely little stories).

Shloyme Lebetag (let us call him that, because the name suits him; his real name we do not wish to mention) came into the house neither dead nor alive, utterly exhausted, after such hard toil as transporting his "better half" to a dacha [summer cottage].

Dead tired, he dropped onto the sofa, not feeling a single whole limb from packing and hauling the heavy baskets of dacha gear.

— Well, thank God — he thinks to himself — half a wish has already been fulfilled: he has managed to send his wife off somewhere far away, and now he will spare himself being torn apart every Friday like the black year and riding out to her loaded with parcels like a mule.

He is already a free bird... Now all that remains is that he be sent the kind of thing every "straw widower" [a husband whose wife is away on holiday] wishes for.

And why not, indeed? A whole year he was torn apart, he listened to all sorts of insults, curses and anathemas; now, when the Almighty has helped and he is rid of his "trouble" — why shouldn't he be like other people, and not treat himself to such a pleasure at home, and also taste "of that red, red stuff" [Genesis 25:30; here a hint at wine]?...

As he lies there sunk in his thoughts, he hears a ring at the door. Quickly he jumped off the sofa and opened the door, where to his great surprise there appeared on the threshold a beautiful young woman, who asked in a tender feminine voice whether "Pani [Mrs] Lebetag" did not live here. On receiving the answer that she was not mistaken and had indeed come to the right place, she introduced herself: Saltshe [Salcia] Blumenthal, his wife's cousin, who, happening to pass by, had dropped in especially to see her cousin, whom she had not seen for a long time.

Shloyme politely led her into the parlour and asked her to make herself comfortable and feel at home, although his wife — her cousin — had gone off to a dacha, which he very much regretted.

He himself ran out to the nearest little shop, where he bought all kinds of good things.

When he came back with the parcels he was simply astounded by her beauty. She was already dressed in a light, bright silk frock, sewn in the latest fashion, with bare arms and a large décolletage.

— Am I not dreaming? — thought Shloyme, admiring her slender figure.

Sitting at the table, already after tea, they became such good friends as though he had known her for almost a year.

Such a successful [?] one, such a lovely one! Let his "Zeresh" [nickname for his wife; Zeresh was Haman's wife] be an atonement for her littlest fingernail; if only all of life were one long summer.

In the evening Shloyme invited Saltshe to the cinema.

On the way back he kept showering her with compliments, at which Saltshe glowed with pleasure and smiled sweetly into his face, nestling up to him more and more.

On coming into the house Shloyme lit a fire, they drank tea and entertained themselves, forgetting meanwhile that another wife existed in the world.

Shloyme remembered that he had forgotten to buy cigarettes; he wanted to run out to buy some, but she would not let him, because he was sweaty from the tea and might, God forbid, catch a chill. She took out of her handbag a silk case of "damske" [ladies'] cigarettes, lit one herself and treated Shloyme too.

Shloyme was so moved by her kind-heartedness that he snatched a kiss from her.

It became so light on his soul; he felt as if he were floating somewhere in the heavens, as if angels in the shape of beautiful women were stroking him and carrying him to flowers, and the flowers smelled like the fragrance of Paradise, and he grew quite drunk from their aroma — — — — — — —

He woke up when it was already broad daylight. Somehow his head was as heavy as if cast in lead. He wanted to take out his watch to see how late it was — but alas.. gone was the gold watch with the chain that he had received as a gift for his wedding.

Bewildered, he began searching his other pockets — a disaster! Gone was the wallet with the 18 hundred złoty that he had set aside to redeem bills of exchange. Gone was the gold signet ring with the ruby, and also the silver tobacco case.

Like a madman he began running through the rooms, where everywhere he came upon terrible devastation: the wardrobes and drawers open, things thrown out onto the floor, of which the best were missing; everything had been turned upside down...

Shloyme began to scream wildly. At his cries all the neighbours came running, but of the "cousin" there was no longer any trace. Evidently she had already gone off to palm herself off on another dacha sucker.

[Sosnowiec — crime.]
On Sienkiewicza Street in Sosnowiec, by Zuckerman's ramp [loading platform], Mrs Abramczyk was counting money. At that moment two attackers ran up and snatched from Mrs A. a bundle of money amounting to 1400 zł.

At Mrs A.'s cries the police came, chased the attackers and caught them. Of the snatched money they had no more than 994 zł. 35 gr. The rest had been scattered along the way as they ran.

[Czeladź — crime.]
The Czeladź police have arrested a local resident, a certain Janota [?], who tried to rape his own child, a little girl aged 10.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion (Matot-Masei)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings and remarks on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and adapted by Y. L.
Parashat Matot-Masei
—o—
a) "And Moses spoke unto the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, saying."
The word "dibbur" means in Hebrew harsh speech, whereas "amira" means soft speech — so according to the homily. To the heads of the tribes, to the community leaders and chiefs — to them "va-yedabber": they were spoken to harshly and sternly; whereas to the children of Israel, to the common people — to them "lemor": softly and gently.
(Apparently one must speak to the leaders harshly and sternly.)
Or Penei Moshe.
—o—
b) "If a man vow a vow unto the Lord" (30:3).
The Talmud says many times that making a vow is good[?] for the pious, whereas for one who is not pious enough it is not desirable to make a vow.
A thief had a neighbour, a poor worker. Both had little girls, and they had to be provided for. The thief asks the worker: how will you provide for your girls? The worker tells him that he had a money box made, locked it with a padlock, and every day he drops a certain coin into the box. That is all his children's fortune. The thief does the same. But whenever he needs money, he breaks open the lock and robs the box. For someone to whom all locks are open, what protection at all will such a little money-box lock be?
A pious Jew who wants to guard himself against a permitted thing makes a vow — hangs on a little lock; whereas the freethinker, for whom the bigger locks — the Torah's prohibitions — are open, what will such a little lock as a vow, so to speak, achieve?..
The Dubno Maggid.
—o—
c) "If a woman also vow a vow" (30:4).
The law of a man's vow is contained in one single verse, because if he makes a vow he keeps it; whereas the law of a woman's vow takes fourteen verses and various complicated rules of regret and annulment, because that is her way: to make a vow and to regret it right away.
Melekhet Mahshevet.
—o—
d) A vow.
The Gemara (Tractate Nedarim) says: "For the sin of vows one's wife dies" — if one does not fulfil a vow, the wife dies, because —
There are two ways to become rich: one — to give charity, "tithe so that you may become rich"; and the other — to treat one's wife with respect, for so says the Gemara: "Honour your wives so that you may become rich." So the wife says to the husband: what good is it to you to keep your vows and give charity in order to become rich? Better honour me, and you'll become rich too.
So such a wife simply has to die, and then the husband will have to give charity.
Sihat Hullin.
—o—
e) "Avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites; afterward shalt thou be gathered unto thy people" (31:2).
God told Moses that once he took revenge on the Midianites he would die soon after; so he could well have delayed the revenge and lived longer. But when it concerned a matter of the people, his own life was worth nothing to him, and at once: "And Moses spoke unto the people, saying: Arm ye."
Midrash Tanhuma.
—o—
f) "The men of war had taken booty, every man for himself" (31:53).
The captains of thousands and captains of hundreds were each asked to bring an ornament for God. The rest of the multitude was not asked. The Torah tells their praise: that they indeed did not bring anything, but "took booty, every man for himself." Yes, it is great praise not to perform "a commandment of men learned by rote" — giving just like that when one is not told to, being pious when one need not. Jacob's attribute is truth, moderation, not senseless ecstasy. A word to the wise.
Kol Simha.
—o—
g) "Now the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of cattle" (32:1).
"Gad" means luck. The children of Gad — those who convince themselves that they are rich thanks to their luck. The children of Reuben — those who say: "re'u ben" — see, by our diligence and ability we have acquired a fortune.
These two categories of people convince themselves that they are God's chosen, that the best portions of this world, and even of the world to come as well, are due to them. Just like the children of Gad and the children of Reuben, who wanted the best portions of the land and did not help the other brothers conquer their land. And of these categories it is said (Rashi, [v.] 16) that with them their property came before their children.
Or ha-Me'ir.
—o—
Avot, Chapter Two.
"Let your fellow's property be as dear to you as your own" (Mishnah 17).
With people, the money another person owns is dearer; even though he himself owns just as much, he envies the other, the other's is more precious. Says Rabbi Yose: "Let your fellow's property be as dear to you as your own" — do not love the other's money more than yours.
Beit Shmuel Aharon.
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: The City "Fathers" Want to "Rest" for 2 Months

[Będzin — City council.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 29 Tammuz 5690 — Friday, 25 July 1930.)
Będzin
The City "Fathers" Want to "Rest" for 2 Months.
For the "last" session they rustle up a "minyan".
On Monday the last city-council session before the recess took place, at which a series of economic items were adopted, among them that the Magistrate [municipal executive] is taking a loan to build a building for teachers.
Adopting such an item requires 26 councillors to be present, and in order to complete the "minyan", 2 councillors were brought in in the middle of the session, and only then was the item concerning the loan approved.
Then the presidium announced that the city council's recess will last until 15 September.
The Synagogue Worshippers Took "the Floor" on the Cantor Question

[Będzin — Kehilla.]
The Synagogue Worshippers Took "the Floor" on the Cantor Question.
Sunday was the first appearance.
Last Sunday morning, while several members of the so-called kehilla board were at the gmina [kehilla] offices, the worshippers of the [Great] Synagogue, 50–60 men strong, went into the gmina and took "the floor" on the cantor question.
The worshippers expressed their demand that at the present time the kehilla board should not stir up any quarrels and should not engage new cantors, which entails large expenses, but should rather renew the agreement with the present cantor, Mr. Żupowicz [?].
The vice-president, Mr. Frazer [?], who was present at the storm, proposed that the worshippers delegate 3 persons with whom the kehilla board would settle the cantor matter.
The "stormers" agreed to the proposal and on their side delegated Messrs. Gershon Rechnik, Henech Kaminski and Moshe Meir Zaks.
Also interesting are the agitation and intrigues being conducted against Cantor Żupowicz. On the basis of reliable "information" the rabbinate acted in advance and sent the gmina an injunction [?] that without its consent no further steps be taken with the cantor, Mr. Żupowicz.
Steiger Was Indeed Innocent, but Ratmensz Will Sit in the Cooler...

[Będzin — Courts.]
Steiger Was Indeed Innocent, but Ratmensz Will Sit in the Cooler...
A peasant from Rokitno [?] was selling potatoes at the local market. Mr. David Ratmensz attached himself to the peasant, helped the peasant sell the potatoes and took part of the money for himself.
Ratmensz was brought to court, and the trial took place in the Sosnowiec District Court. Ratmensz's lawyer rejected the charge, arguing that the peasant had concocted a false accusation against him, just as against Steiger...
The court, however, recognised that Ratmensz could not be compared with Steiger's innocence, and sentenced him to one month's arrest.
Passage of Jewish Motorcyclists from Eretz Israel

[Będzin — Sport.]
Passage of Jewish Motorcyclists from Eretz Israel.
The Maccabi World Union informed the board of Hakoach that, since in the coming days the Jewish motorcyclists will pass through our town, Hakoach should prepare a reception for the guests from Eretz Israel, who will spend several days in Zagłębie.
— In this connection, a consultation was held yesterday evening at the Hakoach premises, at which the question of arranging a proper reception was discussed.
Careful with Geese

[Będzin — Health.]
Careful with Geese.
At Kołłątaja [Street] 34 several Jewish families fell ill at once. The doctors establish that the illness is caused by eating young geese.
At the Tax-Appeal Hearings Będzin Gets a Representative

[Będzin — Taxes.]
At the Tax-Appeal Hearings Będzin Gets a Representative.
Several times already we have touched in our paper on the problem that, when tax appeals were considered at the Izba [Treasury Chamber] in Kielce, the local merchants were left unprotected and had no representative to defend the merchants' interests.
This painful matter has finally found an echo with the boards of the local merchant institutions, and on behalf of the Small Traders' and Merchants' Association an intervention was made at the "Izba", to which the institutions sent a list of candidates.
The "Izba", however, did not take the submitted candidates into account, and nominated the previous representative, Abraham Zylberberg.
The session of the appeals commission takes place on the 31st of this month.
———
We have been asked by the Merchants' Association in Kielce to announce that the commission for considering appeals against turnover and income taxes in a number of branches will sit on the 28th, 30th and 31st of this month, and the Merchants' Association undertakes [?] to defend the persons concerned.
Telegrams with Hebrew Content Are Accepted Without Restriction

[Będzin — Zionism.]
Telegrams with Hebrew Content Are Accepted Without Restriction.
Several weeks ago the local Zionist Organisation sent a telegram with Hebrew content to Warsaw. The post-office clerk, however, made difficulties, demanded a word-for-word Polish translation, and in the end the telegram was not accepted.
The organisation therefore turned with a complaint to the post-office head (naczelnik), asking him whether there exist regulations imposing a restriction regarding the Hebrew language in sending telegrams.
This week the head sent a written reply, in which he stresses that there are no restrictions whatsoever regarding the Hebrew language.
At the same time he reports that the clerk has been reprimanded for his improper conduct.
Panic Among Tram Passengers

[Będzin — Incidents.]
Panic Among Tram Passengers.
On Tuesday morning a tram car began to burn. The fire, which caused panic among the passengers, was extinguished instantly.
Yesodei Torah people! Where is the 'thou shalt not withhold the wages of a hired worker'?..

[Będzin — religious education; labour.] The painter Yehoshua Sztergier [?] worked several months ago in the premises of the 'Cheder Yesodei Torah'. For the work he received [payment] only on the 1st of this month. But for his hard work he received no cash, only a promissory note (bill of exchange), payable, God willing, in Tammuz 5691.. (5 July 1931).
From the Zionist-Revisionist Union.

[Będzin — Zionism, Revisionists.] Last Saturday a 'question-box evening' took place in a packed hall; it aroused great interest and passed off with great success.
The topics discussed were: 1) whether the withdrawal of the Revisionists from the Zionist institutions is desirable, 2) why there is competition between the Revisionists and the Brit Trumpeldor members.
— Today, Saturday, at 2 p.m. the meeting will discuss the last 2 articles by Z. Jabotinsky: 1) 'Cold, calm and logical' and 2) 'Influence on a government'.

Sosnowiec
The kehilla board already has, thank God, a chairman...

[Sosnowiec — kehilla.] On Sunday the kehilla board held a meeting, at which it was decided by a majority of votes that Mr. L. Jungster joins the kehilla board as a member.
At the meeting Mr. Y. M. Weinreb was elected chairman of the kehilla board.

Doctor 'arrests' his 12-year-old patient.
Only the prosecutor frees him from the hospital.

[Sosnowiec — health; crime.] In the Suszek [?] family on Dekerta Street a 12-year-old boy suddenly fell ill, and the feldsher Teichner, who was called, declared that the boy was suffering from appendicitis and had to be operated on at once.
The boy was taken to the hospital in Szelce [?], where the necessary operation was performed, for which the doctor demanded no less than 800 zł.
The family began to bargain and was already willing to give 400 zł., but the doctor would not hear of it and demanded the full 800 zł.
When the family, naturally, did not pay the demanded fee, the doctor of the hospital forbade anyone from the family to be admitted to the child.
Because of this order the family turned to the prosecutor, who went straight to the said hospital and only then freed the child from 'captivity'.
Collision between a car and a cart.

[Zagłębie — road accidents.] On the Koziegłowy—Siewierz [?] road there was a collision between a passenger car and a cart. The collision was a disastrous one: Jadwiga Mszergik [?] of Königshütte broke her arms and legs. The Szczepański couple were seriously injured.
Punished for thefts at the 'Katarzyna' works.

[Sosnowiec — court.] Several workers stood before the local district court, accused of committing thefts at the 'Katarzyna' steelworks.
The trial lasted a whole day. The accused received heavy sentences.
A mass meeting of craftsmen.

[Sosnowiec — craftsmen.] Next Sunday afternoon a mass meeting of craftsmen will take place in [their] own premises. The meeting will discuss very important points such as: granting loans, diplomas, examinations, etc., which are of very great importance for the Jewish craftsmen.
The Jewish craftsmen receive 150 thousand zł.

[Sosnowiec — small trade and crafts; government loans.] As we have already written, the government has granted small traders and craftsmen a sum of 300 thousand zł. as a long-term loan.
Of this sum Sosnowiec receives 100 thousand, Będzin 100 thousand, Dąbrowa and Czeladź 100 thousand zł. The Jewish small traders and craftsmen receive half of it.
A Year and a Half in Prison for Communist Activity

On 6 March, during a demonstration of unemployed workers in front of the local labour exchange, Szmuel Margulies scattered communist leaflets. For this Margulies stood trial this week before the district court, which sentenced him to 1½ years in prison.
Is Industry Reviving? "Huta Bankowa" Receives Large Orders

As we are informed from a reliable source, Zagłębie industry is entering a stage of revival. In many coal mines the working days are being extended; the "Huta Bankowa" [steelworks] in Dąbrowa [Górnicza] has also received large orders from the government.
— Halmain [?]
Olkusz — A Memorial Gathering

On Wednesday evening a Herzl memorial gathering ("academy") was held in the premises of "Hashachar". The gathering opened with the singing of "Techezakna". M. Szwarcberg and Mr. Karcz [?], member of the Central Committee (Warsaw), spoke on current affairs. After the speeches, Miss Z. Brojner (in Hebrew) and M. Szwarcfeld (in Yiddish) gave recitations in memory of Herzl. Then a choir conducted by G. Unger sang "Yizkor" and Yehuda Halevi's sea song. Finally, on the motion of Mr. Goldberg, the meeting adopted a protest resolution against the halting of pioneer (chalutz) immigration to Eretz Israel. The impressive gathering closed with the singing of "Hatikvah".
Summer Resort Life

The number of summer holiday-makers is much greater this year than a year ago, mostly from Zagłębie. Nevertheless the summer flats are not expensive. This is explained by the fact that many new buildings have been added at "Czarna Góra".
A. B.
Zawiercie — Members' Meeting of "Tse'irei Mizrachi" and "Hashomer Hadati"

In connection with the world conference of the "Torah va-Avodah" movement, to be held on 15 Av in Danzig, the local "Tse'irei Mizrachi" called a members' meeting of the organizations "Tse'irei veha-Chalutz ha-Mizrachi", "Hashomer Hadati" and "Bruria" in the Zagłębie district. Taking part were Sosnowiec, Będzin, Ząbkowice, Olkusz, Sławków, Strzemieszyce, Myszków and Zawiercie, with 200 delegates. On behalf of the head office of "Tse'irei Mizrachi" came Mr. Grynberg; on behalf of the Eretz Israel delegation of Hapoel Hamizrachi, Mr. Skarszewski [?].
Mr. Israel Herman (Zawiercie) opened the meeting and in a successful address (in Hebrew) pointed out its tasks. The speaker then recalled the loss Mizrachi had suffered by the death of the Rabbi of Siemiatycze, Rabbi Remigolski [?] of blessed memory, and those assembled honoured the rabbi by rising. Elected chairman was Mr. Moshe Chaim Wajgdman [?] (Zawiercie), secretary Mr. Moshe Oppenheim (Będzin), and members of the presidium Messrs. Grynberg (Warsaw) and Skarszewski (Eretz Israel).
After the reports Mr. Skarszewski gave a very successful lecture (in Hebrew) on the tasks of the "Torah va-Avodah" movement at the present moment and ahead of the world conference. A heated debate followed, in which a large number of members took part.
Comrades Grynberg and Skarszewski answered the opponents, and the meeting closed in an elevated mood.
Finally a resolution was adopted against closing the gates of Eretz Israel to "chalutz immigration".
—o—
A Herzl Memorial
In the local town synagogue (Stadt-Shul) a Herzl memorial was held. After the singing of "El Male Rachamim", Mr. Dawid Werdinger took the floor and spoke of the merits of our late leader; then Mr. Aleksander Turger read out the resolutions against the English government. The memorial closed with the singing of "Techezakna" and "Hatikvah".
P—A—Z.
From Sporting Life.

[Sport — Zagłębie.] „Hakoach“ [Będzin] — „Zagłębie“ 4:3 (1:3) [i.e. Hakoach lost 3:4, after leading 3:1 at half-time].
For a long time sports fans have not had the occasion [to see] a team leading 3:1 in goals let itself be beaten in the way that happened last Sunday. True, the Będzin side had 3 substitute players, but the 3:1 result should have been held. The defeat is owed to the players who, instead of behaving calmly and playing composedly, waste their energy on... squabbling [?]. That is the reason for the lost match.
In the 7th minute Jankielewicz 1 breaks through alone and shoots the first goal. Zagłębie gets to work and wins a corner, from which it scores the equaliser. (Goalkeeper Bechman is to blame for that goal.) „Hakoach“ scores again: Gutman turns a free kick from some 25 metres, with a splendid shot, into the second hit. In the 41st minute Siwek 1 shoots the third and last goal for „Hakoach“ from a corner.
After the break the visitors play with the wind [?]; the Będzin players commit the above-mentioned error and quarrel constantly — the record is beaten by Gutman and Siwek 2. Self-evidently, with such disharmony in the team „Zagłębie“ manages not only to equalise but also to win...
The best on the pitch: the brothers Jankielewicz and the phenomenal Rezen 1. Of the visitors the following distinguished themselves: the defence Łukaszewicz, Szczerbiński.
The referee, Mr. Mazur, did not watch for „fouls“.
„Maccabi“ — „Shvim“ [?] 0:4 (0:2) [i.e. 4:0 to Maccabi, 2:0 at half-time].
At last „Maccabi“ managed to have a bit more luck, and that against the stable opponent „Shvim“. The match was of great importance to both teams, and the Sosnowiec „Maccabi“, with this victory, remained in Class A.
Already the first minutes show that the struggle will be a bitter one. The 15th minute brings the first goal for „Maccabi“, shot by Frachtzweig [?]. 5 minutes later Garitan [?] goes through alone, the „Shvim“ defence commits a „foul“, and Stirm [?] converts the awarded „Elfer“ [penalty] into a goal; „Maccabi“ leads 2:0.
After the change of ends „Maccabi“ is still in front and through Piekarski scores the third goal. The game becomes less interesting owing to the great superiority of the Jewish team. The 30th minute again brings a goal by Frachtzweig [?], this time the last. From „Maccabi“ the half-back line distinguished itself: Stirm [?], Swin [?] and Gulanska [?]. From „Shvim“: the left wing Lewandowski, the centre-half.
Referee Mr. Mazur good.
„Sarmacja“ — „Sosnowiec“ 0:1 (0:1) [i.e. 1:0 to Sarmacja].
„Sarmacja“ unexpectedly beat „Sosnowiec“, which came out with six substitute players... The only goal was shot by the right wing Puszecki [?] with the help of the „Sosnowiec“ goalkeeper. The best on the pitch was Balek [?] Cichon [?]. Referee Kazibucki good.
C.K.S. — „Victoria“ 1:2 (1:2) [i.e. 2:1 to C.K.S.].
The greatest sensation for football fans was brought by the result of the championship match between the above-mentioned teams [drużyny]. „Victoria“ was superior the whole time, and only thanks to the extraordinary defence did C.K.S. win the match. The goals were shot by: Przybyłek and the inside-right for C.K.S.; Zygmański for „Victoria“. Referee Śliwa.
„Arie“ — „Rozwój“ 0:3 (0:2) [i.e. 3:0 to Arie].
This match the Jewish team won deservedly after a splendid game in all lines. Especially distinguished were Weisberg, Mator [?] and Apelbaum; referee Bicki [?] very good.
„Shtern“ (Sosnowiec) — „Kinneret“ 0:1 (0:1) [i.e. 1:0 to Shtern].
The only goal for „Shtern“ was shot by Włodzimierski. Referee Śliwa weak.
C.K.S. (Częstochowa) — „Ruch“ 1:1
Because of the bad ground the match was not interesting.
Police — „Zagłębianka“ 0:0.
The match between the 2 contenders for the championship title of Class „B“ ended in a draw. In the first half the policemen had more of the game, but without success. After the break the „Zagłębianka“ players press hard, but cannot overcome the phenomenal play of the police goalkeeper Sulaush [?]; referee Grabiński very good.
Mandek L.

„Shimshon“ (Modrzejów [?]) — „Sator“ [?] (Wojkowice).
„Shimshon“ goes from one victory to the next and is assured [?] of taking the championship in Class „C“. Up to half-time it is 1:0 for „Shimshon“. Which artisan is exempt from a trade patent and from turnover tax?

In the letter-box of „Moment“ no. 153 of 20 July this year, edited by Adv. M. Surik, we read the following answer to a reader in Bodzentyn:
„Previously[?] the tax offices [went by?] the verdict of the Supreme Court; now, however, the matter has been settled, because the Ministry of Finance has issued a special circular (okólnik) 1342/4/30 V. D. L., according to which artisans who employ one worker are free both of patents and of turnover tax. If your turnover tax has been assessed unlawfully, you must file an appeal“.
So that the artisans concerned should not be misled on reading the answer quoted above, I consider it right to give a few clarifications here, because the Ministry of Finance circular on which Advocate Surik relies is addressed[?] to an entirely different matter and has nothing whatsoever to do with exemption from the patent or from turnover tax.
The said circular V. D. L. 1342/4/30 was issued thanks to the efforts of the representatives of the Central Jewish Artisans' Union in Poland and concerns the turnover from retail or single sale of foodstuffs of prime necessity (bakers and sausage-makers are specifically counted[?] here), sold from the same place where the workshops are located or from a second outlet that serves the artisan enterprise in question and belongs to the same owner — these will pay, instead of 2 per cent as until now, only[?] 1 per cent turnover tax.
On the other hand there is indeed a second circular, issued by the Ministry of Finance on 6 May this year, no. L. D. V. 5237/4/30, according to which all artisan workshops run by the owner with the help of one worker or one family member (of whom art. 8 par. 5 of the Industrial Law speaks) are by law exempt from buying patents and paying turnover tax.
If the tax office has assessed someone's turnover tax unlawfully, one must refer in the appeal to the said circular.
Incidentally, as far as we know, the „offices“[?] [—] no longer issue 8th-category patents if only 1 assistant is stated in the declaration.
———
In the same letter-box we read a second answer, which likewise does not agree with reality and the law[?]:
„To the reader in Gajstat[?]:
If you hold a „karta rzemieślnicza“ [artisan's card], you need not take any examination“.
In our previous articles we have already shown in detail that the „karta rzemieślnicza“ does not yet entitle the artisan to employ apprentices, and in order to possess this right as well as the title of master, a special examination must be passed[?] before the commission appointed[?] by the Chamber of Crafts.
Paragraph 2, point 3 of the examination regulations published by the Chambers of Crafts states explicitly that (among other formalities) the „karta rzemieślnicza“ must be attached to the examination application.
I wish to believe that the points indicated will be corrected by Advocate Surik in the near future.
A. Gancwajch.
General Meeting of the Zionist Organisation in Strzemieszyce / Jewish Protest Meeting in Karlsbad / The Unemployed Demand Work or Bread / Mass Arrests in Zagłębie / Car Runs Over a Boy / A Fire

[Strzemieszyce — Zionism; followed by five short news items: Karlsbad, Będzin and Zagłębie.]
On Sunday the general meeting of the Zionist Organisation was held in its own premises; also taking part was the special delegate of the Central Committee, Menachem Lipszyc.
The meeting is opened by the chairman, Mr. Gliksztajn, who greets the representative of the C. C. and proposes [?] the distinguished guest as presiding officer, to which everyone agrees.
Before proceeding to the agenda, Mr. Lipszyc devotes a few warm words to the recently deceased Zionist leader R' Abraham Podliszewski of blessed memory, whose memory is honoured by rising.
Then the distinguished guest delivers a 2-hour lecture rich in content, in which he unfolds in a masterly form the development of the Zionist Organisation up to now and its prospects for the future.
A report on the activity of the Keren Kayemeth is given by Mr. D. Rechnic [?], from which it can be seen that up to today 170 zł above the quota (contingent) have been collected in Strzemieszyce.
A committee (va'ad) and an auditing committee are elected, and with the singing of "Hatikvah" the meeting is closed.
—o—
Jewish Protest Meeting in Karlsbad
On Sunday, 27 July, a protest meeting against the aliyah decree was held in the great hall of the Kurhaus in Karlsbad. At the meeting, which was called by the local Zionist Organisation, speeches were made by Rabbi Dr. Ziegler, Senator Niemirower [?] and Deputy Yitzhak Gruenbaum, who gave a lecture rich in content (in Yiddish) on English policy. Deputy Gruenbaum related that Balfour had once been the initiator of restricting Jewish immigration to England...
—o—
The Unemployed Demand Work or Bread
A crowd of several hundred people gathered in front of the local magistrate's office and demanded work or bread.
President Wilner [?] calmed the crowd, promising that a building programme would soon be started in which about 300 workers would be employed.
With this promise the crowd calmed down.
—o—
Mass Arrests in Zagłębie
In connection with the Communist preparations for the 1st of this month, a large number of young people suspected of Communist activity were arrested in Będzin and its surroundings during the night of Wednesday.
—o—
Car Runs Over a Boy
On Wednesday evening in Gzichów the 12-year-old boy Fleischhacker was run over by a car. The same car took the boy to the hospital.

On Tuesday at 1 o'clock in the afternoon a fire broke out from an unknown cause in Grabocin, in which two houses burned down.

Academic Emigration Bureau

[Polish Jewry — students abroad.] The Central Executive Committee of the Union of Associations of Jewish Students from Poland studying abroad informs those who are going to study abroad that it is breaking off relations with the Bureau of Petitions and Translations in Warsaw, because of the recent complaints reaching the Central Secretariat from academics. Letters to the Editor

I.
Dear Mr. Editor!
On the basis of the note in your newspaper No. 29 of the 18th of this month under the heading “Right Poale Zion expelled from the Keren Kayemet committee”, we ask you to print the following correction [?] in the next issue of your esteemed newspaper:
1) It is not true that on Monday the 14th of this month a consultation of all Zionist groupings took place in the premises of the Zionist Organisation in order to arrange the 20th of Tammuz campaign in our town, at which our representative was supposed to have declared that we on principle take no part in the 20th of Tammuz campaign and that we had come to disrupt the event. The truth is that the consultation about the 20th of Tammuz event took place 8 days earlier, i.e. on the 7th of this month, where the programme of the whole campaign was laid down and confirmed, and where our representative declared that we on principle take no part in the 20th of Tammuz event, but disrupting the campaign was not considered at all.
2) It is also true that at the consultation held on Monday the 14th of this month, which your esteemed newspaper cites, representatives of childish organisations wanted to overturn the plan of the 20th of Tammuz campaign confirmed 8 days earlier, without making use [?] of the democratic principles of revising and annulling previously adopted resolutions, but wanted to push through their new plans, which contradict the earlier adopted resolutions, by back-door methods. Our representative could not agree to such conduct, for which his right to vote was taken from him in an unheard-of and impermissible manner.
Our representative, seeing the demagogic conduct of the childish organisations, then declared that we are not responsible for such acts and therefore we temporarily withdraw from the K.K.L. committee until the matter takes on a serious character, and that we want to disrupt every kind of campaign that is carried out in a demagogic, brutal manner.
Mr. N. [?] Landner with his whole retinue, wishing to wriggle out of the situation that had arisen, after our declaration that we were leaving the Keren Kayemet committee — submitted a proposal to expel us only with the consent of the Central Committee
At the same time a new note appeared in your esteemed newspaper No. 30 under the heading “From the Keren Kayemet Le-Israel in Będzin”, in which it is asserted that we demanded a denial of the first note in No. 29 about our expulsion. We state that on Tuesday, which your esteemed newspaper cites, it was decided in connection with the note in No. 29 to issue a correction that the Keren Kayemet committee has nothing whatsoever to do with it; however, the irresponsible manipulations of the childish organisations who want to play at politics brought it about that the correction appeared as an announcement of the Zionist Organisation and not of the K.K.L.
We can only reject such childish games with contempt.
We state once more that we will not re-enter the Będzin K.K.L. committee until the arrival of a C.C. representative of the Head Directorate, who will clean up the committee and restore it normally to its proper height, on which it must stand in order to raise those great means for the building of Eretz Israel.
We hope that the honoured Mr. Editor will fulfil our request.
We sign
Respectfully,
Jewish Socialist Workers' Party Poale Zion (united with Ts. S.) in Będzin.

What's Heard in the Summer Resorts?

(A letter from Milówka).
A Jewish Cemetery Desecrated.
The local residents as well as the visitors who have come here [?] are very much dejected by the disgraceful deeds of some hooligans at the local cemetery. Already for the second time this year unpunished hooligans have been breaking gravestones in the Jewish cemetery. The police are conducting an investigation, so far without success.
Dacha Life.
The little town of Milówka, which lies a few kilometres from Rajcza, was "discovered" as a summer resort only a few years ago, and it is one of the most beautiful areas in Poland, where in summer one can find a corner to rest after a hard year of work. This summer too — as every year — a large number of guests have gathered here, most of them from Sosnowiec, Będzin, etc. Food is not expensive here, so almost everyone who has come here for the summer has settled into private lodgings. The only Jewish boarding house (Goldberg's) is about to close, because there are simply no takers for going into a boarding house.
A Herzl Memorial.
Thanks to some Zionists headed by Mr. Y. Ziskind (Sosnowiec), a Herzl memorial was held on Saturday in the local synagogue; Mr. Zeifter [?] recited El Male Rachamim and Mr. Ziskind spoke on current affairs. It is worth noting that only after a struggle of many years did the local rabbi finally permit a memorial in honour of Dr. Herzl to be held in the synagogue.
People Chatter...
It would perhaps not have been [?] in order with my conscience if I did not mention in my report the lovers of the "ace [?] of acorns" with the "red queen". Having, it seems, no better business, the crowd of summer guests "works" very hard at "żydek" [a card game] from dawn until late at night, calling a "Durchmarsch" and a "Bettel" [card-game terms] up to the "Eternal Jew", in which, at quite a small stake, one can lose as much as it costs to keep a person in a boarding house for a week.. Indeed, people talk a great deal here about a family scandal that took place here. Wags even say that it had already come close to a divorce (get), and all because of the "red queen"...
Shakh.

We Must React.

[Upper Silesia — antisemitism; opinion article.]
(Upper Silesian false patriotism. — And what are we doing about it?)
Only recently a fact was noted here in our paper showing in what manner the Upper Silesian chauvinists practise antisemitism in Upper Silesia.
When there is a Christian who sets up a chocolate factory, and the long-established Jewish factories do not liquidate themselves before him and do not hand their customers over to him — he then goes out into the street, frankly and freely, with the slogan „Hura na Żyda“ [„Hurrah, at the Jew!“]; that is to say: Jews are going to exist among me? Jews are going to be a bone in my throat? I'll fix them all right, I'll show them who and what they are — and indeed he stops at nothing, one takes nothing and no one into account, and one writes quite openly:
„We declare war on the Jews and we ask you, honoured gentlemen, for support, in order to destroy Jewry, which is spreading more and more in Upper Silesia, and like leeches [?] they will suck [?] the Christians dry.
In connection with this we offer our products to the following firms; (here follows a list of the firms).“
Do you understand the danger of the Jewish expansion? Do you understand why nothing more and nothing less than a formal war on the Jews is being declared?
And further the firm addresses the consumer with nothing more and nothing less than the following pearls of speech:
„Therefore we turn to you once more, honoured gentlemen, with the request to support us in the struggle against Jewish shoddy goods; their wares are produced in unhygienic premises, in the cellars of unclean Żydzi [pejorative], who have before them as their symbol [?] — to destroy Christendom.
If you, honoured gentlemen, again bring in the Jewish filth (paskudztwo), with which one could poison rats (szczury), you will then lose many customers, and they will no longer have confidence in you.
We are sure that you will protect your business and refuse to buy Jewish products.“
This announcement is signed by the owner of the firm.
How many times do we have the opportunity to observe various negotiations and conferences with our Christian neighbours, both in private social affairs and in matters of the authorities, and then we remain satisfied very, very often, seeing the tolerance that is shown us. We feel then that we are in a cultured country and live with European people in the full sense of the word. And it is precisely this that impresses us; we see then that there is a wish to understand us, and we indeed try to adapt ourselves to the conditions. We give towards everything a cultured state needs to have, whether we can or not; we account to ourselves at this moment that we must bear all the burdens that are necessary for a great government.
And when we come to compare these peaceful relations with the above-mentioned antisemitic slogans, which an individual wants to exploit for himself, for his own use — one can then by no means understand how on the one side such harmony can reign, and on the other side so much chauvinism, so much poison and hatred, which is all in all aimed at nothing but making a fortune on someone else's ruins — and this is permitted in modern Katowice and in industrial Upper Silesia, where the law serves everyone to use his abilities in a cultured way.
By every means, and because of the merest trifle and egoistic self-interest, people want to sow hate and enmity and to underline the distance from Jew to Christian, from human being to citizen, from chauvinist to patriot. It goes without saying that such poisonous conduct is impermissible. We therefore must not pass indifferently by such incitements, by the fact that such people want to make us loathsome in the eyes of our neighbours in such a disgusting way.
It goes without saying that the authorities must intervene and not allow pitch and brimstone to be poured from one nationality upon the other; and if they do not do so, if they do not see it or pretend not to see it, then we must see it and draw the attention of the proper authorities. We are, after all, citizens of Poland, who have the right to defend themselves. We do, after all, bear all the burdens in the country on our shoulders together with all other citizens — if not more, certainly not less — and this is exactly what gives us the right and the courage not to allow everyone to make ashes and mud of the Jewish people.
We must react properly to every antisemitic attack and demand punishment for unjustified incitement.
The Jews of Upper Silesia and the Jewish kehilla of Katowice must establish order in this field among themselves, so that all antisemitic „little flowers“ are recorded and given expression.
Apathy and indifference must not be allowed to reign here, because in that case the dangerous microbe will penetrate [?] the people more and more as time goes on; and the Upper Silesian worker, at whom the bullets are aimed, is still naive enough, and one can easily talk him into anything in the world.
We see that the people, that the Upper Silesian population, is not antisemitic at all; on the contrary, they are tolerant, and the relations between them and us have convinced them that one can trade and live and do business with Jews, so that they have drawn closer to the Jewish merchant, to the Jewish citizen, whom they treat as conscious [?] people equal to all others. They have at long last become convinced that among their own brethren there are chauvinists who are ready to break patriotism as soon as their own pocket is concerned. Formerly, when they were told that the Jew is a different creature, a kind of beast, they believed it; they were too naive not to believe their own brethren. But those times are long past, and they too have had the opportunity to convince themselves of the lies, so that now the chauvinists find it hard to sow the antisemitic little flowers; and precisely for this reason we must stand on guard, protect our interests, and not allow others to make us loathsome in the eyes of our neighbours.
Jewish Upper Silesia must react to every phenomenon unfavourable to it, to every groundless antisemitic incitement that can harm our economic and national interests. We must consciously and with level-headedness try to repel all the bullets aimed at our address, which are only meant to incite and to sow hate and enmity among the peaceful citizens with whom we live in normal relations.
Y. S.

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion (Devarim)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings and remarks on today's portion.
Collected and adapted by Y. L.
Parashat Devarim
—o—
a) "And Hazeroth" (Deut. 1:1).
Rashi explains the word "va-Hatzerot" ("and Hazeroth", literally "and courtyards") as referring to Korah's dispute. This seems incomprehensible: how does the word "va-Hatzerot" allude to a dispute?
On Friday, before the Sabbath, people would make an eruv hatzerot — that is, they collected a piece of challah from every courtyard and placed it in one courtyard. In this way the boundaries between the various courtyards disappeared and everything was turned into one courtyard (therefore one was permitted to carry there on the Sabbath, since there were no separate domains). But when there are "courtyards" — when the courtyards are not united, but each courtyard "makes its own Sabbath", when there is a profusion of courtyards quarrelling with one another — that symbolises Korah's dispute, and for that Moses rebuked them.
[From] Chiddushei ha-Rim.
—o—
b) "And Di-zahab" (ibid.).
Thus Moses said before God: Master of the Universe! Because of the gold and silver that You gave the Jews in such abundance, that they even said "dai" (enough) — this very wealth led them to make the Calf. When things are too good..
Tractate Berakhot 32.
* * *
Rabbi Israel Salanter was once in Frankfurt, in the house of the pious Baron Rothschild. He observed how the Baron's whole house was run in perfect holiness, according to the strictest stringencies, and he said to the Baron:
— As I see it, you do not conduct yourself according to the Torah.
The Baron was beside himself: What! Someone dares to say that he does not conduct himself according to the Torah?! But Rabbi Israel immediately smiled:
— I mean this, Baron. The Torah says "But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked": when a Jew receives gold and silver he becomes [unclear word, "bebrikt"?], throws off his Jewishness and makes himself a golden calf. With you it is different: you are blessed with such wealth, and yet you conduct yourself with strict piety — is that not the reverse of what is written in the Torah?..
—o—
c) "After he had slain Sihon" (Deut. 1:4).
Moses began to rebuke the Jews only "after he had slain Sihon", after he had shown his expertise in the tactics of war, after he had managed to win such a victory over the Amorite king. For had he rebuked the Jews earlier, they would have said: he is indeed a great saint, Moses, but also an idler, ignorant of worldly matters — that is why he preaches morals. Only when he had shown that he could wage war against Sihon, and had distinguished himself not only as an ascetic but also as a warrior, did he feel entitled to preach morals.
Measef Drushei.
—o—
d) "Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this Torah" (Deut. 1:5).
Rashi says on this that it means he translated the Torah into seventy languages.
Language is the life-force of every people. Hebrew is the soul of the Jews, and therefore there are in the Torah individual foreign-language expressions (e.g. "Yegar Sahadutha", "totafot"), because God knew that the Jews would be driven out among the nations; therefore the foreign languages were taken into the Torah, so that the Jews would have a hold on the life-force of the nations.
But only in the land of Moab — in exile the Torah may be studied in a foreign language, but in the Land of Israel only Hebrew reigns.
Kedushat Levi.
—o—
e) "[May the Lord] make you a thousand times so many more as ye are" (Deut. 1:11).
According to Rashi, Moses' words are interpreted thus: "This is mine" — up to here it was my blessing, but may God multiply you a thousandfold.
Twice God wanted to destroy[?] the Jews and to begin creating another people from Moses: so it was at the sin of the Calf and at the spies, but Moses rejected it. Yet it is said that God's blessing is fulfilled even when it was actually spoken only as a condition. It is also said that the measure of good is five hundred times greater than the measure of punishment. It follows that Moses is owed a generation a thousand times larger than all the Jews (for on both occasions he was promised a generation five hundredfold, since "the measure of good exceeds the measure of punishment five hundred times") — that is the meaning of Moses' words: "This is mine" — the blessing of "a thousand times so many" is the one due to me. V-r"l [probably "v-d"l", i.e. enough said to the wise].
Panim Yafot.
—o—
f) "Take you wise men .. and I will make them heads over you" (Deut. 1:13).
Thus Moses said to the Jews: if you do not listen to me and go astray on bad ways, it is not your fault, but "va-asimem (asham — guilt) be-rasheichem": the guilt is on your heads. If the people sins, the leaders are guilty. Like that snake whose tail argued with its head: why should you, head, always go in front, and I, poor tail, behind? Let us change places for once — I want to go in front. So the head agrees, the tail goes in front and the head behind. But the tail has no eyes, so it goes along blindly: now it falls into water, now it pricks itself. So it is when the head goes behind and the tail in front.
Devarim Rabbah 1:8.
—o—
g) "And judge righteously" (Deut. 1:16).
A judge in a small town who was known as a taker of bribes became deaf in the course of time. The town wondered: he should have gone blind, for "a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise" — how come he went deaf of all things?!
A scholar of the town explained it thus:
— You know our town. They did indeed promise our judge to hand over[?] a bribe, and on credit he "judged righteously" [i.e. in their favour], but what they gave him was a fig [i.e. nothing] — you know our town. So it turns out that of the bribe only his ears heard what he had been promised, but before his eyes he saw a fig; therefore he was punished in his ears and not in his eyes.
—o—
Avot, chapter three.
"And anyone whose wisdom exceeds his deeds, his wisdom will not endure."
There are such fools who persuade themselves that if they themselves study and are scholars, they are already exempt from giving charity, from helping anyone. But such Torah has no permanence; the Zohar calls such a learned rich man a villain.
Avodat Yisrael.
The Old and the New Lament

Remarks for Shabbat Chazon. By Ben Amotz.
...And once again we leaf through the yellowed pages of the Scroll of Lamentations, we sit bent over and in the Eicha melody we say:
— "All her people sigh, they seek bread."
The whole Jewish people toils and groans, toils to earn a piece of bread and cannot find it. All their property "they" have already taken away, sucked out like leeches the last drop of blood; "I am not able to rise up" — it is already impossible to straighten one's back, credit has been stopped. The camp of "birds of prey"[?] grows from day to day
— "All her people sigh.."
———
History repeats itself. Today too the Bar Kamtza types are at the helm; they have a say, they push everywhere toward power, and when they meet any resistance whatsoever, they do the same as that Bar Kamtza who was immortalized by his informing.
— "The Jews have rebelled against you," the Jews are refractory, the Jews swindle[?], the Jews rebel against the government..
Yes, we meet the Bar Kamtzas at every step, not only in the various government offices [urzędy][?], where, in order to save[?] their own deeds, they tell everything: they tell about those "who do not want to pay any taxes [podatki]", those who travel to the spas, and in which Jewish schools national pride is instilled in the Jewish children...
— "The Jews have rebelled against you",
———
And when tonight, at the close of the Sabbath, we sit down over the old dirge and lament the national catastrophe that befell us 2 thousand years ago, we must also bear in mind them — the modern Bar Kamtzas, those who disgrace Jewish honour and those who commit various deeds while rolling their eyes up to heaven, in order to deceive those who do not understand and do not know that there were once, and there are today too, Bar Kamtzas who are out for their own interests, and when that does not succeed for them, there is always the device:
— "The Jews have rebelled against you"...
———
And they tell:
1) That a Będzin dozór [member of the kehilla board] was assessed 450 zł. of kehilla tax. So he turned with a complaint to the starosta [district head], to whom he at the same time informed that:
"In the Jewish kehilla deceitful things are done, kehilla money is squandered on severance pay for officials and cantors, the management is lamentable, they engage in politics, etc."...
———
2) A second dozór, also from the same town, "one engaged in communal needs", had hired masons for the mikveh construction. Once he found out that the same work was being carried out by workers from Upper Silesia, so he, the public worker, went off to the labour inspector and reported to him:
— "The Jews have rebelled against you": the Jewish gmina [community] employs German workers, and this happens — he says — at a time when such unemployment reigns here.
And when Hadrianus, I mean the labour inspector, heard this, he could not keep silent and pounced on the Jewish kehilla: how can this be? Such a rebellion!.. Only when several "Roman", I mean Polish, workers got employment at the mikveh did the inspector calm down, and also
— Bar Kamtza triumphed..
———
3) The sages of the well-known "Israel Bank" sat and decided that 5 thousand gulden [złoty] should be set aside from the profit and that the sum should be distributed to Jewish cheders.
And the sum was indeed distributed — but only to certain little shops, to the cheders and schools that are under the influence of the "holy Agudah"... Only so that the "neutrals" should also be satisfied, they also threw a little bone to the hungry[?] poor children who study in the "Talmud Torah"
— 4800 zł. for the Agudah people and all of 200 zł. for the Talmud Torah...
4) And the prophet laments:
"All her friends" — the so-called good friends, those who speak in the name of the Torah and of Jewishness — "have dealt treacherously with her"; they have rebelled, they withdraw their support, they disgrace her name, they scheme so that the present committee of the Talmud Torah should fall — "they have become her enemies". They, the "Torah-loyal", have become real enemies, they rejoice at every failure the Talmud Torah has — "they have become her enemies"...
———
The Torah reader has just finished the Scroll of Lamentations. Sad Jews, in a Tisha b'Av mood, slowly leave the study houses, and from their hearts deep sighs break out over the destruction of long ago, and still more over today's troubles and pain
— the old and the new lament..
The Jewish Tragedy

"Weep for those who wept." Byron, Hebrew Melodies.
No single people in the world is so rich in tears and in laments, nor weeps and wails so much, as the Jewish people, with whose bloody tears the whole of Jewish history is so soaked and drenched.
There has not yet passed a single world event, a single historical epoch, in which Jews did not suffer terribly, bleed cruelly and shed tears without measure.
On every occasion, whatever it may have been, and in almost every country where Jews lived, they were — and remain to this day — candidates for torments and troubles, for suffering and pain, for persecutions and evil decrees, etc.
There is hardly a single day in the Jewish calendar which does not have bloody events to record — massacres, persecutions, blood libels, expulsions and the like — as though bitter fate had condemned the Jewish people never to cease suffering and enduring, to have to bathe forever in its own blood and tears.
When one leafs through the history of the Jewish people on its long march of exile, the great tragedy reveals itself, a tragedy without end, which the Jewish people has had to live through in all ages: in the times of the Roman tyrants (150—117), of the first Christian rulers of Rome (312—361), of the "statutes"[?] of the Catholic Church, of the men of power[?], of the "Crusaders" (1096—1306), of all manner of blood libels, of the English Richards, the French Philips, of the Spanish and Portuguese "autos-da-fé", of the expulsion from Spain, Sicily, Sardinia and Portugal (87—1492), of the Belgian Brabanters, of the "decrees of the Roytsim"[?], the decrees of 1648–49, of the Reformation, etc.
The Moselle, the Rhine, the Main and dozens of other rivers — seas were filled with Jewish blood; and no less than those rivers, the Bug, the Styr, the Narew[?] also drank their fill of innocent Jewish blood — all the rivers from the Baltic Sea to the Black Sea, which was shed by Chmielnicki's Cossacks, Kushibaga's[?] Tatars, Gonta's Haidamaks, Zhelezniak's robber bands (1648—58); which then also found a bloody echo in the Polish valleys — Czarniecki's confederates became their spiritual heirs...
And already at the end of the 19th century those massacres, pogroms and persecutions repeat themselves in dark[?] Romania, in Tsarist Russia, in clerical Galicia, etc., reaching, at the beginning of the enlightened 20th century (1905—7) and in the time of the unfortunate World War, their highest degree in Ukraine, Podolia, Volhynia, etc. (1914—21).
The Tsarist fighters[?], the Ukrainian "liberators", the red Petliurists, the black Denikinists, the white "Makhnovists" and hundreds of other peasant atamans bought their "freedom" with rivers of Jewish blood, and in rivers of Jewish blood drowned whole Jewish towns, whole communities, whole families, etc.
And when we again prepare for the "kinot" (dirges), we must also remember our heroes who heroically looked bitter death in the eye, who went voluntarily to the autos-da-fé, to the gallows, and sacrificed themselves for Jewish honour — of whom Yosef Urfali is not the last.
The last act of the Jewish "tragedy" has not, on the whole, yet been played out.
Moshe Feinkind.
