Why Did I Send My Wife to a Dacha This Year?

[Humour — satire; trade and debts.] (Monologue of a Jewish merchant who owns his own — a wife at a dacha).
As you know, I am a Jew who still has a "fat finger"... and perhaps also a nice signature, so that "financially" I can still afford to send my wife and children to a dacha with ease. Nevertheless I am in principle against all these "letniska" [summer resorts] and summer lodgings — why keep a double book-keeping for nothing, first fatten up and then waste away; what for such complicated stomach-work?..
You see, if one could send today's businesses off to the fresh air to relax [?] a little and cure their weakness, that would be something else; but where do you have the doctor who would make a remedy for this "cancer"? Until "Ne'ilah" I knock on all doors to scrape together the few groszy to redeem my bills of exchange and "rak" [—] [?], so how then can I allow myself, for no reason at all, to go and sit in the field and the forest and bask [?] there like a lazybones [?]?..
This year too I did not even dream of a dacha for my wife; but since it was destined from Heaven that my Yente should rock there in a hammock and I should, may it not befall you, remain a "straw widower", it came to me quite unexpectedly, and you may hear how:
By trade I am an "empty-goer" and a "street-measurer" [an idler], and the end of all of those is, after all, to be merchants — so I too became a dry-goods merchant; thus I have, saving your presence [?], provided myself with shrouds..
As you know from the trade, it has been the custom since ancient times that I take goods on credit and pass them on to the customer just like that; I owe the one, and the other owes me. So naturally, when the other does not pay me, I do the same and do not pay further — for how could it be otherwise?
This winter all my debtors, as if out of spite, agreed among themselves not to pay my bills — and — stop — there is simply no remedy against bad "horses"..
The only "radical" advice is, as our grammarian [?] says: as one sings in, so one sings out — and so it was: I do not ponder long, send all my bills to all the winds, even to where the black pepper grows, and go off to prepare for "Unetaneh Tokef"...
Of course the "groszy-men" [?] do not keep quiet — they grab the bundles of protested "rags" and burst in on me, so agitated, banging on the table and shouting "gevalt": what's this, is that justice, that you'll guzzle and booze at the price of our toil [?], of our blood?, what do you think, that it's a lawless world? You'll grab and borrow [?] from the whole world and they'll keep quiet for you? You won't! — If you don't have, you don't give any [bills?]... Sell the cupboard, pawn the bedding and pillows, and pay! What are you grabbing?! Murderers, killers! You've made us miserable!
But I am already used to such things and listen to them like Jaszka the deaf; let them bang on the table as much as they like — I stand like a cold angel and answer them quite calmly, looking meanwhile at the wall or at the ceiling: what are you raging like that for, Jews, eh? Be so kind as to speak a little more quietly, this is no market or tavern.. Just look how they've boiled over — people owe me perhaps a little more, and I make no such scandals... When I have it — I'll pay you; meanwhile I don't. What's the matter, over time you've flayed the skin off me and made me poor; you don't want to wait? — Don't wait, do what you can. Stop making scandals in my home at once, I beg you, do you hear or not? If you don't stop shouting, I'll call.., and they'll lead you into... that'll be a wedding...
That's how I tell them off properly and shut their mouths; but what is one to do with my Yente, who is not at all used to such a "craft": they bang on the table and she squeals or crows like a rooster, screams and falls right down on the ground and faints... the children burst into tears around her and the heavens open.
Therefore this year I postponed this "bit of work" to the month of Tammuz — I first sent my Yente away to a dacha, and now, staying alone, I'll be able to show the exploiters what dunning others means [?].
Only this: my wife is very surprised that I suddenly sent her off to a dacha and suspects me of meaning, meanwhile, to have a fling [?] with some.. and who knows what cats' concert she will yet play for me; were it not for that, I'd be very pleased that my so-and-so is now sitting in Bystra like a lady.
Now you know why people go to dachas: it is not for pleasure — one simply flees from the creditors..
R' Eliyahu.
What's new in Zagłębie? — Będzin: the Będzin kehilla goes 'Forward'... Cantor question decided by lot

What's new in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 7 Av 5690 — Piątek 1 sierpnia 1930.)
Będzin
The Będzin kehilla goes "Forward" ["Forverts"]...
Cantor question decided by lot.
On Tuesday evening the kehilla board held a meeting at which the question of the cantorate in our town was discussed.
After a lengthy discussion a resolution was adopted to act as our great-grandfathers did, namely that the matter should be settled by drawing lots.
The lot — "Zhupanitsh [Żupanicz?] or not" — was set for yesterday[?] evening.
At the meeting Mr. Goldsztajn announced that the town engineer, Mr. Vigter[?], had agreed to complete the construction of the mikveh without any fee.
'Hakoach' excursion to Złoty Potok.

'Hakoach' excursion to Złoty Potok.
On Sunday the 10th of this month the gymnastics association "Hakoach" is organising an excursion to Zherik [Żarki?] and Złoty Potok. All groups will take part in the excursion, led by the association's own orchestra.
Those who wish to take part must register no later than the 7th of this month.
—o—
The second batch of schoolchildren leaves today for the summer holidays
Today the second batch of schoolchildren is being sent to the summer colony "Zagłębianka" in Sławków.
This time only boys are going, numbering about 300.
A swindle on the bus running Kraków–Będzin

On the bus that runs Kraków–Będzin a woman was travelling to Będzin. The woman had come from France to visit her family.
On the same bus there was also travelling an unknown Christian, who got off at Mysłowice. Unnoticed by anyone, he took the Frenchwoman's suitcase and left.
Arriving in Będzin, the woman only then discovered that her suitcase with clothes and other valuables had been taken.
The police drew up a report and an investigation is under way.
To the address of 'Hashomer Hatahor'.

We have received from the local branch (ken) of "Hashomer Hatahor" an invitation to take part in the festive opening of a summer colony.
The date of the celebration, however — as we see from the invitation — has been set for Sunday, Tisha B'Av..
— Hear, hear! But that such an organisation as "Hashomer Hatahor" should arrange festivities on the day of our national destruction — that is truly a very great wrong..
From the Zionist-Revisionist Union

Last Sabbath, before a large number of members and sympathisers, the latest articles by Jabotinsky on Zionist questions were discussed.
The discussion aroused great interest, and a fairly large number of those present took part in it.
— — —
This Sabbath afternoon a discussion meeting will be held devoted to the recent conference of the Radical Zionists in Lwów (Lemberg).
The 'revenge' of the lovers of bitter drops.

Mr. Weinstein of Sączewska[?] Street, who had a yahrzeit, came to pray at the "German synagogue". The minyan of the synagogue, however, did not want to "go along"[?] and set the yahrzeit-observer the following ultimatum:
— "Hand over some brandy and we'll pray with you"...
And when the yahrzeit-observer would not meet the demand, the brandy-drinkers left the synagogue and went away.
The kehilla board visits Jewish children at the summer colony in Sławków.

On Sunday 5 members of the kehilla board paid a visit to Sławków, where they visited the summer colony "Zagłębianka", in which there were 260 Jewish girls.
In honour of the guests the children performed a series of entertainment numbers.
Afterwards they received sweets from the kehilla representatives.
A great fire in Małobądz.

On Saturday night the town was alarmed by the great fire that broke out in Małobądz.
Several barns were burnt down, [?] of the fodder factory "Patakol".
Posing as a merchant from Zagłębie, he pulled off a swindle of half a million zł.

[Łódź and Piotrków — fraud.] A certain Lejzer Barchański [?], who once lived in Łódź, moved some years ago to Piotrków [printed "Pietrikov"] and set himself up there with a small shop. Barchański had put by a nice bundle, and some time ago he travelled back to Łódź, where he presented himself as a big wholesale merchant doing business with Będzin, Sosnowiec and Upper Silesia, and bargained to buy a consignment of socks for 300 thousand zł. The manufacturer saw the light before his eyes: such a transaction in bad times is a very big thing; the trouble, however, is that the other man wants to get the goods on credit. But a way was found for that too: the firm sent its procurist [authorised signatory] to Piotrków to inquire whether Barchański was really such a big merchant, whether he was solid and whether one could trust him with such a bundle. The procurist came back and said that one could: Barchański had a very big business, big connections, was "sound" as iron, and one could do the deal with him. Having heard such information, the firm gave Barchański the goods, and he signed bills of exchange for 300 thousand zł.
A few months passed, the payment date arrived, and all the bills came back one by one with protests. Only then did the firm learn that it had fallen victim to a fine swindler, who had drawn even its own procurist into his net.
At that moment the firm learned that it had a "brother in misfortune": a large textile (manufaktura) firm from Zgierz [printed "Zgerush"], from which Barchański had taken goods for 200 thousand złoty and had likewise not paid a grosz. When the matter was handed over to the police, it emerged that Barchański had turned the goods into money, bought a house in Łódź with that money, registered it in his wife's name, and himself "fled" (vayivrach) to France.
The Number of Protested Bills of Exchange in Zagłębie

[Zagłębie — economy.] According to the statistics of the Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec, in the month of June (czerwiec) 15362 bills of exchange were protested in the Kielce voivodeship.
The record for protested bills was set by Sosnowiec, with 6426 bills for 1,337 511 zł. Będzin — 5,696 bills for a sum of 864 507 zł. Dąbrowa — 1671 bills for 307 616 zł. Zawiercie — 2188 bills for 315,021.
Sosnowiec — Kehilla council resolves to continue the lawsuit against Rabbi Englard

[Sosnowiec — kehilla and rabbinate.] Under the chairmanship of Mr. Y. M. Wajnreb a meeting of the kehilla board was held, which dealt with a series of questions, among them also the question of continuing the "lawsuit against Rabbi Englard.
On this it was resolved not to stop but to continue pursuing the rabbinate lawsuit.
It was also resolved to paint the synagogue and to announce a tender (concours) for this.
Sosnowiec too is to get the Będzin verdict — a tendency that the express trains should not stop

[Sosnowiec — railways.] As our readers already know, from the 15th of May the stopping of the express (courier) trains at the Będzin station was abolished.
As we are informed, there is also a tendency that the express trains should not stop at the local station either.
She is a "freethinker", but she is afraid she may be punished for the sin

[Sosnowiec — everyday life.] "She" is 17 years old, "he" — 19. For a whole year now they have been "in love", and during that time she has "lost her heart" for him. The couple came to one of the local rabbinical judges (moyrey-hoyroe), from whom they wanted "ptoyrim" [a release from the match].
The rabbinical judge tries to persuade the bride to make it up, but she does not want to hear of it — "I have no heart for it any more"...
During the negotiations the bride bursts into tears. To the rabbinical judge's question why she is crying, she answers thus: "I am actually a freethinker, but I am afraid God may punish me for breaking off a match"...
Mass Meeting of Artisans

[Sosnowiec — artisans.] On Sunday a large mass meeting of local Jewish artisans took place in a hall.
The meeting is opened by Mr. Cymberknop [?], who gives the floor for a report on all current artisans' affairs to Mr. A. Gancwajch, who presents a series of information on the law on holidays for workers — citing in this connection judgments of the Supreme Court — on examinations for artisans, and above all on the long-term loans for artisans which were set up by the state to support the artisans' workshops. From the inquiries that the board made in the competent circles it became clear that all artisans without distinction who comply with the relevant regulations will benefit from the said loans.
In this connection some of those present spoke in favour of dividing the loans into smaller sums, so that more craftsmen could benefit from them.
Besides this, the question of the striking-out of the kehilla subsidy for the artisans' courses was touched upon.
Taking part in the discussion were Messrs. Yaakov Rotsztajn, the parnas Brojner, Posłuszny, Walrbojm [?] and others.
After Mr. Walrman [?] replied to all the discussants, it was resolved to convene a regional conference of all Jewish artisans' associations in Zagłębie on the matter of the loans, and to organise a large mass rally about the struck-out subsidies.
Łakaj Has Died of His Injuries

[Sosnowiec — work accident.] In our last issue we reported on the terrible incident that befell the tinsmith Yaakov Łakaj [?], who fell from the scaffolding (rusztowanie) on the fourth floor of Moszkowicz's house on Wspólna Street.
Łakaj was taken to hospital, where he died a few hours later.
The tragically killed man was 35 years old and left a wife with 4 small children.
Pulled a Noose Round Her Neck and Robbed 600 zł

[Sosnowiec — robbery.] On Femiszna [?] Street, by Schön's factory houses, a robbery was committed on the 62-year-old widow Hajzer [?].
The old woman had saved 600 zł from her hard work, which she wanted to give to the priest so that after her death he would hold an honourable funeral for her.
When Hajzer was going home, she was attacked by an unknown person, who threw a rope round her neck and then robbed her of the 600 zł.
A dangerous bandit arrested.

The bandit Żaczka [?], wanted by the police, finally fell into the hands of the police this week while he was sunk in sweet sleep...
Żaczka is accused of carrying out a series of attacks and burglaries in Upper Silesia and in Zagłębie.
—o—
Resignation of Mr. Neufeld as Vice-President of the Chamber of Commerce.
This week Mr. Neufeld, vice-president of the commercial section of the Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec, officially announced that he is resigning from his post.
—o—
Four months in prison for a swindle
In the dock of the local district court sat a certain Lubelski, living in Warsaw, who, presenting himself as an agent of the firm „Sanatrax“ [?] in Bielsko, made a „transaction“ with the barber Abraham Goldberg in Olkusz and [thereafter?] swindled a bill of exchange out of Goldberg.
Lubelski was sentenced to 4 months in prison.
—o—
In revenge he stabbed his sweetheart with a „bayonet“
The 18-year-old Gwak [?] noticed his sweetheart (kochanka) sitting with another man. Gwak went up to her and begged her not to cast him off, and when she rejected his proposal, he pulled out a bayonet, with which he stabbed her.
—o—
The „Pogotowie“ runs over a child.
On 3 Maja [Third of May] Street the ambulance ran over 6-year-old Dawid Ślepecki [?], who was seriously injured.
The same vehicle took the boy to hospital.
—o—
Great success of the local „Brit Trumpeldor“ in Warsaw.
At the all-Polish sports festival of the Trumpeldor members in Warsaw, the local branch (ken) under the leadership of commander (mefaked) M. Glidman had great success. The Sosnowiec Betar took part in all the guard-of-honour duties and took first place in the exercises.
On Tuesday the local Trumpeldor members returned from Warsaw and marched in closed ranks through the town, which made a fine impression.
—o—
10 months in prison for giving a false oath.
The Żarki resident Lejbisz Krakauer was sentenced by the municipal court to 2 days' arrest. When a policeman wanted to take him off to arrest, Krakauer again showed his obstinacy, tried to put up resistance, and for this he was sentenced a second time, to a month in prison.
Krakauer, however, did not accept this and appealed to the Sosnowiec district court. In the appeal Krakauer stressed that the policeman had taken revenge on him because he had not wanted to „treat“ him (fundować — buy him a drink).
The witness Chaim supported Krakauer's statement with an oath. But the prosecutor realised that Chaim had sworn falsely and brought a case against Chaim and Krakauer.
The trial took place this week, and Chaim was sentenced for the false oath to 10 months, and Krakauer to 1 year in prison and loss of civil rights.
From Sporting Life.

[Sport — Zagłębie.] „Wiktoria“—„Hakoach“ 2:4 (1:3).
The match between the above-mentioned teams [drużyny] was to decide which of the teams would win the championship title. From this contest Sosnowiec's „Wiktoria“ emerged as winner. The Będzin side, who took the field without the disqualified Rotenberg, Szywek 1 and Kokotek, set their excellent technique against the physical superiority of the guests, but that was not enough.
Already in the first minutes the physical superiority of the Sosnowiec team is noticeable. In the 7th minute the outside-left gets the ball, outplays the Hakoach defence, and the first goal is done.
The Hakoach players set to work; the 12th minute brings a fine chance in front of the „Wiktoria“ goal — the well-struck ball from Gutman is turned out for a corner by the goalkeeper. The „Wiktoria“ forwards score again through Margała (29th minute). „Hakoach“ attacks hard, but without success. In the 35th minute Chojnacki again scores the third goal for the guests, and 3 minutes later Jankielewicz finally scores the first goal for „Hakoach“. After the change of ends the Będzin side has enormous superiority, but they do not manage to overcome [?] the excellent defence of the guests. Only in the 25th minute does Rozen score a wonderful goal from 40 metres. Margała unexpectedly scores the 4th goal for „Wiktoria“. Now the Sosnowiec team pulls several players back into defence and holds the victory safely. Outstanding were Skarus, Kapała, Margała of „Wiktoria“, Rozen, Szchajner [?] and the Jankielewicz brothers. Referee Berwald of Kraków was an excellent arbiter. Spectators: over 1500.
„Maccabi“—C.K.S. (Czeladź) 2:2 (2:1).
„Maccabi“ played this match with great luck and managed to snatch one point from the Czeladź team. Already in the 10th minute „Maccabi“ takes the lead through Fiszel, who, with the help of C.K.S. defender Ciapała, scores the first goal. The guests set to work in earnest and score the equaliser through Przybyłek, the best player on the pitch. 5 minutes later Tuszyński receives a cross from the right wing and the ball sits in the „Maccabi“ goal. After the break the teams play brutally, and the referee sends off three players of C.K.S. and Fiszel of „Maccabi“. Despite the weakening the Czeladź men play better than the Jewish club; only the „Elfer“ [penalty kick] taken by Szmidt brings the equaliser in the 29th minute, and the result remains unchanged. The best were Fiszel, Gołanzka of „Maccabi“, Przybyłek, Tuszyński and the right wing of C.K.S. Referee Grabiński good.
„Świt“—„Sarmacja“ 1:2 (1:1).
In the second half the „Świt“ players had great superiority; the first goal is scored by Piotronek for the Będzin side in the 29th minute, and 5 minutes later the right wing of „Świt“ equalises. After the change of ends the Sosnowiec side has great superiority, but they manage „gur“ [= only?] to score the winning goal, through Lewandowski. The best on the pitch was the „Świt“ goalkeeper. Referee Ernrajch not [good].
„Gwiazda“ (Zasg[—]ryk [?]) — „Shimshon“ (Sandwiszów [?]) 1:3 (1:2).
In the second championship contest Sosnowiec's „Shtern“ [„Star“ = Gwiazda] won convincingly, this time against the leader of Class „C“. The match stood at a high level. The goals were scored by the brothers Włodzimirski, and for „Shimshon“ — by Będziowski. Outstanding were the brothers Włodzimirski, Szwajcer and Lewarek, and of the guests the left defender. Referee Lepek weak.
—o—
Będzin „Hakoach“ organises a reception for the motorcyclists from Eretz Israel.
Last Monday, in the premises of „Hakoach“ in Będzin, the organisational meeting of the reception committee took place, which is to deal with receiving the Eretz-Israel motorcyclists. Of the invited organisations the following were present: „Hashachar“, „Brit Trumpeldor“, „Hashomer Haleumi“, „Herzliya“, the Revisionists, „Tzeirei Mizrachi“, „Hitachdut“ and „Hechalutz“. Not represented were the Zionist Organisation and the „Agudah“.
After a short debate appropriate commissions were elected, which will deal with arranging a fitting reception for the guests from Eretz Israel.
—o—
The number of unemployed is growing
Today, Friday, 200 workers of the „Wysoka“ cement factory beyond Łazy are being laid off.
At the joint-stock company „Poręba“ [?] 100 workers and 23 officials will be laid off on the 15th of this month.

A Father Will Not Let His Child Be Circumcised

Yesterday, Thursday, something happened in Sosnowiec that has the whole town in an uproar.
On 1 Maja (1st of May) Street lives the boot-upper maker Jakub Lajzer Waldbaum[?] with his wife, who last Thursday bore him their third boy, and yesterday the circumcision (brit) was to take place.
But in the time leading up to the third boy the couple had become "socialist" and decided not to circumcise the newborn boy.
The rabbinate, on learning of this, held an urgent meeting yesterday in the kehilla premises with the participation of several kehilla board members, who resolved to go to the father and prevail upon him to refrain from this step.
Those who went there were the rabbis Hager, Halberstam (a brother-in-law of the Radomsko Rebbe), Gliksman, vice-president L. Zendel and the mohel Fiszel.
A large crowd of people, curious onlookers, went along with the rabbis, but at the entrance to Waldbaum's[?] flat the landlord planted himself like a doorman[?] and threatened to beat anyone who would dare approach the house.
The threat, naturally, had its effect, and the rabbis were forced to leave the house.

Zawoja

[Zawoja — a resort; correspondence.] (From our correspondent)
Zawoja at the present moment ranks among the Polish health resorts and tourist centres, which are developing from day to day. Its fame as the most beautiful village in Poland after Zakopane has only now been established.
Beneath the majestic "Babia Góra", queen of the Beskids, the steep "Veltshoyn" [?], the wooded "Polica" and many other mountains that ring "Zawoja" round, leaving only a narrow place for the "highway", like a single little window onto the world, and encircled by the eternally rushing mountain stream "Skawica", "Zawoja" is truly a wonderfully beautiful, quiet, dreamlike little corner for those who want rest and for those whose youthful temperament impels them to a free life of excursions [?] in the lap of nature.
As a resort, of which little has been said until now, "Zawoja" presents many possibilities of development. One must admit, however, that as regards European amenities "Zawoja" still lags behind. "Zawoja" does not yet have a swimming pool, a good [?] tennis court, an elegant boarding house, electric light and the like.
This year's attendance has exceeded the number of summer guests ["letniki"] of past years. Writing about summer guests, I am reminded of a joke: that in the Polish resorts they built churches for the Catholics, cerkvas for the Orthodox and synagogues for the... summer guests. In this respect "Zawoja" is no exception...
In Zawoja there are four boarding houses, three Jewish and one Polish, also frequented by Jews. The centre of Jewish life is Mr. Fischer's boarding house. The prayers heard every Sabbath in the boarding house and the sign "Ribipa [?] Żyrowski" already give a good characterisation and tell of the commotion that reigns there without end. An ill-wisher [?] said that in Zawoja the Jews have the Land of Israel. Yes, the Land of Israel lives in Zawoja — but in the hearts of the summer guests; this is shown by the result of the latest events for the Jewish National Fund (KKL).
The young people formed a committee, which organised a Herzl memorial "academy". In a packed hall Dr. Saurkit [?] (Kraków) and Dr. Ellenberg (Łódź) gave addresses. The second event, a large public entertainment for children, brought in an income of 1200 zł., a sum that exceeded all expectations (would it were so with us too). A whole series of further events is being prepared.
Very much of its fame and importance Zawoja owes to the fact that from it lead the best and shortest routes up "Babia Góra", the highest mountain in the Polish Beskids. The gigantic 1725-metre mountain "Babia Góra" is one of the most beautiful scenic spots in Poland.
Many legends are told about "Babia Góra" and its name. Concerning the name, there are hypotheses [?] that the local population, having the Tatras on one side and the Babia on the other, ironically gave it a "feminine" name as a sign of its inferiority compared with the Tatras. It is told that once a devilish [?] castle stood on the Babia, which collapsed, and that from it comes the great mass of stones.
"Babia Góra" has two peculiarities: the sight of the clouds that cover the surrounding villages, which the tourist observes while standing above them; and the sunrise, when the mountains glow in the light of the rising sun.
A. Gertner.

A Letter to the Editor

Dear Mr. Editor!
I ask you to print in your esteemed newspaper the following lines in connection with the item in the newspaper under the heading[?] "A doctor who arrests his 12-year-old patient".
The child of the Tuszek family of Kohalska[?] Street in Sosnowiec suddenly fell ill with a serious internal illness. Having been called out in the middle of the night by Mr. Jakub Landau, who came to me at the hospital, I ordered the child to be moved to the surgical ward.
At the same time, after reaching an understanding with the child's parents, I called by telephone the head of the surgical ward for a consultation, and we agreed that the child had to be operated on immediately.
The operation was indeed performed in the middle of the night in the presence of 3 doctors. Thanks to this rescue the child was saved from death.
The costs of the consultation, the operation and the special[?] supervision I demanded beforehand, before the operation, and not after the operation as is stated in the item.
I pointed out to the child's parents that under the hospital regulations daily visits to the patient are not permitted. It is not true that I issued a special order that the parents should not be admitted; on the contrary, when the first days after the operation had passed, I permitted the mother to see her child every day. Only when I learned from my staff that the mother was making very frequent visits and bringing baked goods from home without my permission did I instruct the attendants to point out that, for the child's good, the visits should not take place often; but "arresting the child" never entered anyone's mind.
No one from the public prosecutor's office came into the hospital, and Mr. Tuszek never offered me 400 zł. at all. Only on the day[?] the child was discharged from the hospital did Mr. Tuszek declare that he was an unemployed commission agent and had nothing to pay with.
The confirmation I requested from the gmina, the magistrate or from several Sosnowiec householders that he was unable to pay the medical costs — Mr. Tuszek did not want (to provide), nor did he want to agree to pay the medical costs.
For this reason there is no other way out but to hand over to the court the parents of the child, who, thanks to the great effort of the surgical ward, was saved from death.
Respectfully,
Dr. Bieńkowski
Doctor of the surgical ward at the Szyflcer[?] hospital in Sosnowiec.
From the World of Sport

"Maccabi"—"Hakoach" 0:1 (0:0)!

Only Not to Be Comforted — (Thoughts of the Time for Shabbat Nachamu)

L. Szpigelman.
(Thoughts of the time for Shabbat Nachamu.)
"Comfort ye, comfort ye my people" — be comforted, my people, you must have the comfort!
These traditional words we hear year in, year out; every Shabbat Nachamu we comfort ourselves. We tell ourselves: things will be good now, a change for the better will now set in. The bad — we say — is already over, it is already after Shabbat Chazon and after Tisha b'Av, there is no need to be in mourning any more, no need to weep; let there be liveliness and gaiety, let us comfort ourselves, for there is, after all, no other way out. We must have the comfort; we look forward to it even before the days of mourning have begun, before we have sat down on the low stools to mourn and weep.
There was once a time when for us Jews, after the days of mourning, came the consolation, the comfort; after it had already been thoroughly dark, the prophet came and lit up the world with bright rays of sunshine. But now — what shall we comfort ourselves with? Where do we see the way out that would brighten our future, that could secure [?] and make possible our existence?
For we live now in the twentieth century, where we have all civil rights without any limitations as Jews — and yet we are admitted to nothing. True, officially no limitations exist for us, but in reality we Jews see where it is intended not to admit us, where they do not want us — there, where we could have settled in and disturbed no one. Today, in modern times, there is no need to introduce any limitations at all; there is no need to play at such "foolishness" [?]; by the way, it would also be out of place — it does not suit the cultured world of the twentieth century that limitations between man and man should be found in black and white. Outwardly all must be equal, but in reality a way is found, an expedient is found: where they do not want to admit the Jew, he is simply not admitted, without a "why" and no more "when" [?].
After all, we live in the 20th century, when there is no time to split hairs over every "trifle": not permitted here and not permitted there — and the matter is settled.
It is an old rule that we live, exist and draw our sustenance thanks to our hope, thanks to the faith in our hearts that some day a bright tomorrow and a beautiful future will come. It has almost been established that no people in the world could have existed under such conditions — and how strong our faith must be, how deep that small spark must lie in every Jewish soul, thanks to which we exist as a unique Jewish people, with all our stubborn traditions, in all countries and among all peoples.
And it is interesting: there are countries with few Jews who, because of their small community, have become assimilated; yet how often are we astonished when we hear that among all sorts of "Jews" there are so many healthy Jewish hearts, ready to sacrifice themselves for the Jewish collective, for the good of the Jewish people. We see even more: there are children of those very assimilated Jews, brought up far from Judaism — and "far" is putting it mildly: the parents took care that the children should, God forbid, never learn of their Jewish descent — and precisely in such ranks a spark kindled of itself, which began to seethe, and with genuine Jewish fervour they take pride in their Jewishness and in the Jewish people.
It is simply to be marvelled at; the mind cannot grasp where so much strength, such great power and patience come from in a people so broken and shattered, hunted and beaten, which has nowhere a place and no resting place — and at precisely such a moment one comes to the realisation that something higher must be hovering above our heads, something sublime that pours into the cup of refreshment great doses of vigorous courage to live, giving the strength to carry on the life of a people that cannot be frightened off the world arena, and that must some day attain the longed-for ideal.
And therefore, if we want to exist as a people under today's difficult and at times almost impossible conditions of existence, we must first of all remember that we are a people equal among peoples. We must not crawl like lowly creatures to the squire to wangle a concession, a favour, for these or other Jews. The practice of shtadlanut (backstairs intercession) must be done away with, without any excuse.
We must exist as one whole people. Frictions may occur in our ranks; we may polemicise, and everyone may have his own ideal, his own train of thought, his own credo — but outwardly, towards the world outside, we must not be several torn-apart peoples. Because of this we lose a great deal at every opportunity, for as soon as it is seen from outside that we are broken and shattered, people want to help destroy what is still left, what can still be saved.
In the Jewish camp, at home among ourselves, anything in the world can be done; we may have all kinds of differences of opinion — but these are our own worries, our own pains and sorrows, our own sufferings and cares. Between our internal affairs and the outside world, however, a boundary must be set; we must always [?] remember where we stand in the world, we must remember well where to set the "thus far and no further" [!].
That is one thing, but there is a second: not weeping and lamenting and shedding tears will help us in any way, just as it cannot help us that we comfort ourselves — for one friend can comfort another, but not himself. Besides, one should not comfort oneself when [?] we have no comfort, when we see no better way out; on top of that one fools oneself only with the laconic "Comfort ye, comfort ye my people", and it seems to us that by uttering the words help has already come.
Better not to comfort; better not to fool ourselves; better to look reality in the face with open eyes, however hard it may appear to us, however much we may fear it. Enough fooling ourselves, enough waiting for miracles, enough hoping and living on dreams. The times are serious, our situation is too dangerous for us to stand with folded arms and staring eyes and wait until what we dream of, what we are waiting to receive, comes along.
And therefore let us not look forward to comfort, let us not comfort ourselves, and let us not allow others to comfort us either, for these words of comfort lead us astray and make us forget the serious situation in which the people finds itself. We had better look reality straight in the face and see to combating the gravity of the situation.
We must begin to become more productive in every field; we must not fool ourselves, and we cannot wait and hope for mere miracles, for that makes a people lazy, one loses one's balance, one does not know what is yes and what is no, which way is in and which way is out.
Only let us not seek in words of comfort the remedy, the rescue, the cure. Let us not allow ourselves to be comforted; let us rather become more productive, more industrious; let us rather learn and study how to arrange life in the present century, so that we can keep up with the times, so that we do not remain backward and fall into helplessness.
Let us go forward in full awareness and with open eyes look reality in the face, however hard and frightening it may appear to us.
Let us thereby prove that we are not afraid of anything and that we have enough courage and awareness to fight for our existence.
And therefore: let us not allow ourselves to be comforted.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion (Va'etchanan)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion.
Collected and adapted by Y. L.
Parashat Va'etchanan
—o—
a) "You shall not add... nor diminish" (Deut. 4:2)
"You shall not add" — do not multiply commandments, do not invent commandments that are not in the Torah, because "whoever adds, diminishes"; too much is worse than nothing... From "you shall not add" you arrive at "you shall not diminish". Da'at Zekenim.
* * *
Once a neighbour came to a Jew and asked to borrow a spoon. The next day he brings him back two spoons. The Jew asks him: why do I get two, when I only[?] lent you one? — The neighbour answers: your spoon gave birth to a second one at my house... so the newborn is yours too. The Jew laughs at the joke and takes the second spoon as well. An old Jewish rule: when you are given — you take. The next day the neighbour comes to borrow a plate; the Jew lends it to him most graciously — after all, he will get double back, since at that fellow's house utensils multiply!... So it went on, day after day. One day he comes to borrow the silver candelabra. The Jew lends it to him with joy — he will surely get back two silver candelabra! — The next day he sees that the candelabrum is not being returned, and goes to demand it. The neighbour answers: "A misfortune has happened, the candelabrum died yesterday"... The Jew is filled with anger: a candelabrum can die?! What kind of foolish swindle are you pulling on me?! — Then the neighbour answers him: — And that spoons and plates can multiply — that you do understand?! Why did you believe me then and take the newborn spoons and plates? And if utensils can be born, they can also die...
If "you add" — if with you commandments multiply — there will be "you diminish": one day commandments will die off too... Ohel Yaakov.
* * *
"And it shall come to pass, when you break loose, that you shall shake his yoke from off your neck" (Gen. 27:40) — There are 613 (taryag) commandments. But people like to add more commandments: "a mitzvah to inform on someone, a mitzvah to tear someone down", and the like. Such commandments people like to add to the Torah. So the verse says: "ve-haya ka'asher tarid" — read "tari'd" (614): when, instead of 613, you devise 614 commandments, adding such commandments as informing on and robbing others, then — "you shall shake his yoke from off your neck". That is what casting off the yoke means. From the mouth of the people.
—o—
b) "You shall not murder" (Deut. 5:17)
The Gemara (Avodah Zarah 19) calls a murderer one who is not qualified to rule and decides questions of law; also one who is qualified to rule but does not want to occupy himself with judging and deciding is designated a murderer —; that is why "lo tirtzach" is vocalized[?] both with a kamatz (in the upper cantillation) under the tsadi and with a patach (in the lower cantillation), to show that both the "mekamtsim" — those who could serve the community with their Torah erudition and do not do so — and the "mefatchim", i.e. those who cannot learn and spread themselves about, become rabbis and decide questions of law — all of them fall under "You shall not murder". Spiritual barbarism... [Attributed to] the Vilna Gaon.
—o—
c) "With all your soul and with all your might" (Deut. 6:5)
"With all your soul" — with your life: you must put your life in danger for God; "with all your might" — with your wealth: you must give up your wealth for God. And therefore both must be said, because there are people to whom life is dearer than money, and there are people to whom money is far dearer than life... Berakhot 61.
— Is there really a person for whom money matters more than life?
— What is meant is: there are people who would rather perform a commandment that demands physical exertion from them than [give] a few groszy... He will run, he will work for the sake of Heaven — but only as far as his pocket. Therefore it is said "with all your might" — with the grosz, too, you must serve God... And of them this is interpreted[?]: "their money is dearer to them than their body". Kol Eliyahu.
—o—
"And these words shall be upon your heart, and you shall teach them diligently to your children (Deut. 6:6–7)
If you want to preach something to others, see that the thing is first found in your own heart. When "these words", the moral teachings, are "upon your heart", in your heart — only then will it be possible that "you shall teach them to your children". For you to pass it on to your children, you must first be in order with yourself. Alshich.
—o—
e) "And you shall teach them to your children and speak of them" (Deut. 6:7)
When the children, too, are raised in the same traditional spirit as their father, then he, the father, is at home with them, at ease[?], and has something to talk about with them at the table. If there is "you shall teach them to your children" — you study Torah with your children — then there is "and speak of them": you can converse with them. If, on the other hand, they are raised as strangers to tradition, then you sit with them at one table and have not a single word to exchange with them. They talk about football, matches, and you sit by silent... Nothing binds you to them. Beit Yitzchak.
* * *
"Over Kamtsa and Bar Kamtsa Jerusalem was destroyed" — Jerusalem was destroyed because there were splits between the "Kamtsas", the elders, and the "Bar-Kamtsas", the young. The genuine Jerusalem coin had David engraved on one side and Solomon[?] on the other. Father and son on one coin — that is the symbol of a liberated Jerusalem. Yalkut Peninim.
—o—
f) "Thus shall you deal with them — you shall break down their altars" (Deut. 7:5)
The nations of the world are likened to water and the Jews — to fire. And the struggle between fire and water goes like this: when fire and water are kept apart, the fire dries up the water — so the fire wins; but when fire and water are mixed together, the water puts out the fire — so the water wins. So it is with the Jews too: when they are mixed together with the nations, the water (= the nations of the world) floods them; but when they stand apart, the fire (= the Jews) wins. "Thus shall you deal with them" — if you do not intermarry with the nations, as was said before ("neither shall you make marriages with them"), then — "you shall break down their altars" — you will defeat them. Rabbi Hirsh Meilech of Dynów.
—o—
Avot, chapter four.
"Be very, very humble of spirit before every man"
"Me'od" (very) means money ("with all your might [me'odecha] — with all your money") — "very, very": even when you possess a lot of money, nevertheless be humble of spirit before every man; do not jump into everyone's face. Petach Einayim by the Chida.

When One Must Console

“The watchman said: The morning cometh, and also the night” (Isaiah 21:12).
When does one console, and whom does one console?
As is the way of the world, one consoles when there is no longer any hope. One consoles when returning from the cemetery, where one has left behind the most beloved, the dearest, and one sits shiva...
As long as the sick one was in the house and a vein still pulsed, as long as there was a shred of hope, nobody consoled; people took counsel, sought remedies — nobody consoles then, nobody seeks to be consoled.
When one comes back from the “pure place” [the cemetery] — then friends come, acquaintances come, and they begin with the age-old formula: you are not the first, you are not the last — it is a “wheel that turns” — that is how it goes in the world.
And there, on the hill behind the town, a freshly heaped mound of sand turns yellow; there a good child, or one of the dear parents, already sleeps the eternal sleep — they will never come back; in the house one is missing, whose place will never be filled.
Then comforters come.
Each comforter tells something similar from his own life, each has a word to say and... life goes on.
The mourners say “I accept consolation”; the shiva passes, they leave the low stool.
On the yahrzeit one lights a candle, says Kaddish and — one has done one’s duty.
* * *
Tisha b’Av is the yahrzeit of the people of Israel. Tisha b’Av is the day on which we, as a territorial people, [went] into exile, died, and “she hath none to comfort her” — nobody consoles on the day of the yahrzeit. She hath none to comfort her...
Every year we mourn, every year we keep the yahrzeit, every year — and the calamity is fresh, fresh... Tisha b’Av is “as if his dead lay before him” — one may not console.
For in truth it is only “as if”; for in truth nobody has died, and Tisha b’Av is not a yahrzeit; it is the day that only reminds us that we are dangerously ill, [yet] a vein still beats [?], the people lives — even when the sharp sword lies on the neck, the neck is not yet cut through; one must pray for mercy, there is still hope.
She hath none to comfort her — nobody consoles her, Jerusalem has no comforter, because Jerusalem is sick, but not dead.
* * *
And the people is in despair, does not know what to do, sometimes grabs at entirely wrong remedies, in its despair does not seek the means that are needed — and the situation gets worse. — The people must be calmed, reassured.
— A time will come, says the prophet, when “a voice will call in the wilderness: Clear a way for God, make straight in the desert a path for our God! Every valley shall be raised, every hill shall be made lower, and the hilly places shall become level ground” [after Isaiah 40:3–4].
* * *
“Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God”..
It was after the seventieth Tisha b’Av, in the days of the Cyrus declaration, which he issued to the Jewish people after the great world war, when Babylon had fallen.
— “Thus said Cyrus king of Persia: All the kingdoms of the world has God, the God of heaven, given to me, and He has commanded me to build Him a house in Jerusalem. What [= who] is of Judah, who among you, of all [?] His people — may his God be with him — let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build God’s house, the God of Israel, He is the God who is in Jerusalem” [after Ezra 1:2–3].
At that time of this declaration came Isaiah and spoke to us his “Comfort ye, comfort ye my people!”
———
He spoke the “Comfort ye” at the right time. People then badly needed such reassuring words.
[—] Not when there was almost no hope did Isaiah speak his “Comfort ye”, not when the people was in its death throes, when it was about to breathe its last — not then; for who can speak at such a time? Who can find words of reassurance at such a time? For such a moment Jeremiah’s “She weepeth sore” is more fitting — weeping helplessly, lamenting inconsolably.
But when the sick one is about to recover, and the recovery, as usual [?], proceeds slowly, gradually; when the sick one tosses about, wavers and flickers like a candle on a windy night — now the wind subsides and the little flame rises, burns straight and pure, and now from one side, unexpectedly [?], a cold, evil wind has blown... the little candle begins to flicker, to go out.
The Jewish people needed, at that hard, very critical time, words of encouragement, words of reassurance, words of consolation; then they needed the “Comfort ye, comfort ye my people”..
* * *
Harder and harder grows the situation of the people — not at the first rays of its hope rising, but precisely at the last [moments] before the day, the normal sunny day, arrives; the night, the darkness, fights very fiercely against the coming day.
The “end of redemption” is much harder than the “beginning”. The end of the deliverance is much harder than the beginning of the deliverance.
Full of hope are the first rays of sunrise, when it begins to redden at the eastern edge; the night is still in full swing, but the rays are the heralds of the good tidings that the night is not eternal.
But before the day is born...
Cold winds blow, restless clouds race across the sky with haste and impetus. The only night-light, the moon, vanishes [?] or pales and blanches. It often happens that the winds bring such black clouds that the first “rays of good tidings” are completely covered, blocked. The joy [?] of the night, the golden stars, are extinguished, and black and hopeless is the “future bright sky”. — One loses one’s way, one begins to think that the hopes were in vain, that the good tidings were false — at such a moment the desperate question tears itself from the heart: “Watchman, what of the night?” — and then the answer is needed: “The morning cometh, and also the night” — the morning has indeed come, although it seems that it is night...
* * *
Today, in the great Palestine crisis, we are living through the same epoch, the same period that Jews historically and actually lived through in the epoch when the prophecy “Comfort ye, comfort ye my people” was spoken — and that is why today’s Shabbat Nachamu is so meaningful for us.
On Tisha b’Av we wept at the sickbed of our national existence, we dispiritedly observed the helpless “She weepeth sore”; now, however, we must come to our people with the encouraging “word of comfort” — true, we are sick, but not helpless.
True, it is dark, very; but it is not the darkness of night — it is “the-morning-cometh”-like, it is only “and-also-the-night”-like; it only seems that it is night..
* * *
Comfort ye, comfort ye, said your God..
A. Shoyer.
A Short Feuilleton: “Żydek.”

[Feuilleton — Poland and the Jews; antisemitism in language.] “Żydek” [“little Jew”, a contemptuous term] — which of us has not heard this word? It seems that it is already a generally accepted form, used not only by the Polish intelligent and, what is more, often even in various documents of an official character.
Present-day Poland inherited this word from the times of the szlachta era, for the great magnates and even the average “pan” regarded the Jew as a kind of low creature that one could treat with disdain and contempt.
We ourselves have become so used to this notion that it makes almost no impression on us at all; it seems to us that this designation is perfectly normal and natural.
And it is precisely a foreigner, who comes for a while and observes our conditions, who often notices things that we ourselves are not capable of noticing.
The well-known author of a whole series of works that have caused a great sensation — Ilya Ehrenburg — gives in his newly published work “Viza vremeni” [“Visa of Time”] an apt characterization of various countries that he recently visited.
To the Polish Jews Ehrenburg devotes a special chapter under the title — “With a Wet Towel”, meaning that in Poland Jews are beaten with a wet towel, so that no marks remain.
There are [?] a number of apt passages in the book, but the main thing here is Ehrenburg’s characteristic remark that the attitude to Jews in Poland is expressed in the contemptuous word “Żydek”.
Perhaps one day people will stop using this word, if not in everyday life, then at least there where the attitude to the citizen must be, at least in theory, an equal one.
The disdain ought to find a little less expression — in public.
A. Tz.

Cantor Żupowicz Placed at the Disposal of the Rabbinate

[Będzin — kehilla.]
What's New in Zagłębie? — Friday, 24 [sic] 7 Av 5690; Piątek 8 sierpnia 1930 (Friday, 8 August 1930).
Będzin
If they give him a “hechsher”, he will pray..
In last week's issue we wrote that our kehilla board (may it live long) had decided to settle the cantorship affair by drawing lots: yes Żupowicz, or not.
As it turns out, however, the “politicians” have withdrawn the lottery decision and pulled off a brand-new manoeuvre.
At Tuesday's meeting of the kehilla board a resolution was adopted that the board shall not decide the dispute with Cantor Żupowicz, but shall hand the matter over to the “supreme tribunal” — the rabbinate, that is — which is to issue a “hechsher” [certificate of fitness] as to whether Żupowicz may lead the prayers or not.
If Cantor Mr. Żupowicz receives such a “hechsher”, then under his contract he will automatically remain cantor in the town.
All the Interventions Achieved Nothing

[Będzin — railways.]
The express trains will not stop at the local stations.
As is already known, the magistrate [town council], the chamber of commerce and a number of merchants' organisations appealed to the Ministry of Railways and to the president of the railway directorate to abolish the ban concerning the non-stopping of express trains at the local stations.
This week a reply arrived from the Ministry of Railways, announcing that in order to improve rail communication with foreign countries the ban cannot be withdrawn..
They Have Found Themselves a New Livelihood...

[Będzin — trade.]
Lately several Christians have been staying here who press Jewish merchants to buy pictures of the President of the State and of Marshal Piłsudski. It happens quite often that the buyer cannot afford to buy the pictures of the Polish government, but out of naivety and out of fear he buys the pictures.
We therefore point out that buying the pictures is no obligation at all; these gentlemen are merely exploiting it to make a living..
Avoid the Dark Alleys.

[Będzin — crime.]
Hooligan attacks on people out for a stroll.
On Monday evening 3 persons were strolling in the dark avenue by the Christian cemetery: a young man with his fiancée and the fiancée's girlfriend.
Suddenly they were attacked by several young Christian hooligans, who threw themselves on the strollers. The young man and his fiancée fled, but the girl fell into the hands [?] of the scoundrels, who stuffed her mouth with earth and thus [?] wanted to rape her.
The couple who had fled called the police, who came to the spot, where they found the girl with her mouth stuffed.
The police are conducting an investigation to find out who these human beasts are.
Those Who Did Not Go to the Foreign Spas Have Waited It Out..

[Będzin — municipal.]
The renovation of the local municipal bath-house is now finished, and from today, Friday, all departments of the establishment are in operation again.
From the Zionist-Revisionist Movement

[Będzin — Zionism.]
At the Saturday meeting the following questions were discussed:
1) Why is the Jewish world silent about the death sentence of Yosef Urfali [printed “Urfaliz”?]. Several speakers took part in the discussion; by a large majority — against 2 votes — it was decided to send a telegram of protest to the Central Committee of the Revisionists; and
2) Whether returnees (yordim) from Eretz Israel should be admitted into the organisation. It was decided by a majority of votes that if the yordim had been there as halutzim [pioneers], the question will be referred to the party court.
———
This Saturday afternoon Y. Langes [?] will lecture on the topic: “The forthcoming 4th World Conference of the Revisionists in Prague.”
A Father Wants to Support His Child, but He Does Not Know Where the Child Is.

[Będzin — community.]
Mr. Dawid Zajghojf [?] Herzberg came to the editorial office and told the following:
Many years ago there lived in Będzin a certain Jekel Ehrenfried, who for economic reasons emigrated abroad, and he is today in Düsseldorf. In the meantime Ehrenfried's wife died here, leaving a child to God's mercy. The deceased woman's mother wanted to take the child.
But the child's father cannot rest; he wants to support the child and also — if he manages it — to take it to himself.
This week two Jews from Warsaw were here passing through, whom the father had asked to look into the matter. The Jews could not find out anything about the son; therefore Mr. Herzberg came to the editorial office so that we should publish the fact, in order that the child's close relatives should concern themselves with the matter.
Fell Out of the Train

[Będzin — accidents.]
While travelling back from an excursion, 16-year-old Kania of Katowice fell out of the train.
Kania was taken home in a serious condition.
Szklarnia Street is becoming like other people's... — By order of Minister Składkowski

[Sosnowiec — municipality; streets; trade.] The board of the local Small Traders' Association [in Sosnowiec] turned to the "iron"[?] Minister Składkowski [Felicjan Sławoj Składkowski, Minister of the Interior] with a memorandum in which it raised the question of watering (sprinkling) the commercial streets, paving the swampy[?] Szklarnia street, and so on.
The memorandum was sent on 12 July (Lipiec) of this year, and 8 days later an order had already arrived from the above-mentioned minister to the Magistrat [city council] that everything indicated in the memorandum be carried out.
The Magistrat apparently took fright at the order and has set about paving and watering the commercial streets.
A railway disaster at the local station
[Sosnowiec — railway; accident.] On Tuesday there was a collision between a locomotive and a freight train. Several wagons were smashed[?] and an official was injured.
An unsuccessful communist demonstration

[Sosnowiec — communists; police.] In front of the "Momus"[?] cinema in Pogoń a crowd of communists gathered who wanted to demonstrate. The police, who were on the spot, dispersed the demonstrators.
A certain Mrs. Krzykawa[?], who had unfurled a red flag, was arrested.
Society's struggle against communism

[Sosnowiec — Polish organisations; communism.] On the initiative of a number of Polish organisations, the founding meeting of the "Bureau for Combating the Import[?] from Moscow" took place on Sunday.
Representatives of the following took part in the board: the Catholic League, the Sokół, the railway engine-drivers, the conductors, "Rozwój", the Polish merchants' associations, etc.
A committee was elected which will run the institution.
—o—
"The Miracle on the Vistula"
[Sosnowiec — Polish national holiday.] Under this name the 10th anniversary will be celebrated next Sunday of the day when the Bolsheviks were driven back from outside Warsaw [Battle of Warsaw, August 1920].
The programme is a festive one.
—o—
A Jewish girl run over
[Sosnowiec — road accident.] On Sunday evening, in Ostrogórska street, 10-year-old Tauba Lefert[?] was run over by a car and her left leg was broken.
The injured child was taken to the Jewish hospital.
A post-office branch in Sielce!

[Sosnowiec — post.] Next month a post-office branch will be opened in Sielce. The branch will be located in Narutowicza street.
The postal directorate also intends to open a post-office branch in Pogoń.
The building of workers' houses

[Sosnowiec — construction; employment.] On Saturday a meeting took place in Lemberg [Lwów] at which the offers of a number of firms wishing to take over the construction of workers' houses in our town were considered.
In the building work, which is to begin on the 15th of this month, several hundred workers will find employment.
Around the World Revisionist Conference in Prague

[Sosnowiec — Zionism; Revisionists.] In connection with the World Revisionist Conference, which takes place in Prague on Sunday the 10th of this month, the Revisionist Union in Sosnowiec is holding this Saturday afternoon a members' talk on the topic: "The tasks of the Revisionist Conference".
Mr. Klarman has been delegated to the conference by the Sosnowiec Revisionist organisation.
———
The Polish government is very accommodating towards the conference. The delegates have received railway discounts of 33 per cent, and a passport to Prague costs no more than 5 zł.
The Czech consulates are issuing the visas entirely free of charge.
Bread has become cheaper

[Sosnowiec — prices; municipality.] At Tuesday's session of the statistical office at the local Magistrat the price was fixed at 38 groszy for a kilo of rye bread and 30 groszy for a kilo of "razowy" (wholemeal) bread.
Personal

[Personal.] Today Dr. M.[?] Mela-Dista[?] leaves for Norway to take part in the International Congress for the Fight against Alcoholism.
A report on this very important congress, and also on the journey, will be printed in our newspaper.
Dąbrowa: Founding of Betar

[Dąbrowa — Zionist movements.] This Saturday the founding meeting of „Brit Trumpeldor” (Betar) takes place in Dąbrowa [Dąbrowa Górnicza].
The meeting will be held in the premises of the Artisans' Association, with the participation of members of the Central Committee (Ts"K) in Zagłębie.
—o—
Staniewski's Circus
[Dąbrowa — entertainment.] Is enjoying great success. The programme is interesting; special interest is aroused by the act in which lions and other animals appear.
Olkusz: Lecture by Rabbi Jakobson

[Olkusz — Zionism and Palestine.] On Sunday evening, in the synagogue and afterwards in the „Workers' House”, a lecture was given in Olkusz by Rabbi Jakobson (a judge[?] in Tel Aviv) on the subject: „The Present Situation in the Land of Israel and Its Future”.
For a couple of hours the speaker presented interesting and instructive[?] aspects of life in the Land of Israel, and at the end called on those assembled to support the Keren Kayemet LeIsrael (Jewish National Fund) with all their might.
—o—
Credit for Artisans
[Olkusz — economy.] The bank „Kredi. Genos.”[?] (credit cooperative) has granted credit of 50 thousand złoty for the artisans of Olkusz county. Of 30 local Jewish declarants, 22 received loans of 300 to 800 zł. — a sum of up to 15 thousand zł. It is regrettable[?] that out of about 130 Jewish artisans only such a small number as 30 persons declared themselves.
—o—
Excursion of the Poalei Zion (Left)
[Olkusz — parties.] On Saturday and Sunday an excursion of the Poalei Zion (Left) took place on „Czarna Góra”. The organisations of Zagłębie, Częstochowa, Wolbrom and Olkusz took part, with the participation of Mr. Zerubavel. It is characteristic that the campaign[?] was conducted in Polish.
—o—
From the Summer Cottages
[Olkusz — municipality.] The Magistrate (town council) has begun to install in the „Czarna Góra” park, for the coming summer-cottage season, a bathing beach and other surprises.
A. B.
A Good Answer

[Disguised advertisement — Aspirin.] The thing happened in a university town; everyone knows that Prof. Miller[?] examines very strictly. To a medical student he puts the following question:
— What means of inducing sweating do you know?
The student lists the well-known remedies, above all Aspirin tablets, which work excellently for a chill and a headache.
„Let us suppose,” says the professor, „that even this did not help — what would you have had[?] to do then?”
„I would have sent the patient to an examination with you, Professor,” the student answers him, impatiently.
Pilica: A Mill Burnt Down

[Pilica — fire.] On Saturday afternoon, while the Jewish public of Pilica was enjoying its „Sabbath sleep”, the „hoarse” alarm bell was heard, announcing that there was a fire!
With frightened faces, men, women and children began running to the Kraków lane [ul. Krakowska], where Gershon Lichtsztejn's mill was burning.
At the site of the fire almost the whole town gathered. Because of the Sabbath nobody touched any rescue[?] whatsoever; only incessant cries were heard: „Where is the fire brigade (the straż)?”...
Only when the tongues of fire (literally: „the fire's teeth”) had almost swallowed the mill building did the firemen „arrive”, with the rescue equipment[?] in their hands, and put out the fire.
The building is burnt.
—o—
A Savage Act of Revenge
[Pilica — violence.] On Saturday night, while Mr. Leibish Steinfeld was sitting in the beit midrash listening to the Torah reader reciting Eikhah (Lamentations), he was struck on the head through the open window with a blunt piece of iron, from which Steinfeld was drenched in blood and fell unconscious.
In the town people say that this happened as an act of revenge by a competitor from whom S. had bought up a sack of grain...
In general, disputes are „settled” in Pilica in such ways. A large share in this lawlessness belongs to the local quarrel-mongers, who have brought in a demoralisation: for if one may give a rabbi a shove, why should one not split open the head of a plain mortal over a sack of grain?
Sh. Hirsz-Zohn.

NOTICE
The Magistrate of the town of Będzin hereby announces that, on the basis of the Industrial Law of 7 June 1927, arts. 117, 118, 120, and of the Local Statute approved by the Town Council on 25 June 1928, juvenile workers of both sexes in industrial, craft and commercial establishments, born in the years 1912, 1913, 1914 and 1915, are subject to compulsory vocational continuation education in the public vocational continuation schools within the town of Będzin.
Enrolment in the public 3-class vocational schools — industrial, commercial and general — and in the preparatory classes will take place on 26, 27 and 28 August this year, from 17:00 to 21:00, in the school building at ul. Małachowskiego 35 ("Piast").
Applicants must bring certificates from their place of work and school certificates.
Admission: to the first industrial classes with certificates of completion of 5 classes of elementary school; to the second industrial classes with certificates of completion of 6 classes of elementary school; for the commercial classes preparation one class higher is required.
Those insufficiently prepared for the vocational classes will be admitted to preparatory classes conducted at the level of the 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th grade of elementary school.
This year there will be: A) an Industrial School with classes for: 1) locksmiths, turners and electricians, 2) joiners and pattern-makers, 3) tailors and shoemakers, 4) seamstresses, 5) mixed trades.
B) a Commercial School for office and commercial employees, male and female.
Classes will begin on 2 September this year at 7 p.m.
Days of instruction: Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays.
Employers and parents of juvenile workers not registered within the said period will be held liable as for evasion of compulsory schooling.
THE MAGISTRATE.

PUBLIC CLARIFICATION
To my great regret and against my will I am nevertheless compelled to publish
the following:
As long as I hoped that my son Jakub Eli Gutman would stop
his ignoble chicanery and ugly abuse against me and my eldest son Nachman
Aharon, I kept silent, wishing to avoid publicity; but since Jakub Eli
Gutman does not stop his "fine deeds", I declare publicly that all the
complaints spread by my son Jakub Eli of Będzin against his brother Nachman Aharon of
Dąbrowa — that he swindled me out of my house in Będzin at 3 Maja 11 without any
money — are lies and falsehood and have only one aim: to disgrace him in order to extort
money from him. I declare that my son Nachman Aharon bought my house in Bę-
dzin from me — at my express request, after many repeated
demands — entirely legally, paying me the requested sum in full,
thereby saving me from a great disgrace[?], and he prevented my property from
going to auction by various creditors. Even though he
paid the full sum, my dear son Nachman Aharon also secured for me regu-
larly the entire income from the house for my whole life, thereby en-
abling me to go on living in dignity, and he also gave me a mortgage sum of eight
thousand zł that was due to him. — I must further stress with pain that my
son Jakub Eli, through his [—] threats, desecrates the holy commandment of
"honour thy father". On this occasion I thank with all my heart my faithful son Nachman Aharon
for everything he has always fulfilled with great love until now, and he continues
to fulfil his duties of "honouring the father". May my dear son Nachman Aharon find in my fatherly
thanks for his kindness to me, known everywhere, satisfaction for the shame-
ful slanders that his brother Jakub Eli spreads so irresponsibly.
I must with pain publicly brand the deeds of my son Jakub Eli against my best child Nachman
Aharon as ugly, groundless slander, which by its
baseness and filth is shortening my days.
I publicly demand of my son Jakub Eli that he leave me, my son Nachman
Aharon and my whole family in peace and not defile our good
name.
Zelig Gutman.

Yizkor / In the Days of Remembrance

[Palestine — Keren Kayemet LeIsrael (JNF); anniversary of the 1929 riots; appeal.]
May the people of Israel remember the holy heroes who gave their lives for the sanctification of God's Name, the people and the homeland in the events of Av 5689 in the Land of Israel.
In the Days of Remembrance
The Jewish people has remembered the days of the month of Av of last year, in which its heroes and martyrs fell for the sanctification of God's Name and the sanctification of the Land, as one of the hardest trials with which the builders of the Jewish Yishuv in the Land of Israel were tested. But it must remember them not only as days of mourning, but also as great days, in which the pioneers of the people withstood the trial and, with their courage and their faith in their holy mission, repelled the hand that was raised for destruction and devastation, and saved our honour and our great cause from annihilation.
The hard trial did not weaken the hands of the people; on the contrary, it made still stronger its confidence in its emissaries, who proved that they can not only build but also defend with their blood what has been built. The great upsurge, the extraordinary awakening that arose in all the Jewish communities after the events, an awakening of faith and hope that has not ceased to this day — all this shows[?] what a feeling of love and reverence the people has for its dear heroes and martyrs.
Now, at the anniversary of the sad events, let the days of remembrance become days of new awakening for the building of the Land and the redemption of the soil — days of consecration[?] and love for all those who gave their lives for us.
The campaign that we proclaim for the days 23—29 Av (16—23/8/30) aims to extend the Yishuv, especially the land areas of the destroyed places, in order to enlarge the Yishuv in them and to strengthen and increase the security of their inhabitants.
Only with these concrete deeds for new values[?] of the Yishuv, deeds that will be bound up with our dear victims — shall we sanctify their memory.
For this they lived and for this they died!
Let us all, then, young and old, all strata of the people, take part in the great campaign, which will in part atone for the blood of the fallen and show that it was not shed in vain!
Let us in these solemn days manifest the will of the people, which remains unshaken, to build its national home!
Let no one be missing with his donation for the work of the redemption of the Land!
Honour to the fallen and help to the builders!
Keren Kayemet LeIsrael
— Central Office for Poland.
Letters to the Editor

[Będzin — letters to the editor: „Hashomer Haleumi"; „Hakoach" and the Palestine motorcyclists.]
I.
Dear Mr. Editor!
Allow us to print the following lines in your esteemed newspaper:
In connection with the note that appeared in your esteemed newspaper last Saturday under the heading „To the Address of Hashomer Hatzair[?]", we have the honour to state the following:
It is not true that we fixed the festive opening of our summer camp on the day of Tisha B'Av; rather on the „Tisha B'Av" of August [the 9th of August], i.e. „alush"[?], when according to Jewish law there is no longer any mourning. We believe, however, that a misunderstanding arose because, although the celebration took place in August, it nevertheless had to be dated by the European date of that day. At the same time we regret the fact that we Shomrim were suspected of arranging festivities on the day of our national destruction, which we mourn just as we celebrate our national holidays.
We hope that you will bring this statement of ours to public knowledge.
We sign with Shomrim greetings,
Hazak ve-ematz!
Jewish Scout Organisation
„Hashomer Haleumi", Będzin.
II.
Esteemed Editors!
I ask you kindly to publish the following lines addressed to the board of „Hakoach".
As a member of „Hakoach" I take the liberty of publicly protesting that the official language at the academy (gala evening) in honour of the Palestine motorcyclists was not Hebrew, not Yiddish, but Polish.
Even the translation of Engineer Moravis's[?] Hebrew speech for the Jewish public — mostly ordinary Jews — the board „honoured" us with in Polish.
Only after the intervention did Dr. Rechtman switch to Yiddish — whereas the official closing was held precisely in the „Polish language".
Respectfully,
A. Diament.
What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — short news items.]
The Fight Between the „Polish“ and the German „Yahudim“ in Königshütte.
In Königshütte [Królewska Huta, today Chorzów] „worlds“[?] are turning over. A dispute has flared up between the large community of „Polish“ Jews and the small handful of German „Yahudim“ [a mocking name for German-speaking Jews], who form[?] a majority on the community board;
The fire broke out because of... butter — not while frying, God forbid, but only because of a hechsher [kashrut certificate] which the universally beloved gaon Rabbi R' Yosele Blumenfeld gave to a certain firm of coconut butter.
When the local „German“ rabbi learned of this, he intervened with the kehilla board, and the latter decided to react in the sharpest manner against the „accursed deed“[?].
The decision was that they, the community heads, sent Rabbi Blumenfeld an ultimatum, in which it was stated that if Rabbi Blumenfeld continues to occupy himself with issuing hechsherim, he is dismissed from the rabbinical office.
When the „Polish“ Jews learned of such a severe ruling, they declared war on the board, and they are collecting signatures for a rabbinical contract [ktav rabbanut] for Rabbi Blumenfeld.
How the incident will end is hard to foresee; meanwhile the little Jewish world in Königshütte is boiling.
—o—
Took 11,200 zł. and Ran Away.
The collector of the joint-stock company „Perun“ collected 11,200 zł. from several firms and has fled.
—o—
The Katowice Opera — Liquidated.
All the attempts to keep the opera in Katowice going have failed, and the opera is being liquidated.
In the coming theatre season dramas and vaudevilles will be performed in the Polish theatre in Katowice; for this purpose significant dramatic talents have been engaged.
Mr. Miller of Warsaw has been engaged as director.
—o—
Pickpockets Arrested.
At the railway station in Katowice several pickpockets who had been „working“ at the station were arrested.
The arrested men are from Radom and Zawodzie.
—o—
Get Water Ready.
This Saturday, from 8 in the evening until Sunday at 12 noon, the water supply in Katowice will not be operating.
—o—
A Terrible Accident.
In Kościuszko Park in Katowice the attendant of the menagerie, Mr. Dziubak [?], fell onto the antlers of a deer. Dziubak received a mortal wound in the abdomen; on the way to hospital he died.
—o—
Death of an Alcoholic.
On Piłsudski Street in Katowice the 50-year-old unemployed man Gawak[?] was found dead. Doctors established that death was caused by drinking too much alcohol.
—o—
A Building Disaster.
In Königshütte, on Sienkiewicza Street, a scaffolding 12 metres high collapsed.
Several workers were working on the scaffolding, and they were seriously injured.
From Sport.

[Sport — football.]
„Sosnowiec“ — „Maccabi“ 0:5 (0:3)
The championship match between the above-mentioned teams [drużyny], which was at the same time the last of the season, ended with an undeserved defeat of the Maccabi. The Sosnowiec club, despite its great superiority, lost, and „Sosnowiec“ came out as winner. The reason for the defeat is to be sought in the very weak goalkeeper Kimelman, who „excellently“ let in all the balls... Already in the first minutes the „Maccabi“ players begin to attack the opposing goal hard. The best chances, however, are not used, because of the small shooting power of the „Maccabi“ forwards. „Sosnowiec“ has more luck, and with the assistance of Kimelman they score three goals. After the change of ends the „Maccabi“ men have more of the game, but the goals are shot by „Sosnowiec“. The goals for the latter were scored by: Cichoń K., Czarnała[?], Żudek III and Bergiel 2. The best on the field were: the halves of „Maccabi“: Schmidt, Jakubowicz and Galański; of „Sosnowiec“ the goalkeeper Girek.
„Wiktoria“ — „Warta“ (Zawiercie) 1:5 (1:1)
Both clubs had fought their way to the championships of their groups and last Sunday played for the voivodeship championship. „Warta“ is a team physically weakly developed, but possesses a fine technique, with which it [kept busy?] the Sosnowiec players. „Wiktoria“, on the other hand, has physically strongly developed players, and with that strength they forced the guests to capitulate. In the first half the guests play very nicely and have a slight superiority. In the 15th minute Makuła shoots the only and finest goal of the day. The Sosnowiec players set to work and equalise through Marusłan[?] in the 23rd minute. The same player had missed an „eleven“ [penalty] a few minutes earlier. After the interval the guests do not recover, and „Wiktoria“ shoots four more goals through Stanisławski 2 and Kunacki[?] 2. The best on the field were: Makuła and Gmażusz[?]. Of „Wiktoria“: Stolarski, Skaros, Kapała. Referee Mr. Scherer (Jug.) of Częstochowa very good.
„Shtern“ (Sosnowiec) — „Kraft“ (Będzin) 2:2 (1:2)
Because of the wet ground, neither team was able to show its skills. The goals for „Shtern“ were scored by Kleinman and Wladyzimerski[?] I; for the Będzin side, Glazer and Weller.
