The Reception in Będzin and Sosnowiec for the Eretz Israel Motorcyclists

On Friday a telegraphic message reached Będzin that the Eretz Israel motorcyclists, who have made such a heroic journey, would come to Będzin on Tuesday.
The board of „Hakoach“ set up a reception committee, which in great haste announced [?] the programme of the reception and called on the entire Jewish population to leave their daily business and welcome the guests.
The time of the reception was set for 11 in the morning. The public, numbering many hundreds of people — from all classes — answered the call of „Hakoach“ and went off to Gzichów, to the reception point.
But the people lost their patience from waiting so long; hours went by, messengers ran back and forth, and „there was no voice and none answered“. Only at 3 in the afternoon did the news arrive that the motorcyclists were not yet even in Siewierz. Hearing this, the public began to wander back home, and the impression was ruined.
The same expectation took place in Sosnowiec too. There the motorcyclists were supposed to arrive at 1 o'clock midday. Already from 12 the corner of Małachowskiego and Trzeciego Maja [3 May] streets was besieged with people; mounted police kept order, and the tension was great.
At 4 in the afternoon the motorcyclists arrived. At the reception place in Gzichów the „Hakoach“ orchestra played the Polish and the Jewish anthem, and after the greetings of Dr. Weinzieher and Dr. Rechtman the motorcyclists set off again on their way and, in great haste, like an army in retreat, rode through the Old Market, and from there along Małachowskiego Street to Sosnowiec.
This dash through the town made a very bad impression.
„In order“ [printed: פרי] „to enlarge the break“ [Hebrew phrase, ironic], several groups of „Hakoach“, with the orchestra at their head, then marched through several streets...
In Sosnowiec the guests were received at the premises of „Maccabi“, where they were greeted, and afterwards went to the Hotel „Agnielski“ to a lunch specially prepared by „Maccabi“.
In the evening the motorcyclists returned to Będzin, where they visited Mr. Fürstenberg's zinc factory; after that a reception was held for them.
The motorcycles were parked in Fürstenberg's garage, and the guests drove in cars to the premises of „Hakoach“, where they were welcomed by the „Hakoach“ members.
A speech of welcome was also given by Mr. S. Fürstenberg, who expressed his wish to rejoice together again at the Olympiad in Eretz Israel.
As we are informed, an „academy“ (festive evening) was also held at „Gawaszczy“ [?], which went on until 2 at night.
After the academy the guests had supper at Mr. Friedler's restaurant.
On Wednesday the motorcyclists visited the starosta (district head).
After lunch at Mr. Fürstenberg's, the Maccabi riders left for Bielitz [Bielsko].
The Number of Firemen Must Be Increased

[Zagłębie — society; article.] (Why are the towns of Zagłębie indifferent to the question? — We, too, must not make light of the matter.)

It often happens in life that there are questions in which no one takes an interest and which no one deals with; people do not talk about them at all and they simply do not come into consideration — and what is characteristic is that we do not know why this is so, why the ice-cold [?] torpor and the incomprehensible apathy have crept in there.

After all, how often do people quarrel [?] among us over nothing and less than nothing, over absurdities not worth dwelling on — and yet over such ridiculous trifles, over foolish intrigues, the harmonious life between one public worker and another, between one institution and another, is disturbed.

We have fire brigades in Zagłębie; there are municipal and factory firemen, and among all of them, as a matter of course, there are no Jews. We say "as a matter of course" because it is not understood otherwise: people do not understand, and are not accustomed to the idea, that there should be Jewish firemen. That is one side of the coin; but if one turns that same coin over to the other side, it is impossible to understand why there should be no Jewish firemen, just as there are non-Jewish ones.

When we are asked one day why Jews take no part during a fire, what answer is there to give? The only answer left to give is that we do not take part in helping to put out the fire because we are not enrolled as firemen — but is that an answer? The question remains the same: why indeed are we not enrolled as firemen, so that we could rescue just as well as non-Jews?

The towns of Zagłębie have their own firemen, which consist [?] of a very minimal number of people, so that during a fire one must call to help the factories and the municipal firemen of the neighbouring towns. It goes without saying that until they get moving it takes [?] — it must take quite a while, which plays a tremendous role during a fire; we know, after all, that the red devil [?] can cause disastrous damage within minutes, and that is precisely why the towns must have enlarged and strengthened fire brigades. And here the question arises: can the municipal firemen in Zagłębie be enlarged, and how can this be done? They will surely say that they are [?] represented, and that since a considerable number of Jews live in the towns, they too should take part in this public action, which is a necessity of the first order. And it may turn out otherwise: it may be that they will not let us in, for we have more than once had occasion to hear that when a few Jews were there, relations were far from friendly, so that the Jews were pushed out or had to give up this assistance — so strained were the relations.

And therefore — we do not know; perhaps other relations prevail there now, perhaps we will now be welcomed with both hands, perhaps it is understood that our help is needed — and from the neighbours' side we are held guilty of a wrong for not enrolling as firemen.

This is, after all, an institution that need not distinguish between Jew and Christian; the red rooster [fire] likewise makes no distinction between Jewish and non-Jewish property, and therefore we must take part in this matter just as well as our non-Jewish neighbours. For we know how it is and can be with them: as long as we do not join them, they will reproach us during a fire on the Jewish side, asking why they must rescue and go into the fire for Jewish property while we stand at a distance and look on — and in that case they are indeed right, because this is an emergency service ["pogotowie"], in which we must take part just as they do, for the towns are inhabited by Jews just as by non-Jews. The municipal fire brigades are absolutely too small in number and too weak in strength; at any price they must be enlarged — in Będzin as well as in Sosnowiec, in Zawiercie as well as in Dąbrowa. In the worst case one could, for the time being, forgo Dąbrowa, because there the coal mines are located in the town itself in considerable number, so that in an emergency the mine firemen turn out quickly enough and in large numbers; in the towns mentioned above, however, an enlargement drive must be carried out, made up of Jewish forces.

One cannot know — perhaps there are people there who at no price want to let the Jewish force in; in that case we must see either to getting in there, or, if not, separate Jewish fire brigades should be created, which will undoubtedly be supported by the municipal authorities.

We believe that we could even undertake to set up separate fire organisations should we need to, because we do not want Christians to reproach us that during a fire we hide and wait for them to rescue us — which is indeed true, for how can one go into a fire when one has nothing, knows nothing and can do nothing.

We have, after all, a youth today that is afraid of nothing and fears no one and nothing — so it can surely be taught the craft of climbing ladders and putting out fires.

We must therefore consider the question seriously and reflect that this is not some entertainment or luxury institution; a fire brigade is an emergency service, a rescue institution, in which a sacred duty rests upon us to take part, and should this not be made possible, we must go to the furthest step, and that is to create our own fire brigade units.

We know that at the present moment such an undertaking involves considerable expense; but, first, one must dwell on the necessity of such a unit, and second, we do have our representatives in the municipal institutions, who can bring us much, much benefit in the creation of Jewish fire brigades, which will come into being thanks to necessity [?], thanks to far-sighted prudence — a matter on which one must at long last dwell and which must be considered seriously and with full attention.

We must not remain indifferent to this important question; we must see to it, first, that the fire brigades in the towns are enlarged, and second, that they are not "Judenrein" [free of Jews], especially when our help is also needed.
R. Les.
With the Left Hand

[Będzin — town life; satirical poem.] (On the opening of the new park on the Old Market.)

On the Old Market
there once was a "market-
stall" scene, hats, haberdashery,
a hubbub, full the whole
"periphery";
crowds of "Ślązaks" [Silesians] stream in,
the urchins [?] spin around them:
"Buying shoes, sir, coats?"
"We'll treat you well,"
"no complaints,"
"we'll pay 'na mahna'" [?] —
it was all "all right,"
heads were spinning.
Bills of exchange were written, [?]
with due dates without end —
until the city fathers came
and cleared away the "rags" —
Lord of Abraham!
Where is my shop?
My stand has vanished!
cries Reb Sender in despair.
—
Green treetops, flowers growing
just like in the "Saxon" Garden,
benches to sit on — in plenty,
in the middle — water spurts
from below upward:
a real fountain with a basin —
there's something to see.
Boys, girls, old folks
take a rest — they have time,
they sigh, they groan, they gaze at the signboards
where long ago one once earned [?]
a gulden.
* * *
On the Old Market
there once was a market,
stalls, hats, haberdashery —
an end to the whole "periphery"...
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion (Ekev)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings and remarks on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and adapted by Y. L.
Parashat Ekev
—o—
a) "And it shall come to pass, because (ekev) you hearken" (Deut. 7:12)
God says this to the Jews: "Vehaya ekev — the end will come anyway (ekev also means: end), that — you shall hearken": in the end you will have to listen to God's word after all; they will not stop tormenting and refining you until you become good and pious. And if so, then be good right away, and you will spare yourselves the blows and beatings, the many torments of exile...
[From? — printed "פארן"] the Rebbe of Kotsk.
—o—
b) "You shall be blessed above all peoples" (Deut. 7:14)
You will be renowned among all nations. "The evil angel must answer Amen against his will." Even the enemies of the Jews will have to acknowledge Jewish greatness.
Rabbati.
—o—
c) "A land of brooks of water... a land wherein you shall eat bread without scarceness" (Deut. 8:7–9)
One of the gentile scholars, in a dispute with me, laughed at the praise with which the Land of Israel is extolled: a land of bread and water? Does it possess gold, silver? — When a land is blessed with gold mines or the like [?], it deserves to be praised, but not for bread and water.
I answered him: a land with gold mines does not make its inhabitants happy at all — "he who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver" — and the chase after gold ends in the abyss. Happier is a land that blesses its citizens with bread and water, with the most modest and healthiest things of nature, which do not bring with them a frenzied chase after luxury.
Tiferet Yehonatan.
—o—
d) "And you shall eat and be satisfied, and bless" (Deut. 8:10)
R' Yeshayele Prager [?] was once asked: why is it that for prayer, to be counted as a minyan, it is enough if there are [?] only six people praying, while for Grace after Meals there must be "seven who have eaten," seven fellow diners [?], and only then are they counted as a minyan to say "Elokeinu" — why must there be one more at eating than at praying?
— Well — answered R' Yeshayele — what harm does it do you if one more Jew eats?..
—o—
e) "And you say in your heart: My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth" (Deut. 8:17)
A person imagines: "the might of my hand" — the fact that I keep my hand shut and give nobody a penny of charity — that is how "it got me this wealth," that is how I amassed a fortune. Yet from giving [?] no one has ever become poor — from helping another.
Yalkut Margaliyot.
* * *
The Maggid of Dubno once came to a town. He was told that a great rich man lived there, who however kept his hand tightly shut and never gave out a penny of charity. The Maggid wasted no time and went to visit him. The rich miser asked him: what have you come to me for?
— I heard that you are ill, so I came to fulfil the duty of visiting the sick — answered the Maggid.
— Who told you that I am ill? — the rich man grew angry.
— King Solomon. In Ecclesiastes (5) he told me so. He writes there: "A man to whom God has given riches and wealth, yet God gives him no power to eat thereof — this is vanity and an evil disease" (the man to whom God has given great riches and a fortune, and he does not have the mastery over it to eat himself and give to others — that is foolishness and a bad illness). You too do not allow yourself anything and give nothing to anyone else, thinking to amass even more wealth — so you are badly ill, as Solomon says.
— Fine — says the rich man, seeing how the Maggid of Dubno had cornered him [?] — you came to visit me as a sick man, very nice of you. But you have already fulfilled the commandment of visiting the sick, and you may go now...
— When one comes to visit a sick person — answered the Maggid — the Gemara says (Nedarim 39) that one takes away a sixtieth part of the illness. Your illness is money, after all — so I too want to take away a sixtieth part of your illness...
* * *
In Słonim there was a wealthy Jew who had a principle of giving charity only to a cripple, but to a poor Torah scholar he would not give a penny. R' Eizikl said to him: you give charity to a cripple because you are afraid that one day you yourself may become a cripple, God forbid, and then people should have pity on you too. But as for a Torah scholar — you are sure you will never become one...
—o—
f) "You shall fear the Lord your God" (printed 6:20; read Deut. 10:20)
On this it is expounded: "Et — to include Torah scholars" (that one must stand in awe of a Torah scholar as of God). And in the name of various great men it is further said: et, to include Torah scholars — Torah scholars too must fear God..
—o—
"And to Him shall you cleave" (Deut. 10:20)
The Rebbe of Ger met Rabbi Kook in the Land of Israel. The latter is known for his mild treatment of the irreligious. Nevertheless the Rebbe of Ger reproached him: you are, after all — he said to him — one who "extends a hand to transgressors"..
Rabbi Kook answered him right on the spot: — On the verse "and to Him shall you cleave" the Gemara asks: is it then possible to cleave to God? It only means: cleave to His attributes — adopt God's attributes: just as He is merciful, so be you merciful, etc. — So by this I too am adopting one of God's attributes, since of God it is said: "You extend a hand to transgressors"...
—o—
h) "And all the substance that followed them (lit. at their feet)" (printed 10:6 [?]; read Deut. 11:6)
The homily says on this: "This is a man's money, which stands him on his feet" — money puts a person on his feet.
Maimonides counts four qualities in a person: wisdom, strength, character traits, wealth. Wisdom is located in the brain, strength — in the heart, character traits too; wealth — under the feet. Is it then worth more than the dust under one's feet? So the other virtues are inside the person, and wealth outside the person, under the feet. A person ought therefore to be able to master money more than anything else — it lies under his feet, after all; but money rises up from the ground and overpowers the person. That is why it is called "yekum" — rising against, uprising.
Kli Yakar.
—o—
Avot, Chapter Five.
"The brazen-faced to Gehenna... May it be Your will that the Temple be rebuilt" (printed: Mishnah 5)
It is said: "In the footsteps of the Messiah, insolence will increase" — in the Messiah's times there will be many brazen-faced people. That is why Yehuda ben Tema, when he saw so many brazen-faced people in his generation, said: may it be Your will that the Temple be rebuilt — if there are so many insolent people around, the Messiah may as well come already...
Tsenuyot [?] Berakhah.
Concerns of the Time

[Opinion — Jewish schooling.] In two weeks' time the school year begins.
For the Pole, the German, the Frenchman this is settled without any upheaval. He enrolls his child in the school of his own nationality, where lessons are given in the language he speaks — the language of his culture.
We Jews for many years had no schools like the Pole, the German or the Frenchman. The Tsarist power did not permit it. It was interested in assimilating us, mixing us into the Russian population, so that we should drown in the remaining 180-million sea of the mixed population, be swallowed up in it, so that no memory of us should remain; we were compelled by force to educate our children in the foreign-language, Russified school.
And not only we alone: the Pole too, the Latvian, the Lithuanian, the Armenian, the Kalmyk, the Tatar and all the other 40 nationalities of great Tsarist Russia suffered the same troubles. All of them, together with us, Tsarism wanted to boil down in one cauldron, so that our national distinctiveness should vanish and we should be the assimilation-meat for the reactionary autocratic policy of showing the world that Russia — that enormous land — consists of one nation of "Great Russians".
Then came the great Russian revolution and put an end to this Tsarist policy of oppressing peoples and their national cultures. In present-day Russia the 40 national minorities send their children to their own national schools with state rights, where the language of instruction is the language of their own cultures.
Poland, too, belongs to the liberated and revived states where the Jewish minority has been given the possibility of educating its children in its own school, in Yiddish. Unfortunately, however, for the time being only the possibility, but not yet the state rights that such schools need.
Here in Poland the governments have not been consistent to the end. Giving us the possibility of having our own schools, they could not reconcile themselves to the idea that these schools must also be given state maintenance, i.e. rights and a subsidy. And even today, 11 years after the liberation of Poland, her state factors still find it hard to reconcile themselves to such an idea.
And a contradiction has arisen: the very same Poland that together with us Jews waged the common struggle against Tsarism for the right to live according to our national cultures — that same Poland, when she was at last liberated herself, did not at once have the courage to renounce once and for all the bad habits and remnants of the Tsarist times, leaving behind in herself a little wild grass from that servile epoch. She gave us Jews permission for our own schools, i.e. a kind of "licence", but with rights she still keeps us waiting.
So we have had to carry the Jewish school system on our own shoulders. We carry it still now and will go on carrying it for a long time yet, with faith and hope that in the end there will come — must come — that happy day when liberated Poland will at last tear off from herself entirely the mould of bad habits, the result of a hundred years of enslavement, and will finally right the wrongs she commits against the Jewish school system. She will give the Jewish school system its full, deserved, hundred-percent possibility of existence: rights and a subsidy.
But for this to become reality, and the sooner the better, much depends on ourselves too.
We must see to the broadening and spreading of our school fact, to its strengthening and its growth.
This can happen by enrolling our children in the Jewish schools!
The more children we enroll, the more schools we shall need; and the more schools we have, the more the edifice of our school fact will grow, until it reaches such a level that the government will by no means be able to avoid it any longer.
That is self-evident.
Therefore those who avoid enrolling their children in the Jewish schools commit a sin: they thereby weaken the very fact of a Jewish school existence, giving the government, with their own hands, a pretext to drag out and delay the rights for the Jewish school.
A Jew.
"Gather Us Together"... (An Overheard Conversation)

[Feuilleton — Będzin traders.] After prayers.
The congregation quickly folds up tallit and tefillin — and splits up: some to their business, some to the inns — to snatch a fresh guest who will do them the honour and allow them to deposit some goods with him without lodging-money... and some to the notary (rejent) — to snatch at 9 o'clock the dying bill of exchange...
Three or four Jews who were late for "communal prayer" hurry to finish praying as fast as possible: one is still at "the front" [the beginning of the service], the second folds his tallit and gulps down the "Uva le-Tziyon" like a hungry man his blintzes, the third "finishes" the Shemoneh Esreh and falls on his face for Tachanun...
Meanwhile a chat is snatched about this and that: protests, sequestrations, prolongations...
— You say — it's bad! Bad, is it?! It's simply unbearable! argues the one who is at "the front", chanting [?] as if the blood were being squeezed from under his nails:
"Eizehu mekoman shel zevachim, kodshei kodashim shechitatan" — at the "Izba Skarbowa" [Treasury Office] they do whatever they like! Do they care, apparently, what is going on in town? "Parim ha-nisrafim u-se'irim ha-nisrafim" — of all of us there will be a mountain of ashes... why, it's shadows walking about — not people... Ha, what do you say? Elsewhere it's better than with us in Będzin — you are, begging your pardon, mistaken... "Mi-klal u-ferat, u-mi-perat u-klal" — everywhere it's the same wedding!... One doesn't let the other earn — and there lies the trouble! "Two verses contradicting one another" — two roosters fight — "until the third verse comes and decides between them" — along come the sequestrators and make peace, even everybody out — all together with one big beggar's bag... no aristocrats anymore!... "Show us, O Lord, Thy mercy" — the Jew groans on: "Arise, help us" — what will be the end of our poor Jews [?]!...
"Ashrei yoshvei veitecha" — it is much better by now to close the businesses — and an end to the troubles!...
— Easy to say: close the businesses! And where does one get a livelihood?! — puts in the second, who is at "Uva le-Tziyon", "It shall not depart from thy mouth, nor from the mouth of thy seed, nor from the mouth of thy seed's seed"... Our grandfathers and fathers were shopkeepers and our children will probably remain so... "U-mekablin den min den" — we have the shopkeeping as an inheritance from our great-grandfathers — and all of a sudden stop being a shopkeeper... Take a briefcase under your arm — and become an agent, or a representative of beaten hoshanot and onion skins! Easy to say: close! And where does one get so many briefcases?! And who will insure whom, if everybody becomes an agent? Shalom aleichem, agents, "Who hath not made our portion like theirs, nor our lot like all their multitude" — ptui, ptui, on such businesses...
— Now you see — closing the shop and becoming a director in a bank, a supervisor in a kehilla — that I can still understand. They lack something, apparently? And we shopkeepers?.. "Even to old age I am He, and even to hoar hairs... I will carry and I will bear" — we drag them on our shoulders... heh-heh, what faces would they have had, all those directors, if we shut our stalls? It would have been a misery for them...
— Leave them alone and don't begrudge them their luck — speaks up the third Jew, who is at "Tachanun", "Let us fall now into the hand of the Lord, but let me not fall into the hand of man" — better to have a small shop and be your own master than to be a "kehilla nag" (klaczka) and have so many people with opinions over you.
— Ech, ech, my dear Jews, everybody has it good — we can envy one another!.. Today is the sixth day of the week... hush, I quite forgot that today is Friday! I have so many payments tomorrow! [?]. Does any of you perhaps have a gemach [interest-free loan]?
— No? Well then [?]! "Gather us together"! One great poverty, one great beggar's bag! Ech—ech!...
Y.
From the Hachshara — with a Prisoner Convoy to Będzin.

In Wieluń (Łódź district), 3 months ago, right after the halting of pioneer (halutz) immigration, a training (hachshara) point of the Zagłębie pioneer youth organization „Gordonia“ was founded. That local antisemitic little town, poor thing, could not bear the Zionism, Hebraism and Palestinism of the halutzim, who became „acquainted“ with all the well-known Jew-baiting articles in the columns of the local gutter rag „Goniec Wieluński“.
This hostile anti-halutz incitement succeeded to a certain extent, and last Sabbath the „Gordonist kvutza was suddenly besieged by police“, who conducted a search, and although nothing illegal at all was found — the former chairman of „HeHalutz“ and „Gordonia“ in Będzin, the head of the hachshara, Mr. Motek Hampel, was arrested on suspicion of... communism.
The interventions of the Wieluń Zionist organization and of the town notables did not help, and Mr. Hampel — the police had not shown[?] any proof against him — was sent off under police guard to Będzin, where he was immediately released. Mr. Hampel has turned in this matter to the National Council in Warsaw as well as to the higher police authority, calling the Wieluń police commandant to account,
What Was Heard, What Was Seen.

By Ben Amotz.
The Eternal Question.
— „It is a great injustice on your part that such an important question is not touched upon in the newspaper“ — with such a preamble the owner of a large drapery (manufaktura) shop on Małachowskiego Street begins his complaint to us. For many years now — he says — an Upper Silesian firm has been cleaning our shop windows and doors. Every Thursday they come here, a few „polishers“, who give a wipe here, a wipe there, and — „the work“ is done...
— Well, what does that have to do with our newspaper? we ask.
— A great deal: week in, week out you sound the alarm in your paper about the sad Jewish situation; in serial[?] articles you rouse and appeal that Jewish society should support the Jewish institutions — but why don't you point out that we should have young people here who would do the „hard work“ for those 3 złoty a month...
At that moment, as the merchant lays out his complaints, young people come in and out, men, women of various ages, not singly — they come in fours and fives: today is Rosh Chodesh, the „money day“ for the army of beggars... who multiply like frogs in water; but to polish window-panes, wash laundry and other occupations — there are non-Jews...
— The eternal question...
———
Mandoszew[?] Street Is Offended.
Once, when the lane was called the „dead lane“, its residents did not feel[?] offended by such „ethical“ expressions; but today, when the finest buildings, commercial halls and the like are being put up on the street, the moral sermon has aroused great bitterness.
A Jew died, a God-fearing man, who worked hard and bitterly for his livelihood, lived by the labour of his hands until he departed to the World of Truth.
As is the custom, „after death — holy“: after death they „made a fuss“ over the deceased, recited his praises and — made circuits (hakafot) with him...
Among those honoured was of course also a representative of the „Chizuk HaDat“ society; here the society has a broad field for its work, nobody interferes — and the „Chizuk HaDat“ representative stopped by the deceased and delivered this eulogy:
„Yaakov Shie! You lived, after all, on Magdrushev[?] Street, where they desecrate the Sabbath, go to the taverns on the Sabbath, gorge and booze — see to it there that this be abolished“...
The residents of the street are perplexed; they don't know what „should be abolished“ — the street or the taverns?
— Perhaps you know what the moralist meant?...
Jews Get Pleasure...
At the cashier's window in the Będzin Magistrat there is a great crush: it is before the 1st, and the public, mostly poor Jewish women, hurries to pay their tax debts.
Among the toil-worn Jewish taxpayers there is also a peasant woman; she came to pay a few guilders of podatek (tax) on her field.
She is from the village, but she has a „town mouth“; at the time she is losing at the cash desk she is very angry and says:
— „We longed for Poland, we fought — and what have we got? Darmozjady (freeloaders) who suck the last drop of blood out of us; oh, have we got a Polska“...
The Jewish women, waiting for the gracious cashier to finally take their bloody groszy from them, shake their heads — they say, as it were, that they agree with the peasant woman...
— „Let her talk, let her — whisper her lips[?]...“
Livelihood Overrides „Hasidism“
The Jews of Dąbrowa wonder: such a thing is kept quiet? Can it be?
And they relate:
— A Jew from Jędrzejów came to Dąbrowa and planned to set up a timber business here.
The „terrible“ news reached a merchant in the timber trade, who took fright at „lest it spread“ and decided to „carry out the sentence“ on the „competitor“...
He met him, the „competitor“, on „Krótka“ (Short) Street and counted out to him one, one and two.
Well, that one Jew beats another is nowadays a „common occurrence“, a thing that happens — but that a Ger hasid should attack one of his own „anshei shlomeinu“ (fellow hasidim)?..
Truly a very „important“ question, but when it comes to a li—ve—lihood, that overrides even Ger Hasidism...
A Cantor with a „Hechsher“.
Będzin, the town which possesses a rich number of „wise and understanding men“, has begun a koshering campaign of the sacred vessels.
The first to be taken for koshering is the cantor, because that is what the 4th „Zvad“[?] demands and orders.
The „strong hand“[?] in the Będzin synagogue was founded in the days of the rabbinical elections; at that time the „synagogue legion“ took over power, and without its permission nobody dared to go up on the bimah to say a few words about the rabbinical elections.
The „Zvad“, under the sign of the „Gmina-Belweder“ (kehilla-Belvedere), cast a [?] on the cantor, because he, the cantor that is, does not wear a shtreimel, does not use a red handkerchief for his nose, etc. — and they came to the rabbinate and said:
— „Rebbe, the cantor needs a hechsher“...
And when the „Fourth Zvad“ speaks one must listen to them, and out came an order:
— „Zawiesić the śpiewak“ (suspend the singer)...
The order will go around beyond the borders of Zagłębie and of the „clever“ town of Będzin. The world will suddenly learn that a cantor need not possess any high „C“, any sweetness, need not know any interpretation of the words, only
— he must have a hechsher from the „4th Zvad“...
After all, a cantor is no worse than outside shechita, machine-made matzot and matzah meal...
The Kehilla Budget "Rests" in Kielce... / In 3 Weeks the Budget Will Be Revealed

[Będzin — Kehilla.]
Since the kehilla budget for 1930 has not yet come back approved by the authorities, the gmina (Jewish community) delegated its secretary, Mr. Frejlich, to Kielce, where it was explained to him that the budget is already back from the Ministry at the voivodeship, and only in 3 weeks will the voivodeship's position on the budget become clear.
On Shabbat Nachamu the Synagogue Worshippers "Got Autonomy"...

[Będzin — Kehilla; religious life.]
Last Sabbath, during prayers, not a single member of the dozór (kehilla board) was present in the municipal synagogue. Even the vice-president in person, who had walked out after "Barchu" on Friday night as a "protest", did not come into the synagogue the next morning.
A Christian Neighbour Tried to Set Fire to His Jewish Neighbour's Flat

[Będzin — Crime.]
In the night from Saturday to Sunday a window-pane was smashed in the flat of Szmul Rotenberg on Czeladzka Street, and through it a small bottle of kerosene and a bundle of burning paper were thrown in.
In the room into which the fire was thrown a 3-year-old girl was asleep. Luckily another child came in, saw that the room was full of smoke and raised an alarm; thanks to this the fire was put out and the sleeping child was rescued from great danger.
Suspicion fell on a young Christian, a neighbour of Rotenberg, who had wanted to commit the deed out of revenge. The Christian was arrested on the order of the investigating judge.
Now That's What You Call a Faithful Husband...

[Czeladź — General.]
In Czeladź a certain Czarniecki stabbed himself in the chest with a knife and was seriously wounded.
The reason for the suicide [attempt] is that the hospital staff did not allow him to visit his sick wife.
"Heroic" Worshippers in the "Mizrachi" Minyan

[Będzin — Religious life.]
The "Mizrachi" organisation has had a minyan for many years. Some of the worshippers are recruited from among the well-known young fellows who, although they have already "[?]" [broken away] from the Ger shtibl, still have the "Hasidic fervour" smouldering in them, which flares up at certain "national" moments.
Thus, for instance, we are told that in this minyan, during the recitation of Eikhah on the last Tisha b'Av, a regular fight took place; little was missing for Tisha b'Av to become a very sad one indeed...
Also last Sabbath a member of this minyan, a young fellow with the "Ger fire", threw himself at one of the worshippers to beat him. Had it not been for the intervention of some worshippers, Shabbat Nachamu would have looked the same as Tisha b'Av...
When One Is Drunk, One Climbs Smooth Walls

[Będzin — Crime.]
Several young Jewish men went into a tavern, gulped down a few glasses too many, then went out into the street and began to make merry: they tore down signboards, banged on doors, etc.
The police led the merry company off to the commissariat, where they spent the night, and when day broke each of them paid 5 zł for the "hotel"...
Working Days in the Coal Mines Will Be Extended

[Zagłębie — Economy and labour.]
We are informed by authoritative circles that the coal mines have recently received larger orders for coal; on account of this the working days are to be extended to 6 days a week.
Ehrenfried's Children Have Responded

[Będzin — General.]
In the previous issue of our paper we published in a note the request of Jekl Ehrenfried of Düsseldorf, who is looking for his children in Będzin.
Through the note the children responded and turned to their long-sought father.
From the Zionist-Revisionist Movement

[Będzin — Zionism.]
Last Sabbath, in a packed hall, a discussion took place devoted to the tasks of the Revisionist World Conference in Prague.
This Sabbath afternoon a discussion meeting will be held, at which the following will be dealt with: 1) the bloody events in Eretz Israel in the month of Av 5689 [August 1929]; 2) should the Jewish language [Yiddish] be insulted at academies [commemorative gatherings]?
———
On the Sabbath, after the Torah reading, Nute Landner delivered a speech in the town synagogue devoted to the martyrs of Eretz Israel.
Poisoned by Sausage.

[Sosnowiec — food poisoning.]
A certain Christian family from Sosnowiec was staying at a summer residence in Paradusheniec [?; unidentified place, apparently near Olkusz]. Suddenly the whole family, which consisted of seven persons, fell ill with terrible stomach pains; the sick were taken to Olkusz, where one child of the family soon died.
Dr. Garczyk [Gorczyk?], who wanted to find out the cause of the child's sudden death and of the family's illness, performed an autopsy on the child and sent a piece of the stomach to Kraków for analysis.
In Kraków it was established that the family had fallen ill from eating sausage that had been bought in Wolbrom.
The next morning a female clerk of the factory “Fitzner and Gamper”, who had also eaten of that sausage, died as well.
The sick are under treatment in the Sosnowiec hospital.
They Left the Child with the Brother-in-Law...

[Rabsztyn — accident.]
The Kamara family came to Rabsztyn from Mys-khov [? perhaps Myszków or Mysłów], and left a little boy of 3 years old with their brother-in-law in Rabsztyn.
While the child was playing on the railway line, a passenger train passed through and tore the child to pieces.
Bandit Attack beyond Wolbrom.

[Wolbrom — crime.]
On the Wolbrom–Pilica road masked bandits attacked the Wolbrom resident Kuta [?], from whom the bandits, threatening with revolvers, robbed 470 zł.
Which German Banknotes Are Valid?

[Economy — currency.]
The German Rentenbank in Berlin announces: the following banknotes have full value as means of payment: 1,000, 500 and 100 German marks without a picture, bearing the date 1 November 1923; 50 marks with a peasant's head, dated 20 March 1925; 10 marks with a picture of a peasant woman, dated 3 July 1925; 5 marks with a picture of a village girl, dated 2 January 1926.
Reb Pesach Has “Made a Pilgrimage”...

[Będzin — economy.]
This week Reb Pesach S. vanished from here; he had “run” a series of firms in the “Turkish” manner...
The “Comers-and-Goers Team” in the Kehilla.

[Sosnowiec — kehilla.]
As our readers know, a few weeks ago Mr. Y. M. Weigreb [?] was elected president of the kehilla, and Mr. L. Jungster was recognized [?] as a board member.
The starosta [district head] challenged the resolutions and authorized Mr. Zendel to continue to conduct the affairs of the kehilla.
But despite this, on Sunday a meeting of the kehilla board was held, which adopted a series of resolutions; a commission was also elected, consisting of Messrs. Abramczyk, Jungster and Saks, whose task is to put in order the synagogues on Dekerta Street and in Old Sosnowiec.
A Cooperative Burgled.

[Sosnowiec — crime.]
By breaking in, thieves crept into the cooperative shop of “Gr. Renard” [the Renard mining company in Sosnowiec]. The thieves took a large quantity of tea, cigarettes (papierosy) and other articles.
The Fate of the Polish Theatre

[Sosnowiec — culture.] The dispute over the local Polish theatre in Sosnowiec has been settled; the well-known actor Mr. Tański has been „appointed director of the theatre.
The performances will begin on the 15th of next month.
Credits for Artisans Will Be Allotted Next Week

[Sosnowiec — economy, artisans.] Artisans who wish to benefit from the credits allocated by the bank „Gosp. Krajowego" [Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego] must submit applications as soon as possible to the Communal Savings Bank in Będzin, because the deadline for accepting applications ends in the course of this week.
Next week the amounts of the credits granted will already be determined.
Proposals for the New Timetable

[Sosnowiec — commerce, transport.] The local merchants' institutions have been requested by the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce that the boards of these institutions put forward their proposals on how to improve the coming (railway) timetable.
The 2nd Advance Payment of the Turnover Tax

[Sosnowiec — taxes.] The 2nd advance payment (zaliczka) of the turnover tax must be paid by today, Friday the 15th of this month. Since today is a (Christian) holiday, after the deadline one will already have to pay with a penalty.
A Landlord "Pays" His Tenant

[Sosnowiec — violence.] The landlord Mr. P. on Ostrogórska Street "treated" a Jewish woman, a tenant in his house, to heavy blows, because she had had the "chutzpah" to take water in the courtyard without the landlord's permission.
108 New Flats Will Be Added

[Sosnowiec — construction, housing.] The Insurance Company for Officials (white-collar employees) in Königshütte [Królewska Huta, today Chorzów] has already concluded an agreement with several building firms, which undertake to build the new workers' houses in Sosnowiec.
Altogether 108 flats will be built. The construction will cost close to one and a half million zł.
Conference to Fix the Price of Baked Goods

[Sosnowiec — prices, bakers.] In the premises of the local Magistrat (city hall) a conference took place, in which representatives of the voivodeship (województwo), the starostwo (district office), the Chamber of Commerce, the Magistrat and bakers from the towns of Zagłębie took part.
On the agenda were the bakers' complaints against the price commission.
After the discussion it was decided to send the entire material of the baked-goods cost calculation to the voivodeship, where the question is to be decided.
During the discussion the baker Wiskowski insulted the representative of the voivodeship.
A Lecture

[Sosnowiec — Zionism, lectures.] This Sabbath, a lecture by Mr. S. Gelgard [?], a medical student, will be held in the Zionist Organisation's own premises, on the topic: "The consequences among Jews of not cultivating the muscles".
Summertime

(In summer) we lose our appetite. One therefore eats [?] improperly and not enough [?], if nothing is done about it. In this way we often [?] cause a weakening of our organism. We must protect [?] against this first of all the children, who are in a stage of rapid development. In summer one should in this case use [?] first and foremost Express pudding [Budyń Ekspres], which contains refreshing salts and a fine aroma; adults [?] too taste it with full appreciation. Express pudding can also be obtained, thanks to its enormous success, always [?] fresh.
Dąbrowa. / A new tax imposed.

The voivode [?] has approved the decision of the local magistrate [town council] to levy an investment tax.
The revenue from the tax, which is projected at 50 [?] thousand zł., is earmarked for economic purposes.
Olkusz. / A dead body found.

Next Sunday the local "Maccabi" is organizing a grand event in the "Czarna Góra" park, with the participation of the following sports clubs: "Maccabi" (Sosnowiec), "Hakoach" (Będzin), "Maccabi" (Chrzanów [?]), "Hakoach" (Zawiercie), "Bar Kochba" (Katowice) and "Maccabi" (Königshütte [Chorzów]). The programme is a very rich one.
A. B.
—o—
A dead body found.
In the Olkusz forest the dead body of a young woman has been found. Judging by its condition, the body has been lying there for about a month already.
No documents whatsoever were found. The police are conducting an investigation.

A Daring Theft

On Wednesday at midday unknown persons got into the flat of Berish Wajsbart, Zawarze [?] Street in Będzin, and stole articles, clothing, etc.
The Christian maid and her fiancé, on whom suspicion rests, have been arrested.
—o—
To Settle 1,000 Jewish Families
This Saturday afternoon a meeting will be held at the Zionist premises, at which the plan of the Zionist Executive in London to settle [at once?] 1,000 Jewish families on Keren Kayemet land will be discussed.
All interested persons should attend this important meeting.
—o—
Personal
Joachim Frenkel, a pupil of the [Real?] School in Będzin, has graduated in Liège [?] (Belgium) as a mechanical engineer and electrical technician.
—o—
Campaign for the KKL
In connection with the first anniversary of the sad events of Av [the August 1929 riots], the Będzin KKL [Jewish National Fund] is holding a collection campaign this coming Sunday under the slogan "Strengthen and enlarge the Jewish edifice [?] in Eretz Israel".
Next Tuesday [evening?] the Będzin KKL [will hold?] an academy [festive evening] with the participation of several speakers from Warsaw. The programme also includes a rich artistic and musical part.
—o—
The Staniewski Circus in Sosnowiec
For several days now the Staniewski circus (1st division) has been staying in Sosnowiec.
The performances are taking place with great success thanks to the thrilling and interesting programme.
The circus will remain for another 3 days, i.e. until next Sunday.

Supplementary tax assessments

[Taxes — commerce.] There are more and more cases of merchants being charged supplementary podatki (taxes) years later, when the circumstances and calculation of the tax actually assessed have long been forgotten. The supplementary taxes are imposed by means of a supplementary assessment.
As is known, the offices (urzędy)[?] have the right, for a period of five years, to make a supplementary assessment and add a handsome dodatek (surcharge)[?]. They "realise" that 3 or 4 years ago the merchant had a larger turnover (obrót) or income (dochód).
Recently a supplementary tax has been imposed on a larger number of merchants.
There are also cases where merchants are suddenly given to understand that a supplementary tax will be made and a supplementary podatek imposed on them. This happens many[?] times when the aim is to make the merchants refrain from filing any appeals against the assessed tax.
It is therefore necessary to explain to the merchant public that making a supplementary assessment is not simply some arbitrary matter that can be applied at any time. The law and the rulings of the Supreme Administrative Tribunal have specified exactly in which cases a supplementary assessment can be made and when it cannot.
First of all, a supplementary assessment with a new supplementary tax can be made only in cases where concrete facts later come to light showing that the turnover or income was larger than was known at the time of the normal assessment.
This does not mean that if the office (urząd), after the assessment, learns of a new fact of income or turnover which it could also have known before, it may on that basis make a supplementary assessment — no!
A new assessment with a supplementary tax, even up to 5 years after the normal assessment, can be made only in cases where the office learns of such new items of turnover or income as it could not have learned of at the normal assessment — for example, the merchant had another business with income that was not known about, or he had another factory, a workshop, a house abroad, or he had side businesses and earnings, or was a silent partner in another business, etc. In such cases, when this is learned later, it means that concrete facts have come to light which could not have been learned of before.
On the other hand, no supplementary assessment can be made if it is learned from the commercial books of factories and firms that the assessed turnover was in fact larger than was taken into account at the assessment — these are not new concrete facts, since the office could have known this earlier too, before the assessment. The commercial books of the factories and firms[?] existed earlier as well and could have been checked at the proper time; if the office neglected to do so, the matter is forfeit.
Nevertheless, it is a frequent phenomenon that merchants are charged a supplementary tax on the basis of what is discovered in the commercial books — that the turnover or income was larger. In such cases one can file an appeal (rekurs) and show that these are not new concrete facts of a larger turnover.

(Addressed to the Trumpeldorites in Zawiercie.)
We thought that Madame Assimilation had been removed for ever from our public life.
Unfortunately, at every step we meet with disappointment: the "Madame" is here, she has seized our whole life, and we must say to our shame that the "Madame" is being brought in by our 100-per-cent nationalists.
The case concerning Yiddish at the gala evening in honour of the Eretz-Israel motorcyclists is not the only one among our national public workers.
We happened to read an invitation from Brit Trumpeldor in Zawiercie to a house-warming, [—] the invitation is printed exclusively in Polish — no Yiddish, no Hebrew. Assimilation in its purest form. Evidently there too, in the "Brit", the "Madame" has settled in comfortably.
— Ignorance, or national schlemiel-ism?
A. Kanai.
A Jew Inciting Against Jews...

Mr G. Frenfrid [?] of Zagórze tells us of the following incident, which took place last Tuesday in Zagórze.
In that place lives a convert (meshumedet) who went bankrupt not long ago, and for that reason her Christian husband was put into the Będzin prison. During the time of [—; apparently: his imprisonment] her own father, from Będzin, has been looking after the convert's business. The Jewish inhabitants, seeing that the father lives in peace with his apostate daughter, greet him with words of reproach.
The father received such a reception on Tuesday too, in [—] of the local Jewish inhabitants. But the father, wishing to show his patriotism, began to raise an outcry, at which a crowd of workers gathered, and then the faithful father shouted: "Jews are thieves, they cheat [?] the Christian customers," etc. Had it not been for the police, who liquidated the "meeting", the Jews of Zagórze would have received a good "lesson"...
The Question of Reducing the Penalty Interest on Payments to the Sickness Fund

On the initiative of the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce, the Union of Chambers of Commerce in Poland has taken up the question of the high percentages charged by the sickness funds as a penalty for not paying on time.
The Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce drew up a memorandum on the question, which was sent to the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare.
The Ministry's reply stresses that, given the present critical situation of the sickness funds, it is not possible for the penalty for irregular payment to be only 6 per cent, as the Chamber of Commerce proposes.
At the same time the reply stresses that under Article 54 of the law (ustawa) on the sickness funds, the management of the institution may in exceptional cases reduce the penalty, or even exempt the [licence-holder / payer?] entirely.
Sport

Jewish Sports Club Katowice — "Maccabi" (Sosnowiec) 0:4 (0:1).
The match between the above-mentioned teams, which took place in Katowice, ended in a sure victory for the home side. Especially in the second half the Katowice players were strongly superior and scored 3 fine goals.
"Sosnowiec" — "Fablok" (Chrzanów) 1:1.
The visitors, who a week earlier had beaten the champion of Zagłębie (0:4), had to bow to the well-playing "Sosnowiec". The latter had a strong advantage, [but] only because of the rainy weather could they not exploit [—?] sure positions. The only goal was scored by Bergiel. The best man on the field was the visitors' defender Ruszin, who is well known to the Zagłębie public as a player of "Zagłębie".
"Victoria" — R.K.S. (Radom) 1:1.
Despite the heavy rain the match took place. Naturally the heavy ground strongly affected the course of this championship match. The visitors from Radom proved to be good technicians, whereas "Victoria" was physically superior. The first half is quite interesting, yet nobody manages to score. The second half is livelier, and already in the 13th minute the visitors' centre-forward Pohanski [?] manages to score the first goal. "Victoria" gets down to work and in the 28th minute Chrzynacki [?] of "Victoria" makes the score 1:1. Both teams strive to change the result, but without success. 2 minutes before the end the referee awards a penalty ("eleven") for a foul. The Radom players did not agree and left the field. The referee whistles the match off. The best on the field were the visitors' goalkeeper and left winger, and the defenders Kapla-Skarus [?], Stolarski. Referee Mr Meier of Częstochowa — nothing special.
"Shimshon" (Sosn.) — "Shimshon" (Modrzejów) 1:1 (1:1).
Sosnowiec's "Shimshon" deserved the victory. The goals were scored for the home side by Steinfeld, for the visitors by the left defender from an "eleven" (penalty). Referee Lebek very weak; he had to leave the sports ground under police supervision.
"Shtern" (Sosn.) — "Saturn" (Woiksh-wik [?]) 0:3.
Only a friendly match was played, because the referee did not turn up. The Sosnowiec team did whatever they liked with their opponent.
"Kraft" (Będzin) — "Kinneret" (Sosn.) 2:3.
"Kraft" has shown once again that it belongs among the strongest clubs of the "C" class. With this victory the Będzin side has fought its way to the same number of points as "Shimshon" Modrzejów. The match itself was very interesting, and although the Sosnowiec side led 1:2, "Kraft" managed not only to equalise but also to win. Referee Mazur kept the "Kinneret" players on a "short" rein.
"Shtern" (Będzin) — "Kraft" (Dąbrowa) — "Shimshon" (Sosn.) combined 0:12.
The result speaks for itself; the combined team played weakly.

A letter to the editor.
Dear Mr. Editor!
Allow me to print in your esteemed paper the following lines concerning the "salvation" for Będzin, which is getting a fifth shochet.
At the meeting of the kehilla board on the 14th of this month, with the participation of Messrs. A. Liwer, S. Plessner, H. Goldstein and the writer of these lines Mr. Bażykowski, a resolution was adopted unanimously, with the consent of the first 3 persons, to announce at once a competition for a fifth shochet. At the meeting I lodged a protest and argued that in the present time of crisis there is no need to engage a fifth shochet with a fine pension of 10 thousand zł. a year; one need only put proper order among the shochtim, and above all the revenues from the slaughter — as was established at that same meeting, the income of recent months is smaller than last year by about a thousand zł.
The question arises: what is a fifth shochet needed for? Perhaps because, as Mr. Prawer explained to me, the fifth shochet will teach the 4 shochtim manners.. Apparently Mr. Prawer holds firmly to the saying "Nothing stands in the way of the will" — so he wants it and so it shall be; they do not even wait for the budget, which, as we have heard — has been altered — and will come back approved.
Elazar Bażykowski.

Reuven Lask, the man with two wives, confesses
In today's issue of our paper, on the third page, the story is told of Reuven Shlomo Lask, who left behind in Dąbrowa a wife with 5 children.
From the "Lubliner Togblat", which unmasked the person, we received at the last minute the following further details:
The young man will not hear of going back to his wife; on the other hand he assures that he is not out simply to run away, but wants to give her a get. With the Dąbrowa wife he only stood under the chuppah, but he never carried out a civil act. With his present wife too he did not carry out a civil act. But it is also not clear whether he did stand under the chuppah with her, because in such a case he could face a trial for bigamy, and the officiant of the marriage would also be punished by law.
The young man declares that he is preparing to leave for Argentina, but he wants first to divorce his Dąbrowa wife; he therefore went to the Lublin rabbinate, but they pointed out to him that such matters are not settled in absentia [?], and that he must therefore bring his Dąbrowa wife down to Lublin. The young man assures that, although he earns no livelihood in Lublin, he will nevertheless postpone his journey to Argentina until he has settled the get with his Dąbrowa wife.

The German Uproar

Because of the great uproar that Germany has now provoked in the world with her extreme demands, the idea arises among others that the attitude to the concept of Locarno [the 1925 Locarno treaties] should be revised — Locarno, which in the last few years had become a kind of stepping-stone [?] to pacifism. In truth it turns out that Locarno carries in her lap the most harmful explosive materials for Europe and the whole world. Locarno took a criminal, opened the prison gates for him, restored to him all civil rights together with a [—?] for life. And now he uses his liberation for hysterical escapades and criminal deeds..
But that is precisely the point: Locarno — though not officially — ceased to regard Germany as a criminal, but rather as a fallen, downtrodden brother of the family of nations. Locarno, by the way, was not merely an act of humanism and compassion, but the result of political calculations [?]: that the League of Nations has no real significance at all as long as such great and important states as America, Russia and Germany stand aside. By "pardoning" Germany and taking her back into the community of nations that are active in conducting world politics, only the first step was taken towards strengthening the prestige and power of the League of Nations. Without Locarno the further stages on the road of pacification could not have come about — stages which, despite their small achievements, nonetheless have a very great significance for the future.
And people certainly [?] knew that a liberated Germany would not remain sitting in her pitiful dejection, but would begin to strain back towards expansion, towards her former glory, and that her first cry would be: the Corridor! One could also foresee that this cry would provoke counter-cries and side-cries, and that an uproar of unrest would arise in the world.
This cry could not have been avoided anyway, sooner or later, and it is perhaps Locarno's greatest merit that she brought these German intentions out "from the lung onto the tongue" [i.e. out into the open].
For — one must reckon — the matter will not go much further than the tongue. One must take quite seriously here the words of Minister Treviranus [Gottfried Treviranus], that he is, after all, not an old-time minister who used to sit in a quiet cabinet and hatch conspiracies against peoples and countries; he is first and foremost an elected representative and leader of masses, who must give expression to their painful grievances [?]. His speeches, then, are directed more inward than outward.
Of course all Germans would like the historical injustice done to them to be put right, but from this alone — that the programme of demands includes not only the Danzig Corridor but also Posen [Poznań] and Thorn [Toruń] and even the distant colonies, and more than that, they even demand back a regular army on an equal footing with all other nations — from this alone one can see that the whole matter is more theory than practice, and that not only is it not directly on the brink of war, but that the matter of war does not enter the German plans at all.
Even if there could now be a great many [?] secret attack plans, as once before the war, it was precisely [?] Locarno that opened Germany up: by taking her into the general company, she gained the possibility of open talks, of democratic struggle, of negotiations, and was spared from coming forward with hatred in her bosom.
Whether the Corridor turns into a second Wilno, or whether ways and means will indeed be sought to solve the problem — in any case swords and rifles will not play the dominant role here.
For Locarno is more than a spirit; she is an actual power that regulates the deeds of nations. And the louder the uproar becomes, the more the world will be convinced that these words do not lead to aggressive deeds.
P. K.
From Dąbrowa via Paris to Lublin

The "Lubliner Togblat" has discovered the hero.
He left Dąbrowa, abandoned a wife with 3 children, ran off to Paris and finally arrived in Lublin, where our hero thought he could remain incognito, but the "Lubliner Togblat" discovered him.
Two weeks ago the Paris Yiddish newspaper "Parizer Haynt" published [?] the following story under the headline: "A Jewish woman from Dąbrowa with three children is searching for her husband in Paris".
How did it happen?
— I will tell you — says the woman.
— We lived in Dąbrowa in Poland. My maiden name is Zauberman [?] and by my husband's name I am Lask.
We lived quietly, had 3 children, traded, struggled; there in Dąbrowa my husband was a men's tailor, a good earner [?] and also a devoted husband. He often used to go trading in a suburb of Dąbrowa, at the "Warpis" [?].
There, near the Koza bridge [?], he got acquainted with a girl; there he used to meet [her] often. I knew nothing at all — who could have believed that my husband, 9 years after the wedding, a householder in the town, a good craftsman, would take "kochankes" [mistresses; Polish kochanki] into his head?
— Well?
— Well? — One day, 2 months before Passover, he says: why should I sit here? — I'll go to America, or Paris, and make a living. So I agreed to it; I believed [?] that our eyes would be opened [things would look up] for me and the family.
So I agreed.
So he ran off.
But that very same day there is an uproar in Dąbrowa:
— A girl has disappeared.
— Ran off with a lover.
— Who is the lover?
— A men's tailor.
Everything went dark before my eyes.
— And my husband has abandoned me with my 3 children, and I remain a forsaken agunah [deserted wife unable to remarry].
I feel my misfortune — my children without a father, I a forsaken agunah — and I weep out my tears:
— But how long?
So I went out into the world to look for him. Perhaps I will find him; if I am not a good wife, if he does not love me — but the children?
Perhaps someone knows of him:
He is now 30 years old, tall, thin, has a long face, is a men's tailor, a good craftsman and a decent man; his name is Reuven Lass.
———
This Sunday the "Lubliner Togblat" succeeded in finding out that the hero of the story is in Lublin; only his first name has he changed, from Reuven to Roman. He lives together with that girl from the "Koza bridge".
He lives on Świętoduska ("St. Duska") Street as a subtenant; his exact address is being sent to his wife and children.
The girl with whom he lives in Lublin is called Leah Czapnik, and her father Shlomo lives in Będzin.

[Będzin — Zionism and sport; visit of the motorcyclists from Palestine.] From "Hakoach" we are informed as follows:
