From Sport.

Y.T.S.S. „Warta“ (Częstochowa)—„Hakoach“ 1:1 (1:1).
The representatives of Będzin's „Hakoach“ had the honour of welcoming Częstochowa's „Warta“, as a Jewish gymnastics and sports association, for the return match, which took place in Będzin. The course of this match was very interesting, and only thanks to the excellent showing of the „Warta“ defence on the one hand and the weak shooting of the Będzin forward line on the other did the guests come away with a draw. In the first half the Będzin side had a slight advantage, yet „Warta's“ attacks were more dangerous. The young „Hakoach“ goalkeeper Bażykowski[?], who defended very well, had some fine individual moments. In the 37th minute Sammel[?] shoots from a distance, the ball strikes [something] and the referee awards a goal to the guests. „Hakoach“ tries to change the result, but without success. After the change of ends „Hakoach“ takes command and does not let „Warta“ have a say. A series of sure chances are not used, among them a penalty kick which Gutman shoots out. Only in the 34th minute does Szychek[?] head in a cross from Gutman and the equaliser is restored. The Będzin players try to score another goal, but without success, and the result remains a draw. The best on the field were the goalkeeper Starkman and the defenders Zezak-Rotsztajn[?], Kornbrat[?] and Sandomirski. Of the Będzin players Jankielewicz 2, Bażykowski, Radziwski[?] and Rozen 2 gave satisfaction. Referee Mr. Miner — good.

Rapid Aid for Zagłębie.

(The local self-governments must see to it that a "pogotowie" [emergency/first-aid service] is created for the towns of Zagłębie as quickly as possible.)

We shall not say anything new here; we have no intention whatsoever of innovating anything here, quite simply because we have already spoken and written about this question more than once in the columns of our newspaper.
We have already said and shown several times that we here, the inhabitants of Zagłębie, need a pogotowie; we must have a rapid-aid institution which would be able, in an urgent case, to come to the aid of the citizens with medical rescue.
True, several times we have discussed this matter, several times we have tried to make our self-governing bodies understand that such an action must be created, that such an institution must be carried out as quickly as possible. But from saying to doing is a long way, and from persuading to introducing it into life is not so easy.
True, our words found an echo both at the meetings of the Będzin self-government and at those of Sosnowiec, and satisfactory resolutions were even adopted, but everything is for the time being on paper; in life nothing at all has been carried out. And as long as a rapid-aid action is not created, as long as a pogotowie is not put into practice on a joint basis, so long shall we not rest; so long shall we keep rousing and persuading, storming and urging [?] about the pressing necessity of this useful institution.
Zagłębie occupies an honourable place in the country; our industry stands at a very high level, the turnovers are colossal, the traffic too is great, so that one must pause on our corner of the country and consider it attentively.
We must not make light of the question; we must see by all possible means to create that which the population needs in its everyday life.
Whoever attentively reads the daily press in Zagłębie sees that the chronicle is full of various incidents — murders and suicides, accidents and assaults — in which rescue actions are needed. How many times are we witnesses, in various incidents, to people dying thanks to the backward medical rescue. How many times does one run around for a long while after a doctor and cannot get one, and getting quickly into a hospital is not one of the easy things either — the various formalities delay the rescue, which must urgently be provided.
How often it happens that innocent people are attacked in the Zagłębie district and do not receive rapid rescue, because the apparatus is not there; there is no preparation to save people when they are attacked — so the attacks ought not yet to be committed, since here we are not yet prepared for them... And meanwhile, meanwhile the bandits, drunkards and all sorts of outcasts do not want to wait until our city fathers get ready with their rescue apparatus; and not only do they not stand still and wait, they even progress with rare speed — the attacks become more and more frequent. Then on top of that there came the modern destroyers — the automobiles, motorcycles and tram traffic — which grow ever greater and cause plenty of victims too. Besides that, we have lately been hearing quite often of sudden deaths, for which urgent medical help is also needed.
Zagłębie is growing, the traffic grows ever greater, and it is self-evident that under such circumstances the accidents must also multiply; so one must prepare for it, one must find means of saving people in case of a misfortune. And here one cannot wait, on the one hand, until a doctor is found, until he is caught and until he is willing to go; and on the other hand it happens in such a case, when strangers come running, that the doctors do not want to stir until so-and-so much is laid down for them on the table — then one can well imagine what kind of rapid rescue that can be. And how many times does one really knock at all the gates and doors and cannot obtain any doctor for any cure, and the person meanwhile departs this world? That is no longer news among us. And all this is said of the daytime; to say nothing of when such an accident occurs in the middle of the night — then the person is surely condemned to depart this world.
Can one remain indifferent to such incidents, which cost human lives? May one remain indifferent in this case? One must not pass over such unheard-of wrongs as though nothing had happened, or as though what has happened were already the last. One must get used to the thought that under the prevailing conditions the chances of accidents grow ever greater, and therefore we must be conscious and alert and see to improving the situation.
It is no great matter to organise a pogotowie. With good will it can be introduced very nicely and easily. Only they tell me that it is not so easy — is that an excuse? In a question that concerns human lives, is there any room to say "too hard", "too expensive"? People in the world create the hardest and costliest things, after all; surely, most surely they deserve [?] that an arrangement be created to save human lives, human suffering, human misfortunes.
This, however, is certain: as long as one does not set about solving the question, so long will it remain hard, however easy it may be; but as soon as one begins to take an interest in the problem, one will see that it is by no means a thing of impossibility.
A sacred duty therefore lies on Sosnowiec as much as on Będzin to take up the question as seriously and as quickly as possible, for there is nothing to wait for here.
But until then, until such time — it would be good already to settle one thing, which can certainly be done in a trice, namely: first of all, doctors on duty should be appointed in one place, let us say at the magistrate [town hall] or in a pharmacy, where one could turn in case of urgent help. That is surely no great thing to arrange, and it brings enormously great benefit — all the more so now, when the nights are beginning to lengthen.
One must therefore not make light of the question, which quite often costs human victims; one must consider it with full attention and approach it with deliberation and full awareness.
Let this important action not be postponed by a single minute; let it be seen to that it is realised as quickly and as well as possible in our everyday life.
Selekt.

[Pen yirbu — ken yirbu ("lest they multiply" — "so they multiplied", Exodus 1:10, 1:12).] [Poland — Jewish demography; feuilleton.]
The state statistics tell us that Jewish births now amount to only 5 percent as against the non-Jewish ones.
It follows that in the second generation there will no longer be 10 percent Jews in Poland, as now, but only five percent.
Is this to be the salvation from Providence on high?
In Egypt, when Pharaoh schemed: "lest they multiply" — Jewish daughters gave birth to six at a time, precisely, and it became a "so they multiplied".
Of course, an "Exodus from Egypt" had to be carried out, so there had to be a crowd of six hundred thousand; for a smaller public it would not have paid to stage the show [séance] of "the Parting of the Red Sea".
But now, when no Exodus from Egypt is in prospect, it goes the other way round: not six children in one womb, but one child to 6 wombs...
If now, of the three million Jews in Poland, one million, a third, is superfluous, then in the coming generation there will be fewer by a whole half, and for the remaining half Poland will indeed be a true paradise.
For the Polish organism, they say, cannot bear ten percent Jews, but five percent is surely not so hard...
Then the Jews will indeed have [?] the true paradise in Poland.
But it is hard to believe that such a policy should come from Providence.
For when there is a paradise, the Jews will start to be fruitful and multiply again, it will become a hell again, people will hold back again — and so on and on. So what kind of salvation is that?
More likely this decrease comes from the Jews themselves. Having tried all [?] kinds of salvations and seen that it does not help, they resort to the means of birth control [—]
One ought to release [?] the Jewish [?] sons and daughters from worrying so much about the community; better they should have themselves in mind, marry and have children — and then it will surely have to be good.
If only to spite the enemies. They say "lest they multiply" — so let it indeed be "so they multiplied".
Abi Ver.
Our Panorama

[Będzin — feuilleton: politics, Hasidism and the kehilla.]
(The "Grandpa" breaks up the "cheder". — The number of idlers grows. — A danger of war in... Wieluń. — In the Będzin Ger shtibl "fountains" are playing. — A "Chelm-style" meeting at the Będzin community (gmina). — Rainwater)..
We have not yet had time to look around after the "holiday" day, to take a look at how we stand in the world, to go through the kosher and treif minutes of our "kehilla" — and the "Grandpa" [Piłsudski, "Dziadek"] already took a fancy to dismiss his "cheder" [the Sejm], and orders the 400 pupils to go to work to earn a living and not to hang about idle and eat from the "communal" bowl...
Well, we must accept it with love — do we have any choice? For when the "Grandpa" says: "Paskudniaki! [scoundrels] Go into the 'Feier-Ru' [?]" — one has to keep quiet, wipe one's mouth in the Sejm buffet and quietly slip away; a trifle, when the "Grandpa" says... The trouble is, however, that the "Grandpa's power" has "influence" elsewhere too. For instance, who could even have dreamt that in the very month of Elul, in the days when peace and unity ought to reign, there would flare up [—] [?] wars unheard of until now, between one's own flesh and blood, between one and the same dynasty, between — Pilica and Ger?..
Would it ever have occurred to you that such events would happen? At the time when Ger and Aleksandrów concluded a peace pact, "war" should be declared between the Pilica and Ger Hasidim. And who do you think brought it about, who was the "destroying Satan" that shattered his own camp?
— Wieluń...
The holy flock of Wieluń took a fancy to a rabbi, and none other than the present Pilica Rebbe, who is truly worthy of that mantle — a rabbi far removed from "court" politics, who walks in the ways of his late father and sits over the Torah and the divine service, etc.
But the "hapove" [?] raised a storm in the "occupation-voivodeship": how can it be? Where are we? True, he is one of ours, but on our map [?] it had long been marked that R' Nechemia was to occupy the rabbinic seat in Wieluń!
And at once a "rozkaz" [order] went off to Wieluń to our people that they should gird themselves with weapons, stop at no means, have no sentiments for the family, but go out to battle with the slogan that has already become famous:
— "He and no other"!..
And once it is said — "there is no reply", almost the same formula [?] as, to make the distinction, with the "Grandpa": when they say go — one goes, and whoever has the power — occupies..
This vexes the Pilica Hasidim, and they grumble quietly in the shtiblekh:
— Oy vey! Such a thing! Oy vey!..
———
In Wieluń Pilica "fights" against Ger, and in the Będzin Ger shtibl there is a full-scale civil war. In that shtibl a battle is taking place among our own people, Ger against Ger...
The rebellion began at the moment when a man who is not a native of the town was engaged as secretary of the Będzin rabbinate. So the Tseirim and the Poalim [Agudah youth and workers] say in anger: how can it be? Are we — they say — merely an element at election time? Is there nobody in our ranks capable of this post? Why engage such an "expert" from Warsaw, of all places?
And since the "attack" on the Tseirim came "from above", they also answer "from above", in the literal sense: they, the fighters so-called, barricade themselves in the shtibl's attic, and instead of praying the attic "spits" water... It often happens that when the prayer leader raises his eyes on high to heaven, he receives a "tishpokh kabin" [a pouring of buckets]...
It goes without saying that when the attic "goes into action" the danger is very great; people shout, make an uproar, but the revolutionaries under the command of the "grandsons" do not back down from their demand:
— The secretary's post or rainwater...
———
With a little "mei geshamim" [rainwater] the Tseirim of the Ger shtibl ought also to honour the heads of the Będzin kehilla. They have "honestly" earned such a portion, especially at the tragicomic act that was "played" on Sunday of parashat Ki Teitzei in the kehilla's premises.
At the last performance, entitled "J'accuse", the prompters stayed at home... On the other hand, the "theatre" was well filled. The "gallery" stood above [?] [—], and the leading actor, R' Gershon the [—]gisher, held the audience in suspense; he won great applause when he turned to the 3 rabbis with the words:
— "You have come here to make theatre; we don't need you, we have our own rabbinate, may it be healthy and strong"...
The "performance" ended at about 11 at night. On 3 Maja [Street], where the kehilla's theatre square is, it teemed; crowds of people with beaming faces marched and talked among themselves:
— "Oy, how low [?] the Będzin kehilla has sunk, to what a low level it has come, oy, how deep is the swamp where the frogs of our kehilla croak"!..
— Tseirim! Where are you with your apparatus? With the rainwater?..
Ben Amotz.

In Our "Kingdom".

[Będzin — Kehilla; opinion.] (Representatives who make themselves ridiculous and surround themselves with boundless shame.)
In our "kingdom" — oh, what a foul smell comes from there. My God, how one wishes that they did not speak and did not write about it. It is nauseating, it is degrading; one feels almost as if among non-humans as soon as one begins to hear what goes on there, how people are treated there, and what kind of understanding there is for the public in general and for the kehilla affairs[?] in particular.
By "our kingdom" we mean our home-grown mouse-nest, the [?] dense crowd, the kehilla representatives, the rabbinate, the so-called synagogue committees and the whole clattering gear among them; but oh, how one would rather not put them down on paper, what a stench comes from them, so that it turns one's stomach — it simply makes one vomit.
[—] one begins to speak when people who make themselves so loathsome in the eyes of the public, who [—] carry on so much disgusting "politics", [—] one gets the impression that we are no longer among people who have human feelings, obligations and responsibilities, and [—] these are our representatives, our leaders, the chosen of the people, the fine householders with good deeds, with noble feelings, with self-respect — the very top of the [?]. Oh, how hard it is for the writer of these lines to speak of these "fine householders" as the providers of our kehilla; how dejected we must be when we look around at who [—] are our protectors, our [—], our leaders and directors. Say what you like — once it was nevertheless not like this; in parallel with progress we are going [—] backwards into the abyss of darkness [and i]gnorance[?] in a straight line. The sense of responsibility has never stood at such a lawless level as the one to which the "statesmen" of our home-grown mouse-nest have now brought it.
Sometimes it seems to them that they are in the roles of statesmen and they want to rule dictatorially over the "people", and sometimes they sink so low that they play with that same "people" like ignorant little children.
The "life" in the Będzin home-grown mouse-nest was asleep and dead; not a fly stirred. One had to stir up the rubbish bin so that the insects would begin to swarm and a putrid stench would rise from there — so for this purpose a "cantor question" was taken up, although there was none and there need not have been one, because the town has a cantor. So what — he gave notice of leaving the post, which many were pleased about; one could have simply accepted the resignation and been rid of the matter. As the saying goes, "a kosher pot and a kosher spoon" — each would have had to look for another post and the town — for another cantor. But who forced whom to make such a racket, create factions, look for intriguers, hold trials at which witnesses come forward from all sides?
And who are those who order the man to be tried — what sins have they found in him? Oh, it is nauseating; it is ugly and hateful to speak of such things.
The gmina [kehilla] could not stand by its own stamp, and it sent the "diplo"[?] on to the highest instance, the rabbinate; and the rabbinate is so wavering that they cannot find themselves a place, and since they would like to satisfy all opinions, they say neither kosher nor treif; once they do it this way and once that way. When has such a thing been heard of among Jews — such kinds of verdicts, neither meat nor dairy?
And whoever watches the whole procedure sees: if there must be a trial at all, in what manner is it being conducted, what a racket is made about it, and for how many weeks is the matter dragged about before the whole congregation? If there must be a trial — something that need not and should not have come to pass — it should at least have been done nicely, quietly and modestly, without noise, so that nobody would know of it. Is it permitted by law to shed a man's blood like this — as you do week in, week out? It is a disgrace and a crime to treat a man so, and all because a gang of intriguers, specially created for this purpose, wanted it so! Oh, into what a swamp the kehilla has crawled; how can it raise its eyes when it looks at what it has created around itself.
There is in Będzin a synagogue ["shul"], a congregation of simple people, a blind mass, which was nevertheless accustomed [unclear phrase, ?] to show respect both for a holy place and for its leaders. But this mass began to be used as a blind tool; it was tossed about like balls[?], now here, now there; whoever needed this mass to stage "orgies" stroked and flattered it and persuaded it that it was the pride and beauty of the town, and after such "operations" they came to the awareness that they were indeed what they had been persuaded from all sides, and that they therefore have a say, and the shul, they say, is theirs and nobody need interfere with them; they can do as they wish and as it pleases them.
No attempt was made to educate the common people of the shul, to lead them onto the path of awareness and restraint; very often they were drastically incited, until they became wild and did not know where the boundary lies between backwardness and awareness; and so now the sown fruits are being reaped...
Of course one cannot blame the naive common folk; they served faithfully. When they were taken to dance, they danced; when they were told to kiss the rod with which they were beaten, they kissed it; after all they are not[?] guilty in their souls, when they were taught to run riot[?]. One cannot blame them; they are faithful pupils of their teachers.
But woe and alas for such an education, woe and alas for the state to which our top people of the [?] have brought the whole holy establishment. There is no respect left, neither for a holy place nor for a Torah scholar; the simple public has been so incited that they do not know what world they are in.
To a fine state have they brought the home-grown mouse-nest; the people imagine they are in a kingdom of their own when they begin to uncover the home-grown mouse-nest, from which such a strong [stench?] is felt.
A whole representation we have, no evil eye — and it is not enough for them that they do not lift a finger [lit. do not put their hand into cold water]; it is not enough for them that, to bribe the public, they are capable of it with such sums as even the State Treasury [skarb] would not be ashamed of; yet they have priceless virtues: at intriguing and cooking up messes they are extraordinarily capable. And here we now stand before the events which arose thanks to their "intelligent" activity, thanks to their energetic willpower in the field of intrigues and lawlessness — for they have such a firm magnetic power that they dragged even the rabbinate there, with the whole holy establishment.
That is what one must wonder at! That is something to which no answer can be given. And these people, together with the rabbinate, are not at all ashamed to find themselves entangled in such a kind of [?], which desecrates not only their own prestige but also the prestige of the entire Jewish community, of the so-called "Jewish kingdom" in which, it seems to them, they find themselves.
R. Let.

Our Exile-Draggers!...

By Baal Lashon.
There was once in Uman a rabbi, Reb Tuvye Leib; he was a pious man, he could study too, but a great sage he was not.
They tell a sort of anecdote about him:
He once went with his rebbetzin to the fair and bought a cow. The local fellows, naturally, recognised at once what kind of a merchant this was, and sold him a cow that not only gives no milk, but also has the habit of butting with its horns and kicking with its hind legs.
They come home with the cow and set about milking a little milk — but the cow by no means whatsoever [will] give even a drop of milk, and does not stand still in one place.
Reb Tuvye Leib ponders with his rebbetzin what to do: should they both hold the cow, he by the horns and she by the tail? Who then will milk?.. Or else what — he alone should hold her by the horns and the rebbetzin should milk? Why, the cow will kick over the milk pail with her hind legs!... It follows that the best advice is for him to hold the cow by the tail while she milks! And the horns? Those will be left to God's providence!..
So Reb Tuvye Leib the rabbi takes the tail and winds it around his hand, like a remedy [bandage], lehavdil, and the rebbetzin starts milking in a good and lucky hour.
The cow gets very angry — what, she has barely begun milking — lifts up her legs and runs off. She runs and drags along with her the rabbi, who holds the tail wound around his hand.
Reb Tuvye Leib shouts with all his might:
— Jews, have mercy, cut off the tail, for I am lost, God forbid..
Several Jews run towards him and shout back:
— Reb Tuvye Leib, for God's sake, let go of the tail yourself, and she won't drag you!
— Oh, bless you — says Reb Tuvye Leib to the Jews — that clever idea never occurred to me at all!...
———
Our Jews usually consider themselves greater sages than the rabbi of Uman.
No small thing! Practical people, not idlers, people who know how to make a dollar and how to give a dollar, and yet...
And yet they do exactly the same as Tuvye Leib the rabbi.
For years now people have been talking about "exile" and "exilism": Jews are steeped in exile in their way of life; on everything lies the stamp of ugly exile.
Once, in Tsarist times, there was an excuse: exile was forced upon us. We had no choice. A "forced exile", and we could not free ourselves from it by any means — they did not let us. So we always had to drag ourselves along after exile to the last of our strength.
But today, in free Poland, where we are "free citizens", where we can conduct our way of life as we wish, we would not have needed to drag ourselves along after "exile" — so what are we doing here?
We Jews do the same as the rabbi of Uman, Reb Tuvye Leib: we ourselves take and wind the "tail" of "exilism" around our hands and let ourselves be dragged along after it.
I feel like shouting:
— Jews, for God's sake, let go of the tail, and exile won't drag you!...
But no sooner do I turn around than I see Jews grabbing hold of the tail of exile and not letting go of it.
And this "voluntary exilism" sometimes makes me laugh, laugh so hard that tears run..
———
I sometimes happen to be at a meeting of Jews only, Jews who speak a delightful, juicy Yiddish and can even speak Hebrew quite well — and indeed they speak Yiddish and Hebrew among themselves.
Suddenly a Jew arrives who himself can also speak Yiddish very well, but he has risen to the "higher windows" and already stands above an ordinary Jew — so for him it is, as a rule, no longer fitting to speak plain Yiddish; the mother tongue is somehow too simple for him, it looks like being buddy-buddy with all the Yankels together, it somehow isn't proper, and what does it matter anyway? So he presumably starts "chopping away in Polish", and since the rich Jew, the communal worker, "chops Polish", all those assembled at once humble themselves before him, and off goes a whole series of speeches in Polish.
The "Yiddish" vanishes, and the poor Jews begin breaking their tongues on their teeth, chopping and botching Polish, so that one pities, alas, the beautiful language.
The poor Jews turn green and yellow searching for suitable expressions and words — it is misery upon misery, but what excuse is there, one simply must!..
I always think at such times:
— Master of the Universe! What an unhappy people we are! Even where we need not torment ourselves, we torment ourselves anyway! If no one torments us, we torment ourselves! Who, for instance, forces us to speak Polish among ourselves? For what and for whom? Is it not finer and better, instead of tormenting ourselves like this and speaking a Polish that one cannot speak so easily — to speak our Yiddish as God gave it, which everyone understands and in which one can converse easily?!..
But that is just how it is: "voluntary exilism", scream bloody murder if you will!
———
People say, supposedly ("jakoby"), that this is a sign not only of liberalism but also of intelligence and progressiveness!
Of course, if intelligence means denying oneself, self-abasement, spitting in one's own face — then that is intelligence.
If intelligence means singing "Mah Yafit" voluntarily before the squire, crawling on all fours before a gentile "button", feeling calf-like rapture over a foreign word from a stranger — is that real intelligence?
But I think that intelligence has, it seems, quite a different meaning, a different sense. It means, it seems, self-respect, self-elevation, and raising up others along with oneself!
And how can we demand national consciousness from our young generation? How can they feel respect for Jewishness and Jewry when the elders themselves are exile-draggers?!
Ah, how I long to cry out so that all Jews hear it from one end of the world to the other, in exactly the words that were shouted to the rabbi of Uman, Reb Tuvye Leib:
— Jews, for God's sake, let go of the tail of exile!... Do not voluntarily wind "exilism" around your hands yourselves, and do not drag yourselves along after it to the point of utter exhaustion!...
Oh, our exile-draggers!...
New Lines in World Politics

By Dr. Jakub Wygodzki.
We stand at the beginning of a turning point in world politics.
In the East, in gigantic Russia, out of the revolutionary chaos and destruction there are beginning to crystallise the still half-misty contours of some new life... They still cannot be seen clearly and distinctly. But to one who has an open eye it is clear and distinct that, apart from all the negative[?] sides of Russian life, there is also taking place there the beginning of some grandiose work of construction.. Nobody knows in what form it will be cast. I think that the Bolsheviks themselves know it least of all. But that a mighty force is beginning to sprout from there, with which the world will have to reckon in one way or another, was clear to me already a year and a half earlier, during my visit to Russia..
Around this force, half-ashamed, half-hidden, all the states that lost the World War and that the Versailles peace treaty „bevolt“[? unclear word; probably: wronged] are for the time being beginning to group themselves.
Germany... supposedly stands aside. Germany has in general kept almost silent until now: the Germans know that weeping[?] cannot help their very difficult situation, and they have kept silent until now and have stubbornly striven to unite and gather their forces... „With Russia“? — „Oh, what [—] nothing can be done“!.. In truth, however, something different can be noticed.
Further — Turkey is clearly and distinctly bound to Russia. Persia — for the time being not yet Afghanistan — with Russia.
Of enormous significance for the European balance here is the new Mussolinian-Fascist, warlike Italy.
Has Italy even concluded a trade agreement with Russia? In any case the lines of Italy's present foreign policy coincide with the Russian lines, or at least stand close to them.
It is clear that the French policy of „encircling“ or „dividing“[?] Russia has not succeeded at all, but is beginning to threaten France itself.
(The situation in the Far East I deliberately do not want to touch on here, because that situation is not yet sufficiently consolidated, and the balance of forces among the antagonistic states is not yet sufficiently clear and distinct.)
Is that perhaps why the silent German (Treviranus) suddenly began to speak clear and firm words?
In a word — there has been created, or is being created, a new regrouping of the states, chiefly those „bevelt“[? probably: wronged] by the Versailles peace treaty, which set themselves against the French hegemony in Europe.
England is drawing ever closer to America. With Russia she is seeking to blunt the sharpness of her policy so far.
France, in the person of her gifted foreign minister Aristide Briand, sees and notices all the clouds gathering in the political sky. Briand understands that there is only one way to liquidate once and for all the „irredentas“ and „revanches“ (acts of revenge) — that is the way leading to a union with Germany, and he strives for this union with all his strength.
But for such a union to be firm and secure, France must make serious sacrifices, and naturally she probably does not want to.. Briand is looking for ways — not the old routine[?] ways of outwitting and grabbing, which cost so dearly and lead in the end to defeat — he is looking for new ways!
Briand strives to organise „the United States of Europe“ — he strives for „Pan-Europe“, more or less in the conception of the Hungarian publisher of the German journal „Pan-Europa“, Coudenhove-Kalergi, whom the foolish Endek [National Democrat] students, apparently taking him for a Jew, booed in such a scandalous manner in Warsaw not long ago!..
Whoever understands anything at all about the „United States of Europe“ knows what enormous difficulties stand in the way of carrying this great idea into life. But difficulties with such a great idea must surely not deter anyone.
And nevertheless something awakens in me.. a suspicion — the haste with which Briand brought this plan, which in any case has not yet been sufficiently thought through and worked out, to the next session of the League of Nations.
Briand is not only looking for ways to unite with Germany. He wants first of all to tear her away from Russia, against which the whole Briandist „Pan-Europe“ is directed, if I am not mistaken.
Briand does not want to allow the above-mentioned union of states to take shape[?] („kontrelirn“) and wants to create a counter-union that would fight — Bolshevism.
The above-mentioned Mr. Coudenhove-Kalergi wrote about a year ago in his „Pan-Europa“ that the time is not far off when all of Europe will have to unite against the dangerous Russian power!..
I consider this fear of the Russian power, which still has to develop, an exaggerated one. It reminds me of the fright of the „Yellow Peril“, with which certain politicians, headed by Wilhelm II, once frightened the world. Now — we laugh at it! I have no fear whatsoever of the Bolsheviks, and I consider the danger to the whole of Europe from Bolshevism an exaggerated one. I therefore very much doubt whether such a „danger“ could unite „all of Europe“ against — Russia.
These are the main lines of the new European policy, which is still in the making.
All clever politicians are afraid of war, seek peace and fill the world with their clamour about peace. One wants peace because he gained much from the last war. The other wants peace because he lost much in the last war and cannot for the time being wage a war — he has to prepare himself.
As you see, everyone wants peace, and wants it so badly — that one must pity poor peace.
Peace, true world peace, will come from another side: it will come when war becomes a bad business that brings no profits at all! Therefore the whole work and the whole energy of state power and of the society of all nations must be turned to this point!
First of all the actual equality of rights of the minority peoples with the majority people in every country must be carried into life.
That is the A of the ABC[?] of peace!
In the „Legendary Building“...

(From a visit to the new mikveh building).
The Będzin kehilla leaders have already been „busy“ with the mikveh building for several years. Year in, year out money is collected for this purpose, the „Shomrei ha-Das“ [guardians of the faith] turn with clamorous proclamations for help, engineers draw up plans — and the „legendary building“ is still not finished.
But as the saying goes: „it is already nearer than further“. R' Mendel Rosensaft is using all his strength and energy so that the mikveh be finished as soon as possible, and then, yes, then — he says — we will see[?] further; the gmina [community] treasury will then have income, and only then will it be possible to finish the Roman sweat-bath, the Priessnitz showers; he will even make a rest room with plush sofas; it will be magnificent — says R' Mendel — „the one mikveh in all of Poland“...
From what we saw during the visit one sees that the building is a model of our kehilla life. We have everything, thank God, and we have nothing.. The same is true of the building: there are (according to the plan, of course) 2 ritual baths, room for 20 bathtubs, sewerage, machinery according to the latest technology, there will even be a glass roof — but the bottom line is that for the money that has been sunk into the walls one could have built a huge building...
My guides, R' Mendel Rosensaft and R' Tobia Tenenbaum[?], show me all the installations; they speak with great enthusiasm about the great pleasure that is in store from the mikveh, which thanks to the technical installation will consist solely of „living water“ with a few drops of „rainwater“, as it must be according to the law.
— When will the building finally be finished?!
— God willing, by 1931. We still need about 50 thousand zł. Don't worry, I will get the money — R' Mendel trusts. — Write in your newspaper that the public should help, so that this spiritual[?] building can soon be handed over to the town; it is after all a great thing. But the main thing: don't mention my name; I want no honour, I do it with all my might only for the good of the town.
— I promise[?] him to do so..
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on the weekly portion (Ki Teitzei)

[Oneg Shabbat — weekly Torah portion.] Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion.
Collected and edited by Y. L.
Parashat Ki Teitzei
—o—
a) "When thou goest forth to war against thine enemies… and thou hast taken them captive" (21:10)
The Baal Shem Tov interprets the verse thus: by "the one waging the war" the evil inclination (yetzer hara) is meant here, which constantly fights against man. The Torah tells you: "and thou hast taken them captive" — learn the method of the evil inclination. It too understands how foolish it is to sin, and nevertheless it fulfils its mission — to talk people into sin — even though it understands the senselessness of it, because God commanded it so. Do likewise, O man, and fulfil God's commandment not to sin, for that, in turn, is your mission: not to obey the evil inclination.
* * *
When Rabbi Naftali of Ropczyce was still a little boy, his father once reproached him for being a rascal. He replied: What can I do, if the evil inclination talks me into it?
"Then don't obey it," answered the father, "for it too obeys only God; you too obey God's command and don't listen to the evil inclination..."
"But it," the boy answered at once, "the evil inclination, has no evil inclination of its own to talk it out of fulfilling God's command — whereas I do have an evil inclination."
—o—
b) "If a damsel that is a virgin be" (22:23)
According to grammar it should read "ki tihyeh", feminine form, not "ki yihyeh", which is masculine. —
The verse that speaks of a girl who is brought to misfortune, violated, hints that the cause of her misfortune is that she behaved like a tomboy... (wanted to go about dressed mannishly, her hair shorn like a boy's); because she was "in the category of a male" ("yihyeh"), misfortune befell her.
Naḥal Kedumim.
—o—
c) "Because they met you not with bread and water… and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor to curse thee" (23:10[?] as printed; the verse is 23:5)
One could have held nothing against the Ammonites for not bringing the Jews bread and water when they came out of Egypt — perhaps they were poor, or stingy. But when they spent so much money hiring Balaam to curse the Jews — for that they were suddenly neither poor nor stingy; therefore: "An Ammonite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord!"
Hosafat ha-Rosh.
—o—
d) "Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam; but the Lord thy God turned the blessing into a curse" [sic in print; the verse reads "the curse into a blessing"] (23:6)
A Jew is travelling with a bundle of merchandise from Leipzig; the day is about to end, and here there is a forest inhabited by robbers and murderers, and it is dangerous to cross it in the evening. So the Jew drives to a nearby inn to spend the night. In the morning, when he wakes up — oh no[?]: the bundle and the little horse have been stolen. They take a good riding horse and chase the thief. They catch him, the thief, a bold and cunning fellow; seeing that he will have to give up the bundle anyway, he stands his ground and argues: Fine, merchant — you get your bundle back, but you must pay me for carrying your bundle across the dangerous forest; I surely deserve a reward for that.
"You thief!" the little Jew bursts out, "did you carry the bundle across the forest for my sake? You wanted to steal it, only they chased you down — and you still want a fee?..."
The moral:
Balaam might still demand a reward from the Jews, since after all he blessed them. But one says to him: You, Balaam, you only wanted to curse, but you did not succeed, because God turned the curses into blessings. And you — what did you want, you Balaam?...
Ohel Yaakov.
—o—
e) "That He see no unseemly thing in thee, and turn away from thee" (23:15)
When a beadle goes to invite a guest to a celebration and escorts him to the host's house, the servant walks ahead of the invited guest; whereas when a policeman leads an arrested man, the policeman walks behind.
— God walks ahead of the Jews to show them the way in life. But when "He sees an unseemly thing in thee" and you deserve to be arrested — "and turn away from thee" (lit. "return behind thee") — God will walk beneath[?] you [as printed, "unter"; probably a misprint for "hinter", behind you]...
Divrei Shaul.
—o—
f) "Thou shalt not lend upon interest to thy brother" — "When thou shalt vow a vow" (23:20–22; printed "23:23")
The Torah juxtaposes the law of taking interest with the law of vows, because a person likes to persuade himself: if the money is not honest, if it comes from interest — well, I'll give charity with it, pay my vows with it. Says the Torah: "Thou shalt not lend upon interest" — in no case whatsoever.
Baal ha-Turim.
—o—
g) "And when she is departed… she may become" (24:2)
The Torah first mentions the laws of divorce and only afterwards those of marriage. The Talmud too arranges tractate Gittin first and only afterwards tractate Kiddushin — why this reverse order? After all, one first marries and only afterwards comes to divorce?
— God sends the remedy before the blow...
From folk sayings.
—o—
h) "When thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God" (25:18)
"When thou wast faint and weary" — if you are tired after a mitzvah, it is a sign that "he feared not God": that you have no fear of God, that the commandments are a burden to you.
Siftei Tzaddikim.
—o—
"Yet thou hast not called upon Me, O Jacob, but thou hast been weary of Me, O Israel."
Two merchants are travelling in a britzka; one has a suitcase with jewellery and diamonds — a light suitcase — and the other has a suitcase with ironware — a heavy suitcase. Arriving in town, the diamond merchant calls a porter to carry his suitcase to the hotel. The porter makes a mistake and takes the heavy suitcase with the ironware. Arriving at the hotel, the diamond merchant pays him a small fee, reckoning[?] that his suitcase is a very light one. But the porter gets angry: How can that be? For such a suitcase, so heavy, such a meagre fee?
"If so," says the diamond merchant, "if you are so tired from carrying the suitcase, it is a sign that you made a mistake: carrying diamonds does not make one tired..."
The moral:
If "thou hast been weary of Me, O Israel" — if you, Israel, have grown weary of My commandments, it is a sign that "thou hast not called upon Me": that instead of diamonds you have exchanged My bundle for ironware. "If you grow weary, you do not mean Me; with My merchandise one does not grow weary"...
The Kotzker Rebbe before the Dubner Maggid [as printed].
—o—
Avot, chapter two.
"Judge not thy fellow until thou art come into his place" (mishnah 5[?]).
Knowing[?] a person is impossible until one comes to his town and inquires about him. "Judge not thy fellow — until thou art come into his place."
Ohel Yaakov.
Festive House-Warming of “Brit Trumpeldor” in Zawiercie

[Zawiercie — Betar and the Zionist movement.] On Sunday the festive opening of its own premises by the organisation “Brit Trumpeldor” took place in Zawiercie. Up to 100 members from various towns took part in the celebration, as well as a representative of the Mifkadah Rishit (Betar headquarters) and representatives of all the Zionist and economic organisations (except “Hashomer Hatzair” and “Hechalutz”).
The assembly point was at 9 o’clock in the morning at the new premises, from where the march route led, together with all the delegations, to the town synagogue, where a memorial service was held for the martyrs of the Av events [the August 1929 riots in Palestine]. Into the synagogue the “commandants” admitted a large number of curious Christians, whereas the Jews who wanted to take part in the memorial were dispersed by the police and even trampled by the horses; and when Mr. Diament reacted to this, the dispersing stopped and they proceeded to the order of the day.
Mr. David Guterman sings “El Male Rachamim”, then the orchestra plays the Polish anthem and “Hatikvah”, and Mr. [?] David Werdiger speaks about last year’s Av events; then the floor is given to the representative of the Mifkadah Rishit, Mr. Rozental, who gives a survey of the Av events and stresses the importance of creating Betar organisations in all towns and townlets.
After the singing of several Hebrew songs and “Hatikvah” the memorial is closed.
In closed ranks the Trumpeldorians march through the streets Marszałkowska, Górnośląska, Old Market, Piłsudskiego, right into their own premises, where a march-past in front of the delegations takes place in the courtyard, led by the [c]ommandants Fiszer, Grigblat and [—]aldmintz. After the march-past the celebration is opened by Mr. Rozental, who thanks all those assembled for taking part in the celebration. [—] Greetings follow. On behalf of the “Ken” (Sosnowiec) greets [Mr. F]ildman [?]; from the council of “Brit HaRevisi[onis]tim” [?] (Sosnowiec) Mr. Klarman; the “Ken” (Będzin) Mr. Furger; the “Ken” (Wolbrom) Mr. Weingarten; “Brit HaTza’ir” (Będzin) Mr. Langnus [?]; “Betar” (Kraków district) Mr. Fridman; the “Zionist Organisation” Mr. Frenk; “Tarbut” Mr. Werdiger; “WIZO” Mrs. Margulies; “Herzliya” Mr. Josef Guterman; “HeChalutz HaMerkazi” Mr. Moshe Hoferman [?]; and finally Dr. Lewensztajn greets, expressing his satisfaction with the development of the Jewish youth in Zawiercie. Greetings are also read from the Artisans’ Association (Zawiercie), the “Ken Betar” (Bielsko [?]) and the “Revisionist Zionists” (Warsaw).
After the greetings the Sosnowiec “Ken” sings “Mizmor Shir Chanukat HaBayit”, and Mr. Wajcman, as the oldest householder of Zawiercie, is honoured with cutting the ribbon leading into the premises. When the crowd enters the beautifully decorated premises, a “hora” is merrily danced.
At 5 in the afternoon, after great efforts, they succeeded in obtaining permission to lay the wreath on the grave of the Unknown Soldier, on condition that the ribbons bear no Jewish inscriptions and that “Hatikvah” not be sung...
After the laying of the wreath the orchestra plays the state anthem and the delegation went off very quietly. It is worth noting that no representative of the authorities was present at this patriotic ceremony. One is reminded here of the “Ma Yafit” dance which the Jew once danced before the squire, and the question arises: is it really the task of “Betar” to dance “Ma Yafit” and to push itself in where it is not wanted?
While the wreath was being laid, a distribution [?] and various sports exercises took place in the municipal park, which went on until 10 in the evening.

An Illegitimate Jewish Child Baptised

[Będzin and Sosnowiec — social affairs.] The tragic story of a girl led astray.
The story we relate here happened in Będzin, and it is one of those stories whose beginning is merry and whose end is tragic.
For understandable reasons we do not mention the name of the Jewish girl who fell victim to light-mindedness, victim of a seductive love..
... Miss L. got acquainted with a young man, not at all ugly, a dashing [?] young fellow with fine manners; the couple began to go out walking, and the couple, i.e. the girl with the lad, fell head over heels in love, the “love” burned and...
What the three dots indicate you will surely guess: the due time passed and Miss L. gave birth to a child, a little girl...
As usual, the one “faithfully sworn never ever to leave her” forgot completely and did not want to know anything about the fate of his “beloved” bride, nor of his illegitimate child.
The situation of the young mother became very critical: she lost her job as a seamstress, she had no support from anyone, the family and especially her parents persecuted her, hounded her to the extreme; she had no place for herself and no resting place for her child, and she went out with the child into the street to look for somewhere to spend the night.
A place to rest she found in the Sosnowiec night shelter maintained by the Magistrat (municipality), and there she spent three whole nights.
In the night shelter she got acquainted with a Christian woman, before whom she poured out her bitter heart, especially about not having the means to keep her child.
The Christian woman, having heard the confession of the desperate young mother, explained to her that the K. family, who are childless, would surely adopt the child as their own.
Hearing such tidings, “Pani” L. became more cheerful and, although the K. family is Christian, she agreed to give them her child, just to be rid of the trouble.
She went immediately to the K. family. The latter liked the child very much and declared that they were ready and willing to adopt the child on condition that a formal deed be executed.
And so it happened: the mother signed a paper stating that she renounces the child and that the K. family may do with the child as they please.
Soon after the adoption the K. family had the child baptised and treats it as their own child.
When the Jewish parents in Będzin learned that their grandchild, the illegitimate child of their expelled daughter, had been baptised, they began to storm and to intervene with their daughter that she should take the child back.
But it is already too late. The young mother’s request that the K. family give her back her child was laughed at; the prosecutor’s office tried to intervene, but it is already lost: the K. family, who hold a written document from the mother, do not wish for the time being to give the child back...
Catastrophe in the Women's Gallery in Lelów

[Lelów — disaster.] We are written to from Lelów:
Last Friday a wedding took place here, to which a rich “uncle” from America also came. The next day, Sabbath, the guest prayed in the synagogue together with the in-laws. The women's gallery was packed full for the “shul-firn” [escorting the bride to synagogue]; almost all the women of Lelów accompanied the bride into the synagogue.
In the middle of the prayers, however, a catastrophe occurred: the floor of the women's section gave way and many women fell through the ceiling. There are many injured, among them also the bride's mother.
The bride herself was saved.

How Matches Fall Apart (Local Tales)

[Humorous feuilleton — matchmaking; Zagłębie.] The “Sequestrator” [bailiff].
Match No. 1.
A girl, not overly pretty, but for that she possesses not only twice eighteen years [i.e. 36], but also a little shop of her own, and on the market of live male merchandise the matchmakers conduct a tremendous trade with this little shop. A trifle — a girl with a secure livelihood! A table, a bed, bread with a knife — you need only take the trouble for a moment to stand under the four poles [of the wedding canopy].
So this week such a bridegroom candidate drops into this little shop, incognito, to catch a glimpse of the shop, so that he should know whether the bride will please him... The bride-girl stands behind the counter and sees a young man with a briefcase under his arm (most idlers carry briefcases). The young man speaks Polish, asks about various articles, has one box after another opened for him and looks around on all sides — she understands at once that this is no customer but surely a sequestrator, or simply some calamity from a tax office. The girl starts trembling and swearing that the goods are not her property, that she owes more than she has hairs on her head, that she has not paid rent for several quarters already, that the shop is a very bad one, that one doesn't take in a thing [“az"kh”, unclear abbreviation].
Of all the goods and articles he had examined, the young man picked out a cufflink [spinka] for 5 groszy and left.
What came of this match you can of course imagine for yourselves.
The Eggs Are to Blame.
Match No. 2.
A girl now without a shop — also a secure livelihood, but only half: a pretty wife is after all half a livelihood; on the other hand barely 19 years old, with a rich father, a large dowry and a weakness for automobilism.
She wants a bridegroom precisely with his own automobile. At the very least he should at least be able to drive a car himself.
Matchmakers wear out the door, bringing all sorts of candidates with ten dozen virtues: they don't smoke, don't drink, don't flirt, with uncles in America, with a knowledge of all kinds of modern dances, football specialists; they brought her [unclear phrase, “samo-razine sendzhes fun goln”, apparently football slang — the very pick of … of goals?]. But the girl insists on one thing: she must have a bridegroom with a “prawo jazdy” [driving licence].
Finally a matchmaker comes with good news: he has a candidate tip-top, he flies in an automobile like the devil.
The first meeting took place, of course, in a car, which the bridegroom candidate drove, and the future bride sat as passenger and [“sbiget”?].
But “the devil had a hangover” [?] and as soon as the bridegroom candidate drove out onto Główna Street, the car ran up onto a handcart on which a porter was carrying a crate of eggs. The car was damaged, the crate of eggs smashed, a great “jajecznica” [scrambled eggs] was made in the street; the police wanted to take the bride and groom to the commissariat, but the groom declared that he wanted no report and paid 250 zł. for the eggs on the spot.
The bride, in hysterics, was taken home, and nothing came of the match.
And she is not wrong: a wife — the bride argues — is like an automobile, a man must know how to drive her.
Young men with a “prawo jazdy” may apply.
Help, Where Is Staniewski's Circus!
Match No. 3.
Dear readers, have pity: perhaps you know where Staniewski's circus is now?
It is a matter of life and death. Imagine the misfortune. Ten years ago the town was already laughing at our Moshele, calling him a “sartsavi [?] kavaler” [an ageing bachelor]; but he endured everything, collected groszy upon groszy, and now, at forty, he has finally made a match. He took, of all things, a young, decent girl, and Moshele is already preparing, in a good hour, for the wedding.
What does the devil do? Staniewski's circus comes to Sosnowiec. Young and old go to the circus and come back with empty pockets — the management knows the secret of how to get the few groszy out of the visitors. Moshele, however, doesn't care for such things and didn't go to the circus.
Now his bride claims that if already while engaged the groom will not go with her to the circus or travel to Katowice to the park — then what will it be like after the wedding!
She will not go to the wedding canopy.
Moshele pleads: Mamele, have pity. You are still a young girl, but I am after all already a man getting on in years, and with every minute I am getting older! Come to the canopy!
The bride, however, dug in her heels: before the wedding she must first see the Katowice park and Staniewski's circus.
So Moshele comes running to the editorial office and, with tears in his eyes, begs to be told in which town the circus now is; he will go there with the bride, and let him consider that he broke a leg — lost, sometimes one must give the devil a few złoty too.
Jews, dear souls [?], perhaps you know the address of Staniewski's circus?
Pik.

What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: Tax Statute on Rail Freight Raised

[Będzin — city council; taxes and budget.]
What's new in Zagłębie?
Friday, 12 Elul 5690 (12). Piątek 5 września 1930 [Friday, 5 September 1930].
Będzin
The tax statute on rail freight raised.
Meeting of the city council.
On Tuesday an extraordinary meeting of the local city council took place. On the agenda were for approval: 1) a short-term loan of 100 thousand zł.; 2) granting the city administration authority to sign bills of exchange up to 370 thousand zł.; 3) raising the tax statute on goods brought in by rail; and 4) amending the statute of the road tax.
Because the vote on the first 2 items requires 2/3 of the votes according to the number of councillors, these items were moved to the end, in the expectation that several more councillors would still arrive; but the number of councillors did not grow by the end.
The president [mayor] Michał then declared that if the first two items are not discussed at the urgent meetings due to take place on Wednesday and Thursday, he casts off from himself the responsibility for the municipal economy.
———
The meeting is chaired by the vice-chairman Mr. Jakub Erlich. At the item on raising the tax statute on rail freight, councillor Lewin takes the floor and says that in the present crisis the merchants cannot be burdened with an increased tax. In the name of the merchants' association he demands that the statute remain as it has been until now.
The president gives a reply; he says that the increase will not at all burden the situation of the merchants.
After the reply nobody speaks on this item any more (no more than 5 Jewish councillors were present), and the statute is raised.
The items on the loan and the bills of exchange are not dealt with, because the required number of councillors was not present.
—o—

Brutal assault on a 'Talmud Torah' melamed.
On Sunday morning, while the Talmud Torah melamed Szmuel Szparn was busy at his work, the father with his sons, the Szulzingers, came in through a side door, and one of them beat Mr. Szparn murderously with a stick, so that he was drenched in blood.
The pupils, seeing what had happened, began to scream and cry, whereupon a large crowd gathered, which only then revived the badly bleeding melamed.
As we are informed, the brutal assault happened for the following reasons: Mr. Szparn moved the pupil Szulzinger from one bench to another, and in doing so the pupil accidentally received a blow in the face. He immediately ran home to his parents and told them that the 'rebbe' had beaten him. When the parents heard this, the father and his sons went to the Talmud Torah to settle accounts with the rebbe.
The revenge was terrible: Mr. Sz. received severe wounds to the head and body.
Mr. Sz. holds a certificate from Dr. Wasserzweig and is taking the matter to court.

How They Take an Interest in the Future Jewish Generation

[Będzin — community and education; criticism.]
On Tuesday morning, in honour of the new school year, almost the entire school youth of the local gymnasiums and public schools assembled in the city synagogue [Stadt-shul].
As usual, at such a ceremony the children should hear a few words from the town's rabbi [moreh ha-ir?], but there was nobody to speak a few words to them; nor did the cantor [?] sing for the children — only the conductor with the choir sang something, and the school orchestra played the Polish and the Jewish anthem.
Our kehilla representatives are busy with 'important matters' and have scant interest in the young Jewish generation.
The Strike of the Journeyman Bakers Continues

[Zagłębie — labour and strikes; bakers.]
The strike of the journeyman bakers in Zagłębie, which broke out last Wednesday, has not been settled at all, and the bread-bakers [owners] do not want to agree to the demanded working conditions.
During the strike days acts of revenge were carried out at a number of bakers in Zagłębie.
In the bakeries of Messrs. Gete [?] and Wolf Welner all the window panes were smashed.
Abraham Morewski in Zagłębie.

The actor and film artist Mr. Morewski, well known to us, is coming shortly to Zagłębie for 2 evenings. On the programme: recitations from the Yiddish classics and modern writers, as well as a lecture entitled „Europe and America“.
Mr. Morewski is coming here at the invitation of the Jewish Dramatic Society „Muza“.
A Brazen Theft.

On the night from Friday to Saturday, while the Malimowski [?] family of Potocka Street was away, unknown persons broke open the doors, got into the flat, and took from it whatever „could be found“: linen, clothes and other belongings.
When Will the Loans for Artisans Be Distributed?

„Jews need not receive any“ — so says a Christian artisans' representative.
On Monday another conference took place, chaired by the starosta Mr. Baksa [?], on the distribution of the government loans for artisans in Zagłębie.
At the conference, attended by representatives of all the Jewish and Christian guilds, the starosta declared that the loans will probably be issued next week.
For each loan, which will amount to up to 4 thousand zł., two responsible persons must act as guarantors (endorse).
Characteristic was the proposal [?] of a Christian artisans' representative, who declared that in his opinion „the Jewish artisans should not benefit from the loans“...
This „clever idea“ was, of course, not taken into consideration at all.
A Lecture.

This Saturday afternoon the League for Labour Palestine in Będzin is holding, in the Nowości cinema, a lecture by the well-known speaker I. Fugsz [?] (Warsaw) on the topic: problems in connection with the Workers' World Congress for Labour Palestine.

From Malbish Arumim.
The board of the Malbish Arumim (Clothing the Needy) society asks us to announce that the pledges (nedarim) made at the Torah reading this Saturday are designated for „Malbish Arumim“.
The proceeds are to help clothe 150 poor children for the winter.
—o—
From the „Gmilas Khesed“ Fund.
At the demand of the „Joint“, the loans of the Gmilas Khesed (free-loan) fund are given against bills of exchange signed by the guarantors.
When the loan is repaid, the guarantor gets back the guarantee bills.

The lawyer of the „Merchants' Association“, Mr. Teitelbaum, has returned from leave and is again performing his duties at the premises of the „Merchants' Association“.
——
The head of the „Bookkeeping and Advice“ department at the „Merchants' Association“, Mr. Feuerman, has returned from leave and has resumed his activity.
Sosnowiec — Jewish Children Will Not Attend the Public Schools 3 Days a Week.

The Jewish community of Sosnowiec must not keep silent.
In the previous issue of our paper we touched on the question of the fresh local decree of the present school inspector, who has reinforced the Sunday rest for hundreds of Jewish children, who will no longer attend school on Sunday.
We ourselves treated the report sceptically; we put a question mark over it, because it was impossible to believe that such an absurdity would be applied against hundreds of Jewish children. But what we considered impossible is becoming a living fact.
This Monday, at the conference of the new school inspector with the school heads, the inspector already announced that 1) girls will study from the morning until noon and boys from 2 in the afternoon until 8 in the evening, 2) on Sunday there will be no lessons whatsoever, and 3) Hebrew is abolished altogether.
Under the new decree it will turn out that in the winter months the Jewish children will not attend school for 3 whole days: Friday, Saturday and Sunday...
The report in our paper about the decree naturally caused bitterness among the Jewish population, but we know, after all, that our brethren the Children of Israel take all restrictions lightly..
In this connection a consultation of the kehilla representatives took place; they decided, together with the rabbinate, to draw up a memorandum and to intervene with the higher school authority.
——
We are also informed of the following fact:
The article in our paper on this question was translated into Polish. When the inspector had read the translation, he is said to have remarked:
„Let them shout themselves hoarse, it will help them little“...
The Sejm Election Campaign Has Already Begun.

The local magistrate (city council) has already sent out election lists to the landlords, on which the list of tenants is to be given.
House owners who have not received the lists must apply to the magistrate.
Workers Attack a Policeman.

The latter, defending himself, shot one of them dead.
On Saturday the following incident occurred on Wspólna Street:
A group of workers at Mr. Langer's building site threw themselves upon the master builder; as a result a policeman was called, who tried to put an end to the assault, but the rowdies threw themselves upon the policeman, knocked him to the ground and wanted to disarm him.
The attacked policeman, wishing to protect himself from the assault, fired and killed one of the workers.
Meeting of All the Boards of the Jewish Guilds.

Under the chairmanship of the vice-president Mr. Rotsztajn [?], a meeting of the boards of the local Jewish guilds took place on Sunday at the premises of the „Artisans' Association“.
The meeting was also attended by the member of the Central Committee Mr. Rak [?].
In the speeches the Jewish press in Warsaw, which constantly conducts attacks against the artisans' institutions, was sharply censured.
A resolution was adopted to rebuild the ruined [?] artisans' institutions in Warsaw and in the provinces.
—o—
The Number of „Converts“ Is Growing...
This Monday, while the local rabbinate was holding its weekly session at the kehilla premises, a young local Christian, an educated young man, presented himself with the proposal that the rabbinate help him convert to Judaism.
The rabbinate told the young man to come a second time.
—o—
Import of „Foreign Goods“.
The Chamber of Commerce informs interested merchants that applications for permits to import from abroad the quota goods for the 4th quarter are already being accepted.
Applications may be submitted until the 15th of this month.
—o—
A Year After the Wedding the Wife Robbed Her Husband
Before the local district court stood a certain woman, Szykora [?], who was accused of having taken 5,500 zł. from her husband a month after the wedding and vanished.
At the trial it emerged that the „woman of valour“ is qualified in the field of thefts.
Szykora was sentenced to 8 months in prison.
—o—
Bill Forgers Arrested.
The local police have arrested here 2 Warsaw residents who came to Zagłębie, where they engaged in forging bills of exchange on the firm „Siemens“, Sosnowiec branch. They discounted the forged bills and lived „the good life“.
The swindlers have been sent off to Warsaw. In the search a large sum of złoty and dollars was found on them.
—o—
Correction.
The Jewish Butchers' Guild in Sosnowiec asks us to publish the following correction: in connection with the note that the butchers demanded that the levy on slaughtering for treif should be only 2 zł. per head.
The truth is that the butchers demanded that the gmina (municipality) take no levy at all on slaughtering for treif.
Czeladź.

A sudden death.
The Jewish carter, the forty-odd-year-old Żelagowara[?], came into the shop of Mr. Y. Grossman and remarked that he was not feeling well; as he said this, he collapsed and died.
—o—
Tragic death of a mine worker.
In the „Juliusz“ coal mine in Klimontów a lump of coal broke loose and seriously injured the worker Laskowski.
He died on the way to the hospital.

A Chase after Thieves from Katowice to Czeladź. A Theft of Tens of Thousands of Złoty Uncovered

[Sosnowiec–Katowice–Czeladź — crime.] A plain-clothes agent of the Sosnowiec police office came upon a suspicious couple in Katowice, carrying a heavy suitcase.
When the couple boarded the tram in the direction of Szopienice—Sosnowiec, the plain-clothes agent kept them under observation and rode as far as Sosnowiec.
In Sosnowiec the couple got onto the tram to Będzin, and from Będzin they went on to Czeladź. The agent kept them „in his eye“, and on seeing that the couple had gone into a local restaurant, he went to the police station, where he obtained police assistance.
During the search of the suitcase, silk garments, costume jewellery and various articles were found, worth tens of thousands of złoty.
All these articles come from the theft committed a few weeks ago by the servant at the house of the architect Dworzański [?] in Katowice,
Two Suicides beyond Golonóg. One Suicide Was Rescued

[Golonóg — suicides.] On the railway line between Golonóg and Strzemieszyce two suicides took place, one of which ended tragically.
Sixteen-year-old Krus, a pupil of the 7th class [„oddział“], had been tormented by his parents because he did not want to go to school. To spite his parents the young man threw himself under the train and was killed.
The second suicide in the same manner was carried out by a young woman from Częstochowa, who threw herself under the train. The engine driver, however, stopped the train instantly, and the would-be suicide received only a blow from the train.
From Sosnowiec to Prutky by Bicycle

[Sosnowiec — youth movements.] On Sunday the 3rd World Conference of „Hashomer Hatzair“ opened in Prutky [?] (near Prague [?]). Delegates from Eretz Israel, Poland, Romania, Germany, England, Belgium, France, the United States and elsewhere are taking part in the conference.
From Poland 200 guests set out, among them 9 from Sosnowiec, of whom 4 travelled by bicycle. The conference is dealing with educational and ideological questions and with the attitude towards the forthcoming Congress for Labour Eretz Israel in Berlin. The conference will last until next Sunday.
Danzig. A New Decree of the Danzig Senate

[Danzig — anti-Jewish decrees.] As is known, there are in the Free City of Danzig over 20 thousand foreigners, mostly Jews, who earn their living here by peddling, collecting instalments and the like. The Senate, which consists in its greater part of the Hitlerites and seeks various means to root out the „Jewish race“, has now issued the following decree: from 1 October every worker and employee must possess a „work card“, and must have been registered for at least 2 years at the tax office, and pay turnover tax, residents' tax and sick-fund contributions. And since among the Jews there are several thousand new emigrants who are now threatened with expulsion from Danzig, the decree has made a terrible impression. Because of this an association of travelling salesmen and collectors has been founded, which will send a delegation to the President of the Senate, Dr. Sahm, asking him to extend the deadline or to abolish the decree altogether. The Danzig „Jewish merchants“ pretend not to know about it; it does not interest them at all whether the poor Jewish masses will be expelled from Danzig.
It must also be noted that only Danzig citizens are to receive the „cards“; it is therefore no wonder that the decree has made such a dreadful impression on the poor working masses in general and on the peddlers and collectors in particular.

Joint Activity of Small Traders and Artisans.
A few months ago an association of artisans and small traders was founded in Königshütte [Królewska Huta, now Chorzów]. Both groups, however, have understood that the system of „making Shabbat for oneself“ brings no benefit at all but, on the contrary, harm; so they reached an agreement to carry on joint work for the benefit of their economic interests.
For this purpose a board was elected, in which there are equal numbers of representatives of both groups. 2 presidents were also elected, and there is peace and harmony.
The board consists of: Goldwasser [?] and Rosenberg (presidents), Feigenblat, Friedman, Nager, Chenczinski, Steiger, M. Kimkowicz, M. Rosenman, Springer, Brager [?] and G. Kimkowicz.
The executive has created a free-loan (gemilut chesed) fund and intervenes in all questions concerning its members.

He Strangled His Children and Hanged Himself.
In Gleiwitz [Gliwice] a local Christian strangled to death his 2 little daughters, one 8 and the other 9 years old, and afterwards the father-murderer hanged himself.
The mother of the tragic victims died 2 weeks ago.
On the table the murderer and suicide left his birth certificate [?], which he had decorated with flowers, and a letter in which he writes that after his wife's death he has no will to live.
While he was carrying out the dreadful deed, his brother-in-law knocked at the door, but the father-murderer did not want to open, saying that he was bathing the children and was afraid they would catch cold.

Polish Jews as „Stepchildren“.
The „Polish Jews“ in Katowice have their own place of prayer throughout the whole year, but when the High Holy Days come the number of worshippers grows. Therefore the Polish Jews turned to the community board, asking it to provide a larger hall for the worshippers. The leaders, however, have no sympathy for the „Polish Jews“ and ignore their elementary rights.

Hakoach Res. – Zagłębianka (combined) 4:4 (4:0).
Last Saturday the second team of Hakoach again achieved a fine result, which could have been a victory. That did not happen, however, because the players could not withstand Zagłębianka's fast play in the second half.
The first minutes pass very interestingly; both sides have good chances, which are not exploited properly. Only the 25th minute brings something new: a fine pass from Wekselman is exploited by Richter and Hakoach takes the lead. A few minutes later Richter again scores a goal, this time from a splendid combination of the whole forward line. Lapek breaks through and in the same move[?] shoots Hakoach's third goal.
The Jewish team does not let the initiative out of its hands, and Szymek 4 scores Hakoach's fourth and last goal with a wonderful header. After the change of ends the Hakoach players cannot keep up the pace, and Zagłębianka manages to equalise through Pobarek[?] 2 and the right back. Winter in goal, the back "Szmulek" and Grajcer distinguished themselves. Of Zagłębianka, the goalkeeper and the left back played well. Mr. Goldsztajn acted as referee; he should not have allowed such rough play.
