[Sport — football, Zagłębie.] "Zagłębianka" (Dąbrowa) — "Hakoach" 2;3 (1:2) and 2:2 (1:0).
On Sabbath the Będzin "Hakoach" played a friendly match against the combined team of "Zagłębianka". For various reasons the Hakoach players took the field with 5 substitutes. The course of the game was not interesting, because the rain had made the sports ground unfit for play. As a consequence, unexpected[?] goals fell which could have brought victory to "Hakoach" as well, but the combined team had more luck and strength. In the 20th minute Guj shoots the first goal for the combined team; Gutman shoots the equaliser. Soon Kopisz scores the second goal. After the break came the only bright moment — the scoring of the second goal for "Hakoach", which was a masterpiece by Szywek[?] 4. The third goal for "Zagłębianka" was shot by Sanieri[?]. Gutman and Rozen distinguished themselves; from the combined team, Swała, Guj and Sołtarski. The referee, Mr. Okularczyk, did not see everything that one ought to see.
* * *
The return match between the above-mentioned teams again suffered from the poor state of the sports ground. The Jewish club took the field with 5 substitutes and had to play the whole second half with 10 men, because the excellent defender Jankielewicz 2 left the ground with a knee injury. Rozen I breaks through without[?] success. In the 19th minute Goldsztajn shoots the ball into the centre, Rozen I is on the spot[?] and "Hakoach" leads 0:1. Right after the change of ends Sabieri[?] shoots the equaliser. Jankielewicz is injured and leaves the field, and soon Hampel shoots the second goal for "Hakoach". In the 30th minute only Stapek manages to equalise. The best man on the field was Rozen I. Referee: Mr. Kiska.
"Sarmacja" — "Jutrznia" 1;7 (1:2).
"Sarmacja" had great superiority and won deservedly. The goals were scored by Konecki, Żmijewski, Puszecki, Widerek and Gawak[?]. The only goal for the workers' club was shot by Fiszel from a free kick. The best on the field were the centre-forward of "Jutrznia" and Żmijewski. Referee Mr. Cichoń — good.
"Maccabi" reserves (Sosnowiec) — "Maccabi" (Dąbrowa) 2;0.
The Dąbrowa "Maccabi" played very brutally and caused the match to end in a brawl between the players.
"Huragan" — Stow. Młodz. Polskiej [Polish Youth Association] 2:3 (2:0).
The already well-known "Huragan" played very carelessly until half-time, during which the S.M.P. scored 2 goals through Hancel[?]. After the break "Huragan" plays excellently and wins surely. Referee: Mr. Chmiel.
"Stern" ["Star"] reserves — "Aryeh" 0;1.
The only goal for "Stern" was shot by Szerer.
"Bogucice 20" — "Sosnowiec" 3;3.
"Sosnowiec" played excellently and certainly deserved a win; the guests too showed fine football. In the 15th minute Cichoń shoots the first goal for the home side, but a single attack by the Bogucice men is enough and the equaliser is restored. "Sosnowiec" attacks again, Czarnola[?] breaks through nicely and shoots home surely. The guests start up — a shot from the inside-left and it is a draw again. 7 minutes later Cichoń seizes a chance and "Sosnowiec" takes the lead again. After the change of ends the game evens out; only in the 22nd minute do the Bogucice men manage to score the equaliser. The game grows ever more interesting; the efforts to shoot a match-winning goal do not succeed. Outstanding were the left back of the guests and the inside trio of the forward line; from "Sosnowiec" — Nirek, Neber[?], Cichoń and Czarnola[?].
Mandek L.
The First Steps.

(Our city fathers at „work“. — What will become of the „consciousness“?)
The Polish Sejm has been dissolved, and the people's elect, the deputies, are, so to speak, „beheaded“[?]; they are now like any ordinary mortal — one may arrest them and in general do with them the same as with any average citizen.
And in the parties and associations a seething and a commotion begins: this one pulls this way and that one that way, these want to cut to the right and those to the left, and there are some who cannot be[?] either here or there — they are hobbled on all sides... And many of them cannot orient themselves at all; they cannot make sense of the present moment and remain standing helpless like little children and see[?] no way out for themselves in the future political arena.
On the other hand there is also a second category: a new kind of element has now taken shape, one that needs to possess no more than a sharpened tongue and a large enough dose of impudence; that is enough to make its way wherever it must, and before it doors and gates truly[?] open. This element needs no intelligence, no education, needs no guiding line; the said weapon suffices for it to push its way[?] in everywhere and to attain everything.
Thanks to this element one begins to spill bad blood between one party and another, between one trend and another; one begins to drag out the dirty laundry and, without shame, without limit, displays it before the whole public. At such a moment it matters nothing to tell lies on which the world stands [i.e. outrageous lies]; one does not reckon with the fact that later everything reasoned and convincing will be denied from beginning to end — one knows[?] perfectly well that at such a moment the second counts: at that instant one must influence the other fellow, and with that one is fully satisfied.
It goes without saying that in the coming Sejm elections, too, all these orgies will be carried on — if not on a larger scale, then certainly not on a smaller one; on the contrary, quite certainly new tricks[?] and combinations, new notions and inventions will be sought out, to influence as much as possible the broad, naive masses of the population.
But before anything at all happens, before anyone has begun to do anything, the Jewish representatives of Będzin have already managed to make the most important, cardinal mistakes, which will echo throughout the whole course of the elections.
It is an old rule that the heart of Jewish Zagłębie is in Będzin; here Jewish life is concentrated in all its magnitude, and our Christian neighbours know it — that here they will achieve little without the Jewish votes — and not for nothing do they needle[?] Będzin that it is „Palestine“; and yet — it goes without saying. It is a disgrace to say it, but whenever[?] we have anything, we have only the failure — and not[?] merely in a light form but truly along the whole front.
Now the Będzin city council has set up the main electoral commission, and in this commission there is not a single Jew, not even for a cure. And it is characteristic and interesting that in this very city council, which elected the representatives to the main electoral commission, there sit 16 — that is, half — Jews, and they managed so honestly and loyally and conscientiously and righteously to elect such a „Jew-free“ electoral committee. And if our own representatives showed so much understanding, how can we still have complaints against the Christians?
Say what you like — it is in no way whatsoever possible to understand how a representation and 16 men can so make light of their own interests, of their own duties. Surely they should have taken into account[?] how much responsibility there is towards the voters, towards the Jewish population, towards the broad masses.
What do they sit there for, these city fathers of ours, if they neglect everything, if everything is ownerless with them, if everything is nothing to them? People will never forgive anything; people will never want to understand that a representation is not put in place in order to do nothing at all, or worse still, in order to harm its [—] at every favourable opportunity.
With what levity must one sit at such a session and let things go however they will? And what do we have our representatives there for? What did we elect them and send them there for, if they have no understanding and no interest in everything that is Jewish? Is it not a disgrace both for us and for the Christian members to suffer such a defeat in a city that provides half the members of the self-government? Will people understand how one can make such incomprehensible mistakes? We here cannot understand it — so how should people who do not know the local conditions be able to grasp it?
If only there were understanding, one would know how to act, and it would be very, very easy to push through the hardest things; but what can one do when people want to understand nothing, when they never see the mistakes they keep making over and over?
How can one treat so arbitrarily[?] matters that play the most important roles in our life? It seems that in the field of the elections nothing has yet begun to be done — and already such a failure, already such a defeat.
Surely the system of intrigues, the system of „neither for me nor for you“, the system of squabbling over the smallest as well as the most important questions should have stopped by now.
It is possible that the councillors did not understand their tasks at the previous session and therefore split things so that what should not have happened did happen; it is possible that for this reason many also did not take part in the session — but is that an answer? Does that justify the defeat they suffered there?
Surely representatives should be ashamed to remain so helpless on the most important questions. Who, then, will wipe out the stain which, by their lack of awareness, they have cast[?] upon the Jewish representation and thereby, of course, upon the whole Jewish population of Będzin?
R. Let.

On Sunday the Centrolew organised in Katowice a demonstration against Germany. The crowd, which numbered thousands of people, was dispersed in some places by mounted police.
When Korfanty's car with passengers arrived at the Kościuszko[?] market, they were met with stones. Several passengers were injured.

The area around the German consulate was heavily guarded.

Letters from Home

[Będzin — Feuilleton; New Year letter.] With God's help, [week of] the portion "the whole land thereof is brimstone and salt, and a burning"... [Deut. 29:22 — portion Nitzavim]
My friend R' Shlomo, may his light shine.
First of all I inform you that, thank God, I am at home. You were frightened for nothing when you read in the papers that "the Grandpa" ["Dziadek" — Piłsudski's nickname; an allusion to the arrests of opposition leaders in September 1930] has made several of our people into "martyrs". I have not, God forbid, been privileged to reach that rank — simply because we live in the town of Będzin, where one accepts everything with love, resents nothing, and swallows every injustice with a blessing on one's lips.
But why busy ourselves again with everyday matters, why chew over again and recall what caused us so much bad blood, disgrace and humiliation all year? This time we must take leave of the old year and sing its praises before it takes away from us the whole bundle of Jewish troubles and pain...
The greatest praise, R' Shlomo, we must address to our town councillors — health to their bones for their good deeds this year. A trifle, their deeds?! Take, for instance, the old market of Będzin. For decades the old market looked like a trading place in Asia. The voices, the shouting, the screech of the barrel organs [katarynki] dulled the senses; on hot summer days it was unbearable, there was no free spot to rest; the "outcry thereof" was very great, until, as it were, we were blessed with wise and understanding councillors who managed to work wonder upon wonder. When you, R' Shlomo, come to Będzin now and see how the market has been turned into a splendid garden where Jewish merchants stroll round and round with folded hands, and when they grow tired and sleepy they sit down in the middle of the garden, where one hears the murmur of the splashing fountain, and without wanting to one falls asleep...
And so it is in every field. Last year dozens of young Jewish men found employment as magistrate [municipal] officials, as collectors for the waterworks, as tram conductors, etc. And this is only thanks to them — the councillors, that is — who have stood guard like brave fighters from the very beginning. We have 3 Jewish aldermen [ławnicy] in the town executive (besides the portfolio of vice-president), Jewish positions are defended in all municipal commissions, dozens of Jewish motions were adopted this year, Jewish unity is as firm as iron pillars [?]; while among the non-Jewish councillors there reigns fragmentation, a "generation of the dispersion" [Tower of Babel] system — no one knows what the other wants, everyone acts on his own — the Jewish front is like a wall [?]: all for one and one for all. Why should I go on at length? We have such power that we could carry a motion to have mezuzot put up in the town-council chamber...
But why such trifles? They, the councillors that is, are not punctilious about matters that are not of first-class value; for example such a foolish matter as the main electoral commission for the Sejm — that they, the councillors that is, handed over to the sons of Esau. Let them busy themselves with politics; we need a budget to maintain an espionage organisation that will not let in any "eye"-blemished [?] cantor.. We need to acquire a fifth shochet, a fourth moreh hora'ah [rabbinic decisor] and similar important things that glorify the G-R-E-A-T name of our community...
Our neighbouring Sosnowiec too gained, in the year 5690, a bright chapter in the history of Jewish communities.
This year the disputes over the rabbinate question ceased; the warring sides threw up their hands and submitted to the influence of a larger number of honest, non-partisan and most respected householders, who brought [?] Sosnowiec a rabbi to its name and glory. The reception was very festive; young and old went out with timbrels and dances to welcome the rabbinic authority. Barely a few weeks later the new rabbi had already managed to bring light into communal life. The outside authorities [?] show great respect for the religious leader. The new school decree, which was meant to rob hundreds of Jewish children of their most elementary rights, was soon withdrawn by the school inspector.
It is even said that a great part in the abolition of the school decree was played by the Jewish councillors too, especially the Orthodox ones, who, seeing that under the new decree Jewish children would have to write on the Sabbath, did not rest, called protest meetings, intervened, threatened [?] until the decree was annulled...
The past year was fruitful not only in the economic but also in the cultural field. The differences of opinion that had prevailed widely in the Jewish street ceased; every party renounced its doctrine and sought only the interests of the community; even the long-standing bitter enemies, the sports clubs "Hakoach" and "Maccabi", made peace with each other and "measure themselves out of each other's mouths" [?; unclear idiom]. In place of the two clubs a unified sports organisation of all Jewish teams [drużyny] in Zagłębie was created.
The unified organisation has set as its first aim to combat football, which brings in wildness, coarseness and cruelty. For the most part the sportsmen are used for gymnastics exercises, choir, a drama section, etc.
In the philanthropic field there are no positives to record. In the course of the whole year Zagłębie was not enriched by a single new institution. On the other hand much was done [?] so that the already existing institutions should be supported with a generous hand. Thus the Torah-faithful of Będzin put much effort into maintaining the "Talmud Torah"; besides collecting large sums of money, they contributed themselves so that the children of the poor, the poor Jewish children, should study Torah.
— — —
I wanted to list for you a long series of salvations and consolations of the past year, but suddenly a little angel appears before me, carrying in his hand a white silk ribbon with the inscription — 5690...
And when I approached the little angel and wanted to embrace him, I heard a cry: Away from me! Praises of the year 5690 you write! It is all a lie. 5690 is stained with Jewish blood, lost [?] a great number of heroes and martyrs; the whole Admonition [Tochacha] was fulfilled in this year...
— — —
... Come then to us, dear angel, with your year of 4 letters [5691, תרצ״א], corresponding to the four expressions of redemption; bring salvation to the people of Israel — "let the year and its blessings begin" — so wishes you and all of Klal Yisrael your friend
Ben Amotz.
Charity Without a System

(Our shameful stain. — How do we look in other people's eyes? — Can this be tolerated any longer?)
We really are abnormal, incomprehensible, unfathomable in every sphere of our life. When we begin to investigate our psychology, our train of thought, our orientation, our outlook, we must come to the conclusion that we ourselves do not understand ourselves, that one cannot grasp the other, cannot see through him.
And if we ourselves do not understand ourselves, if one cannot form any opinion about the other, if our people is so veiled, so hidden, so full of secrets — then we should not take offence when people come from outside, people who are obliged to know and understand Jewish psychology, the Jewish élan, and they discover our shortcomings, our so-to-speak abnormality, which even with the best will and understanding is impossible to grasp logically, to analyse logically.
What are we getting at? At our so deeply rooted professional schnorring (begging), to which we have grown so accustomed that we do not see the shame it brings upon the Jewish people; we do not see the gallery of Jewish schnorrers whom we ourselves raise thanks to our compassionate hearts. It may be said boldly and openly that schnorring is no longer a disgrace among Jews; stretching out one's hand for alms is no longer a shame. The shame that a man come down in the world once felt at stretching out his hand vanished together with the war.
Today we no longer see the delicacy[?], the innocent shame of helplessness, which one could once see, years ago, in such a person when he had to struggle with his conscience, which tormented him: what should he do — should he prevail on himself and stretch out his hand for a crust of bread, or should he go on languishing and starving and struggling with his soul until it goes its way, until he can return it to the Creator of the World crystal-pure, without the slightest blemish...
These ideal, modest souls we no longer see in our everyday workaday life, and who knows — perhaps they do exist, only we do not see them; possibly the great masses of sophisticated modern schnorrers of every kind block their way and one cannot make them out; possibly among the most varied garish colours the modest hue does not stand out...
Everyone knows that the times are bitter and that thousands of well-to-do and rich Jewish families have been completely ruined, so that they have no other recourse but to turn to begging for bread, and it is precisely from this standpoint that one should have set about solving this difficult question, which is bound up with danger to life.
But what do we see? Unfortunately we see nothing being done in this field; no one has even tried to solve this difficult problem, and meanwhile such lawlessness and licence reign in this field that it leads to the most disgusting and incomprehensible things. Whoever has not studied these branches of schnorring can have no idea at all[?] of what goes on in this incomprehensible riddle that "works" under the general mask of begging and of "respectable" people who have come down in the world.
We are, after all, Jews with soft hearts, for whom a donation plays no role: whoever merely stretches out a hand is given something. And thanks to this giving to everyone, without any system whatsoever, so much disorder has been introduced that we get nothing but harm from it all. For what comes of giving alms to a person when he can work and earn? We give him the alms today so that he can get through the day, and the next day he comes again for the same alms, and we give him again, and so it goes on continuously. Such a system has brought things to the point where people who are able to work have become professional schnorrers, who no longer understand how one goes to work when one can live out one's years stretching out one's hand every day, which has become a livelihood just like all other livelihoods; they no longer try to look for any kind of work, they feel no need for any other occupation, because this crowd has become so welded to its "trade" that in their eyes they are just as busy with their occupation as other people are with their livelihoods.
And as soon as this became a business from which healthy people draw a living, people began to make "progress" in this field, for stretching out one's hand for a grosz does not pay; it has to be done in a more modern way, with the grand gesture, so that various combinations have arisen in this field, just as in any business: there are collectors for yeshivas who issue receipts with stamps; authors of books who cannot even look into any book; and various publishers; then come fire victims, pogrom victims, people come down in the world and genuine swindlers, who adapt themselves to everything in the world, because they are already well versed[?] in the "trade" and know how to arrange things; and if such a professional swindler happens to be caught red-handed in one town, he knows how to play a completely different role in the next town.
Besides all these strangers who come from time to time on "tour" to Zagłębie and Upper Silesia, we have, after all, our own permanent local schnorrers, among them young people who cannot have employment only because their "profession" [printed "p-ofession"] is no worse, let us say, than going to clean or to wash laundry — so they can stay in their "trade", which causes the conscious Jew so much shame and pain.
Is it any wonder, then, that under such anarchy the number of schnorrers among us grows — people who could have avoided this easy livelihood? Such disorder was bound to lead to this schnorring, which keeps progressing, because giving without order, without a system, is just as bad as not giving at all, as not wanting to show compassion at all; everything must be done in proper measure; handing out alms to people at random, without any purpose, is harmful and abnormal.
Committees must be set up once and for all to regulate this question. The going from door to door, the pressing of door handles, must at long last be done away with. The committees must have the task of supporting with a monthly allowance those people who are unable to work, and for those who can work, employment must be found, so that they can earn their bread honestly.
As long as we do not introduce a normal, healthy order in this so shameful field, others will look upon us as a people that is abnormal and does not know how to beautify the forms of life, although it is capable of doing so.
It is high time that we took up this shameful matter, which brings us so much shame in the eyes of other nations, and all we get from it is that we raise a generation of schnorrers, idlers and an unwanted, lawless element.
Selekt.
My Interview with 5691

[Feuilleton — Rosh Hashana.] By Ploni ve-Kohen.
If you come upon a writer in the middle of the day sitting with folded hands and yawning, do not brand him an idler, for the writing profession stands "above time" and does not depend on office hours. It depends on the Muse or on the prince of of [sic] inspiration. That is why it is right that precisely in the evening, when everything is closed, when the whole world lies stretched out on its bed snoring away contentedly — the writer sits somewhere alone, or roams like a sleepwalker through the dimly lit streets, racking his brains over some new creation. The creation may be fit only for kapores [i.e., worthless], but it is drudgery, it is toil.
That is what happened to me on the night before Rosh Hashana.
On that Rosh Hashana-eve night I did a little piece of work for our paper. I had an interview with — guess with whom? — with the newborn child — 5691.
It happened like this: the angel Chalmiel [the angel of dreams] apparently carried me off on his shoulders into the editorial office. Suddenly the door opens and two figures come in, one an old man and the other a young man. I naturally give them a sholem aleichem and ask who they are and how I may serve them. The old one tells me that he is the "Calendar" and that his young partner is the — "Molad" [the new moon].
So what do you want? We want nothing — they say — but since they are ardent supporters of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" they wish to hand it an important bit of news. The news is that the "Secret of Intercalation" has just been brought to bed and given birth to the new little year — "Tartsaniu" [sic; a pun on 5691]. It's a fine child, they say, a healthy one, a strong one, a robust one, weighing a full three hundred and sixty-five pounds, and it has all its faculties like a grown man: it walks, it talks and it possesses full understanding.
This tiding put a new soul into me. Here I have material already. I will go and interview it. And both of them, the Calendar as well as the Molad, agreed that it was a good idea.
No sooner said than done. Going outside, I noticed a few steps from the house a big hairy ox. That is "Mazal Shor" [the sign of Taurus]. They explained to me: climb up on it, we will ride together to the lunar sphere, where the cradle of the "newborn babe" stands.
We arrived safely in the lunar regiments, passed through a labyrinth of "blemishes" [the moon's phases] and found the gigantic baby 5691 indeed walking about, or more precisely walking and moving in a certain direction, forward. My companions introduced me to him as a newspaperman who wanted to have an interview with him.
He smiled, put on a polite face and moved on. So, I say to him, you don't want to talk to me. He answers back: "Oh, what are you thinking? On the contrary, I'd be glad to make the acquaintance of and have a chat with people who are already naturalised here and have more experience than I. Only, you must know that this is my nature: I cannot stand still in one place, I must keep going on and on until the last minute of my existence, when I shall expire entirely, like all my predecessors. And if you really want to have an 'interview' with me, as you call it, and get the right information, you must follow me step by step"...
So, having no choice, I complied — talked and walked, walked and talked.
— Have you brought greetings of something important for the Jewish people? — I asked him.
"You speak a strange Hebrew" — he answers — "in the dictionary of the upper world of time, from where I came down, there is no such word as 'greeting', but I can guess what you mean.
"You mean to ask whether I have brought you a joyful greeting or whether I can give you a promise of salvations and consolations. Well, you are in fact mistaken about my whole 'essence'. I am of rather meagre pedigree. The 'Heavenly Household', which decided to bring me out into the light of this lowly world, did not consult me, did not ask me whether I wanted this privilege or not. With me it is the same story as with each of you, human beings — 'against my will was I born' — I was born against my will. I was content with my lot, felt truly happy in my abstract state, without a concrete form. I was a kind of soul floating about naked in the void of the 'Infinite'. I did not constitute any 'substrate', any foundation for deeds and events. True, no beautiful scenes could be played out upon me, but by the same token no ugly scenes could be played out upon me either. I was a neutral being, had nothing to do with good and nothing to do with evil either. Consequently I had no will. I never wanted anything, and the heartache that comes from an unsatisfied will was foreign to me.
"Now, however, they have put an end to my abstractness and turned me into a body made up of many, many large and tiny and teeny-weeny particles called months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds and so on, and each part serves as a place on which your human race does and creates its righteous deeds together with its wicked ones. But the wicked deeds always outweigh the righteous ones. And that, believe me, is a bitter thing. I have as yet very little experience, but when I lay in the womb of becoming, a light of history burned above my head, and an angel who has kept the bookkeeping of time since the Creation taught me the epochs of the world and the fortunes of tribes and nations. From that I learned what horrifying things have happened on the soil of the years. Nations have murdered nations, faiths have persecuted faiths, and in the end the Jewish faith has had to endure more troubles than all of them.
"So I, for my part, tremble before such historical repetitions. I do not want anything to happen on any day of mine that would stain me. Since I am already here, I have a will, and my will is drawn to light. Even my nights I want to be bright. And just as you pray, so do I pray too, that I may be a year of life and peace, a year of redemption and salvation for Jews and for the whole world as well.
"My prayers are earnest; if only your prayers were as earnest. Then I am almost certain that we would be properly answered.
"When I pray for peace I truly mean peace without tricks. I think ill of no one and bear no one an evil thought.
"You, however — I mean some of you — behave like the rulers of the nations of the world: they talk of peace, conclude alliances for peace, and at the same time they sharpen the swords.
"That is what the angel told me about you, and surely it is true. I have already had a little opportunity to see it with my own eyes. Passing by certain houses of prayer, I found Jews with prayer books in hand, with tallises on their shoulders, quarrelling, cursing each other and even making as if to come to blows. Well, is that not a disgrace?! The angel painted the Jewish synagogues for me in such glorious colours — tents of holiness they are — and here I saw on some walls notices of mockery. Are these the synagogues of Israel?! Ah, believe me, if I had the choice I would pick myself up and pack myself off back home"...
At this point I woke up, heard someone saying "Zechor Bris" [the Selichot hymn of Rosh Hashana eve], and ran off to pray with the congregation.

Sayings, remarks and anecdotes relating to Rosh Hashanah. Collected and styled by Y. S.

A) "U-vekhen ten paḥdekha" and — money..
When one says the solemn prayer "U-vekhen ten paḥdekha" ("And so, put Your awe…"), a Jew has in mind that the word "paḥdekha" equals in gematria "gelt" [money] (112). If one had money in mind only at "paḥdekha", it would still not be so bad. In truth, however, one intends: u-vekhen — money, ten — money, paḥdekha — money, nothing but money.
By Rabbi Naftali of Ropshitz [Ropczyce].

B) Exempt from Hallel.
Rabbi Shlomo Kluger once, on Rosh Ḥodesh, visited a rabbi of his acquaintance who was already a little "modernised" and occasionally took a look at secular books too. When Rabbi Shlomo came in, there lay open before him both rabbinic books and a German booklet. Rabbi Shlomo asks him: Did you say Hallel today?
— What sort of question is that? Today is Rosh Ḥodesh, after all.
— You were exempt from Hallel. For the Gemara says that the reason Hallel is not said on Rosh Hashanah is that "the books of the living and the books of the dead" are open, so it is no moment for song. With you, too, there lie open books of the living (— the rabbinic books) and books of the dead (— the German booklet, for "the wicked even in their lifetime are called dead"..) — so you are exempt from Hallel..

[C)] "As a shepherd seeks out his flock, making his sheep pass under his rod."
The hired[?] shepherd who pastures other people's sheep — when he leads them and one strays even slightly off the path, he hits it at once. But one who leads his own sheep is gentle and merciful, and when a lamb strays from the straight path he merely raises the rod but does not strike; he only threatens. God, too, deals with us "as a shepherd seeks out his flock", like a shepherd with his own sheep, "making his sheep pass under his rod" — He only raises the rod, He only threatens..
"Mesamḥei Lev".

D) "If one overlaid the shofar with gold at the place of the mouth — it is unfit" (Rosh Hashanah 27)
The shofar is the preacher of rebuke, the one who wakes and chastises the people and does not let them doze.
But when the shofar is "overlaid with gold", covered with money — when the preacher thinks only of money — he is unfit.
"Yalkut Peninim".

E) The festival of Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat (Rosh Hashanah, ch. 4, Mishnah 1)
When Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat it is a "yom tov" — a good day. For one may not inscribe a person for bad — it is Shabbat, after all.. Good, on the other hand, one may indeed write, since saving life overrides Shabbat; consequently in Heaven they are forced[?] to write only good.
By Rabbi Levi Yitzḥak of Berdichev [Berdyczów].

F) Why is the shofar blown on Rosh Hashanah? — To confound Satan (Rosh Hashanah 16)
Rashi explains the words thus: "Satan will see how Jews love mitzvot and will not accuse" — Rashi's words are truly incomprehensible: if Satan sees that Jews love mitzvot, surely that is exactly when he will want to accuse and search out sins against them.
The meaning is this: the Gemara says that for one who repents out of love, out of love for God, his sins become outright merits. That is what Rashi means: when Satan sees that Jews love mitzvot, he will know that the more sins he reckons up against them, the more those sins will turn into outright mitzvot; therefore he will keep silent and will not even want to mention any sins, lest, God forbid, they turn into mitzvot...
By the author of the "Hafla'ah" [R. Pinḥas Horowitz].
* * *
Rabbi Moshe Leib of Sassov [Sasów] once sees in the street a sinner he knows; he grabs him by the lapels, shakes him and says to him: You should know how I envy you! Just remember what mountains[?] of sins you possess, and if you repent, all of that will turn into nothing but mitzvot — you'll have so many mitzvot! What tzaddik can possess so many mitzvot!... I envy you!..

G) "On Rosh Hashanah it is written and on the fast of Yom Kippur it is sealed: how many shall pass away and how many shall be created, who shall live and who shall die."
Rabbi Levi Yitzḥak of Berdichev interpreted the words of "U-netaneh tokef" thus:
"On Rosh Hashanah it is written" — on Rosh Hashanah the gentiles write; "and on the fast of Yom Kippur it is sealed" — on Yom Kippur they sign; "how many shall pass away and how many shall be created" — how many bastards they bring into the world on the holy days; so I ask You, God: "who shall live and who shall die"? Who should live and who should die — we or they?...

H) "Were Rosh Hashanah a single day, the world could not endure" (Zohar).
"If Rosh Hashanah were only one day, the world could not survive" — why so?
The Midrash says on the verse "He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity" that God judges the Jews by day, when they do mitzvot, and the gentiles by night, when they "sleep off" their sins [i.e. rest from sinning]. And in this way the world can endure.
It follows that if Rosh Hashanah were only one day, the gentiles would be judged first, at night, and the Jews the next morning by day; but after judging the gentiles, even at night when they rest from sins, the Jews next morning could not have been cleared[?] (printed "mekane") after so much anger as would have accumulated with the Judge.. But since Rosh Hashanah is two days, the Jews are judged by day, and the gentiles only on the second night.
"Ḥavot Ya'ir".

I) "For with You is forgiveness, that You may be feared."
In God's tefillin — says the Gemara in Berakhot — is written: "Who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth" (what other people in the world is like the Jews); but if Jews are sinful, then God's tefillin are false, and God wears unfit tefillin. So we say to God: "For with You is forgiveness" — You simply must forgive us, for otherwise Your tefillin are unfit — "that You may be feared", so that Your tefillin may be true...
Rabbi Meirl of Premishlan [Przemyślany].

J) "Each to his own trade."
Reb Hershele Halberstadt was the rabbi of Berlin, and he lived in one house with the cantor, for it was a house belonging to the community. Before Rosh Hashanah, when the cantor started gargling [warming up his voice], Reb Hershele could not sit and study, because the cantor was howling. Reb Hershele sent to ask him to hold his rehearsals later, and in rooms with closed windows — for who is obliged to suffer his shouting[?]. The cantor sent back: Let him not give me any opinions. Each to his own trade — he at studying and I at singing.
Having no choice, and lacking patience for the cantor's singing, Reb Hershele listened closely to all the cantor's melodies and learned them himself. In Berlin the custom was that the rabbi led Shaḥarit before the ark and the cantor — Musaf. At Shaḥarit Reb Hershele sang all the cantor's new melodies, so that the latter had nothing left with which to go up and lead Musaf. The cantor asks him: What have you done to me, Rabbi! He answers him:
— Each with his own trade: you with Musaf and I with Shaḥarit.
Aunt Paltshe and Her Neighbours — The Aunt's Troubles over Her Shared Corridor

[Feuilleton — humour; neighbours and housing.]
You surely know Aunt Paltshe — a Jewish woman with a "knak" [punch, verve], who won't let anyone blow into her porridge. A true woman of valour who "wears the trousers" and doesn't think much of "and he shall rule over her"; on the contrary: she holds the government, she has the say, she runs the household according to her own woman's wits.
Aunt Paltshe.
Who doesn't know Aunt Paltshe? A Jewish woman with a pair of broad shoulders, a pair of healthy hands, a fat double chin. Doctors even say it is no dangerous fatness, that it is just sort of puffed up, that the lard is no great virtue at all.
Yes, true, Aunt Paltshe is not overly healthy, but on the other hand she is a great "briye" [a capable go-getter]. A Jewish woman, a real go-getter. She knows how to put on a good front for people, and thanks to that very front she pushes her way into the richest, most aristocratic houses. Although she is no great expert in the "small print" [drobne letters], she nevertheless rubs shoulders with the very cream of the cream.
Aunt Paltshe's chief virtue is her boldness; she sets great store by the saying "Pieniądze nie mam, ale chucpę mam" [broken Polish: "Money I haven't got, but chutzpah I've got"] — and chutzpah Aunt Paltshe really has. Oh, do you hear, does Aunt Paltshe have chutzpah! And chutzpah is a great virtue, it is a charm for making a living: if you have chutzpah you get a name [?]; if you have chutzpah you get an interest-free loan sooner; without that bit of chutzpah it is hard nowadays to make a living. The only drawback is that Aunt Paltshe has chutzpah only towards her own household. When she goes among strangers, she bows her little head. Among strangers she becomes a poor thing, as if she couldn't count to two.
Aunt Paltshe has already been through all kinds of times. Good times and bad times; once, once she was a really wealthy woman, played a really big role, led a broad (a little too broad) life. Later her luck abandoned her, things fell butter-side down, so long and so broadly, until she became [?] a "sublokatorka" [subtenant].
Now Aunt Paltshe tells it gladly: thank God she has returned to her own household, now she is back on her horse, has her own flat again, and is a person on a par with everyone else.
Everything would indeed be fine and dandy, and perhaps Aunt Paltshe would now want to settle down and look after her household — but here is the trouble: the corridor.
As you know, Aunt Paltshe has a shared corridor. A "paradne" [main, front] passage, it is called, and who the partner in the corridor is you probably know — Reb Yekl. You surely know Reb Yekl; who doesn't know Reb Yekl, who smokes his pipe and [—?]. A cold-blooded robber and a great spiteful one, cold of lung and liver, always with a little smile on his lips — just the thing to lay on a wound [ironic: a real treasure].
Reb Yekl lives door to door with Aunt Paltshe. When he meets the aunt, he wishes her a broad "good morning", while in his heart he would gladly drown her in a spoonful of water; with utter hatred he hates Aunt Paltshe.
So what has he got against Aunt Paltshe? They do no business together, they hardly exchange more than "good morning", and really, what does the coarse, paunchy Reb Yekl have to do with my delicate Aunt Paltshe? And you should know that things are not so festive with Reb Yekl either; Reb Yekl, too, has already groped along the wall [known hard times], now he is back in the feathers [prosperous again] and has started puffing himself up. He lays out claims against Aunt Paltshe, and all his claims are because of — the corridor, because of the shared corridor. He wants no partnership. The corridor, he argues, belongs entirely to me, and if the aunt does not hand the corridor over to him amicably, he will take it from her by force — so Reb Yekl keeps on threatening.
So the aunt shouts: How so! Where is justice? After all, we have a contract, written and signed, that we both have equal rights to the corridor.
And if the aunt shouts — does he care? God forbid. Reb Yekl pulls pleasantly on his pipe, smiles meanwhile under his moustache, as if it were not him being meant. The aunt shouts, raises a hue and cry, and he, Reb Yekl, goes his own way. The corridor, he argues, belongs to me.
Well, what about the corridor? You surely think that Aunt Paltshe is frightened by Reb Yekl's threats; if so, you don't know Aunt Paltshe. Both of them are now studying "Two hold a corridor" [parody of the Talmudic "Two hold a garment"]. For the time being the corridor remains — as until now — shared. Reb Yekl put in a "wieszak" [coat stand], so Aunt Paltshe put in a "wieszak" too. Reb Yekl puts [?] vessels out into the corridor, so Aunt Paltshe also puts out [?] vessels. Reb Yekl nailed a nameplate with his name on the corridor door, so Aunt Paltshe nailed up, facing Yekl's plate, a plate with Aunt Paltshe's name. Reb Yekl hung up a letterbox at the entrance, so Aunt Paltshe nailed up a letterbox too. Reb Yekl got angry and tore down Aunt Paltshe's letterbox, so Aunt Paltshe tore down Reb Yekl's letterbox. Reb Yekl shouts at Aunt Paltshe: "Brazen hussy!" — Aunt Paltshe shouts at Reb Yekl: "You old liver sausage!" Reb Yekl turns off Aunt Paltshe's water — and straight away the "korek" [fuse] in Reb Yekl's electric meter blows. My Aunt Paltshe, you should know, is a "nie daj się" [Polish: "don't give in"] and laughs at Reb Yekl and his claims; Aunt Paltshe knows one thing: she has an explicit contract, written and signed — he can summon her to "Unetaneh Tokef" [i.e. to the Day of Judgement] for all she cares.
Ah, you will ask: why has Reb Yekl only now become such a "knaker" [big shot]? Why hasn't he made a peep until now? Why hasn't he shown his mighty deeds until now? The answer is: Madame Pragie.
As you know, Aunt Paltshe has an old "koleżanka" [girlfriend] — Madame Pragie. Who Madame Pragie is, you surely know: an old coquette, with wrinkles on her cheeks and painted lips, and a false cat into the bargain.
Well then, she — the powdered and painted Madame Pragie — was for a long time Aunt Paltshe's "opiekunka" [protectress]. If Aunt Paltshe suffered a wrong from someone, she ran to Madame Pragie. A true love, a real idyll reigned between Aunt Paltshe and Madame Pragie. Madame Pragie guarded Aunt Paltshe like an only daughter. Madame Pragie's love for Aunt Paltshe was not so much "out of love for Mordecai" as "out of hatred for Haman": because of her hatred of Reb Yekl, she loved Aunt Paltshe.
Now the hot love between Madame Pragie and Aunt Paltshe has cooled [?] a little. Madame Pragie has suddenly begun to flirt with Reb Yekl; until now she flirted only in secret, now she makes Reb Yekl open declarations of love, and, as the women gossip, Madame Pragie and Reb Yekl are said to be already in "intimate relations"...
The truth is that Aunt Paltshe feels deeply hurt by Madame Pragie's relations with Reb Yekl. And no wonder: her very own "koleżanka" goes and "zdradza" [betrays her] — and with whom? With Yekl, her mortal enemy; one could burst with heartache!
And if Reb Yekl has now suddenly raised his head, if Yekl-with-the-pipe has suddenly begun [—?] with such a [?] tone, it is only because he has become [intimate?] with the powdered and painted Madame Pragie.
Meanwhile "the Jews had [light]" [i.e. all is calm]. The corridor is still a corridor. Reb Yekl has his [?] vessels standing, and Aunt Paltshe has her [?] vessels standing. Reb Yekl has his "wieszak" hanging, and Aunt Paltshe has her "wieszak" hanging. Reb Yekl has a plate on the door, and Aunt Paltshe also has a plate on the door. Yekl has a bell with a letterbox, and Aunt Paltshe has a bell with a letterbox. If Reb Yekl turns off the aunt's water tap, the next day the fuse in Reb Yekl's electric meter will blow.
If you think Aunt Paltshe will hand the corridor over to Yekl amicably — if you think so, then, begging your pardon, you are greatly mistaken. You don't know my Aunt Paltshe...
An Unjustified Kehilla Subsidy

[Będzin — kehilla; education.] In the course of the last weeks a whole series of articles written by various authors appeared in the "Zaglembier Tsaytung", in which the dissatisfaction of Jewish public opinion with the so-called "powszechne" [state elementary] schools for Jewish children found expression. And indeed, these schools cannot satisfy any stratum whatsoever of the Jewish population, and there is no party at all in Polish Jewry that would relate positively to this school system, that could point to it and say with full mouth: "Behold this and sanctify it!"
This negative attitude towards the said type of school forms a united front, embracing all Jewish political shades from the extreme right to the extreme left. The fact that Jewish parents send their children more and more to the "powszechne" schools can in no way serve as an expression of sympathy for this educational institution. This sad phenomenon is only the fruit of the difficult economic situation in which the broad strata of our popular masses are sinking [?], and of the fragmentation of the Jewish parties in their views regarding the programme and spiritual content, as well as the language of instruction, of a Jewish people's school of our own — two factors which unfortunately frustrate the striving to create with our own means a Jewish communal school system that would truly correspond to our real needs in this most important field of national life.
In such a state of affairs there remains no other way out but that the Jewish kehilla, which must first of all take care of maintaining national existence through the proper education of the young generation, should as far as possible create suitable school institutions that would form a certain compromise with regard to the demands of the most varied parties. Unfortunately the Będzin Jewish kehilla, one of the largest in Poland, has so far shown no initiative or understanding whatsoever in this field. Worse still, it has shown a l a c k of understanding and of political maturity, by assigning year after year thousands of złoty as support for the "Jewish" powszechne schools, whose task is to estrange our children from the Jewish people and from its distinctive culture. A subsidy given in this manner with so generous a hand cannot be interpreted by the relevant representatives of power otherwise than as a warm expression of sympathy on the part of [?] the appointed Jewish representation towards these schools, which in truth are alien to us in their effect [?]. In this way the Będzin kehilla is acting expressly against the most sacred moral interests of the entire Jewish population it represents.
Azbsh"n.
The Troubles of a Present-Day Merchant... (From the Polish Press)

[Poland — economy and taxes; from the Polish press.] In the latest issue of the Sanacja weekly "Fiora" [?], which appears in Łódź, we find an interesting article which gives a sufficiently clear picture of the situation of a present-day merchant:
"One of the English banks — the article begins — received from one of its clients a letter with the following content: 'Dear Sir! I wish to inform you, dear Sir, that my present financial situation does not allow me to settle my debts with you according to the demand in your letter. My present situation I owe to the various laws of the state, the municipal institutions, the gminas [local authorities], the societies, the corporations, which have been imposed [?] upon a guiltless humanity [lit. 'God's-soul-guilty', a calque of the Polish 'Bogu ducha winny']. All these laws have oppressed me, tormented me, squeezed, broken and persecuted me so much that I have lost the awareness of who I am, what I am, and for what purpose I am actually here.
The laws have forced me and continue to force me to pay turnover tax, tax on capital, on luxury, on income, on property [majątek], real estate, car, gas, water supply, sewerage, light, road tax, school tax, on beer [?], wine, salt, on a ticket to the cinema, theatre, concert, and even on saying prayers in church [kościół].
Apart from the taxes, I am further required to give contributions [?] to various societies and associations, which only the cleverest and most enterprising head could have devised and organised. And here they are: the Society of St. John, the Women's Association, the Maritime League, "Imba" [? perhaps Y.M.C.A.], the Association of Gold Seekers, the Police Aid Fund, the Near East, the Far East, the Red Cross, the White Cross, the Black Cross, the Double Cross, the Blue Cross, the Scouts, aid for poor Jews, hospitals in every town and country, as well as all the well-known charitable associations in the town.
The government treats me in such a way that I do not know who is actually the real owner of my business. I am suspected, interrogated [?], inspected, spied upon, inspected once again, examined — in a word, I am ordered about and tormented to such a degree that I am already beginning to believe that I am suspected of having hidden somewhere an inexhaustible treasure of money, from which I can draw for all kinds of claims, needs, demands and wishes of humanity.
And because I refrain from giving gifts — since otherwise I would have to beg, borrow or steal money — they debate about me, boycott me, talk about me concerning this and that, drag me around and rob me so thoroughly that I am completely ruined, and if I still keep myself alive it is only because I am very curious to know what the hell that will come afterwards will look like.'"
The above-mentioned article, which we bring in abridged form, shows [?] once again what commerce in Poland looks like. Still more characteristic is the fact that the article was printed in a newspaper standing quite close to the regime that governs Poland today.
A sign that even in the Sanacja camp people have already noticed how rotten today's businesses are...
Sh. Sh-kh.

Before Rosh Hashana the artisans will receive the loans

[Będzin — crafts and economy.]
On Tuesday a conference was held under the chairmanship of the starosta [district head], Mr. Baksa [?], with the participation of representatives of the artisans' organizations of Będzin and Sosnowiec.
At the conference, which lasted from 9 o'clock in the morning until 3 in the afternoon, the question of the government loans for the artisans was discussed.
According to the starosta's statement, the loans will range from 500 zł. to 4000 zł. Each loan will be guaranteed by 2 sureties and repaid over the course of 10 months.
The loans will already be handed out in the coming days.
A new synagogue committee elected

[Będzin — community and synagogue.]
At the request of some 100 worshippers of the synagogue [the "shul"] a meeting was held, at which it was considered [decided] to elect a synagogue committee that should restore order in the synagogue.
After a short discussion a committee was elected consisting of Messrs. Moshe Leib Szwajcer, Meir Beri, Aharon Hercinger, Lejbisz Sztrubel, Lej[—]l Landner [?], Shlomo Zaks, Yaakov Goldberg, Jakl Rozen, Leib [?] Szwimer and Jakl Lederman.
The composition of the committee was reported to the kehilla board.
Robbed of 7 zł. 20 gr.

[Będzin area — crime.]
Between Gzichów and Grojec [Grodziec?] an assault took place on a resident of Grojec, Mr. Szyszka, who, under threat of a bayonet, was robbed of the sum of 7 zł. 20 groszy.
The assailant, a resident of the "Grable" [?], has been arrested.
Jewish apprentices, do not neglect your vital interests

[Będzin — crafts and vocational training.]
As is well known, the guild law provides that every apprentice who wishes to become independent must hold a certificate from the vocational courses.
Such vocational courses exist in every town and are financed by the municipal councils; unfortunately, the interest of the Jewish apprentices in the courses is very slight. It is a fact that the number of Christian apprentices enrolled already reaches 80 percent, and of Jewish ones barely 15 percent.
Such an apathetic attitude may be called criminal, for whoever does not hold a certificate from the vocational courses loses the right to become independent in the future.
We therefore call again on the Jewish apprentices to take stock of themselves and enrol in the vocational courses, which are held in the premises of "Piast".
On Sunday the Jewish children "occupy" the new school building

[Będzin — education.]
Next Sunday Public School No. 2 moves into the new school building on Krakowska Street; the municipal administration, school inspectors and city councillors have also been invited to the first entry.
Every child must bring along a pair of slippers; entry into the school rooms in shoes is forbidden.
President Fürstenberg resigns as a member of the main election commission

[Będzin — politics and elections.]
As we are informed, the president of the city council, Mr. Fürstenberg, has notified the main election commission that he resigns as a member of the commission.
Lectures by the actor Morewski disrupted

[Będzin and Sosnowiec — culture.]
The "Muza" had engaged the well-known Jewish actor Avraham Morewski, who wished to appear in Będzin and in Sosnowiec with lectures and recitations.
But at the last moment before the start the performances were disrupted by the police.
A Jew from out of town dies

[Będzin — misfortune.]
Last Monday the 52-year-old Yitzhak Frajnd of Warsaw, who lived at Buszazawska [?] 20, a glove maker, died in the local hospital.
Frajnd fainted in the street on the 16th of August [sierpień] of this year. The police carried him into the hospital, where he died.
Revenge on a Strike-Breaker

[Będzin — labour.] In Lustiger's bakery a Christian journeyman works who did not join in solidarity with the strike of the bakery journeymen.
On Saturday night, when the strike-breaker was on the outskirts of the town, he was attacked by several comrades, who beat him cruelly.
Meetings at the “Hitachdut”

[Będzin — Zionism.] Today, Friday evening, a members' meeting takes place devoted to the First Congress of Working Eretz Israel and to the elections, which will be held next Sunday.
On the same matter a meeting will also be held on Saturday afternoon, organised by the election committee of “Hitachdut” and “Gordonia” [printed “Nordogia”] (list number 3).
Sticker Sale for the Benefit of the Gemilut Chesed Fund

[Będzin — charity.] From Sunday on, delegates of the local “Gemilut Chesed” (free-loan) fund will sell stickers for the badge sale, which takes place during the coming Chol Hamoed Sukkot.
Hundreds of Jewish merchants and artisans make use of the “Gemilut Chesed” fund by way of loans; therefore it is everyone's duty to support the institution, which alleviates the prevailing crisis.
From the Zionist-Revisionist Movement

[Będzin — Zionism.] Last Saturday the continuation of the discussion on the report from the Prague World Conference took place in the movement's own premises.
The discussion was a stormy one; a fairly large number of members took part. At the end a resolution of confidence in the delegate, Mr. Langnus [?], was adopted.
— This Saturday there will be a lecture by Mr. D. Hafer [?] on the political events in Zionism.
Pledges on the Holidays Belong to the Charity Society

[Będzin — charity.] With the consent of the local rabbinate it has been decided that the pledges (nedarim) made by those called up to the Torah on Rosh Hashana, Yom Kippur and Sukkot belong to the charity society.
The income from the pledge campaign is for the 100 orphan boys and girls who are maintained by the society.
A Known Thief Arrested

[Będzin — crime.] The local police have arrested a certain Moshe Goldberg, who carried out the theft in Danziger's pharmaceutical warehouse.
Goldberg is known as a “qualified” burglar, and he has already been a 4-year “resident” of prison.
—o—
A Fine Donation.
[Będzin — charity.] Mr. Ch. L. Galisowski [?] has donated 50 złoty for the girls of the “Orphanage” of the local charity society; the board of the society expresses its thanks to the donor.
—o—
“Beit Lechem” for Rosh Hashana.
[Będzin — relief.] The “Beit Lechem” society supported over 100 respectable (genteel-poor) families with food products for Rosh Hashana. Every family received a sufficient portion of flour, sugar, beans, butter and candles.
—o—
New Deputy Starost.
[Będzin — authorities.] Since Monday the newly appointed deputy starost Składowski [?] from Płock has been in office.
—o—
A Victim of His Trade.
[Będzin — labour.] In the “Jowisz” coal mine a piece of coal broke loose and killed the 26-year-old worker Jan Kupic [?].
The Shochtim Have Withdrawn Their Decision for the Time Being

[Sosnowiec — community.] As we have reported, the shochtim (ritual slaughterers) sent an ultimatum to the kehilla board that the shochtim's pensions be secured according to the earlier agreement; if not — the shochtim threatened that they would no longer be dependent on the kehilla.
This week the shochtim received a reply that, owing to the absence of the kehilla board, the shochtim's claim cannot be settled favourably.
Because of this the shochtim have postponed their claims until the president returns.
A Police Sergeant as Guard at Selichot...

[Sosnowiec — community.] The peace agreement which was concluded a few weeks ago between the warring sides in Pogoń has “lost” its value, and the “battles” over the honours in the beit midrash have started again.
The cause of the new “outbreak” was that the gabbaim of the beit midrash demanded a payment for the “seats”, to which the “victorious” side did not agree, and it decided to storm the beit midrash at the first Selichot.
In order to be protected from the attack, an intervention was made with the commissioner, who assigned a przodownik (police sergeant), who throughout the whole time of the saying of Selichot kept watch that the “enemies” should not force their way in without tickets...
Tragic death of a 7-year-old boy

On Sunday around midday such a tragic incident occurred on the railway siding (bocznica) of the „Szyla“[?] factory: a group of children were playing, and one of them, the 2-year-old [so printed; the headline says 7] Jachar[?], ran across the railway tracks; at that moment a shunting train passed by and smashed the child to pieces.
Tram connection with Upper Silesia

The work on the tunnel is proceeding at a fast pace. According to the estimate the tunnel will be finished still this year.
In this connection the tram directorate has set about laying new tram lines, which will link the tram service through to Upper Silesia.
Jewish representatives on the Social Welfare Commission

The activity of social welfare has been extended. The town has been divided into 14 districts (rewiry), and in each district a representative has been appointed who has the authority to give aid.
Among the 14 representatives there are 3 Jews, Messrs. Zendel[?], Lewenhof and Rajchman.
Improved situation on the coal market

In the course of the current month the situation on the coal market has improved considerably. Not only at home — the export abroad, too, has grown by 15 percent compared with the month of sierpień [August].
Brutal murder in Mandżew
On Monday a brawl broke out in Mandżew[?] among several local Christian neighbours. During the brawl one of them slit open the other's belly with a knife, from which the victim died instantly.
A letter from Brazil for Mrs. Szpira
Rabbi Dawid[?] Jehoszua Halberstam of Stary Sosnowiec asks us to announce that he has received a letter from rabbis in Brazil who have made inquiries about her husband, who abandoned her.
On the Eretz Israel etrogim

We have received a public proclamation (kol kore) from Rabbi Kook of Jerusalem and other rabbinic authorities, who warn etrog buyers that etrogim also from Eretz Israel have appeared on the market, but they are from Arab orchards. The etrogim of the society „Agudat Etrog“ are from Jewish soil.
—o—
A large Tel Hai meeting
This Sabbath at 5 in the afternoon a large public meeting devoted to the Tel Hai campaign will take place in the premises of the Zionist Organization. All Zionist groupings that sympathise with the fund will take part in the meeting.
—o—
Bernsztajn's murderer in court
In the local district court the trial took place of the murderer who some months ago murdered the Dąbrowa merchant Herszel Bernsztajn. The murderer was sentenced to 6 months' prison.
—o—
Minister Składkowski in Zagłębie
Yesterday at 10 in the morning the Minister of the Interior Składkowski was in Będzin and Sosnowiec, where he held a series of conferences in the bodies of his department.
—o—
Strzemieszyce — A blue-and-white evening
On Wednesday 8 October (the evening after the first festival days of Sukkot) the local Zionist Org. is holding a blue-and-white evening in the hall of the „Iluzjon“ cinema, to which all national organisations of the surrounding towns as well as a large number of guests are invited.
Olkusz — A terrible suicide

On Sunday evening the town was shaken by the terrible news that the 32-year-old young man Bendet[?] Fiszel had committed suicide by hanging. The suicide had for a long time not been in his right mind; on the fatal day, around 2 o'clock in the afternoon, he locked himself in his room, drew[?] the curtains and tied himself with a towel to a hook in the ceiling; a few hours later the family broke open the door and beheld their tragedy.
The deceased was a gentle Hasidic young man, esteemed in the whole town; he leaves a wife and a 10-year-old boy orphaned.
Almost the entire Jewish population took part in the funeral, which was held on Monday.
Wolbrom. A Big Fire.

[Wolbrom — fire.]
In the night from Wednesday to Thursday a fire broke out in Gajfeld's [?] house. The fire spread quickly and caught two neighbouring houses, all of which burned down.
Suspicion for the outbreak of the fire fell on the landlord, who was indeed arrested the next morning.
When Gajfeld's wife went to the commissariat [police station] to intercede for her husband's release, she too was detained by the police.
The woman was later released, but Gajfeld was taken to Olkusz, to the starosty [district office].
Final Demand

[Sosnowiec — association notice.]
We hereby call upon Mr. Herszel Nachemja [?] to bring, within 7 days (i.e. by Friday, 26 September 1930), to the secretariat of the Craftsmen's Association (Targowa 9) the sum of association money that has remained with him.
Should the debt not be paid by the set date, we shall be compelled to hand the said matter over to the court.
The Board
of the Jewish Craftsmen's Association in Sosnowiec
They Have Approved the "Agudah" Budget of the Będzin Kehilla

[Będzin — Kehilla.] All subsidies for cultural purposes — struck out.
Yesterday the Będzin kehilla administration finally received back the kehilla budget, approved by the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
The budget was "worked over" so thoroughly that nothing remained of it but "skin and bones". All institutions and associations were "damaged", except the "Agudah" with its "kreplach", which came out unscathed, and only they will enjoy[?] the budget...
All subsidies for the Będzin Jewish schools, libraries, artisans' courses, the yeshivas "Beit Yisrael" and "Keter Torah", etc., were struck out entirely. Exempt from this "Caesarean section", however, were the subsidies for: "Beit Yaakov", "Poalei Agudat Yisrael", "Bnot Agudat Yisrael", "Chachmei Lublin", "Chizuk HaDat", "Tzeirei Emunim", etc., etc...
The Ministry even added 15 thousand zł. for the construction of the mikveh and 15 thousand zł. for the "Beit Yetomim" (orphanage).
All unpaid subsidies from 1929 for a number of institutions were struck out — except the subsidy for the Lublin Chachmim (Chachmei Lublin).
—o—
[Zagłębie — City Council.] Mr. Fürstenberg is active in the Main Electoral Commission
As this issue was going to press, the chairman of the city council, Mr. Fürstenberg, informed us that the circulating report that he is not taking up his mandate on the Main Electoral Commission is untrue.
Mr. F. fulfils his mandate on the Main Electoral Commission properly and takes part in every session.
—o—
[Sosnowiec — Education.] School inspector withdraws the "Sunday rest" decree.
The sharp stand taken by the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" against the decree forbidding lessons on Sunday in the Sosnowiec public (powszechne) schools has had its proper effect. As this issue was going to press we received confidential word from Sosnowiec that the decree forbidding lessons on Sunday has been withdrawn by the school inspector.
—o—
[Sosnowiec — Artisans.] A mass meeting of Sosnowiec artisans.
On Wednesday, the second day of Rosh Hashana, at 8 p.m., an important mass meeting of all Jewish artisans in Sosnowiec (members and non-members) will take place in [the association's] own premises.
Among other things, a position will[?] be adopted on the question of artisans' examinations, the levy for the Unemployment Fund and other current questions. It is therefore the duty of all Jewish artisans to come en masse to the said meeting.
—o—
[Sosnowiec — Zionism.] An academy for Working Eretz Israel.
In connection with the forthcoming World Congress for Working Eretz Israel, which takes place at the end of this month in Berlin, a festive academy will be held tomorrow, Saturday, at 8 p.m., in the hall of the "Hotel Polski".
The academy is organised on the initiative of the Right Poalei Zion in Sosnowiec.

Mass Meeting of the Sosnowiec Artisans' Association

[Sosnowiec — artisans.]
On Wednesday, at the close of the festival [Rosh Hashanah], a mass meeting of the Jewish Artisans' Association in Sosnowiec took place in its own premises, attended by more than 200 members.
The president, Mr A. Szpakowski[?], opens the meeting, dwelling in a longer speech on a whole series of current questions of the Jewish craftsman.
After certain explanations from the secretary, Mr Ganzweig[?], it was unanimously resolved to approach the Ministry of Commerce with a memorandum on reducing the fee for master-craftsman examinations from 140 to 50 zł., and on extending by another 3 years the term of the eased examination for older craftsmen (as is known, the term ends on 15 December of this year).
In addition it was resolved, in connection with the new regulation (which comes into force on 1 July 1931), according to which all craftsmen employing a minimum of 1 worker are obliged to pay into the Unemployment Fund (Fundusz Bezrobocia) — to approach the Minister of Labour with the request that the old regulation (that the levy be taken from those employing 5 workers and more) should remain in force, or alternatively that the implementation of the regulation be postponed for 2 years.
Finally the communiqué of the headquarters of the Jewish Artisans' Union in Warsaw was read, concerning the withdrawal of a number of Zionist members from the executive and the Central Committee for the sake of the unity of the artisans' organisation.
On this last question the meeting adopted no position whatsoever, because this matter is to be considered in the coming weeks by the All-Polish Jewish Artisans' Congress.

Dr Dobrowolski receives a penalty of 14 days' arrest
[Sosnowiec — court.]
At the labour court in Sosnowiec a trial took place on Wednesday against Dr Dobrowolski, the secretary of the municipal slaughterhouse in Sosnowiec.
Dr Dobrowolski was charged by the labour inspector with failing to introduce safety measures for the workers at work in the slaughterhouse, owing to which[?] a worker fell into a cauldron of boiling water and was badly scalded.
The labour court sentenced the accused to 14 days' arrest or a payment of 250 zł. At the same time it was ordered that the proper safety measures be introduced in the slaughterhouse immediately.

The dispute over the Sosnowiec slaughterhouse is settled
[Sosnowiec — municipality.]
For several months now there have been disputes between Mr Zweigenhaft and the city administration concerning the municipal slaughterhouse in Sosnowiec.
The matter has finally been settled thanks to the head (naczelnik) of the administrative department of the Kielce voivodeship, who held several sessions in the form of arbitration.
The terms are as follows: until the end of March 1933 Zweigenhaft will be the proprietor of the slaughterhouse; for this period the Magistrat [city council executive] receives 156 thousand zł., payable in 24 instalments; in addition Zweigenhaft must pay the Magistrat's court costs in the amount of 23 thousand zł.
The terms must be confirmed by the city council, which will hold a session next Monday, the 28th of this month

Tomorrow the World Congress for Labour Palestine Opens in Berlin

[Zionism — World Congress for Labour Palestine, Berlin.]
An important historical document, without doubt, is the call by the famous Jewish scholars, writers and socialist politicians of our generation to take part in the World Congress for Labour Palestine (Eretz Israel). What has united them all [?] is the historic upbuilding work of the Jewish worker in Palestine and the firm will to walk hand in hand with the Jewish worker along the hard road of concrete deeds of construction.
Beside the meritorious veteran of international socialism, Eduard Bernstein, the appeal is signed by the courageous fighting spirit of the French Socialist Party, Léon Blum. [Also] Julius Braunthal, chief editor of the Social Democratic press service in Vienna and editor of the socialist monthly "Der Kampf", and Fritz Naphtali, the important economic-policy expert of German Social Democracy. Also signing are Dr. Oskar Cohn, the old friend of the Jewish labour movement; A. B. Kleerekoper, the meritorious leader of Dutch Social Democracy; and the courageous leader of the Jewish labour movement in America, Abraham Shiplacoff.
Yiddish and Hebrew literature are represented by their most important personalities, Sholem Asch and Hayim Nahman Bialik. The meritorious Jewish historian Prof. Simon Dubnow has, by his signature, once again stressed his heartfelt attachment [?] to the great work of the Jewish workers in Palestine. W. Latzky-Bertholdi too, editor of "Frimorgn" in Riga and one of the founders of the Folkspartei, has by his signature once again shown his loyalty to the Palestine work of the Jewish workers. From among the Western European Jewish scholars and writers: Prof. Albert Einstein, Prof. Sigmund Freud, Lion Feuchtwanger, Max Brod, Martin Buber and Arnold Zweig.
The Only Way Out (On the Situation of the "Hazomir" Library)

[Będzin — culture; the "Hazomir" library.]
Some time ago we acquainted the public, in this place, with the activity of the "Hazomir" library in Będzin. On that occasion we pointed to the goals that the library's management sets itself for the future.
We pointed out that the new and newest books published on the Yiddish book market had been purchased — works both originally Yiddish and translations from world literature.
Within the limits of our restricted means we have tried to beautify and improve [?] the outward appearance of our library, and as the first step of our efforts we considered [?] the catalogue, when we will still be [able] [?] to supply the reader at any time with every newly published work.
But it is hard, almost impossible, for us at the present moment to carry out our first task. Our budget is ridiculously small: 400 zł. a year is given to us by the local magistrate [town council], 200 zł. a year by the Jewish gmina [community] in Będzin; the income from readers' fees does not even cover the administrative expenses, and even when one adds the small donations for the library on the part of [?] the closely associated members, the result is a sum that can in no way suffice for buying and binding new books and keeping the old ones in order.
Lately the situation has grown worse because the Ministry of Religious Denominations [Ministry of Cults] has struck the 200 zł. from the kehilla off our budget;
the debt from the year 1929 has also been struck off for us;
we must redeem bills of exchange for books purchased;
for lack of money, dozens of unbound books lie on the shelves and cannot be issued to the reader;
dozens of volumes have been withdrawn from the inventory and must be rebound — and the number of readers is not growing.
The management has considered the difficult situation and resolved:
The number of readers must be tripled. It must be the duty of every reader to recruit at least 2 new ones.
This is for the time being the only way out at the present moment, in order to keep the library at its present level.
A member of the management.

Theatre Notes: "Arlekin"

[Sosnowiec — theatre; the "Arlekin" revue theatre.]
"We don't feel like it" — with these words the revue at the "Arlekin" began. And indeed the artists may well not feel like it when they see how small the audience is. Attendance — according to the compère — varies: one time the hall is almost empty, another time somewhat fuller; and on top of all that the "Arlekin" has acquired a partner — the magistrate [town council], which has taxed the theatre at 20 per cent. The conditions, we see, are truly hard, and it is therefore really a wonder that the only revue theatre in Zagłębie gets no support from the population. This paralyses the development of the theatre and does not allow it to reach a higher level, because — as far as jokes and monologues are concerned — they are somewhat too "esterlazbar" [?; unclear word, apparently "risqué/objectionable"] from the moral standpoint. We would advise introducing more political and local satire.
Humour and atmosphere in the hall are brought by Mieciarkówna [?]; she is an individuality, with her pleasant voice, artistic maturity, freedom and naturalness on stage. She sings, dances and entertains the audience. Among the men, Mr. Marski stands out, a specialist in monologues and humorous telephone "conversations". But even at the Sosnowiec "Arlekin" one can be convinced: which Polish jokes are the best? — the Jewish ones. Starting from the greatest, such as "Qui Pro Quo" and Krukowski, the whole of Poland is entertained by Jews and Jewish humour.
* * *
The other artists are, on the whole, good material.

A Tkhine for a City Councillor
(To be said with great devotion.)
Master of all worlds, You created a good inclination along with an evil inclination; for a seat on the city council I am the scapegoat. A miracle happened: number 17 put me into the city council, a living corpse. „You created in me a brain“ — a brain You created in me, to bring honour to the voters; I admit and confess that I deserve „wishes“ for sitting on the city council and twisting people’s brains. „You created in me hands“ — You gave me hands, but they are not worth a cent; on an important question I make an effort, and at the vote, instead of raising my hands up high, I scratch my knees. „You created in me a mouth“ — when I open my mouth to speak, the gallery shouts „fie!“. When my mouth stops speaking I think it over, whether it would not have been better had I kept it shut. So I beg You, forgive me for my sinful lust, for the time that I work in vain.
